name: One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 43201 ("Artificial intelligence and information technology modernization initiative")
summary:
Appropriates $500 million to the Department of Commerce for FY 2025 to modernize federal IT systems using AI and automation technologies.

Authorizes the Secretary of Commerce to use funds to replace legacy systems, adopt efficient AI models, and enhance cybersecurity with AI solutions.

Enacts a 10-year moratorium preventing state and local governments from regulating AI models or systems.

Exempts laws facilitating AI deployment or removing legal barriers, provided they do not impose additional requirements unless federally mandated or generally applicable.

name: California Executive Order N-12-23 (State use of GenAI)
summary:
Orders California's Government Operations Agency and related entities to draft a report for the Governor within 60 days on beneficial uses and risks of Generative AI (GenAI) by the state.

Requires the California Cybersecurity Integration Center and related bodies to perform a risk analysis by March 2024 on GenAI threats to energy infrastructure, brief the Governor on findings, and make public recommendations for actions to guard against GenAI threats when appropriate. 

Directs various California departments to issue procurement and training guidelines for GenAI by January 2024.

Instructs relevant agencies to develop guidelines by July 2024 for using GenAI tools with vulnerable communities.

Mandates establishment of GenAI pilot project infrastructure by March 2024.

Urges the Governor's Office to partner with UC Berkeley and Stanford to evaluate GenAI's impact.

Tasks legal counsel to assess GenAI's regulatory impact and recommend updates.

Emphasizes collaboration with civil society, academia, and industry experts in drafting guidelines and conducting analyses.

name: California SB 1288 (Public schools: artificial intelligence working group) (2024)
summary:
Requires the Superintendent of Public Instruction to form a working group to address artificial intelligence in public schools.

Requires the working group to develop guidance and a model policy for safe AI use in education by January 1, 2026.

Instructs the working group to create a model policy by July 1, 2026, for the safe and beneficial use of AI that does not negatively impact students or educators.

Mandates that the working group consist of certain stakeholders, including public school teachers and schoolsite administrators.

Calls the working group to assess AI use in education, including technologies in use, costs, and impacts on educators, and to detail current uses of artificial intelligence in educational settings.

Requires the working group to conduct at least three public meetings for stakeholder feedback.

Requires the working group to identify other ways in which the state can promote effective practices that minimize risk and maximize benefits to pupils and educators, including establishing communities of practice on the use of artificial intelligence in education.

Obliges the group to report findings and recommendations to the Legislature by January 1, 2027.

Dissolves the working group upon report submission and repeals provisions by January 1, 2031.

name: California AB 96 (Public Employment: Automated Vehicle Tech)
summary:
Require public transit employers in California to notify the exclusive employee representative at least 10 months before starting a procurement process for autonomous transit vehicle technology that could eliminate jobs.

Mandate collective bargaining within 30 days upon notification or within 10 days of the public transit employer receiving a written request from the exclusive employee representative, focusing on developing and implementing the autonomous transit technology, creating transition plans for affected workers, and preparing them for new roles.

Ensure that this chapter does not impose any labor requirements that are less protective than existing statutory or contractual obligations.

Grant the Public Employment Relations Board jurisdiction to handle unfair practice charges related to this chapter.

Authorize the board to establish, amend, or repeal regulations necessary to implement the chapter, including emergency regulations for the immediate preservation of public welfare.

name: California SJR 6 ("Artificial Intelligence")
summary:
Urges the President and Congress to develop a comprehensive Artificial Intelligence Advisory Committee.

Urges the adoption of a comprehensive artificial intelligence policy.

Highlights the importance of federal government planning for workforce changes due to AI.

Emphasizes the need for ethical standards in AI development and employment.

Encourages promoting innovation to help American companies grow.

Notes that California has attracted significant global AI investment.

Calls for bridging the gap between technological change and regulatory response.

Directs transmission of the resolution to key federal officials and California representatives.

name: California AB 1831 (Child Pornography Crimes)
summary:
Prohibits the creation, distribution, and possession of child sexual assault material (CSAM) generated by artificial intelligence (AI) in California.

Defines AI as a machine-based system capable of generating outputs that influence environments.

Amends California's Penal Code to include AI-generated CSAM as obscene matter, subject to legal penalties.

Classifies the distribution or possession of AI-generated CSAM depicting minors under 18 engaging in sexual conduct as a felony, punishable by imprisonment and fines.

Omits the necessity to prove commercial intent or obscenity for violations involving depictions of real minors.

Specifies enhanced penalties for repeat offenders and those using government-owned computers for CSAM-related offenses.

Exempts law enforcement, medical, scientific, educational activities, and lawful conduct between spouses from these provisions.

Requires revenue from fines to support sexual assault investigator training and services for human trafficking victims.

Becomes operative only if Senate Bill 1381 is enacted by January 1, 2025.

name: California SB 1381 (Crimes: child pornography) (2024)
summary:
Expands existing child pornography laws to include materials digitally altered or generated by artificial intelligence.

Prohibits the production, distribution, or possession of AI-generated depictions involving minors engaging in sexual conduct.

Imposes penalties including fines and imprisonment for violations involving AI-generated content depicting minors, including recruiting minors to create such content.

Specifies exemptions for legally emancipated minors; law enforcement; legitimate medical, educational, or scientific activities; and lawful conduct between spouses.

Allows forfeiture of AI-generated depictions involving minors engaging in sexual conduct that is in the possession of city, county, or state officials or agencies.

Allows destruction of AI-generated materials regardless of criminal conviction.

Mandates that the act becomes operative only if AB 1831 is enacted by January 1, 2025.

name: California AB 2839 (Election Advertisements)
summary:
Prohibits the distribution of materially deceptive AI-generated content related to elections, such as deepfakes, during specified periods before and after elections in California. 

Requires disclosures for manipulated content used by candidates, stating "This [media type] has been manipulated," ensuring transparency.

Allows recipients of deceptive content, candidates, or election officials to seek injunctive relief and damages against violators.

Exempts broadcasting stations from liability under certain conditions, such as bona fide news coverage or compliance with existing federal laws.

Defines key terms like "deepfake," "materially deceptive content," and "malice" to establish clear guidelines.

Applies provisions to all languages and mandates that disclosures match the language of the advertisement.

Includes an urgency clause, making the act effective immediately to protect upcoming elections from AI-driven disinformation.

name: California 2023 SCR 17 (Relative to AI)
summary:
Affirms the California Legislature's commitment to President Biden’s vision for safe AI and the "Blueprint for an AI Bill of Rights."

Commits the Legislature to examining and implementing principles, including Safe and Effective Systems, Algorithmic Discrimination Protections, Data Privacy, Notice and Explanation, and Human Alternatives in AI-related policies.

Directs the Secretary of the Senate to transmit copies of this resolution for distribution.

name: California (2024) AB 2885 (Artificial Intelligence)
summary:
Requires, by September 1, 2024, the California Department of Technology to inventory high-risk automated decision systems used or proposed by state agencies, detailing decision-making roles, data usage, and risk mitigation measures.

Mandates an annual report on high-risk systems to legislative committees until 2029.

Defines "artificial intelligence" as systems that infer inputs to influence environments, and outlines "high-risk automated decision systems" that impact significant areas like housing and employment.

Obliges the evaluation of deepfake technologies' impact on state governance and residents, with a report due by October 1, 2024.

Stipulates annual public reporting on automation impacts, including AI, within economic development subsidies for warehouse distribution centers, focusing on job effects and workforce changes. 

Ensures public access to information about economic subsidies and associated impacts from AI and automation developments.

name: California AB 2355 (AI in political advertisements), Sec 8
summary:
Requires committees creating or distributing qualified political advertisements to include a disclosure stating, “Ad generated or substantially altered using artificial intelligence,” in a clear and conspicuous manner.

Mandates that the disclosure be displayed or spoken as specified in existing sections of the Government Code.

Excludes alteration or negation of rights under Section 230 of Title 47 of the U.S. Code for interactive service providers.

Authorizes the Commission to seek injunctive relief or pursue administrative or civil remedies if committees fail to comply with disclosure requirements.

Defines "artificial intelligence" and specifies conditions under which media is considered "generated or substantially altered using artificial intelligence.”

Clarifies that immaterial alterations, such as cosmetic adjustments or resizing, do not qualify as being substantially altered by artificial intelligence.

Specifies that non-compliance does not constitute a misdemeanor.

name: California AB 1836 (Use of likeness: digital replica)
summary:
Amends the California Civil Code to impose liability on individuals using a deceased personality's likeness without consent, including AI-generated digital replicas. Requires violators to compensate for unauthorized use, with statutory minimums and profit disgorgement. Excludes certain uses such as news, satire, and fleeting references from consent requirements. 

Recognizes posthumous rights as transferable property interests, extending rights to heirs or designated persons. Limits rights duration to 70 years post-death and outlines specific inheritance rules. Mandates registration with the Secretary of State for enforcing claims, making these registrations public records.

Clarifies that certain artistic and informational works are exempt unless they serve commercial product promotion. Outlines exceptions for media owners unless knowingly complicit in unauthorized use. Enforces consistency with existing law by rendering remedies cumulative. Establishes retroactive application of rights back to those deceased before January 1, 1985.

name: California AB 107 (Budget Act 2024), Sec. 2.00, Item 0511-001-0001 (For support of Secretary of Government Operations)
summary:
Establishes monthly Generative AI meetings with legislative staff to discuss Executive Order N-12-23 implementation.

Requires updates on deliverable completion, proof of concept implementation, and funding source identification.

Supports budget requests for generative AI technology solutions if additional resources are needed.

Defines "artificial intelligence" and "generative artificial intelligence" within the provisions.

Treats data collected in GenAI pilot projects as personal information per Civil Code Section 1798.3.

Prohibits GenAI pilot projects from including sensitive personal information, data on minors, educational records, or medical information.

Mandates compliance with California's GenAI Guidelines for departments in GenAI pilot projects.

Permits the use of de-identified data for research to justify resource requests if expanding pilot program scope.

name: California AI Transparency Act (2024)
summary:
Enacts the California AI Transparency Act, requiring covered providers of generative AI systems with significant user bases to offer free AI detection tools.

Mandates that AI detection tools assess whether content was created or altered by the provider's AI, output system provenance data, and avoid personal provenance data.

Prohibits the collection or retention of personal information from detection tool users, barring specific opt-in scenarios.

Requires AI-generated content to include both manifest and latent disclosures identifying it as AI-generated, with details about the provider and system.

Demands that licenses for GenAI systems include obligations for content disclosures.

Imposes civil penalties of $5,000 per violation for non-compliance, with each day constituting a separate violation.

Excludes specific entertainment products from applicability and sets the operative date as January 1, 2026.

name: California SB 1120 (Health care coverage: utilization review) (2024)
summary:
Mandates health care service plans and disability insurers using AI for utilization review or management to comply with specific regulations.

Requires AI tools to base decisions on individual clinical data and prohibits reliance solely on group datasets.

Prohibits AI tools from denying, delaying, or modifying health care services based on medical necessity; such determinations must be made by licensed professionals.

Ensures AI tools do not replace human decision-making or discriminate against enrollees.

Requires AI tools' criteria to comply with state and federal laws and be open for audits.

Mandates regular review and revision of AI tools for accuracy and reliability.

Prohibits misuse of patient data beyond intended purposes, in line with privacy laws.

Stipulates that AI use should not harm enrollees and requires disclosure of AI usage policies.

name: California AB 2876 (Pupil instruction: media literacy: artificial intelligence literacy: curriculum frameworks: instructional materials) (2024)
summary:
Mandates the commission to consider incorporating AI literacy content into the mathematics, science, and history-social science curriculum frameworks when those frameworks are next revised after January 1, 2025.

Requires the commission to consider including AI literacy in the criteria for evaluating mathematics, science, and history-social science instructional materials adopted by the state board after January 1, 2025.

Defines "AI literacy" as the knowledge, skills, and attitudes related to how artificial intelligence works, including its principles, concepts, applications, limitations, implications, and ethical considerations.

Directs the commission to also consider including media literacy content in the curriculum frameworks and instructional materials for English language arts and English language development, mathematics, science, and history-social science when these are revised or adopted after specified dates.

name: Take It Down Act
summary:
Amends the Communications Act of 1934 to criminalize the publication of nonconsensual intimate visual depictions, including digital forgeries created using AI, in interstate or foreign commerce.

Defines digital forgeries as depictions created with AI or other technological means that are indistinguishable from authentic depictions.

Prohibits the publication of such depictions for both adults and minors, with specific intent requirements such as causing harm or for sexual gratification.

Imposes penalties, including fines and imprisonment, for offenses involving adults and harsher penalties for those involving minors.

Mandates covered platforms, such as websites with user-generated content, to establish a process for the removal of nonconsensual depictions within 48 hours of receiving a request.

Enforces compliance through the Federal Trade Commission, treating violations as unfair or deceptive acts.

Provides exceptions for certain authorized law enforcement and good faith activities and outlines processes for restitution and forfeiture related to violations.

name: TAKE IT DOWN Act (2025)
summary:
The TAKE IT DOWN Act mandates covered platforms to remove nonconsensual intimate visual depictions, including those created by artificial intelligence (AI), known as digital forgeries. 

Prohibits intentional disclosure of such depictions without consent, especially targeting AI-altered, identifiable images. 

Imposes penalties, including fines and imprisonment, for offenses involving adults and minors. 

Requires covered platforms to establish a removal process within one year of the Act’s enactment, responding promptly (within 48 hours) upon receiving a valid removal request.

Mandates reasonable efforts to remove identical copies across platforms. 

Exempts platforms from liability for good faith removal of purportedly nonconsensual depictions. 

Empowers the Federal Trade Commission to enforce compliance, treating noncompliance as an unfair or deceptive act. 

Specifies legal exceptions, including disclosures for lawful or investigative purposes. 

Defines covered platforms as public websites or applications hosting user-generated content.

name: California AB 2013 (AI Training Data)
summary:
Defines key terms such as "artificial intelligence," "developer," "generative artificial intelligence," and "synthetic data generation" to clarify the scope and applicability of the regulations.

Mandates developers of generative AI systems, including parties that release a new system or make substantial modifications to a system, released on or after January 1, 2022 to publicly disclose training data documentation on their websites by January 1, 2026, and for each subsequent release.

Requires documentation to include a summary of datasets, sources, purposes, data points, intellectual property status, personal information, any data processing or modifications, and the use of synthetic data generation.

Exempts AI systems solely for security, aircraft operation in national airspace, or national security and defense provided they are only available to federal entities.

name: California Assembly Bill 2905 (Telecommunications: automatic dialing-announcing devices: artificial voices) (2024)
summary:
Amends the Public Utilities Code to regulate the use of automatic dialing-announcing devices in California.

Requires person calling to make a natural voice announcement before using an automatic dialing-announcing device, which includes stating the nature of the call and the business or organization details; inquiring whether the called person consents to hear a prerecorded message; and informing the called person if the message uses an artificial voice.

Requires person calling to disconnect the device after call termination by either party.

Defines the terms “artificial intelligence” and “artificial voice."

name: California AB 3030 (AI Health Care Services)
summary:
Requires health facilities, clinics, and physician offices using generative AI for patient communications in a variety of modalities to include a disclaimer indicating AI generation.

Mandates the disclaimer's prominence at the beginning, end, and/or throughout written, audio, and video communications, with instructions for contacting a human provider.

Exempts communications reviewed by a licensed health care provider from disclaimer requirements.

Defines key terms, including "artificial intelligence," "generative artificial intelligence," and "patient clinical information."

Subjects licensed health facilities, clinics, and physicians violating these requirements to enforcement mechanisms.

name: FY2025 NDAA, Section 222 ("Modification to artificial intelligence education strategy")
summary:
Amends Section 256 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2020 to mandate the development of AI and machine learning education platforms.

Requires the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer of the Department of Defense, in coordination with the Under Secretary of Defense for Personnel and Readiness, to create distance education courses on foundational AI and machine learning concepts and their ethical and responsible use.

Mandates making these courses available to Armed Forces members within 180 days of the enactment of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025.

Requires the Secretary of Defense to report to congressional defense committees on the progress of implementing this educational initiative within 270 days of the subsection's enactment.

name: FY2025 NDAA, Section 1066 ("Reports on approval and deployment of lethal autonomous weapon systems")
summary:
Mandates the Secretary of Defense to submit annual reports to congressional defense committees on lethal autonomous weapon systems by December 31, 2025, and annually until December 31, 2029.

Requires inclusion of a comprehensive list of lethal autonomous weapon systems approved for use, waived from review, under review, and not approved, along with relevant dates.

Specifies that the initial report should cover all relevant periods as determined by the Secretary, while subsequent reports cover periods since the last report.

Allows for reports to be unclassified but permits a classified annex.

name: H.R.2246 Foreign Investment Guardrails to Help Thwart (FIGHT) China Act
summary:
Imposes sanctions on certain Chinese entities and individuals engaged in defense or surveillance sectors through the International Emergency Economic Powers Act.

Requires notification for U.S. investments in prohibited technologies and establishes penalties for violations, reflecting stringent oversight on national security transactions involving China.

Mandates divestment of securities by U.S. persons from entities on the Non-SDN Chinese Military-Industrial Complex Companies List, prohibiting holding after a specified period.

Outlines procedures for approving exceptions to these prohibitions through waivers, subject to congressional notification and review.

Establishes a framework for using collaborative reports and a public database for covered foreign persons while protecting sensitive information.

Outlines regulations and processes to enforce prohibitions, commands an annual report to assess developments, and encourage multilateral cooperation to prevent China’s acquisition of sensitive technologies. 

Designates Commerce and Treasury authorities to oversee implementation and allows Presidential delegation of some powers.

name: S257 Promoting Resilient Supply Chains Act of 2025
summary:
Requires the Assistant Secretary of Commerce to promote the resilience of critical supply chains and emerging technologies vital for U.S. national security, in consultation with key government figures.

Mandates the creation of a Supply Chain Resilience Working Group within 120 days, comprising multiple federal agencies, to evaluate and model critical supply chains, including those for emerging technologies such as AI.

Directs the Assistant Secretary to identify vulnerabilities, develop response strategies, and assess domestic and allied manufacturing capacities within one year.

Prohibits disclosure of voluntarily submitted critical supply chain information under FOIA, providing protection against unauthorized use.

Necessitates annual reporting to Congress detailing strategies and evaluations of supply chain resiliency, including the role of technologies such as AI.

Limits the Act’s funding to existing resources and imposes a 10-year termination period for the Act’s provisions.

name: H2444 Promoting Resilient Supply Chains Act of 2025
summary:
Assigns the Assistant Secretary of Commerce new responsibilities to promote the resilience of critical supply chains and emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence. 

Establishes a Supply Chain Resilience Working Group to assess and address vulnerabilities in critical supply chains and technologies.

Mandates consultations with various stakeholders, including government entities and international allies, to improve supply chain readiness and response to disruptions.

Encourages domestic production and reduced reliance on countries posing national security risks for critical goods and technologies, including AI.

Protects voluntarily submitted critical supply chain information from public disclosure under the Freedom of Information Act.

Requires periodic assessments and strategy reports to Congress on supply chain resiliency and emerging technology impacts.

Sets a 10-year term for the act's provisions and requires a public comment period for certain designations and reports.

name: Next Generation Pipelines Research and Development Act
summary:
Establishes a demonstration initiative to fund advanced pipeline technologies via competitive merit reviews, focusing on AI-driven advancements in leak detection, sensor technologies, and machine learning for pipeline monitoring.

Directs funding of $45 million in 2026 and $50 million annually from 2027-2030 for relevant projects, with a sunset provision five years post-enactment.

Forms a Joint Research and Development Program involving the Department of Energy and other federal agencies to advance AI and machine learning models for pipeline systems, ensuring security and integrity.

Creates a National Pipeline Modernization Center to commercialize AI-assisted pipeline technologies, requiring competitive selection and location adjacent to existing infrastructure.

Mandates the National Institute of Standards and Technology to develop standards supporting AI in pipeline safety, with a $2.5 million annual allocation from 2026-2030.

Aims to leverage and complement existing energy and pipeline safety infrastructure and programs through collaborative interagency efforts and non-federal funding matching.

name: Promoting US Leadership in Standards Act of 2025
summary:
Mandates the Director of the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), in coordination with the Secretary of State, to brief Congress about opportunities for U.S. support in developing AI standards within one year.

Requires the establishment of a web portal to inform U.S. industry and federal agencies about international AI standards efforts and participation opportunities.

Initiates a pilot program to support AI standards meetings in the U.S. by awarding grants to eligible entities.

Specifies eligibility criteria for these grants and defines allowable costs.

Requires annual briefings to Congress on the pilot program's effectiveness.

Directs the development of recommendations for a permanent program if deemed feasible within two years.

Authorizes a budget of $5 million for the program from fiscal years 2024 through 2028. 

Ends the pilot program five years post-enactment, with consideration for permanent implementation.

name: Leading Ethical AI Development (LEAD) for Kids Act
summary:
Establishes the LEAD for Kids Standards Board to govern AI systems affecting children in California.

Requires AI developers to classify systems as "covered products" with risk assessments ranging from prohibited to low risk.

Mandates developers to register covered products and submit risk assessments by July 1, 2028.

Prohibits AI use that adversely impacts children's health, safety, or privacy without informed consent.

Requires companion chatbots and systems that assess emotional states or collect biometric data to receive additional scrutiny.

Mandates independent audits based on risk level and public incident reporting for adverse impacts.

Obligates deployers to prevent unauthorized child access and adhere to usage requirements that do not increase system risk.

Prohibits retaliation against employees reporting violations.

Allows the Attorney General to enforce violations with penalties, and provides a private right of action for harmed children.

Creates the LEAD for Kids AI Fund to support these regulatory activities.

name: Department of Energy Quantum Leadership Act of 2025, Sec 2 ("Department of Energy quantum information science research program")
summary:
Amends the National Quantum Initiative Act to enhance quantum information science, engineering, and technology research led by the Secretary of Energy.

Mandates the establishment of National Quantum Information Science Research Centers to drive breakthroughs and collaborate with industries and other entities.

Directs cooperative research and commercialization efforts to advance various quantum fields, including AI, quantum computing, communications, and security.

Requires the development of a strategic 10-year plan for high-performance computing systems integrating quantum and AI.

Funds a new $20 million per year program for quantum high-performance computing R&D from 2026 to 2030.

Establishes a university-led traineeship program and prohibits funding to entities affiliated with Confucius Institute or certain foreign entities.

Prioritizes coordination with other federal agencies and entities.

Allocates $175 million annually for these initiatives from 2026 to 2030 with specific restrictions.

name: TAME Extreme Weather and Wildfires Act
summary:
Directs the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) to use artificial intelligence (AI) for adapting to extreme weather and wildfires.

Mandates the development of comprehensive weather forecasting training datasets and AI weather models.

Requires NOAA to explore advanced AI applications to enhance weather forecasts and improve information delivery.

Instructs NOAA to provide technical assistance for AI weather model usage and establish best practices.

Directs the creation of an AI-driven program to predict, detect, and analyze wildfires.

Advocates for partnerships with private and academic entities for innovation in environmental forecasting.

Obligates NOAA to strengthen its workforce expertise in AI applications for weather forecasting.

Allows public access to data and code developed under the Act, with considerations for national security and intellectual property.

Provides guidance on minimizing environmental impacts when using AI technologies in these initiatives.

name: New York A6453 (RAISE Act)
summary:
Amends New York's general business law to introduce the Responsible AI Safety and Education (RAISE) Act, implementing transparency requirements for deploying AI frontier models.

Requires large AI developers to implement and retain a written safety and security protocol that must be published with redactions and submitted to the Attorney General and Homeland Security.

Stipulates annual reviews of the protocol to accommodate any advancements.

Requires prompt reporting of safety incidents to authorities within 72 hours.

Prohibits knowingly making false or misleading statements concerning AI documentation.

Empowers the Attorney General to bring civil actions for violations, with penalties up to $30 million for repeated offenses.

Confirms that the Act applies exclusively to frontier AI models developed or operating in New York State.

Clarifies that this Act doesn't establish a private right of action and is cumulative with other legal obligations.

name: AI and Critical Technology Workforce Framework Act of 2025
summary:
Expands the functions of the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) to include the development of workforce frameworks for critical and emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence.

Mandates the Director of NIST to develop, publish, and periodically update a workforce framework specifically for artificial intelligence within 540 days of the Act's enactment.

Requires the inclusion of competencies, workforce categories, and work roles relevant to AI in the workforce framework, highlighting career pathways for individuals with nontraditional backgrounds.

Obligates consultation with federal agencies, industry, and educational institutions to develop these frameworks.

Demands reports to Congress on the updates and practical applications of the frameworks, with a focus on increasing employer and educational adoption.

Promotes global adoption by producing resources in multiple languages.

Incorporates professional and employability skills relevant to AI workforce frameworks and assesses additional framework needs for emerging technologies, such as quantum information science.

name: H.R.1851 Fighter Force Preservation and Recapitalization Act of 2025
summary:
Amends U.S. Code to increase the required minimum number of fighter aircraft in the Air Force to 1,900, extending compliance to 2030, but allows temporary reductions for transitions, provided levels don't fall below 1,800.

Mandates annual reports by the Secretary of the Air Force to Congress on the status of fighter aircraft inventory, including new acquisitions, unit assignments, and any legacy retirements, with penalties for late submission.

Requires prioritization of recapitalized fighter allocations to existing Air Force squadrons, allowing one-for-one legacy aircraft retirement.

Obligates the Air National Guard to maintain 25 fighter squadrons and restricts retiring legacy or fifth-generation aircraft unless unserviceable.

Directs an annual recapitalization plan for Air National Guard squadrons, assessing financial and readiness impacts, with a focus on acquiring F–16 Block 70 aircraft.

Defines terms such as "advanced capability fighter aircraft," "fifth-generation fighter aircraft," and "next-generation air dominance fighter aircraft."

name: H.R.1569 CATCH Fentanyl Act
summary:
Mandates the establishment of pilot projects by the Secretary of Homeland Security within one year to evaluate technologies for enhancing inspection processes at U.S. land ports of entry.

Requires testing of at least five types of nonintrusive inspection technology enhancements, including artificial intelligence and machine learning, to aid in detecting contraband and threats.

Ensures private sector involvement and emphasizes cost-effectiveness in technology selection.

Obligates safeguarding data privacy during inspections, with adherence to laws, data anonymization techniques, and regular audits.

Demands reports analyzing effectiveness, recommendations for widespread technology use, and cost breakdowns.

Includes necessary privacy and civil liberties impact assessments and reports before implementation and post-pilot.

Prohibits new appropriations, relying on existing resources for implementation.

name: Advancing AI Education for American Youth EO
summary:
Establishes a White House Task Force on Artificial Intelligence Education to promote AI literacy and proficiency in the United States, chaired by the Director of the Office of Science and Technology Policy.

Requires the Task Force to coordinate Federal efforts on AI education, including organizing the Presidential Artificial Intelligence Challenge to encourage collaboration and innovation in AI.

Mandates public-private partnerships to provide K-12 AI education resources and calls for increased funding and resources to develop AI literacy.

Prioritizes AI-focused training for educators and the integration of AI tools in classrooms through grants and public-private partnerships.

Instructs the Secretary of Education and other Federal entities to support the use of AI in educational settings to improve outcomes.

Directs the Secretary of Labor to increase AI-related Registered Apprenticeships and promote AI skill development through the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act (WIOA).

Encourages agencies to prioritize AI in educational grant programs.

name: TAME Extreme Weather and Wildfires Act 2025
summary:
Mandates the improvement of weather, water, and wildfire forecast accuracy through artificial intelligence (AI) by federal agencies.

Promotes public-private partnerships to expedite AI adoption for mitigating environmental hazards.

Directs the development and curation of comprehensive weather forecasting training datasets in consultation with various federal and research entities within four years.

Permits exploration of AI weather models for global, regional, and local forecasting.

Encourages the use of AI to enhance communication and public understanding of weather risks.

Mandates regular reporting to Congress on activities and potential risks of foreign access to U.S. weather data.

Allows the Under Secretary to enter partnerships, including co-investment strategies, for AI and environmental forecasting innovation.

Provides for public access to operational AI weather models, subject to national security and intellectual property considerations.

Authorizes appropriations to support these initiatives through fiscal years 2026 to 2030.

name: Fair Grocery Pricing Act
summary:
Prohibits food producers from using algorithmic systems to artificially inflate prices or reduce supply through coordinating functions or tacit agreements.

Deems any such use as a per se violation of the Sherman Act.

Mandates the Federal Trade Commission and the Attorney General to enforce this prohibition using applicable antitrust laws.

Authorizes civil actions by the FTC, state attorneys general, and aggrieved persons to recover damages and seek penalties.

Invalidates pre-dispute arbitration agreements and joint action waivers related to violations of this Act at the plaintiff’s election.

Ensures that this Act does not modify existing antitrust laws or preempt state or local laws.

Includes a severability clause to uphold remaining provisions if any part is deemed unconstitutional.

name: Coast Guard Authorization Act of 2025, (Subtitle C - "Matters Involving Uncrewed Systems")
summary:
Establishes a National Advisory Committee on Autonomous Maritime Systems to advise the Secretary on regulation and use within U.S. territorial waters, comprising 15 expert members representing diverse maritime sectors.

Implements a two-year pilot program exempting small uncrewed maritime systems from certain regulatory requirements when operated by the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, unless immediate safety concerns arise.

Mandates the Coast Guard to develop a training course on small uncrewed maritime systems, addressing operations, safety, and communication aspects over three years.

Incorporates National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration representation into the Automated and Autonomous Vessel Policy Council.

Requires the Coast Guard to submit a report within one year establishing an uncrewed systems capabilities office, detailing strategies for technology acquisition, coordination, collaboration, and expanding capabilities using AI and machine learning.

Defines relevant terms, including "counter-uncrewed system" and "small uncrewed maritime systems."

name: Wildfire Prevention Act of 2025 (Sec. 302 "Public-private wildfire technology deployment and testbed partnership.")
summary:
Establishes a deployment and testbed pilot program for new and innovative wildfire technologies within 60 days of enactment.

Requires coordination among the Secretaries of Agriculture and Interior and covered agencies to identify technology priority areas like AI, quantum sensing, and augmented reality for wildfire prevention and mitigation.

Prioritizes covered entities with emerging technologies that address identified issues for participation in the pilot program.

Mandates real-time testing and on-the-ground coordination between selected entities and covered agencies.

Requires public outreach to invite applications from entities for technology testing and demonstration in key priority areas.

Obligates annual reporting to appropriate committees, detailing participating entities, tested technologies, cost estimates, and outreach efforts.

Sets the program's expiration at 7 years after enactment, with annual assessments and recommendations to foster the adoption of promising technologies.

name: Supporting Innovation in Agriculture Act of 2025
summary:
Establishes a tax credit of 30% for investments in innovative agricultural technology projects under the Internal Revenue Code.

Defines "innovative agricultural technology project" as technology used to produce, store, process, and package specialty crops with precision agriculture or controlled environment agriculture, effective through December 31, 2035.

Specifies "qualified property" includes tangible personal property, software, and technology necessary for these projects and subject to depreciation rules.

Includes provisions for specific modern technologies, such as AI, machine learning, robotics, and various sensors, under both controlled environment and precision agriculture technologies.

Prohibits double benefit from using both this tax credit and specific government grants.

Amends sections of the Internal Revenue Code to incorporate the innovative agricultural technology investment credit.

Sets the amendment's applicability to projects starting construction after January 1, 2025.

name: Department of Homeland Security Vehicular Terrorism Prevention and Mitigation Act of 2025
summary:
Requires the Secretary of Homeland Security, alongside TSA and CISA, to submit a report on the prevention, deterrence, and response to vehicular terrorism.

Mandates the report to assess threats related to connected and autonomous vehicles and ADAS technologies, including AI-driven cybersecurity vulnerabilities.

Instructs inclusion of evaluations regarding DHS's engagement with public and private stakeholders, focusing on vehicle rental and ride-sharing platforms to prevent misuse.

Calls for recommendations on AI-enabled predictive analytics and vehicle immobilization technologies to detect and mitigate threats.

Demands coordination with enforcement agencies to address vehicular terrorism through intelligence sharing and joint training.

Ensures countermeasures and AI use respect privacy and civil liberties.

Obliges publication of an unclassified report summary for public access and annual briefings to Congress on developments and recommendations.

Defines “vehicular terrorism” as the use of vehicles to commit acts of terrorism.

name: Leveraging AI to Streamline the Code of Federal Regulations Act of 2025
summary:
Requires the Director of the Office of Management and Budget, in consultation with the National Institute of Standards and Technology, to annually implement a process using artificial intelligence to identify redundant or outdated federal regulations.

Mandates the use of an AI system that meets strict standards for accuracy, transparency, accountability, and national security risk.

Obliges agencies to review identified redundant or outdated regulations within 30 days and make a final determination of their status.

Commands the rescission or amendment of regulations found to be redundant or outdated within 30 days after determination.

Requires the public publication of any determination with a brief explanation, with an option for a classified annex to Congress if necessary.

Amends Title 5 of the United States Code to facilitate the expedited rescission and amendment of redundant or outdated regulations identified through AI review.

name: Promoting Precision Agriculture Act of 2025
summary:
Mandates the Secretary of Agriculture, in consultation with the National Institute of Standards and Technology and the Federal Communications Commission, to develop voluntary interconnectivity standards for precision agriculture within two years of enactment.

Requires coordination with public and private stakeholders, including industry organizations and voluntary standards bodies, to create these standards.

Includes the consideration of evolving demands, connectivity needs, cybersecurity challenges, and the impacts of advanced wireless technology and AI on precision agriculture.

Directs the Comptroller General to conduct studies assessing these standards' development, voluntary nature, industry coordination, and adoption success, with reports due to Senate and House committees.

Aims to enhance precision agriculture participation in the U.S. and promote U.S. leadership in setting standards for precision agriculture through voluntary consensus standards development organizations.

name: One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 60003 ("U.S. Customs and Border Protection technology, vetting activities, and other efforts to enhance border security")
summary:
Appropriates $1,076,317,000 to U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) for AI, machine learning, and non-intrusive inspection equipment to combat illicit narcotics at U.S. borders.

Restricts funds for certain surveillance towers unless they are tested and federally accepted for autonomous capabilities.

Defines "autonomous" as systems using AI, sensors, and onboard computing to automate identification tasks traditionally performed manually by CBP personnel.

name: Health Tech Investment Act
summary:
Amends the Social Security Act to classify algorithm-based healthcare services under Medicare’s new technology ambulatory payment classification.

Requires the Secretary of Health and Human Services to assign payment classifications based on cost data submitted by manufacturers, including diverse factors like invoice prices and overhead.

Specifies that algorithm-based services cannot be removed from their payment classification until adequate claims data is available, and mandates a minimum tenure of five years within the initial classification.

Adjusts the criteria for eligibility in new technology classifications to include distinct procedures that use AI, machine learning, or other software when used adjunctively with underlying services.

Defines algorithm-based healthcare services as those using FDA-approved AI or software for clinical guidance.

Mandates the payment system for software services as described in a 2022 Medicare rule, effective from January 2023.

name: H.R.1142 Amending the Public Health Service Act for Drug Adherence Guidelines
summary:
Amends the Public Health Service Act to mandate the Secretary of Health and Human Services to establish drug adherence guidelines aimed at 90 percent adherence for Medicare part B and D drugs.

Requires incorporation of artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies in these guidelines.

Promotes, to the greatest extent possible, the use of generic and biosimilar drugs.

name: Copyright Office Part 3 Generative AI Training Pre-Publication Version 2025
summary:
Recognizes the importance of voluntary licensing agreements for AI training and notes that these arrangements have developed in some contexts, particularly with high-volume or limited copyright owners.

Suggests that voluntary collective licensing can reduce transaction complexity and cost, while offering flexibility for both copyright owners and licensees.

Raises concerns that a compulsory licensing regime would inhibit market-based solutions and prove inflexible and slow to adapt.

Views Extended Collective Licensing (ECL) as a potentially less intrusive solution in sectors where voluntary licensing fails.

Discourages requiring copyright owners to opt out, emphasizing consent for uses within statutory rights, though acknowledges Congress may consider exceptions allowing opt-outs.

Encourages the Department of Justice to clarify antitrust concerns related to collective licensing.

Recommends allowing the licensing market to evolve organically, suggesting targeted interventions only if specific market failures arise.

Notes the nascent state of AI law, markets, and technology, and urges reliance on collaborative market-based solutions as legal clarity evolves.

name: Copyright Office Part 1 Digital Replicas 2024
summary:
Recommends that Congress establish a federal right to protect individuals from the distribution of unauthorized digital replicas during their lifetimes. 

Proposes that this right be licensable and subject to guardrails but not assignable, with remedies such as monetary damages and injunctive relief available. 

Requires traditional rules of secondary liability, with a safe harbor for online service providers suitably conditioned.

Suggests explicit First Amendment accommodations in the law.

Advises against full preemption of state laws, recognizing established state rights of publicity. 

Offers the Copyright Office as a resource for Congress, the courts, and the executive branch in implementing these recommendations and addressing future developments in AI governance.

name: One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 100001 ("Coast guard assets necessary to secure the maritime border and interdict migrants and drugs")
summary:
Appropriates $140 million for long-range unmanned aircraft systems and related infrastructure to improve the US Coast Guard's capabilities. 

Allocates $180 million for maritime domain awareness equipment and services, including $75 million specifically for autonomous maritime systems. 

Allows, through 2030, for entities other than the Coast Guard to acquire, procure, or construct floating dry docks, provided they meet defined requirements. 

Limits design, planning, and engineering expenses to 15% of specified funding allocations for maintenance facilities. 

Exempts acquisitions funded under this act from sections 1131, 1132, and 1133 of title 14, United States Code. 

Mandates compliance with reporting requirements and submission of an expenditure plan to relevant Congressional committees.

Prohibits expenditure during any fiscal year if the Coast Guard is non-compliant with specified sections of title 14, United States Code. 

Requires prior notification to Congress before procurement actions affecting cost or timelines.

name: Emerging Innovative Border Technologies Act 2025
summary:
Mandates the Secretary of Homeland Security to submit a plan within 180 days to integrate and deploy emerging technologies, such as AI and machine learning, for border security.

Specifies the contents of the plan, including assessment of privacy impacts, coordination with private and public sectors, and scaling of current programs.

Authorizes CBP Innovation Teams to research and adapt commercial technologies for border security, setting strategic goals and operating procedures.

Requires annual reporting by CBP on Innovation Teams' activities, including descriptions of piloted technologies and their effectiveness.

Promotes identifying and phasing out obsolete technologies in favor of advanced systems, with cost assessments.

Encourages collaboration across sectors to leverage innovative technologies and incentivizes private sector participation. 

Obligates CBP to evaluate authorities and potential needs for new authorization to facilitate technology acquisition and integration, ensuring effective border security operations.

name: Western Wildfire Support Act of 2025 (Sec. 205 "Study on modernizing wildfire response technologies.")
summary:
Require the Secretaries to conduct a study on modernizing wildfire response technologies.

Include in the study necessary improvements to radio communications systems and infrastructure during wildland fire or prescribed fire operations, assessing the quality, reliability, failure impacts, and improvement options.

Assess real-time or near-real-time situational awareness tools for operational firefighters, ensuring interoperability and evaluating additional remote sensing and mapping capabilities.

Conduct a cost analysis of commercially available systems versus internally developed systems.

Analyze wildland fire predictive modeling, focusing on data requirements, computing needs, and the feasibility of using artificial intelligence for more accurate predictions.

Require the submission and public availability of the study results within one year of the Act's enactment to congressional committees and the public.

name: Healthy Technology Act of 2025
summary:
Amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to include artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies as practitioners eligible to prescribe drugs.

Requires that such AI and machine learning technologies be authorized by state statutes to prescribe the specific drug involved.

Mandates that these technologies be approved, cleared, or authorized by the Food and Drug Administration under sections 510(k), 513, 515, or 564.

name: PATHS Act
summary:
Extends the use of other transaction authority for research and development acquisition under the Homeland Security Act of 2002 from September 30, 2024, to September 30, 2028.  
   
Mandates notification to congressional committees within 72 hours after the use or extension of transaction authority involving artificial intelligence (AI) technology.  
   
Requires the Secretary of Homeland Security to offer a briefing explaining the reason for using or extending AI-related transaction authority.  
   
Reduces the maximum amount for covered contract awards under the James M. Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023 from $4,000,000 to $1,000,000.

name: One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 20004 ("Enhancement of Department of Defense resources for munitions and defense supply chain resiliency")
summary:
Appropriates $400 million for accelerated one-way attack unmanned aerial systems with advanced autonomy, emphasizing AI capabilities for defense.

Allocates $1 billion to expand the industrial base for one-way attack unmanned aerial systems, further enhancing AI-driven military operations.

Provides $58 million for development, production, and integration of counter-unmanned aerial systems programs, highlighting AI's role in defense against drone threats.

Designates $350 million for non-kinetic counter-unmanned aerial systems programs, demonstrating focus on AI-based alternatives to traditional munitions.

Earmarks $250 million for land-based, and $200 million for ship-based counter-unmanned aerial systems programs, underscoring AI use in diverse defense environments.

Allocates $62 million for AI-enhanced hypersonic strike programs, underscoring importance of AI in cutting-edge military technology.

Requests $500 million for Department of Defense Credit Program to support critical mineral industries, indirectly promoting AI technology development by ensuring material availability.

Permits up to $100 billion in loans and guarantees, indicating a strategic commitment to fortifying supply chains essential for AI advancements within the defense sector.

name: One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 20005 ("Enhancement of Department of Defense resources for scaling low-cost weapons into production")
summary:
Appropriates $124 million to enhance the Test Resource Management Center's AI capabilities.

Allocates $145 million for developing AI to support one-way attack unmanned aerial systems and naval systems.

Assigns $250 million to advance the AI ecosystem and another $250 million to expand Cyber Command's AI initiatives.

Provides $250 million to develop the Test Resource Management Center's digital test environment.

Designates $1 billion for expanding programs to accelerate innovative technology procurement, affecting AI initiatives.

Directs $2 billion to scale commercially developed technology, including AI, for military use through the Defense Innovation Unit.

Supports the acceleration of Quantum Benchmarking Initiative with $250 million.

Earmarks $500 million to avoid delays in delivering autonomous military capabilities that involve AI technologies.

Includes a $1 billion appropriation for a capital assistance program, including loans and guarantees, aiding AI projects.

Ensures these appropriations and initiatives remain available until September 30, 2029, supporting ongoing AI and technology development in defense.

name: One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 112204 ("Implementing artificial intelligence tools for purposes of reducing and recouping improper payments under Medicare")
summary:
Mandates the implementation of artificial intelligence tools by January 1, 2027, to reduce and identify improper payments under Medicare Parts A and B.

Directs the Secretary to contract with AI vendors and data scientists to support the implementation.

Requires the recoupment, where practicable, of improper payments identified through AI tools.

Obliges the Secretary to report to Congress by January 1, 2029, and annually thereafter on AI implementation and payment recoupment, including potential improvements and recoupment statistics.

Allocates $12.5 million each from the Federal Hospital Insurance Trust Fund and the Federal Supplementary Medical Insurance Trust Fund to fund these AI initiatives for fiscal year 2025, with funds available until expended.

name: Duplicative Grant Consolidation Act, Sec. 4. "Report on feasibility of leveraging artificial intelligence to identify duplicative Federal grant applications."
summary:
Mandates the Director of the Office of Management and Budget to submit a report to Congressional committees.

Requires consultation with the Secretary of Energy, the Director of the National Science Foundation, and the Director of the National Institute of Standards and Technology.

Focuses on assessing the feasibility of using AI to identify duplicative Federal grant applications.

Seeks to determine whether an applicant has received or submitted another grant application for the same purpose.

Aims to identify waste, fraud, and abuse in the grant application process through AI technology.

name: Nondiscrimination in Health Programs and Activities, § 92.210
authority: Department of Health and Human Services
summary:
Prohibits covered entities from discriminating based on race, color, national origin, sex, age, or disability through the use of patient care decision support tools in health programs or activities.

Requires covered entities to make reasonable efforts to identify uses of such tools that employ input variables or factors measuring race, color, national origin, sex, age, or disability.

Mandates covered entities to make reasonable efforts to mitigate discrimination risks from identified tools in their health programs or activities.

name: United States-Israel Defense Partnership Act of 2025, Sec. 6. "United States-Israel Emerging Technology Capabilities Cooperation."
summary:
Supports and encourages defense collaboration between the United States and Israel in emerging technologies, specifically artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, robotics, quantum, and automation. 

Authorizes the Secretary of Defense, in coordination with the Secretary of State and the Director of National Intelligence, to jointly conduct research, development, testing, and evaluation with Israel in these areas. 

Requires protection of sensitive information and national security interests during any activities carried out under this authority. 

Prohibits activities from commencing until a report is submitted detailing a memorandum of agreement for cost-sharing and intellectual property rights, and ensuring semiannual expenditure reporting by Israel.

Designates the Irregular Warfare Technology Support Directorate as the lead agency once the report is submitted. 

Mandates semiannual reports to Congress on program developments. 

Authorizes $50,000,000 annually from 2026 to 2030 for this program.

name: One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 20002 ("Enhancement of Department of Defense resources for shipbuilding")
summary:
Appropriates $450,000,000 for the application of autonomy and artificial intelligence to naval shipbuilding.

Allocates $1,534,000,000 for the expansion of small unmanned surface vessel production.

Sets aside $1,800,000,000 for the expansion of medium unmanned surface vessel production.

Provides $1,300,000,000 for the expansion of unmanned underwater vehicle production.

Designates $188,360,000 for the development and testing of maritime robotic autonomous systems and enabling technologies.

Earmarks $174,000,000 for the development of a Test Resource Management Center robotic autonomous systems proving ground.

Funds $250,000,000 for the development, production, and integration of wave-powered unmanned underwater vehicles.

name: Air National Guard Squadron Preservation Act of 2025, sec. 2., subsection (c)
summary:
Mandates the Secretary, with the Air National Guard Director, to study the necessity of acquiring advanced capability fighter aircraft for the Air Force.

Requires consideration of plans to implement unmanned or autonomous capabilities in fighter aircraft.

Includes evaluation of cost savings linked to foreign sales of F-16 variants.

Identifies eligible Air Force units for recapitalization with advanced fighter aircraft.

Assesses how these aircraft meet current and contingency mission needs of combatant commanders.

Determines whether a multiyear contract is the optimal acquisition method.

Obligates the Secretary to report findings to congressional defense committees within 180 days of enactment.

name: IRONDOME Act of 2025
summary:
Accelerates the development of autonomous agents to defend against cruise missiles and drones.

Requires the Secretary to use all available authorities to achieve this goal.

Aims to enhance cost-effective defense of the United States homeland and forward-deployed armed forces.

name: One Big Beautiful Bill Act 2025, Section 20006 ("Enhancement of Department of Defense resources for improving the efficiency and cybersecurity of the Department of Defense")
summary:
Appropriates $200 million for the deployment of automation and artificial intelligence to accelerate audits of the Department of Defense's financial statements, as outlined in chapter 9A and section 2222 of title 10, United States Code. 

Specifies that these funds remain available until September 30, 2029.

name: FY2025 NDAA, Section 1638 ("Sense of Congress with respect to use of artificial intelligence to support strategic deterrence")
summary:
Expresses the sense of Congress that artificial intelligence and machine learning can strengthen strategic communications, improve planning efficiency, and enhance modeling capabilities for stockpile stewardship.

Emphasizes the need for caution to prevent AI from compromising critical strategic assets.

Establishes U.S. policy that AI use should not undermine nuclear safeguards, affect weapon system functionality, or alter the validation of command communications.

Requires positive human actions for nuclear weapon employment decisions by the President to remain intact.

name: FY2025 NDAA, Section 1007 ("Use of technology using artificial intelligence to facilitate audit of the financial statements of the Department of Defense for fiscal year 2025")
summary:
Encourages the Secretaries of Defense, Army, Navy, and Air Force to use AI and machine learning technologies to facilitate audits of the Department of Defense's financial statements for fiscal year 2025.

Requires the Director of the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Office, in coordination with the Under Secretary of Defense for Research and Engineering and the Inspector General, to oversee the adoption of AI and machine learning technologies for financial management and enterprise business operations.

name: Texas Responsible AI Governance Act (2025 Update) (HB 149)
summary:
Regulates AI systems in Texas under the Texas Responsible Artificial Intelligence Governance Act.

Prohibits AI systems from inciting harm, criminality, manipulation, or discrimination based on political viewpoints or protected classes.

Establishes the Artificial Intelligence Council and a regulatory sandbox program for controlled AI testing.

Requires government disclosure to consumers when AI is used in interactions.

Instructs the attorney general to enforce regulations, manage complaints, and impose fines for non-compliance.

Prohibits government use of AI for social scoring or capturing biometric identifiers in violation of rights.

Mandates that AI must not produce certain unlawful content and must adhere to consumer protections and data privacy.

name: FY2025 NDAA, Section 233 ("Management and utilization of digital data to enhance maintenance activities")
summary:
Mandates the development and implementation of policies to manage and utilize digital data for maintenance of aircraft, ships, and ground vehicles within one year.

Requires investment in advanced data infrastructure for efficient data processing.

Instructs the development of a strategy incorporating AI and automated systems for data organization.

Demands collaboration with vendors to overcome proprietary data limitations through open data approaches.

Addresses enhancement of data transmission capabilities with high-speed technologies and secure methods.

Mandates central compilation of maintenance data and creation of user interfaces for data analysis.

Requires vendor-agnostic, interoperable tagging systems unless exceptions are justified.

Calls for review of classification policies to ensure appropriate classification without limiting usability.

Establishes protocols for detecting unauthorized access to vehicle or platform systems.

Obligates a briefing to Senate and House Armed Services Committees on policy development and implementation status.

name: FY2025 NDAA, Section 237 ("Pilot program on use of artificial intelligence for certain workflow and operations tasks")
summary:
Requires the Secretary of Defense to initiate a pilot program within 60 days to evaluate AI-enabled software for optimizing workflows and operations at Department of Defense facilities, including depots and shipyards, and in contract administration.

Mandates the use of top-tier software platforms, consideration of industry best practices, implementation based on human-centered design, and connection to authoritative enterprise data sources.

Obliges consultation with the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment, and the Secretaries of the Army, Navy, and Air Force.

Requires a report within one year detailing software evaluations, workflow modifications, and a quantitative assessment of the software's impact.

name: FY2025 NDAA, Section 6504 ("Establishment of Artificial Intelligence Security Center")
summary:
Mandates the Director of the National Security Agency to establish an Artificial Intelligence Security Center (within the Cybersecurity Collaboration Center of NSA) within 90 days of the Act's enactment.

Requires the Center to develop guidance to prevent or mitigate counter-artificial intelligence techniques.

Promotes secure artificial intelligence adoption practices for managers of national security systems and the defense industrial base.

name: FY2025 NDAA, Section 1069 ("Biodefense posture reviews")
summary:
Requires the Secretary of Defense to conduct comprehensive biodefense posture reviews by December 31, 2026, and December 31, 2029.

Mandates inclusion of an inventory and assessment of existing biodefense strategies and policies, relevant biological threats, and current Department of Defense programs related to biological threats.

Identifies methods using artificial intelligence and cyber capabilities to address biological attacks.

Recommends strengthening biodefense capabilities and improving interagency coordination.

Requires submittal of a review to congressional defense committees within 30 days of completion.

Specifies that reviews must be unclassified but may include a classified annex.

name: FY2025 NDAA, Section 1032 ("Competitive demonstration of large and extra large unmanned underwater vehicles")
summary:
Mandates the Secretary of the Navy to conduct a competitive demonstration of large and extra large unmanned underwater vehicles by June 1, 2025, in coordination with relevant military entities.

Requires evaluation of user feedback on these vehicles as well as vehicles' integration with mission autonomy planning, capability in contested environments, performance attributes, technical maturity, and cost to procure, operate, and sustain.

Permits the use of fiscal year 2025 Navy funds for research, development, and demonstration activities.

Obligates the Secretary of the Navy and the Commander of the United States Indo-Pacific Command to submit assessments to congressional defense committees by September 1, 2025, which may include recommendations and validation of underwater vehicle requirements.

Defines the vehicles as capable of submerged operation while supporting one or more missions with modular payload integration and a minimum range of 1,000 nautical miles.

name: FY2025 NDAA, Section 232 ("Expansion of participation in the Digital On-Demand Program")
summary:
Mandates the Secretary of Defense to expand the Digital On-Demand Program to all organizations and elements, Armed Forces members, and civilian employees within the Department of Defense.

Requires active promotion of the Program throughout the Department.

Obligates the Secretary of Defense to submit a progress report to the Senate and House Armed Services Committees within 180 days of enactment and annually through 2029.

Defines the Digital On-Demand Program as an initiative overseen by the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer, providing on-demand educational resources on AI, emerging technologies, and data literacy to Department of Defense personnel via a digital platform.

name: FY2025 NDAA, Section 1515 ("Protective measures for mobile devices within the Department of Defense")
summary:
Requires the Secretary of Defense to evaluate cybersecurity products and services for mobile devices to enhance the Department of Defense's cybersecurity.

Evaluates technologies such as anonymizing-enabling technologies, network-enabled content inspection, on-device VPNs, and AI-based protection against smishing, phishing, and text/email compromises.

Assesses the efficacy and scalability of these technologies within the Department of Defense and their integration with existing cybersecurity architecture.

Mandates submission of a report to congressional defense committees within 270 days detailing findings and recommendations on procuring or incorporating evaluated technologies.

name: Council of Europe Framework Convention on AI
summary:
Mandates Parties to adopt measures ensuring AI systems align with human rights, democracy, and the rule of law.

Requires transparency, accountability, and non-discrimination in AI systems' lifecycle.

Obligates implementation of measures to protect privacy, human dignity, and democratic processes.

Demands risk assessment and mitigation strategies for AI, considering human rights impacts.

Establishes a follow-up mechanism for international cooperation and compliance monitoring.

Provides for accessible remedies for human rights violations arising from AI systems.

Calls for public consultation and digital literacy to address AI-related impacts.

Stipulates that Parties must ensure effective procedural safeguards and oversight mechanisms.

Allows exceptions for artificial intelligence systems related to the protection of national security interests but insists on adherence to international human rights law and democratic processes.

Facilitates international cooperation and information exchange on AI's human rights impacts.

Permits amendments and dispute settlements through negotiation or the Conference of the Parties.

name: Security Management Measures for the Application of Facial Recognition Technology
summary:
Regulates the use of facial recognition technology for processing facial information within China, ensuring compliance with relevant laws and ethical standards.

Exempts the use of facial recognition in research and development or algorithm training.

Requires a specific, necessary purpose for processing, with minimized impact on individual rights.

Obligates personal information processors to inform individuals transparently about processing activities, including purposes, methods, and rights.

Mandates obtaining consent separately for processing, with provision for withdrawal.

Requires parental consent for processing minors' facial information and formulating specific rules for handling such data.

Restricts storing facial information within devices unless consent or laws allow external transmission and limits retention to what is necessary.

Mandates conducting personal information protection impact assessments in advance and retaining assessment reports for three years.

Prohibits using facial recognition as the sole identity verification method if alternatives exist.

Requires filing procedures with local cyberspace administrations if information volume reaches 100,000 individuals.

Empowers cyberspace administrations and public security authorities to supervise, inspect, and handle complaints regarding facial recognition misuse.

name: Illinois HB 0645 ("Future of Work Act")
summary:
Creates the Illinois Future of Work Task Force to proactively plan for the future of work and address current labor issues.

Requires the Task Force to identify and assess emerging technologies, particularly automation and AI, that significantly impact employment, wages, and skills.

Mandates the development of job standards and working conditions to build a vibrant middle class.

Instructs the Task Force to identify future job opportunities and shape them to improve life in Illinois.

Compiles research and best practices from other regions on deploying technology for the public good.

Develops tools to evaluate the impact of proposed technologies on workers, employers, and the state.

Proposes workforce development and training programs for future jobs.

Requires the Task Force to submit a report with findings to the Governor and General Assembly by May 1, 2022, and dissolves upon report submission.

name: NYC Rules Amendment for Automated Employment Decisionmaking Tools
summary:
Mandates that employers or employment agencies conduct a bias audit of Automated Employment Decision Tools (AEDTs) at least annually.

Requires bias audits to calculate selection and scoring rates, and impact ratios across sex, race/ethnicity, and intersectional categories.

Mandates AEDT users to publish bias audit summaries online, detailing data sources and impact ratios, accessible for at least 6 months after each AEDT use.

Requires notification to candidates and employees 10 business days before AEDT use, offering options via website, job postings, mail, or email.

Enforces online publication of AEDT data retention policies and types of data collected.

name: Basic Safety Requirements for Generative Artificial Intelligence Services (National Standard - Draft for Feedback)
summary:
Establishes basic safety requirements for generative AI services, focusing on training data safety, model safety, and safety measures.

Requires service providers to conduct safety assessments and manage training data sources, ensuring data does not contain over 5% illegal content.

Mandates the verification of intellectual property rights and personal information consent before using data for training.

Stipulates regular security audits and monitoring of models to prevent malicious attacks and ensure content accuracy.

Obliges disclosure of service limitations, models, and personal data usage to users.

Demands the implementation of mechanisms for complaints and a backup strategy for service continuity.

Sets specific guidelines for minors, requiring parental controls and restrictions on unsuitable content.

Requires transparency in service provision, detailing applicable scenarios and user consent for data use in training.

Mandates service providers to construct banks of unsafe key words and questions which AI models should and should not refuse to answer.

name: JSP 936 V1.1 Dependable Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Defence (UK MoD)
summary:
Sets the Ministry of Defence (MOD) Responsible Officers to ensure the ethical and safe development and use of AI in Defence.

Requires MOD staff to implement this JSP in AI system lifecycles, from inception to disposal, ensuring alignment with MOD's AI Ethical Principles: Human-centricity, Responsibility, Understanding, Bias and Harm Mitigation, and Reliability.

Mandates TLB Holders and Chief Executives to issue appropriate AI-related directions and ensure competent management within their areas and maintaining Governance as outlined in Section 4.

Stresses the need for a holistic approach aligned with the UK National AI Strategy and addresses unique AI security risks, advocating continuous security monitoring.

Obliges the assessment and mitigation of ethical risks, providing evidence of responsible AI use, and addressing novel and contentious AI applications with special attention.

Emphasizes human collaboration with AI, requiring competency assessments, training, and ethical governance, particularly in human/AI teams, AI legal considerations, and supplier competence and conformance with AI-specific requirements.

name: AI Diffusion Rule (US BIS)
summary:
Imposes export controls on AI models, excluding publicly available models, and expands licensing requirements for AI chips to additional countries.

Establishes three tiers of countries for purposes of determining applicable export restrictions, including eighteen countries able to import AI chips without restrictions (tier 1); countries able to import AI chips through validated end-user (VEU) programs, limited-volume exceptions, and licensing, but otherwise subject to restrictions (tier 2); and countries subject to ongoing restrictions, including arms-embargoed countries (tier 3).

Establishes a Data Center Validated End User (DC VEU) program to govern compute exports related to major AI infrastructure development in second-tier countries, with different pathways and restrictions depending on data center operator nationality. Imposes cybersecurity, physical and personnel security, and sourcing mandates on DC VEU participants, as well as reporting requirements.

Imposes specific computing power deployment restrictions on companies operating in second-tier countries, including relative ratios and numerical caps.

Controls the export of AI models developed using compute above a given threshold, to be adjusted over time based on assessments of publicly available models. Requires cloud computing providers to implement security measures preventing the unauthorized training of models otherwise subject to export controls.

name: Guidance on Algorithmic Discrimination and the New Jersey Law Against Discrimination
summary:
Clarifies that the New Jersey Law Against Discrimination (LAD) applies to algorithmic discrimination through automated decision-making tools similarly to traditional discrimination.

Prohibits any form of discrimination facilitated by automated tools, regardless of intent or third-party involvement in tool development.
