Mandates accountability for secure AI development, compliance with laws and standards, and prohibits using state-managed passwords for third-party apps.

Incorporates NDIT’s Security Risk Management Program in AI operations, mandates regular risk assessments, and restricts inputting moderate/high-risk data into public AI/ML services.

Requires NDIT to offer AI training and workshops, maintain an AI technology inventory, and ensure entities use vetted technologies.

Demands compliance with data protection laws, ethical AI use, and fairness without bias.

Stipulates AI must adhere to legal standards, including copyright, with review of licensing agreements and recognition that AI-generated content lacks copyright protection.

name: North Carolina Government Responsible Use of AI Framework
summary:
Establishes the North Carolina State Government Responsible Use of Artificial Intelligence Framework to ensure ethical AI application across state agencies.

Requires state agencies to follow guidelines which emphasize human-centered AI with oversight ensuring AI use benefits citizens without negatively impacting rights or access to services.

Stipulates transparency, requiring agencies to notify individuals of AI use and its impacts in accessible language.

Mandates robust security measures, ongoing monitoring, and risk assessments to ensure the safety and effectiveness of AI systems.

Demands strict data privacy controls throughout AI lifecycle stages and promotes equitable AI development free from biases.

Insists on accountability where agencies must audit AI use and provide necessary training to personnel.

Empowers staff through AI training to maximize public service effectiveness.

Requires agencies to maintain an AI inventory, report it for transparency, and conduct risk assessments using NIST AI RMF guided by state offices for comprehensive risk management.

name: New Hampshire State Use of AI Policy
summary:
Requires all New Hampshire State Employees to adhere to ethical guidelines for AI use, emphasizing protection of Personal Identifying Information (PII) and sensitive data.

Dictates a human-centric approach, transparency, fairness, privacy, and continuous monitoring in AI deployment for government services.

Allows AI for decision support, public engagement, predictive analytics, image and video analysis, natural language processing, generative content, healthcare, environmental monitoring, and transportation, subject to stringent data protection and human oversight.

Mandates AI systems to explain decisions and actions and undergo ethical reviews when high-risk.

Instructs employees to ensure data protection and adhere to cybersecurity measures per the Statewide Information Security Manual and NIST-800-53 standard.

Requires informing users about AI interactions and data handling.

Assigns Agency heads responsibility for policy adherence, with AI technologies reported to the Business Relationship Management Division.

References New Hampshire AI ethics code and laws related to deepfakes and AI use.

name: New Jersey EO 346
summary:
Establishes the Artificial Intelligence Task Force responsible for studying AI technologies' societal impacts and recommending government actions for ethical use.

Includes the Chief Technology Officer, Chief Innovation Officer, Chief Executive Officer of the Economic Development Authority, and other key officials as members.

Authorizes the Task Force to gather data from state departments and agencies.

Requires executive branch cooperation and assistance to fulfill the Task Force's objectives.

Directs the Task Force to consult with academics, industry professionals, and consumer advocates.

Issues a reporting requirement to the Governor within 12 months of the Order’s enactment, to be shared with the Legislature and public.

Permits additional appointments by the Governor as necessary.

Clarifies the Task Force’s advisory nature in providing advice to the Governor and executive branches. 

Takes effect immediately upon issuance.

name: Rhode Island EO 24-06 (AI and Data Centers of Excellence)
summary:
Establishes a single state data governance structure, creating a federated data platform to manage data effectively across Rhode Island state agencies.

Mandates the Department of Administration (DOA) to appoint a Chief Data Officer (CDO) to oversee the Data Center of Excellence, enhancing data operations and readiness for AI integration.

Creates an AI Center of Excellence to formulate AI policies and ethics, minimizing bias and guiding AI implementation in state operations.

Directs all state agencies to participate in the federated data system, sharing data for policy analysis and exploring AI applications to improve operations.

Forms an AI Task Force to assess AI risks and opportunities, providing advice to policymakers.

Instructs the Department of Labor and Training (DLT), Rhode Island Department of Education (RIDE), and Office of Post Secondary Commissioner (OPC) to develop AI training programs for state and private-sector workers, integrating AI topics into existing curricula.

name: Mississippi Artificial Intelligence in Education Task Force Act (SB 2062)
summary:
Establishes an Artificial Intelligence in Education Task Force in Mississippi to evaluate and recommend AI applications in K-12 education.

Requires the State Superintendent of Education to chair the task force, with administrative support provided by the Department of Education.

Comprises twelve members appointed by the Governor, Lieutenant Governor, and Speaker of the House, possessing expertise in education, technology, and data privacy.

Instructs the task force to assess AI's ethical, legal, and data privacy implications, develop policy recommendations, and propose guidelines for AI integration in education.

Tasks the force with identifying workforce needs and strategies for data protection, and fostering collaboration between educational sectors and industries.

Requires submission of interim and final reports detailing findings and recommendations to state officials and public posting of the final report.

Dissolves the task force on January 1, 2025, and takes effect on July 1, 2024.

name: Legal Advisory on the Application of Existing Law to AI in Healthcare (California Attorney General)
summary:
Requires healthcare entities in California using AI to comply with existing state laws related to consumer protection, civil rights, competition, and data privacy.

Prohibits the use of AI to deny health insurance claims or make medical decisions that override licensed care providers’ determinations.

Prohibits the use of AI systems that discriminate against patients based on historical access to healthcare.

Demands transparency and auditing of AI systems, ensuring they do not introduce bias or replicate human error.

Insists that entities uphold patient privacy, especially regarding sensitive information like reproductive and genetic data.

Mandates informed consent from patients when AI tools impact their healthcare.

Outlines existing protections under laws like California’s Unfair Competition Law, Unruh Civil Rights Act, and Confidentiality of Medical Information Act.

Instructs healthcare AI developers to prevent discriminatory impacts and consider the effects of training data.

Emphasizes the need for compliance with both state and federal regulations with no exceptions for AI-related practices.

Prohibits the involvement of AI as a defense to liability under any law.

name: New York 2025-A768 (NY AI Consumer Protection Act)
summary:
Enacts the New York Artificial Intelligence Consumer Protection Act to manage risks of  AI decision systems. 

Requires developers to ensure systems do not cause algorithmic discrimination through regular audits, starting January 2027. 

Mandates developers provide comprehensive technical documentation and risk assessments to deployers. 

Obligates deployers to notify consumers when high-risk AI systems make significant decisions affecting them and to offer explanation and recourse for adverse decisions. 

Imposes a risk management program for deployers to identify and mitigate potential discrimination. 

Allows the attorney general to enforce compliance through audits and penalties, with the possibility of corrective actions to avoid litigation. 

Establishes exceptions for preempting federal law compliance and protects trade secrets from disclosure.

name: Advancing Governance, Innovation, and Risk Management for Agency Use of Artificial Intelligence
summary:
Requires federal agencies to appoint a Chief AI Officer (CAIO) within 60 days to enhance AI governance and innovation while managing risks, particularly those affecting public rights and safety.
Requires agencies to develop AI strategies to responsibly adopt AI, including generative AI, and to facilitate sharing and reuse of AI models, code, and data.

Imposes new requirements for agencies to manage AI-related risks, including following minimum risk management practices for AI impacting public rights and safety. Obligates agencies to annually inventory AI use cases, identifying those impacting rights and safety, and to report on associated risks and mitigation strategies. Encourages removing barriers to AI innovation related to IT infrastructure, data, and workforce while ensuring compliance with existing federal policies and risk management practices.

name: OMB Requirements for AI Acquisition in Government
summary:
Directs agencies to improve responsible AI acquisition, emphasizing cross-functional and interagency collaboration, risk management, and market competitiveness.

Requires agencies to update acquisition policies to reflect AI governance responsibilities and share AI acquisition information across the executive branch.

Mandates compliance with risk management practices for AI impacting rights or safety, including managing privacy, security, and discrimination risks.

Urges agencies to prevent vendor lock-in by prioritizing interoperability, transparency, and innovative acquisition practices.

Encourages the acquisition of generative AI for experimentation, while emphasizing transparency, risk mitigation, and environmental considerations.

Applies to all federal agencies, excluding the Intelligence Community and National Security Systems, and sets specific deadlines for compliance and reporting. 

Fosters a diverse AI marketplace by minimizing vendor lock-in and promoting competition through strategic contractual requirements.

name: Illinois HB 3506 (AI Safety and Security Protocol Act)
summary:
Mandates developers to produce, implement, and publish a "safety and security protocol" to respond to critical risks, along with quarterly risk assessment reports.

Defines "critical risk" as deriving from the development or deployment of foundation models in a manner which could cause serious injury, death, or financial loss.

Defines "foundation model" as an AI model applicable to many different contexts and capable of self-supervision in training.

Requires an annual third-party audit to assess compliance with these protocols.

Allows redactions in published documents for protecting trade secrets or public safety, with unredacted versions available to the Attorney General.

Imposes civil penalties up to $1,000,000 for violations, with consideration of the severity and potential materialization of critical risks.

Establishes whistleblower protections and procedures for reporting internal risks related to AI development.

Authorizes the Attorney General to seek injunctive relief if a developer's activities pose imminent threats to public safety.

Emphasizes the cumulative nature of this Act, not limiting duties or remedies under other laws.

name: Opinions on Strengthening the Governance of Science and Technology Ethics
summary:
Establishes the National Science and Technology Ethics Commission to guide and promote S&T ethics governance, with the Ministry of Science and Technology overseeing daily operations.

Instructs institutes engaged in AI and other sensitive fields to form S&T ethics review committees to address ethical risks independently.

Mandates that stakeholders comply with ethics requirements and enforce rigorous review procedures for S&T involving human and animal subjects.

Requires strict governance and dynamic regulation aligning with China’s national conditions and international trends.

Directs entities, such as local oversight departments and innovation entities, to manage, monitor, and report S&T ethics risks, ensuring agile responses to emerging challenges.

Prompts legislative actions to strengthen legal provisions related to S&T ethics, particularly in AI, by the end of the 14th Five-Year Plan.

Encourages public and local awareness of S&T ethics through education, laying emphasis on both stakeholder compliance and societal benefit.

name: Massachusetts EO 629 (AI Strategic Task Force)
summary:
Establishes an AI Strategic Task Force within the Office of the Governor of Massachusetts to study AI and Generative AI (GenAI) technologies and their impacts on the state.

Charges the Task Force with advising the Governor on making Massachusetts a leader in AI research and development.

Requires the Task Force to identify collaboration opportunities in key industries such as life sciences, healthcare, and finance, and explore public investments in AI.

Advises on AI-related job creation, assessing workforce impacts, and suggesting workforce training.

Recommends policies for responsible AI development, addressing ethical concerns like bias, privacy, and security.

Empowers the Task Force to convene subcommittees for addressing specific AI issues.

Obligates the Task Force to submit a report summarizing its work and recommendations to the Governor.

Specifies an effective date immediately after issuance until 30 days post-report submission.

name: OECD AI Principles (May 2024 update)
summary:
Recommends that AI actors and stakeholders promote principles for responsible AI, including inclusive growth, respect for human rights, transparency, robustness, and accountability.

Calls on governments and AI actors to invest in AI research and development, focusing on ethics, privacy, and reducing bias.

Advises governments to develop flexible governance environments and adapt policies to facilitate the deployment of AI systems.

Promotes building human capacity and preparing for labor market changes through skills training and fair transitions for workers as AI is deployed.

Urges governments to cooperate internationally to share AI knowledge, establish global technical standards, and promote use of internationally comparable indicators for AI progress.

Instructs the Digital Policy Committee to continue advancing AI governance by developing practical guidance and reporting on the implementation of these recommendations.

name: AI in America: OpenAI's Economic Blueprint
summary:
Defines a US strategy emphasizing national competitiveness, model safeguards, and national security for AI, with the federal government leading and consulting with industry.

Promotes export policies to securely share frontier AI models with allies while limiting exports to adversary nations.

Encourages federal support for AI companies, including sharing national security insights and reducing bureaucratic obstacles for collaboration.

Advocates infrastructure development to support AI, emphasizing chips, data, energy, and talent to maintain US leadership.

Proposes common-sense rules for AI safeguarding public safety while fostering innovation, emphasizing provenance data in AI-generated content, and AI user personalization.

Suggests creating AI Economic Zones and a nationwide AI education strategy to enhance AI ecosystem support and competitiveness.

Envisions a Compact for AI among allies for capital and supply chain access, contrasting Chinese-backed infrastructure projects.

Engages in developing training programs for future AI talent, promoting collaboration between government and industry.

name: (Trial) Measures for Science and Technology Ethics Reviews
summary:
Regulates S&T ethics reviews for activities with ethical risks, including AI research, under China's ethics laws. 

Requires committees in life sciences, medicine, and AI to manage ethics reviews independently and transparently.

Obliges these committees to guide risk assessments, conduct ethics reviews, and manage interdisciplinary membership for unbiased decision-making.

Stipulates S&T ethics reviews to cover data handling, ensuring compliance with relevant data security and personal information laws.

Mandates expert reconsiderations for high-risk emerging technologies, including algorithms and automated decision-making systems.

Empowers MOST to guide overall S&T ethics oversight and manage the information registration platform for ethical review activities.

Allows simplified procedures for low-risk S&T activities and establishes emergency procedures for rapid ethics review during urgent public incidents.

Authorizes corrective measures for violations, including possible penalties and liability for misconduct in S&T ethics. 

Implements from December 1, 2023.

name: Workforce for AI Trust Act
summary:
Amends the National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020 to authorize the National Science Foundation (NSF) to support interdisciplinary AI fellowships, encouraging ethical AI practices.

Mandates the NSF to conduct outreach to diverse institutions and groups underrepresented in STEM fields for fellowship applicants.

Directs the NSF to promote AI-based training and workshops across STEM fields to accelerate scientific discovery and technology development.

Requires the integration of diverse disciplinary perspectives in AI research peer review panels.

Instructs the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) to support education and workforce development to expand the AI governance workforce, focusing on managing AI-related risks.

Mandates NIST to develop technical standards and guidance for AI risk management careers, including mapping, measuring, and validating AI systems.

name: New Mexico AI Act
summary:
Enacts the Artificial Intelligence Act to regulate the use of AI in New Mexico, focusing on high-risk AI systems that make consequential decisions.  

Requires developers to use reasonable care to prevent algorithmic discrimination and disclose known risks to recipients and the state.  

Mandates impact assessments for deployers, updating them annually or upon modification of AI systems.  

Obliges deployers to notify consumers of AI's role in consequential decisions and provide appeal opportunities for adverse outcomes.  

Exempts trade secrets from mandatory disclosure, but requires consumer notification when information is withheld.  

Confers enforcement authority to the state department of justice, allowing consumer civil actions for violations.  

Sets the effective date for July 1, 2026, with rulemaking by the state department of justice due by January 1, 2027.

name: City of Long Beach Data Privacy Guidelines (2021)
summary:
Defines Artificial Intelligence as machines that have the ability to "learn" and "problem solve".

Mandates human review of algorithmic and AI decisions to avoid discrimination, using evidence-based evaluation of potential discriminatory consequences.

Requires training input informed by outcomes from AI or related technologies.

name: Mississippi EO 1584 (Foster Stakeholder Collaboration and Harness AI)
summary:
Directs the Mississippi Department of Information Technology Services (ITS) to inventory all AI technologies across state agencies by providing a standardized form.

Mandates ITS to evaluate current AI processes and guidelines at state agencies.

Instructs ITS to develop policy recommendations for the responsible use of AI, emphasizing fairness, privacy, security, transparency, and accountability.

Encourages statewide coordination on AI use, enabling ITS to engage with government stakeholders and industry experts for best practices and strategies.

Requires state agencies to cooperate with ITS by completing AI inventories and designating a staff member for AI coordination.

Implements the Executive Order immediately, with provisions to remain effective until amended, superseded, or rescinded.

name: Google DeepMind Frontier Safety Framework Version 2.0
summary:
Establishes the "Frontier Safety Framework" for managing risks of advanced AI, focusing on Critical Capability Levels (CCLs) related to misuse and deceptive alignment.

Outlines CCLs for high-risk domains, including chemical, biological, radiological, nuclear attacks (CBRN), cyber threats, and machine learning R&D, needing security and deployment mitigations.

Mandates regular evaluations of frontier AI models to assess approaching CCLs, employing "early warning evaluations" for proactive risk management.

Specifies mitigations when models near CCLs, using internal and external expertise to develop response plans, emphasizing automated monitoring for deceptive alignment risks.

Describes governance protocols, involving review and approval by corporate bodies like the Google DeepMind AGI Safety Council, and outlines disclosure criteria to government authorities and external organizations.

Plans continual updates to risk modeling, capability assessments, and risk-appropriate actions as AI capabilities evolve.

name: National AI Strategy 2024-2025 Action Plan (Turkey)
summary:
Implements mechanisms under the TechVisa Program to attract AI talents to Turkey.

Increases support for international research and doctoral programs to bolster AI workforce competence.

Coordinates curriculum updates to include AI and data science across non-AI scientific fields.

Establishes associate, undergraduate, and graduate AI degree programs based on workforce analysis.

Provides AI training post-education tailored to sectoral applications for workforce development.

Sets standards for private AI certification training programs.

Launches advanced analytics and AI training for public personnel competence.

Develops national occupational standards and qualifications in AI with relevant infrastructure.

Establishes ethical and technical standards for locally developed generative AI models.

Supports the development of a Turkish large language model in collaboration with the international community.

Creates a "Legal Assessment Guide for AI Applications" to ensure legal compliance of AI. 

Designs a customized AI education model to support workforce transformation.

name: Indiana Senate Bill 2024-150 (AI and Cybersecurity)
summary:
Establishes an Artificial Intelligence Task Force to study AI technologies used by Indiana state agencies, assessing their benefits, risks, and impacts on privacy, civil rights, and legal protections.

Requires the Task Force to produce annual reports with findings and recommendations for policies or legislation to govern AI use by state agencies.

Mandates state agencies compile and submit inventories of AI technologies in use or development, detailing vendors, intended use, data security measures, benefits, risks, and financial implications.

name: Hiroshima Process International Code of Conduct for Organizations Developing Advanced AI Systems
summary:
Promotes the safe, secure, and trustworthy development of AI by providing voluntary guidance for organizations developing advanced AI systems.

Encourages organizations to identify, evaluate, and mitigate risks across the AI lifecycle, employing diverse testing methods and ensuring traceability through documented development practices.

Urges ongoing monitoring of AI systems post-deployment to identify vulnerabilities and misuse, through collaboration with stakeholders to mitigate risks, while advocating for public reporting and enhanced transparency regarding identified limitations.

Encourages information sharing and incident reporting, as well as the development and disclosure of AI governance and risk management policies among stakeholders to promote safety and trustworthiness.

Recommends robust security controls, including cybersecurity measures and insider threat safeguards, to protect AI system components from unauthorized access.

Promotes the development of content authentication mechanisms to identify AI-generated content and the creation of international technical standards for AI development.

name: Hiroshima Process International Guiding Principles for Advanced AI Systems
summary:
Establishes international guiding principles around the safe, secure, and trustworthy development and deployment of artificial intelligence worldwide.

Recommends proactive mitigation of risks across the AI lifecycle and investment in physical, cyber, and insider threat security controls.

Recommends the public disclosure of advanced AI systems' capabilities, limitations, and appropriate or inappropriate uses.

Recommends information sharing and reporting of incidents among relevant industry, government, and civil society stakeholders

Recommends the deployment of content authentication and provenance mechanisms to enable users to identify AI-generated content.

Encourages development of advanced AI systems foremost to address key global challenge in alignment with the UN SDG goals.

Recommends the development and adoption of international technical standards.

Recommends the implementation of personal data privacy and IP protection measures.

name: Political Declaration on Responsible Military Use of AI and Autonomy
summary:
Require States to ensure military AI use complies with international law, particularly international humanitarian law.

Mandate accountability through a responsible human command chain.

Impose legal reviews to align military AI with international obligations and enhance civilian protection.

Demand oversight by senior officials for high-consequence AI applications.

Advocate minimizing unintended bias in military AI.

Insist on transparent, auditable methodologies and documentation for military AI development.

Oblige training for personnel to understand AI capabilities and limitations, preventing automation bias.

Prescribe explicit, well-defined uses for military AI, with rigorous testing for safety and effectiveness.

Implement safeguards to detect and mitigate AI failures, with the ability to deactivate systems if needed.

Encourage States to publicly commit to these measures, support responsible AI use, and engage internationally to refine and promote these standards.

name: UN General Assembly Resolution on AI (2024)
ELVIS Act (Tennessee)
summary:
Expands the "Personal Rights Protection Act of 1984," renaming it the "Ensuring Likeness, Voice, and Image Security Act of 2024."

Grants individuals property rights over their name, photograph, voice, or likeness across all mediums.

Defines "voice" to include both actual and simulated sounds identifiable to an individual.

Terminates exclusive commercial rights after two years of non-use, beginning ten years after death.

Imposes civil liability for the unauthorized commercial use of an individual's name, photograph, voice, or likeness.

Prohibits distribution of technology primarily used to produce unauthorized likenesses. 

Allows individuals or parties with exclusive contracts for personal services or sound recordings to enforce rights. 

Exempts certain uses protected by the First Amendment as fair use, including news, commentary, and satire. 

Mandates that employees or owners of any medium used for advertising be liable if they publish or disseminate an advertisement in violation of this act, and if they should have known about the violation.

name: FY2025 NDAA, Section 235 ("Competitive demonstration of automated target recognition algorithms")
summary:
Require the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer of the Department of Defense to establish a venue and processes for testing automated target recognition algorithms by June 1, 2025.

Mandate the testing of mission capability for at least two programs in the Replicator initiative using the developed venue by September 1, 2025.

Oblige the Secretary of Defense to brief the Senate and House Armed Services Committees on activities under this section within one year of the Act's enactment.

name: FY2025 NDAA, Section 1547 ("Joint partner-sharing network capabilities for Middle East defense integration")
summary:
Obliges the Chief Data and Artificial Intelligence Officer to develop policies for a combatant command warfighter forum on AI, considering purposes such as AI tool use cases, risk categorization, and training needs.

Demands identification of opportunities for AI cooperation with regional partners and allies.

Directs the Secretary of Defense to submit a report to congressional defense committees detailing the initiatives, challenges, and policy needs for a combatant command warfighter forum on AI.

name: FY2025 NDAA, Title XV, Subtitle D ("Artificial Intelligence")
summary:
Establishes an initiative to improve the usability of AI systems, that are used by Department of Defense personnel, by considering human factors and cognitive ergonomics. It mandates the development of a guidance plan for their inclusion and evaluation in current and future programs. 

Establishes a program for high-performance computing infrastructure to support advanced AI capabilities, ensuring non-duplication with Department of Energy efforts. The instrument mandates the development of a roadmap that assesses the anticipated compute requirements, security standards, and relevant resources for the infrastructure required to enable advanced AI capabilities. 

Mandates developing a plan for costs and budgeting related to data used for various stages in the AI development and deployment lifecycle. This plan must include budgets for current programs and programs established by the enactment of this Act, as well as, costs related to data procurement, preparation, protection, and analysis. 

Requires the Secretary of Defense to evaluate the feasibility of centers of excellence for AI-enabled weapon systems, focusing on national and international collaboration, training of personnel, and best practices. Requires a report and briefing to Congress.

name: FY2025 NDAA, Section 221 ("Improvements relating to defining, identifying, and planning the artificial intelligence workforce of the Department of Defense")
summary:
Appoints a civilian official as the Chief Digital Engineering Recruitment and Management Officer by April 30, 2025, responsible for AI workforce policy and planning in the Department of Defense.

Requires the Officer to define and identify the AI workforce, clarify roles, code roles in workforce data systems, and develop qualification programs.

Mandates updating the Department's Human Capital Operating Plan to align with strategic goals and ensure consistent AI terminology.

Sets the expiration of the Officer's appointment on September 30, 2030.

Demands a briefing to congressional defense committees within 240 days, detailing AI workforce positions, required skills, current workforce state, and future requirements.

name: FY2025 NDAA, Section 1087 ("Establishment of Department of Defense working group on multilateral artificial intelligence coordination")
summary:
Demands the Secretary of Defense to establish a Department of Defense working group to coordinate AI initiatives with U.S. allies and partners within 90 days of the Act's enactment.

Designates a senior civilian or military officer to lead the group and determines allied participation.

Requires the group to develop AI strategies and interoperability for intelligence sharing, battlespace awareness, and other defense operations.

Mandates managing AI data security and evaluating defense industrial capabilities for AI integration.

Ensures knowledge and technical data remain under the control of the originating country’s export laws.

Terminates the group on September 30, 2028, unless extended for national security reasons by the Secretary.

Defines key terms such as "battlespace awareness" and "covered operational use."

name: FY2025 NDAA, Section 236 ("Pilot program on development of near-term use cases and demonstration of artificial intelligence toward biotechnology applications for national security")
summary:
Mandates the Secretary of Defense to implement a pilot program demonstrating artificial intelligence in national security-related biotechnology applications.

Requires collaboration through public-private partnerships to execute the program.

Permits the use of Department of Defense laboratory facilities and computing infrastructure to support biotechnology experimentation and AI model validation.

Stipulates the program's commencement within one year of enactment and its termination five years after starting.

Obligates the Secretary to submit annual reports to congressional defense committees, detailing program progress, data resource assessments, cybersecurity measures, collaboration mechanisms, and AI roles in biotechnology.

Requires a transition plan to be submitted one year before program termination, outlining steps for operationalization, including costs, infrastructure needs, and ecosystem analysis.

Aims to assess the viability of transitioning technology developed in the pilot into operational use within the Department.

name: FY2025 NDAA, Section 225 ("Duties of Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer Governing Council relating to artificial intelligence models and advanced artificial intelligence technologies")
summary:
Amends the John S. McCain National Defense Authorization Act to include duties for the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer Governing Council.

Requires the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer Governing Counci to evaluate and assesses AI models and technologies that could pose national security risks if accessed by U.S. adversaries.

Calls for the development of strategies to prevent unauthorized access and use of powerful AI models by adversarial countries.

name: FY2025 NDAA, Section 6506 ("Enhancement of authority for intelligence community public-private talent exchanges")
summary:
Amends section 5306 to require public-private talent exchanges in intelligence or counterintelligence to focus on fields including artificial intelligence.

Extends the duration of temporary details for such exchanges from 3 years to 5 years.

Prohibits private-sector employees detailed to the intelligence community from accessing trade secrets or proprietary information.

Clarifies that participation in the exchange program does not create an organizational conflict of interest solely by virtue of involvement.

Requires implementation of systems to address any identified conflicts of interest.

Mandates the Director of National Intelligence to submit annual reports to Congress on the implementation and use of the exchange program, including recommendations for improvements, for three consecutive years.

name: FY2025 NDAA, Section 1514 ("Management and cybersecurity of multi-cloud environments")
summary:
Mandates the Secretary of Defense to develop a multi-cloud management and cybersecurity strategy within 180 days.

Requires the strategy to include the assessment of means to increase AI adoption in multi-cloud environments and the identification of opportunities for better data use and storage planning, enforcing government data protection in AI training.

Requires a briefing to congressional defense committees within 240 days.

name: FY2025 NDAA, Section 1078 ("Study and report on Department of Defense use of unmanned ground vehicle systems manufactured by certain foreign entities")
summary:
Mandates the Secretary of Defense to study the use of unmanned ground vehicle systems by the Department of Defense manufactured by certain foreign entities.

Requires submission of a report to congressional defense committees within 180 days, assessing usage, national security threats, and identifying foreign manufacturers.

Calls for the evaluation of cybersecurity risks, technological vulnerabilities, and the foreign entities' military-civil nexus.

Demands an assessment of the feasibility of the Defense Innovation Unit developing a list of U.S. manufacturers.

Mandates an evaluation of whether a prohibition on procuring and operating these systems is advisable for U.S. national security.

Prohibits procurement and operation of these systems by the Department of Defense one year after the report submission, unless deemed in the national interest.

Exempts this prohibition if recommended as not in the best national security interest.

Defines "covered foreign countries" including China, Russia, Iran, and North Korea.

name: FY2025 NDAA, Section 1031 ("Requirements for the unmanned maritime autonomy architecture")
summary:
Require the Secretary of the Navy to provide a forum and resources for industry participation in developing a vendor-agnostic and platform-agnostic modular open systems architecture for maritime unmanned systems.

Adopt or join a governance model that includes both Government and industry for the maritime unmanned systems standards.

Implement a process for incorporating industry feedback into these standards and align them with leading industry practices.

Tailor the standards for each Navy program or contract to meet the minimum requirements necessary for desired operational capabilities.

Label and distribute the standards as open and publicly releasable information to the greatest extent possible.

name: Executive Order on Advancing United States Leadership in Artificial Intelligence Infrastructure (EO 14141)
summary:
Requires federal agencies to identify, solicit proposals for, and lease federal lands suitable for AI data centers and related clean energy projects, aiming for full-capacity operation by the end of 2027.

Emphasizes high labor standards and community collaboration, among other factors, in the selection of projects to account for health, safety, and ecological risks/harms.

Mandates cybersecurity, model evaluation, supply-chain protection, and other requirements for AI infrastructure developed pursuant to the executive order.  

Requires the Secretary of Energy to facilitate grid interconnection for AI infrastructure developed pursuant to the executive order. 

Directs expedited permit processing for federal sites hosting the infrastructure.  

Requires relevant agencies to take additional enumerated measures to expedite permitting and power procurement for AI infrastructure nationwide.

Directs creation of a plan for robust engagement with allies to encourage global AI infrastructure development including the necessary workforce, ensuring security and resilience in international supply chains.

name: Executive Order on Removing Barriers To American Leadership In Artificial Intelligence
summary:
Revokes existing AI policies that hinder American innovation, clearing obstacles to U.S. leadership in AI.

Requires development of an action plan within 180 days to sustain and enhance America's global AI dominance, focusing on prosperity, competitiveness, and security.

Mandates review and potential suspension, revision, or rescission of actions under the revoked Executive Order 14110 that conflict with the new policy.

Instructs Office of Management and Budget (OMB) to revise relevant memoranda to align with the new policy.

Directs that implementation not impair existing legal authority of departments or create enforceable rights against the U.S.

Ensures that actions are consistent with applicable laws.

name: New York S1169 (New York AI Act)
summary:
Establishes the "New York AI Act" to ensure AI development and use in New York State is safe, responsible and non-discriminatory.

Requires developers and deployers of high-risk AI systems to undergo independent audits for algorithmic discrimination before and after deployment.

Mandates detailed reporting by developers and deployers of high-risk AI systems to the Attorney General, covering system capabilities and potential risks.

Prohibits the deployment of AI causing algorithmic discrimination or of systems that have not passed the mandated audit.

Establishes whistleblower protections for employees disclosing AI-related non-compliance.

Forbids the use of social scoring AI systems evaluating individuals based on behavioral data resulting in unfair treatment.

Allows the Attorney General to enforce compliance and allows a private right of action for those harmed by AI non-compliance.

name: Framework to Mitigate AI-Enabled Extreme Risks
summary:
Establishes a framework for federal oversight of advanced AI models, termed "frontier models," to mitigate extreme AI-enabled risks like biological, chemical, cyber, and nuclear threats.

Defines frontier models as those requiring computing power exceeding 10^26 operations, and capable of diverse tasks or intended for specific high-risk areas.

Mandates entities selling or renting large computing resources to report usage and exercise due diligence, particularly concerning foreign clients.

Requires developers to notify an oversight entity before training frontier models and integrate safeguards against extreme risks.

Obligates developers to adhere to cybersecurity standards and report risk mitigation steps.

Imposes an evaluation and licensing process before deploying frontier models, using a tiered structure based on risk level to determine deployment scope.

Suggests options for an oversight entity, including an interagency body, new agency, or existing federal agencies, emphasizing expert involvement.

Tasks the oversight entity to report on emerging challenges and risks, ensuring framework adaptability.

name: Artificial Intelligence Safety Commitments (China AI Industry Alliance)
summary:
Calls for the establishment of safety teams and risk management mechanisms for AI safety and security.

Mandates safety and security testing for AI models, prioritizing evaluations in critical domains.

Implements data security measures to protect training and operational data, ensuring privacy and accuracy.

Enhances infrastructure security through regular penetration tests and incident response protocols.

Requires transparency in AI model capabilities, limitations, and risk disclosures.

Advances research in AI safety and security, addressing potential biases and risks in frontier applications.

Signatories include Alibaba, Baidu, Huawei, Tencent, and other major Chinese tech companies.

name: AI Safety Governance Framework v1.0 (TC260)
summary:
Establishes principles and mechanisms for AI safety governance, emphasizing a balance between development and security and involving all stakeholders in a coordinated approach.

Commits to enhancing AI safety by identifying risks, promoting inclusivity, and ensuring all participants take responsibility.

Advocates for international cooperation in AI safety governance, pursuing best practices and consensus building.

Outlines safety guidelines for developers, service providers, and users, focusing on ethics, data protection, risk assessment, and mitigation strategies.

Mandates developers to uphold a people-centered approach, strengthen data security, and assess the risk of biases in AI models. 

Requires service providers to disclose the capabilities and limitations of AI systems, ensure users can make informed choices about their use of AI, and provide users with information on the accuracy of AI products. 

Encourages users in key areas to assess AI impacts, ensure protection of sensitive data in usage of AI systems, guarantee AI products remain subject to human control, and avoid complete reliance on AI for decision making. 

Recommends general users of AI systems to increase their awareness of potential risks, review the terms and conditions of AI products before use, be wary of entering sensitive information unnecessarily, and keep in mind the potential impact of AI products on minors.

name: Joint Statement on Risk Assessment of Advanced AI Systems (International Network of AI Safety Institutes)
summary:
Highlights six key aspects for risk assessment of advanced AI systems: actionable, transparent, comprehensive, multistakeholder, iterative, and reproducible.

Commits to developing a shared scientific basis for risk assessments via joint evaluations and cooperative research, allowing flexibility for members to adapt assessments according to international and domestic frameworks.

Emphasizes actionable assessments that inform effective mitigation based on specified criteria, and transparency to ensure evidence-based outcomes and broader understanding.

Advocates for comprehensiveness by linking potential risks to real-world harms and benefits, considering impacts from large-scale AI adoption, and aligning assessments with Sustainable Development Goals.

Stresses a multistakeholder approach, incorporating diverse perspectives from industry, academia, civil society, government, and multiple disciplines.

Calls for iterative assessments, adapting to AI advancements, ongoing safety research, and post-deployment monitoring.

Encourages reproducibility to enhance verification, validation, and interoperability among methods and actors.

name: Texas Responsible AI Governance Act
summary:
Establishes the Texas Responsible Artificial Intelligence Governance Act to regulate high-risk AI systems and prohibit certain harmful AI uses.

Requires developers, distributors, and deployers of high-risk AI systems to protect consumers from algorithmic discrimination and complete impact assessments.

Mandates the disclosure to consumers when interacting with high-risk AI systems and provides consumer rights to contest decisions made by these systems.

Prohibits AI systems from manipulating behavior, social scoring, using biometric identifiers without consent, inferring sensitive attributes, causing harm, and producing unlawful content.

Creates an Artificial Intelligence Council to guide ethical AI use, issue advisory opinions, and suggest legislative reforms.

Initiates an AI Regulatory Sandbox Program for controlled testing without full compliance.

Implements AI workforce development grants to address workforce gaps and support AI-related education.

Allows enforcement by the Attorney General with civil penalties for non-compliance.

Effective from September 1, 2025.

name: UK Code of Practice for the Cyber Security of AI
summary:
Requires organizations to raise awareness of AI security and incorporate AI security content into cyber security training, tailored to staff roles.

Requires assessments of AI system design for security alongside functionality and performance, including documentation of business needs, data needs, and potential security risks.

Mandates threat modeling and risk management targeting AI-specific attacks and ensure human oversight capabilities in AI systems.

Requires asset tracking and protection, disaster recovery strategies for AI systems, and secure data management.

Specifies secure infrastructure practices, including strong access control, secure development environments, and clear vulnerability disclosure policies.

Mandates secure supply chain processes and thorough documentation of data, models, and prompts.

Calls for rigorous security assessment testing, share findings, and support End-users during incidents.

Encourages maintaining regular security updates and system behavior monitoring.

Ensures secure disposal of data and models during transfer or decommissioning processes.

name: Freedom Online Coalition Joint Statement on Responsible Government Practices for AI Technologies
summary:
Endorses the responsible use and regulation of AI to enhance public service delivery while safeguarding human rights, as reiterated by the Freedom Online Coalition (FOC).

Acknowledges the potential risks of AI misuse, including bias, privacy violations, and exacerbation of inequalities, especially for marginalized populations.

Urges governments to adhere to international legal obligations, including the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, when employing AI systems.

Mandates assessment and management of AI risks in high-risk contexts.

Advocates for continuous monitoring and external audits of AI systems to maintain fairness and rights protection.

Mandates support for adequate training for personnel involved in AI to comprehend its impact on human rights.

Demands transparency, public consultation on AI uses, and mechanisms for public feedback and opting out of AI-enabled decisions.

Calls for effective remedies and redress for individuals harmed by AI systems.

Incorporates these practices into government procurement to ensure AI trustworthiness and conformity with human rights standards.

Defines high-risk AI as those that may impact human rights and safety with likely applications in healthcare, law enforcement and justice, and provision of public benefits.

name: Massachusetts HD 4053 (protecting consumers in interactions with AI systems)
summary:
Amends state law to introduce Chapter 93M, mandating consumer protections in interactions with artificial intelligence (AI) systems.

Requires developers and deployers of high-risk AI systems to use reasonable care to prevent algorithmic discrimination and disclose foreseeable risks.

Defines "high-risk AI systems" as those influencing consequential decisions in areas like education, employment, and healthcare.

Mandates developers to provide detailed documentation about AI system data usage, limitations, and discrimination mitigation measures.

Obligates deployers to establish risk management policies aligned with recognized standards, and perform annual impact assessments.

Demands transparency from deployers by notifying consumers before consequential decisions are made using high-risk AI systems, and offering appeal opportunities for adverse decisions.

Empowers the attorney general with exclusive enforcement authority, classifying violations as unfair trade practices.

Prohibits private rights of action, leaving enforcement to the state.

Allows attorney general to create rules for implementing these requirements, ensuring alignment with national standards.

name: CPPA Draft Risk Assessment and Automated Decisionmaking Technology Regulations
summary:
Defines "artificial intelligence" as a machine-based system generating outputs to influence environments, recognizing variations in autonomy and adaptiveness post-deployment. 

Mandates businesses to conduct risk assessments for using AI and automated decision-making technology when handling consumer data, especially for decisions impacting financial, employment, or educational opportunities.

Requires transparency through Pre-use Notices for consumers, detailing the use of AI in decision-making and providing opt-out or appeal options.

Specifies exceptions where consumers cannot opt-out, relying on the necessity of the use, with provisions for human review.

Demands businesses to ensure AI does not discriminate against protected classes through evaluations and safeguards.

Obliges businesses to disclose AI processes upon consumer request and prohibits retaliatory actions against consumers exercising their rights.

Mandates comprehensive documentation and regular updates for risk assessments, maintaining consumer privacy as a priority.

name: Outbound Investment Security Rule (U.S. Treasury)
summary:
Implements Executive Order 14105 by requiring U.S. persons to notify the Department of the Treasury about transactions involving national security technologies in "countries of concern," and prohibits certain transactions that pose acute national security threats.

Defines AI systems as machine-based systems capable of making predictions, recommendations, or decisions that affect environments, thereby impacting transactions involving AI development and deployment.

Specifies which transactions are notifiable or prohibited, including those involving AI systems intended for military, intelligence, or surveillance uses as well as those of a specified computing power.

Mandates U.S. persons to file notifications and prohibits knowingly directing others to undertake prohibited transactions.

Details civil and criminal penalties for violations, including fines up to $250,000 or imprisonment up to 20 years.

Outlines exceptions, including certain public securities transactions and specific national interest exemptions.

Permits the Secretary of the Treasury to compel divestment of any prohibited transaction, with the aid of the Attorney General.

name: Artificial Intelligence Law Proposal (Turkish Parliament)
summary:
Ensure the safe, ethical, and fair use of AI technologies to protect personal data and privacy rights.

Apply to all stakeholders, including providers, users, importers, and distributors of AI systems.

Mandate adherence to principles of safety, transparency, fairness, accountability, and privacy in AI systems.

Require risk assessments and registration for high-risk AI systems with supervisory authorities.

Obligate AI operators to comply with the Law and allow supervisory authorities to monitor compliance and detect violations.

Impose fines up to 35 million Turkish Liras or 7% of annual turnover for violations, with varying penalties based on the nature of the breach.

Enforce the Law upon publication, with the President executing its provisions.

name: California SB 53 (CalCompute and Whistleblowers)
summary:
Establishes a consortium to create CalCompute, a public cloud computing framework promoting safe and ethical AI.

Mandates CalCompute to foster research benefiting the public and expanding access to computational resources.

Obligates submission of a report by January 1, 2027, detailing CalCompute's framework, including infrastructure analysis, costs, governance, and workforce recommendations.

Introduces whistleblower protections for employees disclosing critical AI risks, including practices leading to severe harm, damage, or misinformation.

Mandates developers to establish anonymous internal reporting processes and ensures responsive investigation.

Authorizes courts to grant attorney’s fees, shift burdens of proof to developers, and issue injunctive relief in whistleblower cases, prioritizing employee protections.

name: (Trial) Measures for Science and Technology Ethics Reviews (Draft for Feedback)
summary:
Establishes that work units engaged in sensitive areas, including AI, must form ethics committees to conduct thorough ethical reviews of S&T activities.

Requires these reviews to ensure AI activities comply with ethics principles, such as fairness and controllability.

Stipulates review committees to include diverse experts and provide training on ethics reviews.

Mandates reviews of AI systems and algorithms adhere to national data security and ethical norms, ensuring transparency and reliability.

Grants committees the authority to approve, revise, or reject AI projects based on ethical evaluations.

Introduces simplified and emergency review procedures for low-risk or urgent situations, with detailed conditions.

Calls for procedures to handle violations within AI ethics reviews, including potential penalties.

Insists on a national ethics management registry for committee activities and checklisted high-risk AI activities.

Implies that the Ministry of Science and Technology oversees interpretation and enforcement of these measures, which include significant provisions for governance of AI research and its ethical implications.

name: Guiding Opinions on Strengthening the Governance of Science and Technology Ethics (Draft for Feedback)
summary:
Establishes the National Science and Technology Ethics Commission to guide and coordinate the governance of S&T ethics, with the Ministry of Science and Technology handling day-to-day affairs.

Requires institutions in life sciences, medicine, and AI to create S&T ethics (review) committees.

Mandates comprehensive ethics reviews for S&T activities with high ethical risks, ensuring adherence to principles of independence and transparency.

Instructs local governments and relevant departments to oversee S&T ethics, including risk assessment and emergency handling in high-ethics-risk fields.

Promotes legislative development for S&T ethics, focusing on transforming norms into regulations and ensuring accountability for violations.

Encourages S&T personnel to enhance ethical awareness and report violations.

Supports educational initiatives in S&T ethics for students and professionals.

Urges transparent communication with the public about S&T ethics issues.

Outlines punitive measures for S&T ethics violations, including restrictions on government-funded activities and legal consequences for violators.

name: Boise Regulations 4.30q (City Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI))
summary:
Mandates IT Department approval before accessing or acquiring AI products, with a maintained list of approved AI technologies.

Requires fact-checking and reviewing AI-generated content, especially for public communications, to ensure accuracy, proper attribution, and absence of bias or harmful material.

Stipulates disclosure of AI usage in significant public communications to build trust and transparency.

Prohibits sharing sensitive or private information in AI prompts to prevent unintended data exposure.

Directs annual reviews and updates of the regulation to align with technological advancements and best practices.

Tasks the Information Technology department with overseeing AI initiatives, compliance, and periodic audits for effectiveness and ethical considerations.

Aims to govern AI use responsibly and ethically, enhancing public services and fostering innovation for community benefit.

name: Oversee Emerging Technology Act
summary:
Requires the head of each covered federal agency engaged in emerging technologies to appoint or designate a Senior Executive Service individual or equivalent as an emerging technology lead.

Mandates that these leads advise agencies on the responsible use of emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence.

Obliges these leads to provide expertise on responsible policies and practices, collaborate with interagency bodies, and input on procurement policies.

Instructs the President to inform Congress within 180 days of enactment about the appointed leads and their authorities and responsibilities.

name: H. R. 4913 NOAA Precipitation Forecasts
summary:
Establishes a program within the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) to improve precipitation forecasts.

Requires the use of fully coupled Earth System Models to enhance precipitation prediction.

Mandates the utilization of high performance computing and other technologies, including machine learning and artificial intelligence, to advance precipitation forecasts.

Supports research and development in collaboration with academic and private sector partners to test and evaluate emerging technologies.

Improves the accuracy, reliability, and timeliness of precipitation predictions across various timescales.

Incorporates social and behavioral sciences to enhance precipitation forecast products and communication.

Coordinates efforts with Federal, State, local, Tribal, and academic entities.

Authorizes appropriations of $15 million annually from fiscal year 2024 through fiscal year 2028 for the program.

name: AI Grand Challenges Act of 2024
summary:
Establishes the AI Grand Challenges Program to stimulate AI research, development, and commercialization through prize competitions addressing grand challenges in various sectors like national security, health, and environment.

Requires the Director of the National Science Foundation, in coordination with public and private entities, to identify AI grand challenges and develop problem statements.

Mandates the creation of a specific grand challenge for AI-enabled cancer breakthroughs.

Sets eligibility criteria for participants, requiring private entities to be U.S.-based and individuals to be U.S. citizens or permanent residents.

Requires submission of a report within 60 days of awarding a prize, detailing the winning submission and its benefits, as well as biennial reports to Congress on program activities and public outreach, to be made publicly accessible.

name: Federal Civilian Agency AI Testing and Certification Act
summary:
Establishes federal civilian agency laboratories for AI testing and certification under the Secretary of Homeland Security through FEMA.

Mandates development of AI training and testing centers to evaluate AI systems for federal use, prioritizing privacy, transparency, accountability, and protection of individual rights.

Prohibits automated decision-making that threatens due process and constitutional rights.

Requires real-world use cases to inform AI system outcomes in federal settings, ensuring no personal data is used.

Creates a digital repository for use cases, ensuring Federal agencies can train and test AI systems appropriately.

Establishes an Office of Artificial Intelligence Incident Reporting within the Department of Homeland Security for agency collaboration and reporting on AI experiences.

Requires biannual reports from DHS to Congress on implementation, challenges, and resource needs, and agency reports on adverse AI experiences.

Authorizes $20 billion in appropriations to implement these measures.

name: Singapore National AI Strategy 2.0
summary:
Aims to harness AI for public good and position Singapore as a leader in AI innovation. 

Sets two primary goals: achieving excellence in AI to maximize value creation and empowering communities to use AI with confidence. 

Outlines a focus on three systems: Activity Drivers, People & Communities, and Infrastructure & Environment, supported by 10 enablers. 

Plans to establish AI Centers of Excellence, strengthen the AI start-up ecosystem, and drive public sector AI adoption. 

Aims to attract global AI talent and boost its AI practitioner pool to support AI demand. 

Emphasizes building a trusted AI environment through updated regulatory frameworks, security measures, and international collaboration. 

Seeks to enhance data management and privacy technologies for responsible AI development and position Singapore as a global AI governance leader.

Encourages making more public sector data available for AI development that serves the Public Good.

name: American Aviation Act, Sec. 908 ("Part 107 Waiver Improvements")
summary:
Requires the Administrator of the Federal Aviation Administration to leverage big data analytics and machine learning in reviewing requests for certificates of waiver under section 107.200 of title 14, Code of Federal Regulations.Adopts a performance- and risk-based approach for reviewing waiver requests under section 107.200 of title 14, CFR.

Improves the waiver application process and prohibits the use of open-ended descriptive prompts, except for unusual or irregular operations.

Leverages data, including big data analytics and machine learning, from previous waiver requests.

Requires consideration of control over access to real property within the operation area and recognizes safety enhancements from such control.

Publishes all issued certificates of waiver on the FAA website, including terms, conditions, limitations, and airspace class, while protecting proprietary information.

Allows streamlined approval for waiver applications substantially similar to previously approved ones.

Establishes an expedited review process for modifying or renewing previously issued waivers.

name: Canadian Guardrails for Generative AI – Code of Practice
summary:
Proposes a voluntary code of practice for generative AI systems in Canada to ensure safety, security, and trust ahead of binding regulation.

Requires developers, deployers, and operators to identify and prevent malicious and inappropriate uses, mitigating safety risks of AI systems throughout their lifecycle.

Mandates assessment and curation of datasets to avoid biases and ensure fairness.

Emphasizes transparency through methods like watermarking AI-generated content and explaining system development processes.

Encourages human oversight and monitoring, including mechanisms to report adverse impacts and routine model updates.

Calls for accountability with internal governance, independent audits, and defined roles and responsibilities.

name: H. R. 6425 (Five Eyes countries AI initiative)
summary:
Directs the Secretary of Defense to establish the Five AIs Strategic Artificial Intelligence Working Group to develop and coordinate AI initiatives among Five Eyes countries. 

Outlines the organization of the working group, designating a senior civilian or military officer as head, and encouraging participation of Five Eyes Intelligence Oversight and Review Council members. 

Tasks the working group with comparing AI systems, identifying interoperability solutions, and testing AI model redundancy.

Instructs the development of shared strategies for AI research, development, and data management.

Requires the submission of a plan for the establishment and activities of the working group within 60 days and biannual reports to congressional committees.

name: Wisconsin Executive Order #211 (Governor’s Task Force on Workforce and Artificial Intelligence)
summary:
Creates the Governor’s Task Force on Workforce and Artificial Intelligence, chaired by the Secretary of the Department of Workforce Development or a designee.

Appoints additional members from key state departments, educational institutions, and other stakeholders, as determined by the Governor.

Instructs the Task Force to gather and analyze information to produce an advisory action plan for the Governor.

Requires the plan to assess generative AI’s impact on Wisconsin’s labor market, predict future impacts, and identify effects on key industries and skillsets.

Explores initiatives to advance equity and economic opportunity related to AI-driven changes.

Recommends solutions, including policy changes in workforce development and education, based on identified impacts.

Attaches the Task Force to the Department of Workforce Development.

name: Indianapolis City Council Proposal No.362, 2023 (Commission on AI Development)
summary:
Establishes a study commission named the "Commission on Artificial Intelligence Development" to review and analyze the City and County's current use of artificial intelligence.

Requires the commission to gather insights from AI experts, industry leaders, and community members on future AI applications to improve city services.

Mandates the commission to recommend policies for trustworthy and transparent AI usage to the Mayor and City-County Council.

Directs the commission to suggest modifications or new ordinances for AI usage.

Composes the commission of nine members, including Councillors, IT directors, and citizen members, all residents of Marion County.

Requires city departments to share information and cooperate with the commission.

Obligates the commission to present a final report by the July 2024 meeting, available on the City’s website.

Initiates operations as soon as practical and outlines a meeting and research timeline. 

Permits public comment under commission-devised rules.

name: New York A7838 ("Long-term impact of AI on workforce")
summary:
Mandates the Department of Labor to begin a study on the long-term impact of artificial intelligence on the state workforce within six months.

Requires consultation with the Department of Civil Service and the Office of Information Technology Services.

Calls for examination of job performance, productivity, training, education requirements, privacy, and security.

Obligates the Department of Labor to issue an interim report every five years and a final report by January 1, 2035, with recommendations for legislative action.

Prohibits all state departments and governmental entities from using AI to displace any natural person from their employment until the final report and recommendations are received.

Ensures immediate effect upon enactment.

name: Rhode Island SB 146 ("Consumer Protection Gaming Act")
summary:
Prohibits the use of facial recognition technology and biometric recognition programs in video-lottery terminals and online betting applications.

Prohibits the use of algorithmic programs that modify gaming based on a consumer's betting history to increase wagers.

Prohibits the use of artificial intelligence or automated decision systems to promote increased play through intermittent reinforcement based on cognitive-behavioral algorithms and prior gaming data.

Applies these prohibitions to sports betting applications and vendors of gambling products licensed by Rhode Island.

Excludes standardized rewards programs from these prohibitions.

Takes effect upon passage.

name: Pennsylvania HR 170 ("AI Advisory Committee")
summary:
Directs the Joint State Government Commission to establish an advisory committee to study artificial intelligence's impact in Pennsylvania.

Mandates an assessment of AI development and use, including benefits, risks, and fiscal impacts on the state.

Proposes legislation for state AI regulation and a definition for AI.

Recommends evaluating AI's effects on students' academic performance and addressing AI-driven disinformation.

Urges studying potential job displacement due to AI automation and assessing implications for organized labor.

Calls for a proposal on ethical and responsible AI development in Pennsylvania.

Advises considering the creation of a permanent commission for AI study.

Allows the Joint State Government Commission to request information from state agencies for the study.

Requires a report with findings and recommendations within 18 months to various governmental leaders and committees.

name: Protecting Kids on Social Media Act
summary:
Requires social media platforms to verify the age of users beyond simple attestations, using current age verification technologies.

Prohibits social media platforms from allowing individuals under 13 from accessing their services.

Mandates parental or guardian consent for users under 18, requiring platforms to take reasonable steps to verify this consent.

Prohibits the use of algorithmic recommendation systems on individuals under 18, except for contextual suggestions or advertising.

Establishes a Pilot Program for secure digital identification credentials to facilitate age and parental consent verification, overseen by the Secretary of Commerce.

Empowers the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) and state attorneys general to enforce compliance, with civil penalties for violations.

Grants extraterritorial jurisdiction for violations involving individuals in the United States.

name: TAG Act
summary:
Requires the Director of the Office of Management and Budget to issue guidance for transparent automated governance, ensuring compliance with privacy, civil rights, and civil liberties protections.

Mandates agencies to disclose and allow appeals when utilizing automated systems for critical decisions affecting individuals’ rights or status.

Instructs agencies to design systems providing plain language notifications and establish appeals processes for decisions made using AI-augmented processes.

Obligates agencies to track the accuracy and reliability of AI systems, and share data with relevant authorities; encourages consultation with governmental and private sectors for guidance development.

Requires the Comptroller General to report on agency compliance, with reports submitted biennially.

name: Advanced Weather Model Computing Development Act
summary:
Directs the Department of Energy (DOE) and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) to collaborate on AI and high-performance computing research to improve climate models and weather prediction.

Requires the establishment of a memorandum of understanding to facilitate this collaboration through a competitive, merit-reviewed process.

Authorizes the Secretary of Energy and NOAA Administrator to conduct research on modeling, simulation, machine learning, data assimilation, and predictive analysis techniques.

Mandates the promotion of collaboration and data sharing among federal agencies, National Laboratories, educational institutions, and nonprofits, while ensuring compliance with national security policies.

Instructs the submission of a report within two years detailing interagency coordination, research achievements, and future opportunities.

Initiates a high-performance computing project to enhance weather prediction models, requiring a comparative analysis with current forecasts.

Sunsets the authority for this initiative five years post-enactment.

Ensures compliance with research security provisions under the CHIPS Act of 2022.

name: Digital Defense Content Provenance Act
summary:
Requires the Department of Defense to establish a course at the Defense Information School to provide education on digital content provenance for DoD media content, covering challenges from digital content forgery, industry-open technical standards, and techniques for secure digital content documentation.

Mandates a report on the curriculum development and implementation plan for the course, including resource needs.

Initiates a pilot program to assess the feasibility of using industry-open technical standards for digital content provenance in DoD media.

Directs the pilot program to verify digital content provenance, apply technology solutions, assess historical records, and develop effectiveness measures.

Requires a report detailing findings, consultations, effectiveness, and recommendations on the pilot program's permanence.

name: Artificial Intelligence and the Information Privacy Principles
summary:
Requires organizations in New Zealand using AI tools to comply with the Privacy Act 2020 and its Information Privacy Principles. 

Mandates senior leadership approval for AI tool usage and a privacy impact assessment (PIA) to evaluate privacy risks.

Demands transparency about AI tool usage, including engaging with Māori on potential impacts, assessing the necessity and proportionality of AI tools, and considering privacy implications.

Advises on proactive privacy measures, including developing privacy policies, engaging with affected communities, and evaluating training data provenance.

Highlights potential privacy issues with AI, such as automation blindness and overseas data disclosure risks.

Encourages organizations to secure personal information and comply with access, correction, and disclosure requirements.

name: AI Cloud KYC Proposed Rule (Department of Commerce)
summary:
Requires U.S. Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) providers to implement a Customer Identification Program (CIP) for verifying foreign customers' identities and maintaining relevant records to prevent malicious cyber activities. 

Obligates foreign resellers to adhere to similar CIP standards and mandates U.S. IaaS providers to report on these. 

Obligates reporting on transactions involving training of large AI models that could be misused for cyber activities. 

Authorizes the Secretary of Commerce to enforce special measures against foreign jurisdictions or persons using U.S. IaaS for cyber threats. 

Ensures compliance by conducting assessments and requiring annual certification of CIPs by IaaS providers. 

Institutes penalties for non-compliance, including civil and criminal liabilities. 

Mandates reporting to the Department of Commerce for violations or suspicious activities associated with AI model training.

name: ICTS Transaction Review Rule (Department of Commerce)
summary:
Regulates ICTS transactions designed, developed, manufactured, or supplied by individuals or entities owned by, controlled by, or under the jurisdiction of foreign adversaries, assessing undue risks as per Executive Order 13873.

Defines key terms such as "Covered ICTS Transaction" and "Person owned by, controlled by, or subject to the jurisdiction or direction of a foreign adversary."

Charges the Secretary of Commerce with determining transaction risks, involving consultation with agency heads like the Secretary of Defense and Director of National Intelligence.

Outlines procedures for initial and final determinations on ICTS transactions, including conditions for prohibitions or mitigation measures.

Establishes penalties, both civil and criminal, for engaging in prohibited ICTS transactions, aiding violations, or providing false information during assessments.

Mandates confidentiality of sensitive information and allows disclosure to government entities under national security considerations. 

Requires recordkeeping and provides interagency consultation procedures during transaction reviews.

name: St Louis MO, Board Bill No. 185 2023-24 ("Regulating the City's Use of Surveillance Technology")
summary:
Requires a City Entity in St. Louis to obtain Board of Aldermen approval before accepting funds, acquiring, or using surveillance technology, including AI surveillance tools.

Defines surveillance technology broadly to include AI-based systems.

Mandates public availability and Board approval of a Surveillance Use Plan (SUP) before technology use.

Prohibits unauthorized surveillance use that discriminates or infringes civil rights.

Obligates annual reporting on surveillance technology use, data sharing, and impacts.

Protects whistleblowers disclosing ordinance violations.

Allows temporary use of surveillance technology in exigent circumstances with strict limits and reporting requirements.

Establishes remedies and disciplinary actions for ordinance violations.

Ensures public participation and transparency in the surveillance approval process.

Seeks to balance surveillance benefits with civil rights protections, assessing potential discriminatory impacts.

name: San Jose Generative AI Guidelines
summary:
Establishes guidelines for using Generative AI within the City of San José, emphasizing privacy, accuracy, transparency, equity, accountability, and beneficial use.

Requires users to cite AI where substantial content is AI-generated and to verify AI output against trustworthy sources.

Prohibits submission of personal or confidential information into Generative AI platforms and mandates the creation of separate accounts for City-related work using Generative AI.

Subjects AI usage to public records laws, recommending users to opt out of data collection where possible and verify AI-generated content for copyright compliance.

Offers collaborative working groups to enhance AI governance and provides risk assessment criteria for Generative AI use cases.

Encourages active participation in AI workgroups and emphasizes the importance of adapting guidelines as technology and laws evolve.

name: Los Angeles AI Roadmap 2024, Best Practices and Roadmap
summary:
Establishes two distinct user segments for AI tools: City Employees and IT Professionals, requiring tailored training for each group.

Instructs non-technical department leadership to set clear goals before AI tool deployment.

Encourages piloting AI tools to understand their strengths and weaknesses before widespread use.

Anticipates most AI tools will be accessed through existing software platforms.

Emphasizes the need for adaptable AI tools that align with evolving data and requirements.

Advises staying current on AI tools and frameworks for maximized effectiveness.

Requires comprehensive AI training for both users and developers, highlighting security and ethical considerations.

Insists on cybersecurity and data privacy for AI implementation.
