Highlights AI as a long-term investment needing high-quality data and data transparency.

Asserts City data ownership and the need for ethical, transparent, and human-centered AI tools.

Outlines a roadmap for training, deploying AI tools, and developing ethics guidelines for the City.

name: City of Boston Interim Guidelines for Using Generative AI
summary:
Instructs the City agencies and departments of Boston, excluding Boston Public Schools, to use generative AI responsibly, with guidelines focusing on transparency, accountability, and inclusiveness.

Requires fact-checking and reviewing AI-generated content for public communication to avoid inaccuracies and biases.

Emphasizes disclosing AI usage, including model type and version, to promote trust and transparency.

Prohibits sharing of sensitive or private information in AI prompts to protect residents' data privacy.

Encourages responsible experimentation with generative AI to support efficient, equitable city services while managing risks.

Directs the Department of Innovation and Technology to facilitate learning events and workshops on generative AI.

Advises consultation with relevant city offices and community organizations before publicizing AI-created content to ensure accessibility, accuracy, and sensitivity.

Promotes AI use in drafting documents, summarizing text, coding, and creating multimedia, while highlighting the importance of human oversight and editing.

Encourages engaging stakeholders for potential impacts on arts and society.

name: Miami Dade County Artificial Intelligence Report, County Administrative Order (EMPLOYEE USE OF AI)
summary:
Guides Miami-Dade County employees in the responsible and ethical use of AI, focusing on transparency, data security, and privacy.

Requires adherence to public records laws and ethical guidelines.

Instructs the Human Resources and Information Technology Departments to provide AI training, emphasizing ethical use, bias recognition, and data management.

Mandates risk assessments prior to AI implementation.

Tasks the Information Technology Department with overseeing AI procurement, deployment, and system security.

Establishes protocols for data governance, encryption, and privacy.

Defines roles for directors, supervisors, and employees in AI project management, ethical leadership, and compliance.

Implements regular audits, assessments, and vendor evaluations to maintain AI system integrity.

Encourages community engagement and stakeholder discussions on AI deployment.

Commits to continuous improvement with annual assessments and updates by the IT Department, involving multidisciplinary teams and beta testing initiatives.

Provides resources through the IT Department’s website.

name: Department of Energy Quantum Leadership Act of 2024, Sec 2 (Quantum Information Science Research Program)
summary:
Amends the National Quantum Initiative Act to mandate the Secretary of Energy to conduct a program focusing on quantum information science research, development, and commercialization.

Operates National Quantum Information Science Research Centers to facilitate breakthroughs in quantum technologies.

Requires collaboration with industry, National Laboratories, and educational institutions for technology development.

Engages with the quantum technology industry to promote the commercialization of applications relevant to the Department of Energy's activities.

Submits a 10-year strategic plan to integrate quantum and AI with high-performance computing systems.

Establishes an early-stage quantum high-performance computing research program.

Conducts a study on the quantum supply chain to identify growth obstacles and recommends strategies to bolster domestic manufacturing and workforce development.

Launches a university-led traineeship program to develop the quantum workforce.

Coordinates activities with other federal entities to prevent duplication.

Restricts funding from foreign countries of concern and entities deemed harmful to U.S. national security.

name: Open Translation Center Act
summary:
Establishes the Open Translation Center (OTC) to translate and analyze foreign language materials from designated countries for public dissemination, enhancing understanding of foreign governments, economies, and cultures.

Administers OTC either as a separate entity or a nonprofit and requires a governing board of five appointed members with relevant expertise, independent of the U.S. Government.

Tasks OTC with translating documents into English, providing analyses, and making materials publicly available while respecting copyright laws.

Requires cooperation with federal agencies and stakeholders, and authorizes consultation with foreign governments after certification by the Secretary of State.

Designates the Secretary of State as the primary sponsor, with potential sponsorship from other federal agencies such as the CIA.

Allocates funding of $85 million for fiscal year 2024 and $80 million for subsequent years through 2028 for OTC operations.

name: Seattle Generative AI Policy
summary:
Regulates City departments' acquisition and use of generative AI, requiring adherence to principles of innovation, transparency, and bias reduction.

Requires Seattle IT to evaluate generative AI acquisition requests and has authority to approve, deny, or revoke use based on risk assessments.

Mandates human review of AI-generated outputs before official use with documentation of review processes.

Requires attribution for AI-generated content, specifying inclusion of system names and review assertions.

Obliges the use of Racial Equity Toolkit prior to using generative AI tools to combat bias and discrimination.

Prohibits submission of confidential City data to AI systems without adequate enterprise controls and data protection.

Classifies AI-generated records as public and mandates retention and disclosure compliance.

Assigns the Chief Technology Officer responsibility for policy enforcement, with potential penalties for non-compliance.

Specifies the Director of DPAC and Chief Privacy Officer maintain risk criteria and exception processes.

name: Tempe Ethical AI Policy
summary:
Establishes the City of Tempe's commitment to ethical AI use, emphasizing transparency, fairness, accountability, and protection of rights.

Applies this policy to all AI technologies in city operations, including predictive analytics, machine learning, and automated decision-making.

Requires defined objectives, data privacy, and human-AI collaboration, while ensuring human control.

Tasks departments with setting AI objectives, conducting reviews, and collaborating with IT for oversight.

Instructs the Technology and Innovation Steering Committee to monitor AI compliance, develop reporting mechanisms, and define non-compliance consequences.

Mandates Information Technology to develop a review process, conduct training, and support compliance.

Commits to ongoing monitoring, stakeholder engagement, and ethical improvement of AI practices.

Promotes public engagement and awareness campaigns about AI activities.

Requires compliance with applicable laws and regulations and supports ethical AI frameworks development. 

Commits to periodic policy reviews to address emerging AI challenges and advancements.

name: County of Santa Cruz AI Appropriate Use Policy
summary:
Establishes the County of Santa Cruz's principles for responsible use of generative AI by employees, contractors, and third parties, ensuring alignment with ethical and legal standards.

Requires compliance with data privacy laws, such as HIPAA and CCPA, and informs the public of AI tool interactions, offering alternatives.

Prohibits the use of AI for unauthorized access, handling of personally identifiable information, unlawful activities, hiring decisions, and entering sensitive data into AI systems.

Permits only approved AI tools like Google Bard, OpenAI's ChatGPT, Anthropic's Claude, and Scribe.

Requires employees to exercise judgment, report concerns, and use County email for AI tool accounts.

Encourages comprehension of AI policies and participation in workgroups while emphasizing responsible, ethical, and transparent AI usage, avoiding bias, and not relying on AI for significant decision-making.

name: Kendall County Generative AI Chatbot Usage Policy
summary:
Outlines the use of generative AI chatbots, like ChatGPT and Bard, for Kendall County employees. 

Prohibits using county email addresses and submitting proprietary or confidential data into these platforms. 

Requires employees to consult with Executives regarding chatbot use, who may approve, deny, or modify usage parameters. 

Mandates proper citation and accuracy checks for AI-generated content. 

Enforces disciplinary actions, including termination, for policy violations or inappropriate use, ensuring ethical compliance with conduct and antidiscrimination policies. 

Instructs employees to undergo training on proper chatbot use. 

Applies Technology and Record Retention Policies when using AI with County equipment. 

Addresses training queries with Human Resources or the Information, Communication and Technology Department Director.

name: The City of Tulsa Municipal Court Rules 2024, Rule 25. "Generative AI"
summary:
Require any attorney, pro se defendant, victim, or other party using generative AI in drafting documents for the Municipal Criminal Court to disclose the use of such AI.

Specify the name of the generative AI tool used in the filing.

Include ChatGPT, Bing AI, and Google Bard under the definition of generative AI.

Maintain the applicability of 12 O.S. §2011 to all filings, ensuring compliance is certified by the person signing the document.

name: Guidance on generative AI for City of St. Louis employees
summary:
Instructs City employees to adhere to the Information Technology Acceptable Use Policy when using generative AI tools.

Requires ITSA to vet the purchase of AI-related technology and software.

Prohibits the use of City passwords for logging onto AI platforms and advises caution due to evolving malware threats.

Forbids the upload of sensitive or confidential information when using AI systems.

Advises a review and validation of AI-generated content due to potential bias or inaccuracies.

Cautions that AI-generated content might be copyright-protected and requires proper attribution.

Warns that content generated by AI may be subject to disclosure under Sunshine Law.

Indicates that ITSA and the Mayor’s Office will continue to evaluate the use of AI and develop policies accordingly.

name: Artificial Intelligence (Regulation) Act 2024
summary:
Establishes the AI Authority to ensure regulators take accountability for AI, align regulatory approaches, review legislation, monitor regulatory frameworks, assess risks, support testbeds, and promote international interoperability.

Mandates the AI Authority to adhere to principles ensuring AI safety, transparency, fairness, accountability, compliance with laws, and inclusivity.

Requires the creation of regulatory sandboxes for testing AI innovations with consumer protections.

Obligates businesses using AI to appoint AI responsible officers to ensure ethical use and unbiased data.

Imposes transparency and IP obligations, requiring disclosing records of data used in AI training and independent audits.

Mandates the implementation of public engagement programs on AI opportunities and risks.

name: Candidate Voice Fraud Prohibition Act
summary:
Prohibits the distribution of political communications containing materially deceptive AI-generated audio that impersonates a candidate’s voice, with actual malice, intended to harm the candidate’s reputation or deceive voters.

Applies to communications distributed within 90 days of a general election or 60 days of a primary, special, or runoff election.

Exempts certain entities from liability such as radio or television stations that air deceptive AI-generated content as part of news coverage or communications that clearly constitute satire.

Defines "materially deceptive audio" as AI-generated impersonation of a candidate’s voice without approval and lacking a clear disclaimer.

Imposes criminal penalties of fines or up to 2 years imprisonment for individuals who knowingly and willfully violate the prohibition.

Requires the Federal Election Commission (FEC) to issue regulations to clarify disclaimer requirements and mandates the submission of annual compliance reports to Congress.

name: New Technologies at Borders Act
summary:
Requires the Department of Homeland Security to develop a comprehensive plan within 180 days to identify, deploy, and integrate emerging and advanced technologies to enhance situational awareness along the northern and southern borders of the United States.

Mandates the inclusion of artificial intelligence, machine learning, automation, fiber-optic sensing, nanotechnology, optical and cognitive radar, modeling and simulation technology, hyperspectral and LIDAR sensors, and other similar technologies.

Includes an assessment of current technology utilization by U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) and how capability gaps can be addressed through technology integration.

Requires cost estimates for technology acquisition and maintenance, metrics for measuring technology impact, and an assessment of multi-domain awareness improvements.

Mandates an analysis of other Federal technologies, procurement authorities, and the transition of new technology systems.

Requires coordination with the Department of Homeland Security's Science and Technology Directorate for research, development, and incentivizing private sector innovation.

name: Further Continuing Appropriations and Disaster Relief Supplemental Appropriations Act ("Prohibition and Notification on Investments Relating to Covered National Security Transactions")
summary:
Prohibits U.S. persons from engaging in investments involving covered national security transactions in prohibited technologies, with exemptions permissible by the Secretary for activities deemed in the national interest. 

Allows the Secretary to issue regulations that require notifications for such transactions. 

Introduces penalties for violations, including civil penalties and potential divestment requirements, with the burden of proof resting on the Secretary in enforcement actions. 

Establishes processes for self-disclosure of violations and requests for non-binding feedback regarding transactions. 

Mandates annual reports to Congress detailing enforcement actions and technology assessments. 

Provides for confidentiality of transaction information, but outlines exceptions for disclosure relevant to U.S. national security interests. 

Encourages international cooperation to prevent prohibited technology development or acquisition by countries of concern, such as China. 

Defines key terms, including "prohibited technology" and "country of concern."

name: Further Continuing Appropriations and Disaster Relief Supplemental Appropriations Act ("Promoting Resilient Supply Chains")
summary:
Expands the responsibilities of the Assistant Secretary of Commerce to include promoting the resilience of supply chains related to critical and emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence.

Mandates the creation of the Supply Chain Resilience Working Group composed of relevant federal agencies to assess and model supply chain stability, including those involving AI technologies.

Requires the group to identify vulnerabilities and prepare for potential supply chain shocks that might impact AI and other critical technologies.

Encourages domestic production and manufacturing, specifically focusing on AI and technological advancements.

Obligates periodic reports and assessments to Congress regarding the resilience and capacity of AI-related supply chains and industry preparedness for shocks.

Prohibits reliance on critical goods from countries identified as risks to national security, advocating for sourcing from allies.

Sets a 10-year expiration for these provisions.

Protects confidential data shared voluntarily under this title from disclosure, ensuring privacy concerns in relation to AI-related supply chain information.

name: Diabetes Act
summary:
Mandates the Secretary of Health and Human Services to recognize algorithms in automated insulin delivery systems as medically necessary under Medicare, ensuring their separate reimbursement.

Ensures care continuity for individuals using diabetes technology when enrolling in Medicare Part B by January 2026.

Requires development of a process to consider diabetes technologies not currently covered under Medicare Part B for potential inclusion.

Mandates creation of new coding for insulin pump training and education by 2026, to enhance billing and reimbursement transparency.

Obligates the issuance of a national coverage determination for insulin pumps within 180 days from enactment.

Instructs the Comptroller General to report within a year on barriers hindering access to diabetes technologies and services in Federal healthcare programs, reviewing legal and policy issues affecting access.

name: St. Louis Executive Order No. 87 (police use of AI)
summary:
Establishes transparency and accountability requirements for the St. Louis Metropolitan Police Department’s (SLMPD) use of surveillance technology, including artificial intelligence (AI).

Prohibits using surveillance technology to monitor political, religious, or social groups unless tied to criminal activity or public safety threats.

Mandates public, written policies for SLMPD’s use of surveillance technology and AI.

Requires annual transparency reports detailing the SLMPD’s surveillance technology usage, capabilities, impacts, and related complaints.

Obliges vendors to protect data privacy, prohibiting unauthorized access or sale of collected data.

Ensures compliance with federal and state laws regarding data storage, retention, and access.

Directs cooperation with the City’s Information Technology Services for technology acquisitions.

Requires adherence to 28 C.F.R. Part 23 for participation in criminal intelligence systems.

Mandates policies for data sharing, following "need to know" and "right to know" standards for law enforcement agencies.

name: Emerging Innovative Border Technologies Act
summary:
Mandates the Secretary of Homeland Security to submit a plan for deploying innovative border technologies within 180 days. 

Requires the plan to assess artificial intelligence’s impact on privacy, civil rights, and civil liberties, and include mitigation measures. 

Directs the establishment of CBP Innovation Teams to evaluate and integrate advanced technologies, ensuring compliance with DHS policies on AI use. 

Focuses on transitioning technologies to CBP programs, addressing potential negative outcomes and capability gaps. 

Instructs annual reporting on Innovation Teams’ activities, technologies piloted, and their success rates. 

Requires coordination with DHS's AI policies to ensure responsible AI use. 

Demands cost-benefit analysis before large-scale technology deployment, ensuring security effectiveness and governmental cost-efficiency. 

Emphasizes collaboration with the private sector, other government entities, and stakeholders for optimizing advanced technology deployment.

name: Further Continuing Appropriations and Disaster Relief Supplemental Appropriations Act ("Report on Wearable Medical Devices")
summary:
Mandates the Comptroller General to conduct a technology assessment of wearable medical devices within 18 months of the Act's enactment.

Requires submission of a report to Congress on the capabilities and limitations of these devices in supporting clinical decision-making.

Includes a description of the potential for wearable devices to accurately prescribe treatments.

Examines the benefits and challenges of using artificial intelligence to augment these capabilities.

Suggests policy options to enhance the benefits and address the challenges of developing or using wearable medical devices.

name: Google DeepMind Frontier Safety Framework Version 1.0
summary:
Establishes protocols within the Frontier Safety Framework to address severe risks from future foundation models' capabilities.

Defines "Critical Capability Levels" (CCLs) to identify when AI models pose heightened risks, focusing initially on Autonomy, Biosecurity, Cybersecurity, and Machine Learning R&D.

Implements periodic evaluations to detect when models approach CCLs and articulates developing mitigation plans.

Proposes security mitigations to prevent model weight exfiltration and deployment mitigations to control access and expression of critical capabilities.

Outlines graded mitigation and security protocols based on AI capabilities and risks from potential misuse. 

Plans to implement the framework by early 2025 and expects it to evolve with emerging risks and insights.

Commits to periodically reviewing and updating the framework as understanding of AI risks and benefits improves.

name: Arizona HB 2482 (2023)
summary:
Creates a law enforcement crime victims notification system to automatically update crime victims on their crime reports, investigations, and cases.

Requires the notification system to provide a virtual agent that employs artificial intelligence to answer citizens' questions and respond to their comments through voice, text, or email. 

Appropriates funds for the creation of the notification system.

name: FY2023 NDAA, Section 11226 ("Artificial intelligence strategy")
summary:
Requires the Commandant of the Coast Guard to coordinate activities and data related to identifying, demonstrating and deploying AI technology.

Requires the Commandant to designate a senior Coast Guard official responsible for identifying, demonstrating and deploying AI technology and for convening other Coast Guard officials for AI-related purposes.

Requires the designated official to develop, and submit within two years, a strategic plan for identifying, demonstrating and deploying AI technology.

name: FY2022 NDAA, Section 226 ("Review of artificial intelligence applications and establishment of performance metrics")
summary:
Directs the Secretary of Defense to study potential applications of artificial intelligence to Department of Defense platforms, processes, and operations, and to establish related metrics and objectives.

Specifies study and metric requirements related to AI-related skill gaps; modernization activities; exercises, wargames, and experimentation; logistics and sustainment; and business operations.

Requires the Secretary to report to Congress within 120 days after completion of the required study.

name: FY2022 NDAA, Section 227 ("Modification of the joint common foundation program")
summary:
Instructs the Secretary of Defense to modify the Joint Common Foundation Program and to ensure that the Department of Defense (DoD) can more easily contract with commercial AI companies for better support in efficiently developing new capabilities and applications. 

Instructs the Secretary of Defense to facilitate an increase in the number of eligible commercial AI companies to support DoD components, including cybersecurity processes.

name: FY2023 NDAA, Section 1554 ("Roadmap and implementation plan for cyber adoption of artificial intelligence")
summary:
Requires the Commander of the United States Cyber Command and the Chief Information Officer of the Department of Defense to develop a five-year implementation plan for rapidly adopting artificial intelligence systems to support the Department of Defense. 

The plan shall: 

(a) Identify and prioritize AI systems and data that currently affect, or may benefit in the future, the Department's cybersecurity and cyber operations. 

(b) Lay out a plan to acquire AI systems and data identified in part (a).

(c) Identify relevant skill deficiencies.

(d) Identify opportunities to solicit AI system operator feedback.

(e) Identify and address long term technology gaps for the Department's cyber war fighting mission.

(f) Evaluate the risks posed by adversary AI-based attacks.

(g) Furnish a timeline with target milestones, investments, and required expenditures.
 
(h) Incorporate metrics to evaluate AI adoption.

(i) Identify further funding, authorities, and policies that may be necessary.

(j) Define a maturity model describing desired cyber capabilities independent of specific technology solutions.

name: FY2022 NDAA, Section 1531 ("Digital development infrastructure plan and working group")
summary:
Instructs the Secretary of Defense to develop a plan for establishing AI-related information technology infrastructure, including a technical plan and guidance, a governance structure with relevant guidance and policies, and prototype development and platform environments.

Instructs the Secretary to harmonize the required plan with various existing plans and strategies. Establishes a plan working group comprised of senior DOD officials.

Instructs the Secretary to assemble enterprise data sets in various AI application domains.

name: FY2023 NDAA, Section 6723 ("Requirements and report on workforce needs of intelligence community relating to science, technology, engineering, and math, and related areas")
summary:
Instructs the Director of National Intelligence to submit a single report on the workforce needs of each element of the intelligence community relating to emerging technologies, with a specific focus on artificial intelligence.
        
Requires a list of personnel in work roles whose primary official duties include artificial intelligence responsibilities.
          
Requires an assessment of the quality and sustainability of the talent pipeline of the intelligence community with respect to talent in emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence. 

Requires a description of the education, recruitment, and retention programs personnel of the intelligence community.

Requires an assessment of any gaps in authorities, resources, recruitment or retention incentives, skills-based training, or educational programs, that may negatively affect the quality or sustainability of such talent pipeline.

name: NYC Local Law 144
summary:
Defines "automated employment decision tools" as computational processes used in discretionary employment decision making, including AI- and machine learning-derived processes.

Requires businesses using automated employment decision tools in New York City to obtain impartial bias audits of the tools from independent auditors, and to disclose the results of the audits to the public online.

Requires businesses using automated employment decision tools in New York City to notify and disclose specified information to job candidates for whom such tools are used.

Establishes civil penalties for violations of the law and empowers the city corporation counsel to enforce the law.

name: FY2023 NDAA, Section 1513 ("Establishing projects for data management, artificial intelligence, and digital solutions")
summary:
Instructs the Deputy Secretary of Defense to establish projects for data management, artificial intelligence, and digital solutions for business efficiency and war-fighting capabilities intended to accelerate decision advantage.

Instructs the Deputy Secretary to task senior DOD officials with developing an actionable plan to integrate various AI applications into government operational environments, and to boost the population of government personnel with AI expertise.

name: Public Law 117–173
summary: Amends Section 41001(6)(A) of the FAST Act to include semiconductors, artificial intelligence, machine learning, cybersecurity, and various related technology-powered infrastructure to the FAST Act permitting program.

name: FY2023 NDAA, Section 11227 ("Review of artificial intelligence applications and establishment of performance metrics")
summary:
Directs the Commandant of the Coast Guard to study potential applications of artificial intelligence and to identify resources necessary to improve the use of artificial intelligence in Coast Guard platforms, processes, and operations; instructs the Commandant to establish related metrics and objectives.

Requires that the Commandant assess AI-related skill gaps and civilian and military personnel qualification and establish related metrics.

Requires that the Commandant establish performance objectives and accompanying metrics of specified AI-related modernization activities.
 
Requires the Commandant to report to Congress within 180 days after completion of the required review.

name: Information Technology Modernization Centers of Excellence Program Act
summary:
Instructs the administrator of general services to establish the Information Technology Modernization Centers of Excellence Program.

Requires this program to assist executive agencies with planning and adoption of technology in Artificial Intelligence, cybersecurity and cloud computing.

Promotes modernization of information technology and consumer interactions with executive agencies.

Requires the program to improve cooperation of Information Technology sectors between executive agencies and the commercial sector.

name: Research and Development, Competition, and Innovation Act, Title IV, Section 10402 ("National engineering biology research and development initiative")
summary: Instructs the President, acting through the Office of Science and Technology Policy, to support the development of artificial intelligence tools aimed at facilitating research and innovation in the field of engineering biology. The AI tools would analyze omics data, which is data on genomics and the other fields that explore the functions of the various types of molecules that make up organisms' cells and systems.

name: IOGAN Act
summary:
Directs the Director of the National Science Foundation to support research on manipulated or synthesized content and information authenticity.

Directs the Director of the National Institute of Standards and Technology to support research for the development of measurements and standards on generative adversarial networks and other technologies that synthesize or manipulate content.

Requires the Directors to submit a report within a year to Congress of research findings and policy recommendations.

name: FLOODS Act, Section 14 ("National Weather Service hydrologic research fellowship program")
summary:
Outlines the criteria and expectations for a Fellow in the Hydrologic Research Fellowship Program with NOAA.

Explains that activities Fellows may engage in include applying AI and machine-learning capabilities to advance existing hydrologic modeling capabilities.

name: 21 CFR § 876.1520 ("Gastrointestinal lesion software detection system")
summary:
Requires devices that used advanced algorithms to help detect gastrointestinal lesions ("gastrointestinal lesion software detection systems") to undergo specified clinical and non-clinical performance tests and to demonstrate reliability and safety.

Requires gastrointestinal lesion software detection systems to be labeled with use instructions, warnings, and summaries of testing.

name: Energy Act of 2020, Title VI, Section 6006 ("Development of National Smart Manufacturing Plan")
summary:
Instructs the Secretary of Energy to develop a national plan for the development and deployment of "smart manufacturing" technologies, including relevant AI technologies. Defines representative functions of "smart manufacturing" technology including manufacturing simulation, energy efficiency modeling, digital prototyping, and networking.

Requires that the plan includes an assessment of previous actions of the Department, an establishment of performance standards, actions to increase cybersecurity, and a consideration of the impact on manufacturing jobs.

Requires that the plan be submitted within 3 years and revised every two years after initial submission.

name: FY2022 NDAA, Section 232 ("Pilot program on data repositories to facilitate the development of artificial intelligence capabilities for the Department of Defense")
summary:
Allows the Secretary of Defense to carry out a pilot program under which the Secretary establishes repositories of Department of Defense datasets relevant to AI development.

Requires data in the potential repositories to be accessible to appropriate public and private organizations for purposes of software and AI technology development for DoD procurement.

Requires repositories to include tools for correcting errors and gaps in data and evaluate model performance.

Requires the Secretary to report to Congress within 270 days after enactment whether the Secretary will, will not, or already has carried out the program.

name: Executive Order on the Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence (EO 14110)
summary:
Requires federal government to develop and apply standards to ensure the safety and security of AI systems and minimize their risks, including biological risks, cybersecurity risks, and deceptive content risks.

Orders the development of a National Security Memorandum that directs further actions on AI and security.

Directs federal government to support privacy-preserving research and technologies and develop guidance on the collection and usage of commercially available information by federal agencies.

Instructs federal government to prevent algorithmic discrimination by developing guidance and best practices in order to ensure fairness.

Calls for federal government to support the safe, responsible deployment of AI in healthcare, transportation, education, and communications networks.

Requires a report on AI's potential labor-market impacts and the identification of options for strengthening federal support for workers facing labor disruptions

Urges federal government to facilitate the immigration of AI talent to the U.S., catalyze AI research and innovation through a pilot of the National AI Research Resource, and promote competition in the AI ecosystem by providing resources to small businesses.

Directs federal government to maintain U.S. leadership in global AI efforts by expanding multilateral engagements, implementing international standards, and developing guidelines to secure critical infrastructure.

Calls for the advancement of federal government use of AI through the issuance of guidance for agency use of AI, support for agency acquisition of AI products/services, and authorization of rapid hiring of AI professionals.

name: AI Video Interview Discrimination Act
summary:
Requires employers that rely solely on AI to analyze video interviews to collect information on the race and ethnicity of candidates who are and are not consequently interviewed in person or hired and to report this information annually to the Illinois Department of Commerce and Economic Opportunity.

Requires the Department to analyze the data reported and report annually to the Governor and General Assembly on whether the data discloses a racial bias in using AI.

name: Artificial Intelligence, Automated Decision-Making and Personal Data Privacy Act
summary:
Requires the Department of Administrative Services to establish a public inventory of state agencies' existing use of AI systems; this inventory should include whether the system was employed to independently make or inform decisions, and whether it undergone an impact assessment before implementation

Requires the Office of Policy and Management to develop policies to govern state agencies' procurement and use of AI systems; this includes requiring state agencies to conduct impact assessments for these systems and to ensure systems do not unlawfully discriminate against individuals or groups

Bans state agencies from implementing any AI system unless it had performed an impact assessment to prevent unlawful discrimination, effective February 1 2024

Requires the Judicial Department to establish a public inventory of its systems that employ AI, including whether the AI system had undergone impact assessments and was used to make or support conclusions; also requires the department to introduce policies to govern the use of AI, and to prevent unlawful discrimination

Establishes a working group comprising industry representatives and academics to engage stakeholders and experts and make recommendations on the state government's use of AI; this includes recommendations on the adoption of a Connecticut artificial intelligence bill of rights based on the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy's 'Blueprint for an AI Bill of Rights'

name: California AB 302 (2023)
summary:
Requires the California Department of Technology, in coordination with other agencies, to analyze the benefits and risks of all high-risk automated decision systems that have been proposed for use, development, or procurement by, or are being used, developed, or procured by, state agencies. 

Requires the analysis to include a description of, among other things, the categories of data and personal information the automated decision system uses to make its decisions. 

Requires the Department of Technology to submit an annual report on the above-described comprehensive analysis to specified committees of the California Legislature.

name: Copyright Registration Guidance: Works Containing Material Generated by Artificial Intelligence
summary:
Clarifies that content generated by artificial intelligence without significant creative contribution from a human is ineligible for U.S. copyright protection.

Also clarifies that contributions made by a human to content that was created with the assistance of AI remain eligible for copyright protection.

Describes various situations in which content generated with the assistance of AI would, and would not, qualify for copyright protection. 

Instructs copyright applicants on how to apply for copyright protection for content generated with the assistance of AI.

name: North Dakota HB 1361 (2023)
summary: Clarifies that artificial intelligence cannot qualify as a "person" for the purpose of North Dakota state law.

name: Artificial Intelligence Video Interview Act
summary:
Requires employers who use AI to analyze video interviews of applicants in Illinois to notify and receive consent from the applicant before the interview and provide information explaining how the AI system works and what characteristics it uses to evaluate applicants.

Requires employers to refrain from sharing applicant videos except what’s necessary to evaluate the applicant and delete videos, including any copies shared with other actors, upon applicant request within 30 days.

name: FY2021 NDAA, Division A, Title II, Section 247 ("Pilot program on the use of electronic portfolios to evaluate certain applicants for technical positions")
summary:
Defines the term "technical position" as a Department of Defense position that (1) requires expertise in artificial intelligence, data science, or software development and (2) is eligible for direct hire authority under section 9905 of title 5, United States Code, or section 2358a of title 10, United States Code. 

Instructs the human resources manager of each Department of Defense participating organization to identify a subset of technical positions for which electronic portfolios should be evaluated during the hiring process.

Requires the Human Resources manager to evaluate applicants for such positions by reviewing their best electronic portfolios, as chosen by the applicant.

Directs the Secretary of Defense to submit a report to the congressional defense committee on the results of the program that describes how electronic portfolios affected the timeliness of technical position hiring, the level of satisfaction with new hires based on electronic portfolio evaluations, and recommends expanding the use of electronic portfolios in the hiring process or making it permanent.

name: FY2021 NDAA, Division A, Title XCIV, Section 9407 ("National cybersecurity challenges")
summary:
Directs the Secretary of Commerce to establish national cybersecurity challenges by 2028 through building more resilient cyber systems, increasing American digital literacy, and advancing efforts to develop emerging technologies.

Directs the Secretary of Commerce to coordinate with other agencies to address these challenges through competitions and soliciting funds from both government and non-government entities. 

Directs the Secretary of Commerce to designate an advisory council to seek further recommendations.

name: FY2021 NDAA, Division A, Title XCII, Section 9203 ("Spectrum information technology modernization efforts")
summary:
Use updated algorithms, data, AI tools, and algorithms to modernize infrastructure. Ways to improve infrastructure include efficiency, validation, accuracy, modeling, and monitoring. The directive aims to enhance covered agencies' capacity to meet mission requirements in congested Federal spectrum environments through the implementation of automated adjustments, the creation of a time-based mechanism for collaborative spectrum sharing among agencies, and fostering collaboration to ensure interoperability. 

Within 240 days of the enactment of this Act, the Assistant Secretary of Commerce for Communications and Information is required to submit to Congress a report outlining a plan for the National Telecommunications and Information Administration (NTIA) to modernize and automate its infrastructure for managing the use of Federal spectrum by covered agencies, with the goal of improving efficiency in spectrum management in ways such as a timeline for implementation, plans for security enhancement, data model improvement, and workflow automation. 

Within one year of the enactment of this Act, the head of each covered agency is required to submit a report to the Assistant Secretary of Commerce for Communications and Information and the Policy and Plans Steering Group outlining a plan to modernize the agency's infrastructure. Each submitted report must include an assessment of their current capabilities, a timeline for completion, management capabilities, agency requirements or restrictions, existing infrastructure, and a plan for safe integration of government data.

The Comptroller General of the United States is mandated to conduct a review of covered agencies' infrastructure within 180 days of the Act's enactment and subsequently oversee the implementation of modernization plans submitted by the Assistant Secretary and covered agencies, providing regular reports and briefings to relevant congressional committees until December 31, 2030. The term "covered agency" includes any Federal entity, as determined by the Assistant Secretary, encompassing the Department of Defense, and "infrastructure" is defined as information technology systems and related tools and databases.

name: FY2021 NDAA, Division A, Title II, Subtitle C ("Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology")
summary:
Instructs the Secretary of Defense to assign roles and responsibilities relating to the research, development, testing, procurement of, requirements for, and operational use of artificial intelligence technologies to appropriate officials within the Department of Defense.

Supports the incorporation of standards for artificial intelligence into the strategies and doctrine of the Department.

Stipulates the roles of the Director of the joint Artificial Intelligence center.

Encourages the systematic evaluation of AI systems.

Instructs the Secretary of Defense to establish a board of advisors for the Joint Artificial Intelligence Center with responsibilities like providing strategic advice and expertise to the Secretary and the Director on matters relating to the development and use of artificial intelligence.

Instructs the Secretary of Defense to identify a set of no fewer than five use cases of the application of existing artificial intelligence enabled systems to support improved management of enterprise acquisition, personnel, audit, or financial management functions.

Instructs the Secretary of Defense to conduct an assessment to determine how the Department can most effectively implement ethically and responsibly developed artificial intelligence.

Requires the secretary to pilot technology development and prototyping activities that leverage commercially available technologies and systems to demonstrate new artificial intelligence enabled capabilities to support the use cases.

Permits the secretary of Defense to establish a steering committee on emerging technology and national security threats, which committee shall develop a strategy for the organizational change, capability development, and technology investments in emerging technologies needed to maintain the technological superiority of the United States military.

name: FY2021 NDAA, Division A, Title II, Section 227 ("Limitation on contract awards for certain unmanned vessels")
summary:
Mandates that the Secretary of the Navy must submit a report of risk and performance to the congressional defense committees 30 days before the purchase of unmanned surface vessels or vehicles.

Mandates that the Secretary cannot integrate offensive weapons systems into unmanned surface vessels or vehicles until 30 days after certifying that the vessel will comply with legal and performance requirements.

Requires that the Secretary submit an analysis of alternatives related to the offensive military use of unmanned surface vessels or vehicles within a year of enactment.

name: FY2021 NDAA, Division A, Title VIII, Section 801 ("Report on acquisition risk assessment and mitigation as part of Adaptive Acquisition Framework implementation")
summary:
Requires each Department of Defense service acquisition executive to submit to the Secretary of Defense, the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment, the Under Secretary of Defense for Research and Engineering, and the Chief Information Officer a report on how they are assessing, mitigating, and reporting risks in acquisition programs.

Requires the reports described above to cover, among other risk categories, technical risks in engineering, software, manufacturing and testing; integration and interoperability risks posed by changes to Department systems created by artificial intelligence; and supply chain risks, including those related to cybersecurity and the defense industrial base's potential inability to produce technology and systems as needed.

Requires the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment to submit to the congressional defense committees a report on their own views, and the views of the service acquisition executives, with regard to the risk mitigation measures covered herein.

name: FY2021 NDAA, Division A, Title II, Section 248 ("Pilot program on self-directed training in advanced technologies")
summary:
Instructs the Secretary of Defense to execute a pilot program that offers online courses related to advanced technologies for civilian employees of the Department of Defense and members of the Armed Forces.

Requires the Secretary to develop procedures to document course completion, incentivize course completion, and evaluate course quality and effectiveness.

Requires the Secretary to carry out the program within a year after enactment, and decrees that the program terminate on October 1, 2024.

name: FY2021 NDAA, Division A, Title II, Section 249 ("Part-time and term employment of university faculty and students in the Defense science and technology enterprise")
summary:
Instructs the Secretary of Defense to establish a program to offer Defense science and technology employment opportunities to selected faculty and students of higher education institutions to carry out research projects. 

Specifies that no fewer than five positions must be given to faculty who conduct research in artificial intelligence and machine learning.

Requires the Secretary to carry out the program within 180 days of enactment and submit three annual reports of program results to Congress.

name: FY2021 NDAA, Division A, Title XXXV, Section 3521 ("Maritime security and domain awareness")
summary:
Instructs the Secretary of the Navy, in coordination with the Secretary of the department in which the Coast Guard is operating and with the Secretary of Commerce, to assess the available commercial solutions relating to illegal maritime activities.

Requires the assessment to build on the ongoing Coast Guard assessment related to autonomous vehicles, and to consider other appropriate commercially and available technological solutions.

Requires the Secretary of the Navy to submit the report to the specified congressional Committees.

name: FY2021 NDAA, Division A, Title I, Section 152 ("Transfer of responsibilities and functions relating to electromagnetic spectrum operations")
summary:
Instructs the Secretary of Defense to transfer all the responsibilities of the Commander of the US Strategic Command that are germane to electromagnetic spectrum operations (EMSO).

Instructs the Secretary to develop a transfer plan with consideration of all appropriate entities, while considering whether the receiving electromagnetic spectrum operations organization should have a unitary structure or hybrid structure.

Requires the Secretary to develop the transfer plan while considering the resources required by the receiving electromagnetic spectrum operations organization to fulfill the responsibilities and functions as well as the results of the evaluations carried out.

Requires an evaluation and assessment of the need for automated and machine learning- or artificial intelligence-assisted electronic warfare capabilities.

name: FY2021 NDAA, Division A, Title XCIV, Section 9414 ("Study on Chinese policies and influence in the development of international standards for emerging technologies")
summary:
Instructs the Director of the National Institute of Standards and Technology to work with an entity with relevant expertise to conduct a study on PRC policies and influence in the development of emerging technology international standards, and make recommendations on how the U.S. can mitigate PRC influence and bolster U.S. participation in international standards-setting bodies.

Identifies potential areas of study, including examining previous PRC practices in international standards setting organizations to predict future international standardization engagement in critical technologies like artificial intelligence and quantum information science. 

Requires the entity conducting the study to submit a report on its findings to the Committees on Science, Space, and Technology, on Foreign Affairs, on Commerce, Science, and Transportation, and on Foreign Relations.

name: FY2021 NDAA, Division A, Title II, Section 513 ("Grants to support STEM education in the Junior Reserve Officers’ Training Corps")
summary:
Instructs the Secretary and Secretary of Education to create and support grants to fund STEM education programs for students specifically in the Junior Reserve Corps. 
Instructs different departments of the government, such as the National Science foundation, as well as local governments to carry out programs that are supported by said grants.
Outlines what activities are allowed under the grants, and what specific area of studies and subjects that they would work under. 
Details subjects that are eligible for said grants, which include science, technology, engineering, mathematics, computer science, and more.
Allows for the Secretary of Defense to determine which additional subjects and areas of studies could be applicable to the grant.

name: FY2021 NDAA, Division A, Title XV, Section 6505 ("GAO studies on trafficking")
summary:
Instructs the Comptroller General of the United States to carry out a study in consultation with law enforcement, relevant federal agencies, private sector stakeholders (such as financial institutions, data and technology companies), to investigate major trafficking routes used by transnational criminal organizations and to what extent the trafficking routes are related.

Directs the study to include commonly used methods to launder and move the proceeds of trafficking; the types of suspicious financial activity that are associated with illicit trafficking networks, and how financial institutions identify and report such activity.

Directs the study to include steps financial institutions are taking to detect and prevent bad actors who are laundering the proceeds of illicit trafficking, including data analysis, policies, training procedures, rules, and guidance,

Necessitates the study to include the role those emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, digital identity technologies, distributed ledger technologies, virtual assets and online marketplaces can play in enabling the laundering of proceeds from trafficking. 

Requires the Comptroller General of the United States to submit a report to the congres, summarizing the results of the study and any recommendations for regulatory action.

name: FY2021 NDAA, Division A, Title LXII, Section 6211 ("Financial crimes tech symposium")
summary:
Requires the Secretary of the Treasury to periodically convene a global anti-money laundering and financial crime symposium -- attended by domestic and international financial regulators, senior executives from regulated firms, technology providers, representatives from law enforcement and national security agencies, and experts -- focused on how new technology can be used to more effectively combat financial crimes and other illicit activities.

Requires the Director of the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network -- a bureau of the Treasury Department -- to brief the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs of the Senate and the Committee on Financial Services of the House of Representatives on the current and potential future use of artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies in its work, along with policy recommendations for enhancing the efficacy of utilizing such technologies in combating financial crimes.

name: FY2021 NDAA, Division A, Title XC, Section 9004 ("Department of Homeland Security reports on digital content forgery technology")
summary:
Instructs the Secretary of the Department of Homeland Security to submit annually, for a period of 5 years, a report to Congress on the state of digital content forgery technology. 

Requires the report to include an assessment of the underlying technologies used to create or propagate digital content forgeries, including the evolution of such technologies and patterns of dissemination of such technologies. 

Requires the report to include a description of the types of digital content forgeries, including those used to commit fraud, cause harm, harass, coerce, or silence vulnerable groups or individuals, or violate civil rights.

Requires the report to include an assessment of how foreign governments, proxies and networks thereof, and non-governmental entities use, or could use, digital content forgeries to harm national security. 

Requires the report to include an assessment of the uses, applications, dangers, benefits, and impact on individuals of deep learning or digital content forgery technologies used to generate realistic depictions of events that did not occur. 

Requires the report to include a description of the methods and technological countermeasures that are, or could be, used to identify forgeries and address concerns with digital content forgery technology.

name: FY2021 NDAA, Division A, Title LVXXXIV, Section 8411 ("Unmanned maritime systems and satellite vessel tracking technologies")
summary:
Mandates that the Commandant, acting through the Blue Technology Center of Expertise, biennially assess unmanned maritime systems and satellite vessel tracking technologies for potential use to support the Coast Guard.

Requires that the Commandant submit a report to Congress on the actual and potential effects of such technologies on the mission effectiveness of the Coast Guard.

Requires that the report include an overview of current system and technology usage and a list of mission requirements that could be met with additional systems and technologies.

name: FY2021 NDAA, Division A, Title II, Section 218 ("Executive agent for autonomy")
summary:
Instructs the Secretary of the Navy to designate an existing Navy program executive officer as the acquisition executive agent for autonomy by February 1, 2022.

Requires that the acquisition executive agent for autonomy be responsible for the acquisition of autonomous technology, along with the officer's current executive duties.

name: FY2021 NDAA, Division A, Title VII, Section 808 ("Acquisition authority of the Director of the Joint Artificial Intelligence Center")
summary:
Instructs the Secretary of Defense to delegate acquisition authority to the Director of the Joint Artificial Intelligence Center, and outlines responsibilities of an acquisition executive in the execution, supervision, discussion, and coordination of relevant acquisition activities.

Allocates personnel and funding to support Center missions and the transition of artificial intelligence capabilities into appropriate acquisition programs or into operational use. 

Requires the Secretary of Defense to provide to congressional defense committees a demonstration of operational capability and an implementation plan that describes relevant acquisition activities, plans the oversight of an acquisition executive, and assesses the acquisition workforce, tools, and infrastructure needs of the Center.

name: FY2021 NDAA, Division A, Title XI, Section 1102 ("Enhancement of public-private talent exchange programs in the Department of Defense")
summary:
Requires the Secretary of Defense to use their authority for personnel exchanges with private sector entities focusing on Department of Defence modernization priorities.  Including exchanges in Research and Engineering, the Chief Information Officer, and each Armed Force under the jurisdiction of a military department.

Insructs the Secretary of Defense to develop a system to identify, mitigate, and manage public-private talent exchange conflicts of interest.

Requires the Secretary of Defense to brief the Senate and House Armed Services Committees on Public-Private Exchange programmes. This briefing should highlight seeking opportunities for exchanges with private sector entities working on Department of Defense modernization priorities, including Artificial Intelligence.

Requires such briefing to explain barriers preventing supervisors from nominating staff for and encouraging participation in public-private exchange programmes; ways to incentivize senior leaders for programme encouragement, and the Department's conflict of interest requirements.

name: FY2021 NDAA, Division A, Title XVI, Section 1601 ("Space Development Agency development requirements and transfer to Space Force")
summary:
Instructs the Director of the Space Development Agency of the Department of Defense to lead the development of a resilient military space-based sensing, tracking, and data transport architecture.

Instructs the Director to lead the integration of next-generation space capabilities, including novel sensors and autonomous battle features.

Instructs the Director to lead the procurement of relevant commercial capabilities and services, including low-Earth orbit or innovative capabilities. 

Instructs the Secretary of Defense to transfer the Space Development Agency from the Office of the Secretary of Defense to the Space Force by October 1, 2022.

name: FY2021 NDAA, Division A, Title II, Section 241 ("Measuring and incentivizing programming proficiency")
summary:
Authorizes resources for managing government support for AI-related education and proficiency

Instructs the Secretary of Defense to leverage existing civilian software development and architecture certification programmes to implement DOD coding language proficiency and AI competency tests.

Requires the Secretary of Defense to update record keeping systems to track artificial intelligence and programming certification testing results just like the foreign language competency system.

Instructs the secretary of Defense to share information with the heads of other intelligence agencies about the coding language proficiency and artificial intelligence competency tests and encourages them to implement tracking and reward systems. 

Requires the Secretary of Defense to implement a system of rewards for Department of Defense employees who perform successfully on specific language coding proficiency and artificial intelligence competency tests.

Advocates for special pay for a Department of Defense employee who is certified and proficient in a computer or digital programming language but may not exceed 20% of basic pay.

name: FY2021 NDAA, Division A, Title XVII, Section 1751 ("Guidance and direction on use of direct hiring processes for artificial intelligence professionals and other data science and software development personnel")
summary:
Instructs the Secretary of Defense to review existing guidance and create new guidance for secretaries of military departments and heads of defense on the direct hiring processes for AI professionals and other software and data science personnel.

Requires that the guidance instructs HR to utilize direct hiring authorities.

Instructs hiring authorities to use a panel of subject matter experts to review qualifications, authorizes the use of ePortfolio reviews, and encourages the use of referral bonuses for recruitment.

Instructs the Secretary of Defense to submit a report of the guidance issues to Congress within one year of the issuance of the guidance and highlights the requirements of the report.

name: FY2021 NDAA, Division A, Title V, Section 589F ("Study on cyberexploitation and online deception of members of the Armed Forces and their families")
summary:
Instructs the Secretary of Defense to assess threats posed by foreign actors with malicious intent that use machine learning techniques to generate or modify media featuring members of the Armed Forces and their families.

Instructs the Secretary to assess the maturity of the machine learning technology used and how the media could be used to conduct information warfare.

Instructs the Secretary to present policy recommendations to reduce individuals' vulnerability to cyberexploitation and deception.

name: FY2021 NDAA, Division A, Title I, Section 164 ("Acceleration of development and fielding of counter unmanned aircraft systems across the joint force")
summary:
Instructs the Executive Agent of the Joint Counter Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Office to develop a plan to develop and produce a counter unmanned aircraft system that can be deployed by 2021.

Requires that the selected systems use autonomous and semi-autonomous systems and
processes and meet current military and operational requirements.

Instructs the Executive Agent to ensure the developed plan will guide future programmatic and funding decisions for counter unmanned aircraft systems.

name: FY2024 NDAA, Section 7510 ("Requirement to ensure intelligence community directives appropriately account for artificial intelligence and machine learning tools in intelligence products")
summary:
Requires the Director of National Intelligence to brief the congressional appropriations and intelligence committees on whether intelligence community directives provide sufficient guidance on how to use, document, and disclose AI and machine learning tools in intelligence. 

Requires the Director to either (a) justify the assertion that existing intelligence community directives do sufficiently provide such guidance or (b) provide a plan and timeline for updating the directives as necessary.

name: FY2024 NDAA, Section 7513 ("Policies established by Director of National Intelligence for artificial intelligence capabilities")
summary:
Instructs the Director of National Intelligence, in consultation with the Director of the Office of Management and Budget and other intelligence officials to maintain, develop, and annually revise various AI policies.

Requires the establishment of a lexicon relating to machine learning and AI use by the intelligence community.

Requires the establishment of guidelines for evaluating model performance by specifying conditions for AI capability monitoring, documenting performance objectives, specifying model auditing processes, and specifying conditions for vulnerability testing and privacy evaluations.

Requires the establishment of guidelines for tracking dependencies in related systems, documentation requirements for capabilities procured from third-party and training data usage, and guidance on the usage of third-party-trained models.

name: FY2024 NDAA, Section 856 ("Pilot program to analyze and monitor certain supply chains")
summary:
Directs the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment to establish a pilot program enhancing the analysis, mapping, and monitoring of supply chains for covered weapons platforms using artificial intelligence and machine learning tools.

Requires the Under Secretary to submit an annual report (until 2028) that specifies the vulnerabilities of the supply chains and the efficiencies achieved through using the new tools.

name: FY2024 NDAA, Section 811 ("Modernizing the Department of Defense requirements process")
summary:
Requires the Secretary of Defense in coordination with military leaders to develop streamlined requirements of development processes for the Department of Defense, in order to modernize war fighting technology and reduce the time needed to deliver capabilities to warfighters.

Requires revisions to requirements management practices that maximizes the use of commercial products or services and allow for a broader range of new or alternative technological opportunities to be incorporated without the requirement being validated again.

Establishes a process to rapidly validate the ability of commercial products and services to meet capability needs or opportunities.

Requires retiring and replacing the Department of Defense Architecture Framework with a new structure focused on enabling interoperability  through application program interfaces, enterprise architectures and platforms, and government and commercial standards.

Requires the secretary to develop a formal career path, training, and structure for requirements managers.

Establishes the required processes for software, artificial intelligence, data, and related capability areas to be more rapid and iterative than the requirements processes for traditional hardware systems.

Requires the Vice Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff to collaborate with industry partners, contractors, and Department of Defense science and technology reinvention laboratories in designing the new requirements development process.

Requires the Secretary of Defense to submit to the congressional defense committees an interim report and a final report on the development and implementation of the new requirements development process.

name: FY2024 NDAA, Section 1507 ("Review and plan relating to cyber red teams of Department of Defense")
summary:
Requires officials from the Department of Defense -- namely the Principal Cyber Advisor to the Secretary of Defense, the Chief Information Officer of the Department of Defense, the Director of Operational Test and Evaluation, and the Commander of the United States Cyber Command -- to assess the status of the implementation of recommendations made by the Secretary of Defense to enhance the capabilities of the Department of Defense's cyber red teams.

Requires the same officials listed above to submit to Congress a plan for ensuring that the Department's cyber red teams possess the capabilities necessary to execute their duties, including with respect to threats stemming from artificial intelligence systems abroad.

Requires the Director of Operational Test and Evaluation to evaluate annually, from 2025 through 2031, the status of the implementation of the plan described in the paragraph above.

name: FY2024 NDAA, Section 7507 ("Programs for next-generation microelectronics in support of artificial intelligence")
summary:
Requires the Director of National Intelligence, acting through the Director of the Intelligence Advanced Research Projects Activity, to establish or oversee a program to advance microelectronics research. 

Requires the program described above to focus on applications in artificial intelligence, advanced computing, advanced computing materials, optical communication networks, quantum technologies, or other emerging technologies. 

Requires the Director of National Intelligence to consider a variety of factors when crafting the research program, including input from the Secretary of Commerce and from an array of stakeholders including representatives of industry and academia.

Requires the Director of the Intelligence Advanced Research Projects Activity to brief the congressional intelligence, appropriations, and commerce committees on the progress of the research program described above and recommendations for future research priorities.

name: FY2024 NDAA, Section 224 ("Next Generation Air Dominance family of systems development program accountability matrices")
summary:
Submit goals for Next Generation Air Dominance and Collaborative Combat Aircraft programs to congressional defense committees and the Comptroller General concurrent with the President's budget submission. Include key milestones, testing events, and performance goals, subdivided into six-month increments. 

Provide information on technology readiness levels, design maturity, software maturity, integration maturity, manufacturing readiness levels, reliability, availability for flight operations, and maintainability.

Provide updates on progress and cost estimates for the program every 6 months. It details progress made toward the goals identified in the matrices and provides updated cost estimates for air vehicles, propulsion, mission systems, software, program management, system test and evaluation, support and training systems, and more.

Develop key performance parameters (cost KPPs) for cost thresholds and objectives for the programs. Specify threshold and objective values for categories such as unit recurring flyaway cost, average procurement unit cost, gross/weapon system unit cost, aircraft cost-per-tail-per-year, and aircraft cost-per-flight-hour. 

Ensure that each Secretary concerned works on these parameters for the respective programs and includes them in the related documents.

Ensure assessment of the sufficiency of matrices by the Comptroller General, who will review them and submit assessments to congressional defense committees, identifying any cost, schedule, or performance trends.

name: FY2024 NDAA, Section 1090 ("Conduct of weather reconnaissance in the United States")
summary:
Requires the Secretary of Commerce to submit to the congressional science committees a report on the resources necessary for the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration to invest in emerging technologies that improve weather forecasting.

Permits the 53rd Weather Reconnaissance Squadron of the Air Force Reserve Command and the Administrator of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration to use aircraft, personnel, and equipment necessary to improve the accuracy and efficacy of weather monitoring and water management, including through advanced technological methods.

Instructs the Squadron to use autonomous platform observations to improve water management decision-making and flood forecasting, if it uses the resources named in the above paragraph.

Requires the Secretary of the Air Force to submit to the appropriate congressional committees a report on the resources used and required by the Air Force and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration to improve weather monitoring and water management.

name: FY2024 NDAA, Section 251 ("Congressional notification of changes to Department of Defense policy on autonomy in weapon systems")
summary: Requires the Secretary of Defense to brief the congressional defense committees on the nature and purpose of any modifications to Department of Defense Directive 300.09, which relates to autonomy in weapons systems, within 30 days of making the modifications.

name: FY2024 NDAA, Section 1682 ("Electromagnetic Warfare")
summary: Requires leaders of the Army, Navy, Air Force, Marine Corps, and Space Operations to evaluate their ability to conduct electromagnetic spectrum operations. The evaluation should include the need for AI-assisted operations.

name: FY2024 NDAA, Section 903 ("Establishment of Office of Strategic Capital")
summary:
Creates a new Office of Strategic Capital in the Department of Defense.

Directs the new Office to invest in companies developing critical technologies, including autonomous robots, that may benefit the Department of Defense. 

Permits the Office to launch a pilot program for providing capital assistance that supports the defense industrial base. 

Requires the Office's investments to meet certain criteria, including restrictions on interest rates and loan repayment periods as well as requirements for non-Federal investments in selected companies, subject to various exceptions. 

Requires the Secretary of Defense to submit to the congressional defense committees an annual report on the Office's activities, in addition to notifying the congressional defense committees whenever it provides capital assistance.

name: FY2024 NDAA, Section 253 ("Annual review of status of implementation plan for digital engineering career tracks")
summary:
Requires the Secretary of Defense to conduct annually, through 2029, an internal review of the Department of Defense's plan for the digital engineer career track. The review shall include consideration of how the rapid rate of technological change in data science and machine learning may affect the implementation of the plan.

Requires the Secretary to submit annually, through 2029, a report to the congressional defense committees on the findings of that internal review. The report shall include the Secretary's plan for addressing the digital engineer personnel needs of the Department.

name: FY2024 NDAA, Section 7511 ("Expanded annual assessment of economic and technological capabilities of the People's Republic of China and related briefing")
summary:
Instructs the Director of National Intelligence to provide a briefing to the congressional intelligence committees on the status and implementation of working groups on the People's Republic of China's activities regarding certain technologies, including artificial intelligence. 

Instructs working groups to assess the investments made by the People's Republic of China in AI, the competitive practices of the People's Republic of China relating to AI, opportunities to counter those practices, and US vulnerabilities in the supply chain of AI.

name: FY2024 NDAA, Section 7356 ("Analysis of commercial cloud initiatives of intelligence community")
summary:
Requires the Director of National Intelligence to produce a comprehensive analysis of the intelligence community's cloud initiatives relating to the Commercial Cloud Enterprise contract entered into by the Director of the Central Intelligence Agency in November of 2020. 

Requires the above analysis to include projected cloud computing costs, plans for the termination of legacy data storage mechanisms, an assessment of the value and efficacy of cloud computing tools and analytics, and the suitability of existing computing arrangements to service artificial intelligence systems for the intelligence community. 

Requires the Director of National Intelligence to brief the congressional intelligence and appropriations committees on the findings of the analysis detailed above.

name: FY2024 NDAA, Section 350 ("Strategy and assessment on use of automation and artificial intelligence for shipyard optimization")
summary:
Requires the Secretary of the Navy, in coordination with the Shipyard Infrastructure Optimization Program of the Department of the Navy, to develop a strategy for using artificial intelligence to better predict maintenance needs at U.S. Navy shipyards.

Requires the Secretary of the Navy to evaluate the potential cost savings of adopting artificial intelligence predictive maintenance technologies.

Requires the Secretary of the Navy to brief congressional defense committees on the strategy and evaluation described above.

name: FY2024 NDAA, Section 1521 ("Control and management of Department of Defense data; establishment of Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer Governing Council")
summary:
Grants the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer of the Department of Defense the authority to access and control data on behalf of the Secretary of Defense.

Requires the Secretary to establish the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer Governing Council, which will provide policy oversight to ensure the responsible, coordinated, and ethical deployment of AI across Department of Defense missions and operations.

Requires the Council to submit a report on its activities in the past period to the Secretary and Congress at least once every 18 months.

name: FY2024 NDAA, Section 112 ("Strategy for Army tactical wheeled vehicle program")
summary:
Requires the Secretary of the Army to submit to Congress a report on the strategy of the Army for tactical wheeled vehicles, including autonomous vehicles. The report shall be submitted with the budget justification materials submitted in support of the budget of the Department of Defense for each of FY 2025, 2030, and 2035.

Requires the report to include a description of the force structure and funding necessary for the tactical wheeled vehicle program to support the U.S.'s national security strategy, along with detailed rundown of a program for the construction of tactical wheeled vehicles and the estimated cost of such a program. 

Requires the Secretary of the Army to, within 15 days of the budget materials submission described above, brief the congressional defense committees on the investment needed for each platform of tactical wheeled vehicle.

name: FY2024 NDAA, Section 6303 ("Establishment of the Chief Artificial Intelligence Officer of the Department of State")
summary:
Creates the Chief Artificial Intelligence Officer position, who will be responsible for (a) the evaluation and facilitation of responsible AI and machine learning usage and (b) advising the Secretary of State on ethical AI and analytics usage in diplomacy.

Instructs the Chief Artificial Intelligence Officer to partner with the Chief Information Officer on scaling AI use cases.

name: FY2024 NDAA, Title XV, Subtitle E ("Artificial Intelligence")
summary:
Updates and extends the DoD's AI and ML acquisition framework and requires a plan for acquisition authority delegation and a demonstration of acquisition authority capabilities.

Mandates the creation of a bug bounty program for foundational AI models within the DoD, promoting collaboration with federal entities and cybersecurity experts. Requires briefing the congressional defense committees on the program within one year.

Instructs the Secretary of Defense to establish a competition to advance technologies for detecting and watermarking generative AI content. Requires annual briefing to the congressional defense committees.
