Directs the Secretary of Defense to issue DoD-wide guidance and policy on AI, including with regard to ethical AI use, bias mitigation, cybersecurity, technical workforce assessments, AI literacy needs and related training programs, protection against adversarial AI, protecting the intellectual property of DoD AI system suppliers, AI's potential role in developing offensive actions, availability of inputs for AI, verification and evaluation frameworks, potential vulnerabilities of AI models and human oversight of autonomous systems. Requires briefing the congressional defense committees within 150 days.

Requires a study on the vulnerabilities of AI-enabled military applications, focusing on explainability, security risks, and the integration of decision support systems, with a final report for the congressional defense committees detailing findings and research gaps.

name: FY2024 NDAA, Title XIII, Subtitle B ("Other Matters Relating to Foreign Nations: Matters Relating to the AUKUS Partnership")
summary:
Requires the Secretary of State, in consultation with the Secretary of Defense and other agency heads, to submit to Congress a biennial report on the AUKUS partnership, including an assessment of efforts to enhance AUKUS collaboration on artificial intelligence.

Requires the Secretary of State, in consultation with the Secretary of Defense, to create an expedited technology transfer approval process for transferring artificial intelligence systems and other defense technologies to AUKUS partners.

name: FY2024 NDAA, Title XV, Subtitle C ("Cyberspace-Related Matters: Information Technology and Data Management")
summary:
Instructs the Secretary of Defense to establish the 'Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer Governing Council' to oversee policy ensuring responsible and ethical use of data and AI in Department of Defense missions.

Requires  The council, led by the Chief Digital and AI Officer, to develop, implement, and oversee AI, coordinating governance, and providing ethical guidance. 

Instructs the council to identify, monitor, and update recommendations for AI use, review program funding,  and ensure compliance with AI policies. 

Instructs the council to issue guidance on access and distribution restrictions relating to data, models, tool sets, testing or validation infrastructure.

Instructs the council to implement and oversee an educational program on data and artificial intelligence, to familiarize personnel department on the applications of artificial intelligence.

Mandates all data collection, use, or retention measures  to comply with relevant laws and regulations, including those concerning data related to US persons.

Requires an establishment of a course of education at the Defense Information School, the purpose of which shall be to provide instruction on the practical concepts and skills.

Instructs the Director of the Defense Media Activity to carry out a pilot program to assess the feasibility and advisability of implementing industry open technical standards for digital content provenance for official photographs and videos of the Department of Defense

name: FY2024 NDAA, Section 346 ("Pilot program on optimization of aerial refueling and fuel management in contested logistics environments through use of artificial intelligence")
summary:
Mandates the Department of Defense and the Air Force to work together in launching a pilot program that optimizes aerial refueling and fuel management using artificial intelligence and advanced digital technologies.

Directs the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer to (a) coordinate with the Commander of the United States Transportation Command and the Commander of the United States Indo-Pacific Command to align the pilot program with existing operational requirements and (b) consult relevant experts in AI.

Requires the pilot program to assess the feasibility and effectiveness of artificial intelligence-driven approaches and evaluate the interoperability and compatibility of artificial intelligence-enabled systems with the existing logistics infrastructure of the Department of Defense.

Requires an assessment of potential challenges and risks associated with the integration of artificial intelligence and other advanced digital technologies, including those related to cybersecurity.

Requires the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer to submit a report on the pilot program's design, progress, and results to the Committees on Armed Services of the House of Representatives and the Senate within one year.

name: Virginia HB 2154 ("Patient Access to Intelligent Personal Assistant")
summary:
Requires hospitals, nursing homes, and certified nursing facilities to establish and implement policies for patient access to intelligent personal assistants while receiving inpatient services.

Ensures policies protect health information in accordance with the federal Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA).

Defines "intelligent personal assistant" as a combination of an electronic device and specialized software application that assists users with tasks using natural language processing and artificial intelligence.

Mandates that these facilities allow the use of intelligent personal assistants for patients, ensuring compliance with privacy and security standards.

Includes intelligent personal assistants like "digital assistants" or "virtual assistants" in the definition provided.

name: Illinois HB 3563 ("GenAI Task Force")
summary:
Amends the Department of Innovation and Technology Act to establish the Generative AI and Natural Language Processing Task Force.

Requires the Task Force to investigate and report on generative AI and natural language processing software.

Comprises the Task Force of appointed members from various government, educational, and expert backgrounds.

Mandates the Task Force to hold at least five public meetings across different regions of Illinois.

Tasks the Task Force with recommending legislation for consumer information protection, model policies for schools, and assessing AI's impact on public services, civil rights, employment, and cybersecurity.

Obligates the Department to provide administrative and technical support to the Task Force.

Requires the Task Force to file a comprehensive report by December 31, 2024, with the Governor and the General Assembly.

name: Alabama SB 78 ("Council on Advanced Technology")
summary:
Establishes the Alabama Council on Advanced Technology and Artificial Intelligence.

Requires the council to review and advise the Governor and Legislature on the use and development of advanced technology and artificial intelligence.

Composes the council of 22 members, including appointees from the Governor, Lieutenant Governor, Speaker of the House, and Senate President Pro Tempore, and ex officio members from commerce and information technology departments.

Mandates that non-legislative appointees have expertise in AI, technology, ethics, privacy, workforce development, or computer science.

Stipulates that the council meets at least twice a year and allows virtual participation.

Obliges the council to submit an annual report with recommendations on AI and advanced technology to the Governor and Legislature.

Enforces diversity in appointments regarding gender, race, and geography.

Prohibits salary for non-legislative members but allows expense reimbursement; provides legislative members with regular compensation for meeting attendance.

Sets the act’s effective date to one year post-approval.

name: New Jersey S 2723 ("Integrated Digital Experience Act")
summary:
Requires each state agency to develop and submit an information technology modernization and improvement plan to the Chief Technology Officer within one year of request.

Mandates the plan to include strategies for improving digital services using data analytics, cloud computing, electronic forms, and digitized workflows, ensuring mobile-friendly and accessible websites.

Authorizes the Chief Technology Officer to review these plans in collaboration with the Chief Innovation Officer.

Mandates the Chief Technology Officer to annually evaluate the feasibility of using AI, machine learning, and cloud services for public services, and to develop data analytics capabilities for policy development.

Requires the development of metrics to assess each agency's implementation of a modern digital experience, updated at least every two years and reevaluated every three years.

name: Arkansas SB 656 ("Data-Driven Decision-Making Task Force")
summary:
Creates the Data-Sharing and Data-Driven Decision-Making Task Force, comprised of twelve members appointed from the Senate and House of Representatives.

Mandates the task force to study and recommend the implementation of a statewide data-sharing system across state agencies.

Requires the task force to evaluate current data management inefficiencies, and propose necessary legislation and funding mechanisms for system implementation. Empowers the task force to hire external consultants if necessary.

Requires the task force to meet at least monthly and report findings to the Governor and legislative leaders by December 31, 2019; expires the task force on January 1, 2020.

name: FY2023 NDAA, Section 6731 ("Report on establishment of technology acquisition cadre")
summary:
Mandates the Director of National Intelligence to submit a feasibility report on establishing a cadre of experts in emerging technologies.

Requires such cadre to accelerate the adoption of emerging technologies.

Requires such cadre to assist with software development and develop training requirements for acquisition professionals.

Requires an assessment of whether the establishment of the cadre would necessitate additional statutory authorities or resources, including to recruit, hire, and retain the talent and expertise needed to establish the cadre; and the benefits, risks, and costs of establishing a cadre.

Addresses the acquisition of a plan for implementation of the cadre, including the proposed size of the cadre, its management, and organization.

name: FY2023 NDAA, Section 916 ("Strategic management dashboard demonstration")
summary:
Requires the Secretary of Defense to demonstrate a strategic management dashboard within one year of the Act's enactment. This dashboard will automate data collection and data visualization of the Department of Defense's primary management goals, enabling real-time monitoring of DoD's performance in achieving its management goals.

It will use artificial intelligence and machine learning tools to improve data analytic capabilities and decision making. The development of the dashboard will leverage commercial best practices and leading research in management and data science.

name: FY2023 NDAA, Section 212 ("Clarification of role of senior official with principal responsibility for artificial intelligence and machine learning")
summary: Makes various technical amendments largely pertaining to modification of titles of senior officials with duties relevant to artificial intelligence.

name: FY2023 NDAA, Section 557 ("Study and report on professional military education")
summary: Mandates the Secretary of Defense to conduct a thorough evaluation of the curricula at Professional Military Education (PME) institutions, specifically demanding an assessment of how these curricula align with innovative technological and strategic areas, including AI. Requires report to Congress by Dec 2025.

name: FY2023 NDAA, Section 911 ("Updates to management reform framework")
summary: Updates the DoD Management Reform Framework that mandates the Secretary of Defense to introduce reforms within DoD that enhance its efficiency and efficacy. Adds AI tools for management decision-making as one of eight elements of reform.

name: FY2023 NDAA, Section 861 ("Strategy for increasing competitive opportunities for certain critical technologies")
summary: Requires the Secretary of Defense to submit a strategy to increase competitive opportunities for U.S. companies in transitioning critical technologies into major weapon systems and defense programs. AI and machine learning are mentioned as one of the 13 critical technologies and several other technologies mentioned may relate to AI.

name: FY2023 NDAA, Section 835 ("Curricula on software acquisitions and cybersecurity software or hardware acquisitions for covered individuals")
summary:
Requires the Defense Acquisition University President to enhance curricula on software, cybersecurity, and hardware acquisition with information on various digital technologies, including AI and machine learning.

Requires the Secretary of Defense and the Defense Acquisition University President to submit a plan for the implementation of the new curricula within 180 days. The new curricula must be offered within one year of the submission.

Requires said roles to submit a cost-benefit assessment to Congress one year after the first report.

name: FY2023 NDAA, Section 6513 ("Lead intelligence community coordinator for countering and neutralizing proliferation of Iran-origin unmanned aircraft systems")
summary:
Instructs the Director of National Intelligence to designate an official from the intelligence community to serve as the lead coordinator for countering and neutralizing the proliferation of Iran-origin unmanned aircraft systems.

Requires this Coordinator to develop a comprehensive plan of action, driven by intelligence information, for countering and neutralizing the threats posed by the proliferation of Iran-origin unmanned aircraft systems and submit a briefing of such plans to the Congress.

Requires the Director of National Intelligence to submit a final report on the activities and findings of the Coordinator to the appropriate committees of Congress.

Mandates the report to include an assessment of the threats posed by Iran-origin unmanned aircraft systems and a detailed description of intelligence sharing efforts, as well as other joint efforts driven by intelligence information, with allies and partners of the United States, to assist in countering and neutralizing such threats. 

Mandates the report to include recommendations for any changes in United States policy designed to improve the capacity of the intelligence community to assist in countering such threats.

Encourages collaboration and the expansion of existing cooperative efforts among members of the Five Eyes Partnership and Israel for the purpose of countering Iran-origin unmanned aircraft systems.

name: Advancing American Artificial Intelligence Act
summary:
Encourages AI-related programs and initiatives to enhance the competitiveness of the US based on innovation and entrepreneurialism. 

Promotes modernized business practices and advanced technologies aligned with US values, including protection of privacy, civil rights and civil liberties across the Federal Government.

Defines the term "artificial intelligence system".

Instructs the Secretary of Homeland Security, Chief Procurement Officer, Chief Information Officer, Chief Privacy Officer, and the Officer for Civil Rights and Civil Liberties of the Department to work together on policies for acquiring AI and considering the risks of AI.

Instructs the Inspector General to identify training and investments to enable the employees of the Office of the Inspector General to advance their understanding of AI and its usage.

Instructs Director of the Office of Management and Budget to develop guidance for policies for AI use in government, with inputs from both government agencies and non-governmental actors. 

Requests the Director of the Office of Management and Budget to brief congressional committees on the activities carried out under this Act.

name: FY2023 NDAA, Section 862 ("Key advanced system development industry days")
summary:
Requires each Secretary of a military department to hold an event every 180 days designed to collaborate with the private sector on, and raise awareness of, innovation in autonomous systems with military applications. 

For each such event, requires the Service Chief concerned to identify military requirements, capability gaps, and opportunities for experimentation or exercises related to the autonomous systems covered at the event. 

For each such event, requires the service acquisition executive of the involved military department to identify acquisition strategies and potential acquisition funding mechanisms for the autonomous systems covered at the event.

Requires Department of Defense officials to draft reviews of each such event, analyze the reviews to identify trends and key takeaways, and distribute the reviews within the Department.

name: FY2023 NDAA, Section 11225 ("Establishment of unmanned system program and autonomous control and computer vision technology project")
summary:
Requires the U.S. Coast Guard to establish a program for using unmanned vehicles -- designed to operate in the air, on the water, and/or below the water's surface --  to improve mission execution. 

Requires the Commandant of the Coast Guard to conduct a project that retrofits at least two small boats with the sensors, communication systems, computer vision systems, and autonomous control technology necessary to conduct unmanned search and rescue, surveillance, and interdiction missions. Requires the Commandant to collect and analyze operational data from this project to inform future requirements. 

Requires the Commandant to submit a project briefing including analysis of operational data and projected costs to the congressional transportation committees.

Requires the Commandant to submit to the congressional transportation committees a detailed description of the Coast Guard's strategy for integrating unmanned systems across mission areas, including an estimate of the resources needed to achieve such integration.

name: FY2023 NDAA, Section 11504 ("At-sea recovery operations pilot program")
summary:
Requires the Secretary of the Department of Homeland Security to conduct a pilot program to assess the potential for the autonomous, or remotely controlled, operation and monitoring of certain Coast Guard vessels.

Requires the pilot program described above to assess the complexities and risks of autonomous or remotely controlled vessel operation, gather data on the practice, and assess the regulatory environment necessary to facilitate the practice going forward. 

Permits the pilot program to include operations relating to the launch and recovery of unmanned spaceflight vessels and components.

Permits the Secretary to modify or waive applicable regulations or guidance that would otherwise interfere with the pilot program.

Requires the Secretary to provide the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation of the Senate and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure and the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology of the House of Representatives with a quarterly briefing on the pilot program.

Requires the Secretary to submit to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and 
Transportation of the Senate and the Committee on Transportation and 
Infrastructure and the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology of 
the House of Representatives a final report assessing the execution of the pilot program and its implications for preserving safety and environmental quality. 

Requires the Comptroller General of the United States to consult with stakeholders and then submit to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation of the Senate and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure of the House of Representatives a report on the commercial availability, barriers to use, safety and security risks, use abroad, and impact on labor of autonomous and remote technologies used in the operation of shipboard equipment.

name: FY2023 NDAA, Section 1535 ("Department of Defense Cyber and Digital Service Academy")
summary:
Requires the Secretary of Defense to establish a new program that provides financial support to individuals studying digital technology-related areas critical to the Department of Defense, including AI. The program shall be called "Department of Defense Cyber and Digital Service Academy" and have a board of directors consisting of representatives from federal departments and agencies.

Eligible individuals need to be enrolled in a relevant program at an institution of higher education and commit to work for the Department of Defense in an area relevant to the program for a duration equivalent to the duration of the scholarship.

Requires a report to Congress on the success of the program every two years.

name: FY2023 NDAA, Section 10305 ("Modifications to the ocean exploration program of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration")
summary:
Instructs the Administrator of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration to promote the development and use of emerging technologies (e.g., sensors and autonomous vehicles) for research, communication, navigation, and data collection in marine science as part of the Administration's national ocean exploration program. 

Otherwise adjusts the precise parameters of the national ocean exploration program, including with regard to data collection and data sharing practices.

name: FY2023 NDAA, Section 9218 ("Report on changes to the Foreign Service Officer Test")
summary:
Requires the Secretary of State to submit to the appropriate congressional committees a report that describes and justifies any changes made during FY 2022 and 2023 to the Foreign Service entry process.

Includes the use of artificial intelligence, including deep textual analysis, and its impact on recruitment in the scope of the report.

name: FY2023 NDAA, Section 6504 ("Annual report on concentrated reeducation camps in the Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region of the People's Republic of China")
summary:
Requires the Director of National Intelligence to create an annual report to Congress for five years that includes a list of Chinese AI businesses that are involved with or are supporting concentrated reeducation camps in the Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region of China.

Directs the Director of National Intelligence to work in consultation with the heads of elements of the intelligence community to create the list of Chinese AI businesses for the report.

name: FY2023 NDAA, Section 1092 ("National Commission on the Future of the Navy")
summary:
Establishes an independent Commission on the Future of the Navy within the legislative branch, whose duties include studying opportunities to incorporate advanced technologies, including artificial intelligence, in the fleet.

Requires the Commission to consider specific changes to the Navy's Shipyard Infrastructure Optimization Program and ship depot maintenance program, in order to expand the use of advanced technologies in shipyard infrastructure and ship operations.

Requires the Commission to submit to the congressional armed services committees an unclassified report on the findings of its study.

name: FY2023 NDAA, Section 6717 ("Policy on required user adoption metrics in certain contracts for artificial intelligence and emerging technology software products")
summary:
Authorizes government support for AI-related activities

Instructs the Director of National Intelligence to establish a policy regarding user adoption metrics for contracts and other agreements for the procurement AI and emerging technology software products.

Requires an evaluation of AI systems, or of broader systems or processes that involve AI.

Requires each contract or agreement to include an understanding of the anticipated use of the covered AI or emerging technology product with a clear metric for success, for collecting user adoption metrics and for assessing the adoption of the covered product by such users.

Requires that prior to the procurement of, or the continuation of the use of, any AI and emerging technology product procured by the head of an element of the intelligence community, the head must determine a method for assessing the success of the covered product from user adoption metrics.

name: FY2023 NDAA, Section 6742 ("Code-free artificial intelligence enablement tools policy")
summary:
Instructs the heads of the elements of the intelligence community to draft a policy to promote the intelligence community-wide use of code-free artificial intelligence enablement tools.

Requires the given policy to include the objectives and a set of incentives for using code-free artificial intelligence enablement tools.

Instructs the intelligence community to devise a plan to ensure coordination and consideration in designating an official of each element of the intelligence community to oversee implementation of the policy.

Requires an assessment of the personnel and funding requirements, and any other resource requirements, that would be necessary to implement the draft policy in the given timeline.

name: FY2023 NDAA, Section 9506 ("Cybersecurity recruitment and retention")
summary:
Requires the Secretary of State to establish positions within the Bureau of Global Talent Management that are solely dedicated to the recruitment and retention of Department personnel with backgrounds in cybersecurity, engineering, data science, application development, artificial intelligence, critical and emerging technology, and technology and digital policy.

Requires the Secretary to submit a plan to the appropriate congressional committees that describes how the initiative described above will be implemented. 

Authorizes the appropriation of $750,000 for each of the fiscal years 2023 through 2027 to carry out this initiative.

Requires the Secretary to submit to the appropriate congressional committees an annual report, for a period of 5 years, on the implementation of the initiative, including the hiring authorities used to implement it, the number of employees hired through it, and recommendations to enhance the efficacy of the initiative.

Requires the Secretary to include computer programming languages within the Recruitment Language Program and provide appropriate language incentive pay.

Requires the Secretary to provide a list to the appropriate 
congressional committees that identifies (a) the computer programming languages included within the Recruitment Language Program and the language incentive pay 
rate and (b) the number of individuals benefitting from the inclusion of such computer programming languages in the Recruitment Language Program and language incentive pay.

name: FY2023 NDAA, Section 6718 ("Certification relating to information technology and software systems")
summary:
Mandates compatibility of information technology or software systems with new and emerging technologies, such as artificial intelligence.

Incentivizes adoption and integration of new technologies and decommissioning outdated systems, including potential funding enhancements.

Holds intelligence community personnel accountable for integrating new technologies, supported by training programs and evaluations.

name: FY2023 NDAA, Section 6505 ("Assessments of production of semiconductors by the People's Republic of China")
summary:
Begins discussing the phrase “appropriate committees of Congress” and what organizations are actually a part of this phrase when benign referred. Also defines the term “legacy semiconductor” in terms of the definition given in another legislation document.

Annually for 3 years after this act is passed, the Director of National Intelligence must submit an unclassified assessment report regarding China’s production of semiconductors through China’s firms and business sectors to the appropriate committees of Congress.

The Director of National Intelligence must meet with the heads of federal agencies to discuss the elements of the assessment. They must discuss the self-sufficiency of China in the fields of artificial intelligence, cloud computing, autonomous vehicles, and other newer-technological areas. They must discuss China’s access to intellectual property related to leading edge process nodes, including electronic design automation technology. They must discuss Chinese firms’s production of semiconductors that are not legacy conductors and stockpiling efforts of semiconductor manufacturing equipment. They must discuss the relative market share and its trends of Chinese semiconductor manufacturers at different process nodes. They must discuss the outside recruitment activity into Chinese semiconductors firms and the capability of the Chinese workforce in developing semiconductors that are not legacy semiconductors and relevant equipment.

name: FY2023 NDAA, Section 6702 ("Additional responsibilities of Director of National Intelligence for artificial intelligence policies, standards, and guidance for the intelligence community")
summary:
Creates a new institution to govern, investigate, advise, produce, or otherwise act in relation to AI.

Requires the Director of National Intelligence and intelligence heads, to review and establish AI-related policies, aiming to boost AI adoption in the intelligence community.

Requires the heads of the elements of the Intelligence Community to ensure established or updated policies are consistent with the principles outlined in the guidance of the Office of the Director of National Intelligence.

Avails budget guidance to the heads of the intelligence community for developing the National Intelligence Program budget to facilitate the acquisition, development, use, and maintenance of element-specific artificial intelligence capabilities.

Instructs each lead and the Director of National Intelligence to identify a senior official within the element to serve as the designated element lead responsible for coordinating AI efforts.

Addresses government support for AI-related development activities.

name: FY2023 NDAA, Section 6721 ("Reports on integration of artificial intelligence within intelligence community")
summary:
Addresses government support for AI-related research and development activities, the development of the AI workforce, including education and training in AI-related disciplines.

Requires a description of all authorities related to artificial intelligence use.

Requires a stipulation of element’s roles, responsibilities, and authorities for accelerating AI adoption.

Requires an evaluation of efforts to enhance intelligence capabilities through AI.

Requires a progress of each intelligence element in AI adoption.

Requires details of contracts with small or medium-sized emerging tech companies for AI products.

Requires details of positions established or filled within the element.

Requires a description of Intelligence community policies related to AI adoption and compliance assessments by elements.

Necessitates recommendations for efficient AI adoption in the intelligence community, considering technological advances.

Requires an overview of foreign adversaries' AI advances and steps to ensure U.S. outpaces them.

Requires an identification of resource or authority gaps and administrative or technical barriers to AI adoption.
require

name: FY2023 NDAA, Section 6812 ("Increased intelligence-related engineering, research, and development capabilities of minority institutions")
summary:
Requires the Director of National Intelligence to develop and submit to Congress a report and a plan to promote intelligence-related engineering, research, and development activities at institutes of higher education whose students are predominantly of minority ethnicities. 

Requires the plan described above to include an analysis of (a) the opportunities for advancing engineering, research, and development in computer sciences, including artificial intelligence, quantum computing, and machine learning, and synthetic biology, and (b) the investments necessary to do so.

Requires the plan to include metrics of success and actionable recommendations for the Director, Congress, and higher education institutions, and permits the Director to award contracts, grants, or other agreements to support the institutions.

Instructs the Director to establish goals and incentives to encourage the 
Intelligence Advanced Research Projects Activity to develop partnerships between itself, its partner institutions, and institutes of higher education whose students are predominantly of minority ethnicities.

name: FY2023 NDAA, Section 162 ("Assessment and strategy for fielding capabilities to counter threats posed by unmanned aerial system swarms")
summary:
Directs the Secretary of Defense to assess threats posed by unmanned aerial system swarms to installations and deployed Armed Forces, the use of these swarms by adversaries and their national security implications such as autonomous intelligence and machine learning, current capabilities of the Defense Department and their effectiveness in countering these threats, and efforts by the Defense Department to develop and field technology that can counter swarms.

Directs the Secretary of Defense to develop and implement a strategy to field capabilities to counter threats from unmanned aerial system swarms. The strategy should define "unmanned aerial system swarm," outline plans for developing, testing, fielding, and acquiring capabilities to counter swarms, estimate resources needed by each Armed Force to implement the strategy, and determine the legislative action necessary for the Defense Department to counter swarm threats.

Directs the Secretary of Defense to consider incorporating the strategy into a comprehensive strategy to defend against unmanned aerial systems and to report the assessment findings and strategy to the congressional defense committees within 270 days.

name: Alabama AI Commission Act
summary:
Establishes the Alabama Commission on Artificial Intelligence to review and advise on AI growth and use in governance, healthcare, education, transportation, and future industries.

Requires the commission to consider the establishment of a permanent AI commission.

Comprises members appointed by the Governor, Lieutenant Governor, House Speaker, and Senate President Pro Tempore, including experts in AI, workforce development, technology, ethics, privacy, or computer science.

Requires the commission to submit a report by May 1, 2020, with findings and recommendations for administrative or policy actions related to AI, available on the website of the Office of the Governor.

name: FY2022 NDAA, Section 216 ("Improvements relating to steering committee on emerging technology and national security threats")
summary:
Amends Section 236 of the FY 2021 National Defense Authorization Act by adding the Director of National Intelligence as an official that can, with the Secretary of Defense, establish a steering committee on emerging technology and national security and receive recommendations from the committee. Amends members of the steering committee to consist of the Principal Deputy Director of National Intelligence, the Deputy Sector of Defense, the Vice Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staffs, and other appropriate officials. Adds that the Steering Committee shall be chaired by the Deputy Secretary of Defense, the Vice Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, and the Principal Deputy Director of National Intelligence jointly.

Amends the responsibilities of the steering committee by clarifying that the committee's strategy is to maintain the technological superiority of both the US military and intelligence community according to not only the National Defense Strategy, but also the National Intelligence Strategy and the National Security Strategy. Adds that the steering committee is responsible for making recommendations on any changes to the guidance for developing the National Intelligence Program budget and determining whether sufficient resources are available for the intelligence community, in addition to the Department of Defense, to defeat threats to the US.

Adds that the list of technologies classified as emerging technologies is to be determined jointly by the Secretary of Defense and the Director of National Intelligence. Adds the definition of intelligence community from the National Security Act of 1947.

name: FY2022 NDAA, Section 1511 ("Comparative analysis of cybersecurity capabilities")
summary: Instructs various government departments to sponsor an analysis of cybersecurity tools and capabilities. Outlines which specific departments are involved in the analysis. Describes the features and tools that must be functional and applicable to the Department. Identifies the capabilities and usage of artificial intelligence and machine learning algorithms within the government. Focuses on analyzing software at the enterprise level, which enhances the productivity and capability of the government departments.

name: FY2022 NDAA, Section 557 ("United States Naval Community College")
summary:
Provides guidelines for the educational goals of the U.S. Naval Community College, including by naming skills relating to artificial intelligence and other digital technologies as a key focus of the college's educational programs.

Sets eligibility requirements for enrollment in, and graduation from, the college.

name: FY2022 NDAA, Section 909 ("Digital talent recruiting officer")
summary:
Requires the Secretary of Defense to designate a chief digital recruiting officer.

Instructs the chief digital recruiting officer to identify Department of Defense skill gaps relating to artificial intelligence, distributed ledger technologies, cybersecurity, and other digital technology fields. 

Instructs the chief digital recruiting officer to lead the Department's efforts to close those skill gaps. 

Requires the chief digital recruiting officer to provide the congressional defense committees with an annual briefing on the Department's efforts to close those skill gaps.

name: FY2022 NDAA, Section 247 ("Reports and briefings on recommendations of the National Security Commission on Artificial Intelligence regarding the Department of Defense")
summary:
Directs the Secretary of Defense to submit an annual report to the congressional defense committees on recommendations made by the National Security Commission on AI about the Department of Defense. The report shall cover the Secretary of Defense's intent to implement recommendations, plans for implementing recommendations including timelines and resources, and justifications for not implementing recommendations, including recommendations that are already being implemented.

Directs the Secretary of Defense to brief the congressional defense committees at least annually on progress in analyzing and implementing recommendations and any activities carried out in pursuit of the recommendations, including funding for each activity.

name: FY2022 NDAA, Section 1509 ("Assessment of cyber posture and operational assumptions and development of targeting strategies and supporting capabilities")
summary: Requires the Commander of Cyber Command, Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence, and Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence to assess offensive and defensive cyber capabilities of US adversaries and the U.S. military's plans for potential offensive cyber operations during conflict. One part of the assessment should cover the impact of emerging technologies such as AI. Requires briefing to the congressional defense committees.

name: FY2022 NDAA, Section 126 ("Acquisition, modernization, and sustainment plan for carrier air wings")
summary:
Requires the Secretary of the Navy to submit to the congressional defense committees a 15-year acquisition, modernization, and sustainment plan for the carrier air wings of the Navy.

Requires the plan to include an analysis of how advanced technologies such as Next Generation Jammer can be utilized to maximize operational use of existing platforms, particularly the EA-18G aircraft and the E-2D aircraft.

name: FY2022 NDAA, Section 246 ("Report on autonomy integration in major weapon systems")
summary:
Requires the Secretary of Defense to submit to the congressional defense committees a report on the Department of Defense's efforts to ensure that appropriate military systems can operate autonomously in GPS-denied environments.

Directs the report described above to include a list of systems which can be upgraded with autonomy software; the timelines for doing so; the funding required for doing so; plans to leverage artificial intelligence for such systems; plans for ensuring the safety and security of such systems through testing, evaluation, verification, and validation; and a list of Department policies that would require modification to facilitate this project.

name: Georgia House Bill 203 (2023)
summary:
Requires all eye assessments that utilize artificial intelligence or other advanced technology to conform to the traditional standards of in-person care.

Requires a medical professional to analyze any information collected or generated by an automated system during the eye assessment process.

Requires all eye assessments to involve the collection of a patient's relevant medical information, which must be stored in a medical record for at least 7 years.

name: AI Training Act
summary:
Requires the Director of the Office of Management and Budget to establish an artificial intelligence training program for the acquisition workforce to garner knowledge of the capabilities and risks associated with AI.

Requires the program to include information relating to AI risks mitigation and the identification of  reliable, safe, and trustworthy AI.

Requires the program to include information relating to future trends in AI, including trends for homeland and national security and innovation.
           
Requires the Director of the AI program to develop an interactive learning portfolio with technologists, scholars and experts from private, public and non profit sectors.

Requires the Director of the AI program to develop an evaluation system to track participation and improve the program

name: Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2022, Section 834 ("Plan for Artificial Intelligence Digital Ecosystem")
summary:
Instructs the Director of National Intelligence to develop a plan with other heads of the intelligence community for a modern digital ecosystem that enables the development and progress of artificial intelligence applications and present it to Congress within one year of the enactment of the Act.

Requires that the plan include policies to allow flexible access to classified facilities to select companies, establishes a system to allow for investments into the ecosystem that would address technical issues including but not limited to common interfaces, authentication, and software, and includes policies to prevent duplication of AI capabilities within the intelligence community.

Requires that the plan establish a governance structure to standardize implementation throughout the intelligence community and adheres to community and federal standards.

name: National AI Initiative Act
summary:
Requires the President to establish a National Artificial Intelligence Initiative to support AI-related research, education, workforce development, planning, and international cooperation. 

Requires the creation of an office, interagency coordinating committee, external advisory committee, and a task force for a potential National AI Research Resource. Directs the interagency committee to create and periodically update a strategic plan for artificial intelligence.

Requires a National Academies study of the impact of AI on the workforce.

Directs the Director of the National Science Foundation to fund new AI research institutes as well as various activities related to AI research, education, engineering, and ethics.

Amends the National Institute of Standards and Technology Act to give NIST various duties and powers related to AI and data.

Directs the Administrator of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration to establish a Center for Artificial Intelligence.

Directs the Secretary of Energy to carry out an AI research and development program on topics including AI for science and trustworthy AI.

name: Countering Human Trafficking Act of 2021, Section 4
summary:
Establishes a department of Homeland security center for countering human trafficking.

Establishes (under section 4), a specialized initiative in conjuction with the Science and Technology Directorate Office of Science and Engineering to modify systems and processes towards countering human trafficking. 

Instructs the CCHT Director, in conjunction with the Science and Technology Directorate Office of Science and Engineering to apply analytics to automate manual processes.

Instructs the CCHT Director, in conjunction with the Science and Technology Directorate Office of Science and Engineering to provide artificial intelligence and machine learning techniques towards increasing system capabilities and enhancing data availability,  reliability, comparability, and verifiability.

name: American COMPETE Act
summary:
Directs the Secretary of Commerce and the Federal Trade Commission to conduct a study on the state of the AI industry and its impact on the US economy.

Directs the Secretary and the Commission to conduct a survey of the AI market and supply chain, identify risks of exploitation by third parties, and provide recommendations to reduce bias, and protect privacy and security in AI applications.

Requires the Commission to conduct a study on how AI can be used to address online harms, including harmful content, disinformation, and crime.

name: Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023, Section 101 ("Manufacturing.gov Hub")
summary:
Instructs the Secretary of Commerce in coordination with the Information Officer of the Department of Commerce to modify the manufacturing.gov website to include a section called the manufacturing.gov hub. 

Instructs the Secretary of Commerce to use machine learning in this hub to identify frequently asked questions and disseminate the answers to these questions to the public.

name: Health Extenders, Improving Access to Medicare, Medicaid, and CHIP, and Strengthening Public Health Act of 2022, Section 1432 ("Research on the Health and Development Effects of Media and Related Technology on Minors")
summary:
Directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to produce a report about the effects of media and technology use on the cognitive development, physical health, and mental health of infants, children, and adolescents.

Authorizes the Secretary to provide financial support to research agendas and programs on the same issues.

Instructs the Secretary to submit the aforementioned report, including grants and research funded under this act, to Congress no later than two years after the passage of this legislation.

name: AI in Government Act of 2020
summary:
Defines Artificial Intelligence

Creates a program called ‘‘AI Center of Excellence’’, (CoE) which shall facilitate the adoption of AI technologies in the Federal Government and improve cohesion in the adoption of artificial intelligence.

Stipulates certain functions of this program which includes; 
a.  Collaborating with individual agencies, federal laboratories, nonprofit organizations, institutions and other entities to discuss recent developments in AI.

b. Assisting agencies in applying Federal policies on the management and use of data in the use of AI.

c. Consulting with agencies, including the Department of Defense, the Department of Commerce, the Department of Energy, the Department of Homeland Security, the Office of Management and Budget, the Office of the Director of National Intelligence, and the National Science Foundation, on issues relating to AI.

Identifies the skills needed for future job positions within the CoE and establishes jobs within the CoE and their duration (2 and 5 years).

Instructs the Director of the CoE to submit a comprehensive plan to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs and the Committee on Oversight and Reform with a timeline to achieve paragraphs a,b,c,d within 120 days of the date of the enactment of the instrument.

Instructs the Director of the AI CoE to recommend approaches to remove barriers for use by agencies of AI technologies in order to promote their innovative application while protecting civil rights, and economic and national security; identify best practices for assessing and mitigating any discriminatory impact or bias on the basis of any classification protected under Federal nondiscrimination laws, or any unintended consequence of the use of AI.

name: Texas AI advisory council
summary:
Establishes an artificial intelligence advisory council -- to be disbanded at the start of 2025 -- to study and monitor AI systems developed, employed, or procured by Texas state agencies.

Instructs the advisory council to assess the need for an AI code of ethics for the state government, review automated decision systems inventory reports submitted by state agencies, and recommend administrative actions as needed. 

Requires the advisory council to submit a report on its activities and findings to the legislature. 

Requires each state agency to submit to the legislature and advisory council an inventory report of all automated decision systems that are being developed,
employed, or procured by the agency.

Requires the inventory reports described above to assess each AI system's purpose, capabilities, data management practices, data output, and fiscal impact, as well as any information available on bias testing conducted on the system and the forms of data inputted into the system.

name: Energy Act of 2020, Title IX, Section 9008 ("Veterans' health initiative")
summary:
Directs the Secretary of Energy to establish a research program in AI and high-performance computing, focused on developing tools to improve veteran healthcare provisions.

Instructs the Secretary to dedicate $27,000,000 for the construction of new data enclaves, development of new analytical methods, and use of algorithms suitable for large biomedical data sets.

Mandates the Secretary to submit a report two years after the passage of this legislation summarizing the progress of the research program.

Authorizes $15,000,000 for each of the fiscal years from 2021 to 2025 to coordinate and further the above research with other Federal agencies, institutions of higher education, nonprofit research organizations, and industry.

name: Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2021, Division W, Title V, Section 502 ("Seedling investment in next-generation microelectronics in support of artificial intelligence")
summary:
Lists the findings of Congress which detail importance of the development of AI technology 
Instructs the Director of National Intelligence to award contracts or grants to encourage microelectronics research
Specifies that the funds awarded be used towards advanced engineering and applied research to enable the advancement of AI and machine learning, research to overcome existing challenges with engineering and applied research of microelectronics, and long-term advancements in computing technology 
Limits the amount able to be awarded to no more than $15,000,000

name: Research and Development, Competition, and Innovation Act, Title III ("National Science Foundation for the Future")
summary:
Instructs the Director of the National Science Foundation (Director) to develop a report on the need and feasibility as well as construct plans to implement a program to recruit and train the next generation of AI professionals in US government. Mandates that the report include statistical data on the federal AI workforce, assessments of current and future demand for AI expertise across the federal government and the ability of higher education institutions to prepare students to meet this demand, and an evaluation of the need for and feasibility of establishing a scholarship-for-service program for AI professionals in US government, as well as the possibility of leveraging existing programs such as the Federal Cyber Scholarship-for-Service Program. 

Authorizes the Director and other appropriate agency heads to establish a Federal AI scholarship-for-service program to recruit and train AI professionals to achieve the missions of US government. Requires the Director, in coordination with other agency heads, to establish criteria such as excellence in AI education and the ability to attract diverse students to designate qualified institutions of higher education that shall be eligible to participate in the program. Requires the program to provide scholarships through qualified higher education institutions to students pursuing fields of study related to AI, provide scholarship recipients with temporary appointments related to work on AI in the federal government, prioritize placement of scholarship recipients in executive agencies, identify opportunities to promote multidisciplinary programs of study, support capacity building for educational institutions to enable them to train the next-generation AI workforce, create courses in technology ethics for scholarship recipients, and award fellowships to masters and doctoral students who are pursuing degrees or research in AI and related fields. Instructs scholarship amounts to cover a student’s tuition and fees for not more than 3 years with an additional stipend, and obligates scholarship recipients to work for a period of time equivalent to the length of the scholarship in the AI mission of the US government entity or affiliated entity.

Instructs the Director to establish competitive awards to institutions to advance knowledge of risk assessment including the utilization of AI in our ability to understand and predict extreme events and natural hazards, create engineered system solutions and develop instrumentation for innovation in resilient infrastructure, and advance research on multidisciplinary wildfire science and behaviors related to increasing resilience.

Amends Section 506(a) of the America COMPETES Reauthorization Act of 2010 by adding AI and machine learning to the list of research areas that fall under information technologies for manufacturing that the Director can award grants to.

Instructs the Director to make competitive awards to institutions to support basic research to advance critical minerals mining strategies to make better use of domestic resources and eliminate national reliance on minerals subject to supply chain disruptions, including the application of AI for geological exploration of critical minerals and the application of machine learning for detection and sorting of critical minerals.

Requires the Director to conduct or support the development of a study on AI research capacity at US institutions of higher education. Requires the study to, at minimum, address which universities are putting out significant peer-reviewed AI research based on quantity and number of citations, which factors of these universities such as computing power enable their research, promising practices at these universities for advancing diversity, equity, and inclusion in AI research programs, geographic diversity of universities that have AI research-enabling factors, and how universities that are not currently top producers of AI research could improve, including potential pilot programs that the federal government could develop or support to help universities produce AI research.

Instructs the Director, in consultation with the Director of the Office of Management and Budget and the interagency committee established under the National AI Initiative Act of 2020, to develop and test models to inform the implementation of a government-wide data linkage and access infrastructure for statistical activities.

Requires the Director to identify, and annually review and update a list of not more than 10 key technology focus areas, which includes AI, machine learning, autonomy, and related advances.

name: Energy Act of 2020, Title III, Section 3002(g) ("Advanced Geothermal Computing and Data Science Research and Development")
summary:
Amends the Energy Independence and Security Act of 2007, instructing the Secretary of Energy to carry out a research and development program of advanced computing and data science tools for geothermal energy. Supports the use of artificial intelligence and related computing tools to assist in locating geothermal resources, to increase site characterization reliability, to increase drilling rate and efficiency, to improve induced seismicity mitigation, and to support enhanced geothermal systems technologies.

Instructs the Secretary of Energy to, in carrying out these programs, ensure consultation with DOE's Office of Science and maximize coordination with DOE National Laboratories, institutes of higher education, and the private sector.

name: Research and Development, Competition, and Innovation Act, Title VI, Section 10771 ("Department of Energy research, development, and demonstration activities")
summary: Authorizes the appropriation of $200 million -- spread across FY 2023-2026 -- to the U.S. Department of Energy for its Office of Environmental Management to carry out research, development, and demonstration activities, including those relating to artificial intelligence.

name: Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, Section 25005 ("Strengthening Mobility and Revolutionizing Transportation Grant Program")
summary:
Directs the Secretary of Transportation to establish a grant program to advance smart city infrastructure projects that improve transportation efficiency, safety, and accessibility. 

Requires eligible projects to demonstrate focus in directed areas, including the deployment of automated transportation, autonomous vehicles, and intelligent, sensor-based infrastructure. 

Requires grant-receiving entities to submit to the Secretary an implementation report, supported by data describing the effectiveness of projects in meeting their specific goals.

name: Research and Development, Competition, and Innovation Act, Title II ("National Institute of Standards and Technology for the Future"), Subtitle B ("Measurement Research")
summary:
Instructs the Director to carry out research and testing to improve the effectiveness of Artificial Intelligence-enabled cybersecurity, Artificial Intelligence defense systems and evaluating the performance of varying network architectures at strengthening network security.

Requires the Director to carry out a program of measurement research for advanced communications technologies which among others would include Artificial Intelligence systems to enable internet of things networks, immersive technology, and other advanced communications technologies

Instructs the Director to support the development of technical standards and guidelines that promote safe and trustworthy Artificial Intelligence systems, such as enhancing the accuracy, privacy, explanability, reliability, robustness, safety, security, and mitigation of harmful bias in Artificial Intelligence systems

Instructs the Director to create a framework for managing risks associated with Artificial Intelligence systems.

Instructs the Director to develop and publish cybersecurity tools, encryption methods, and best practices for Artificial Intelligence and data science. 

Requires the Director to establish testbeds to support the development of robust and trustworthy Artificial Intelligence and machine learning systems, including testbeds that examine the vulnerabilities and conditions that may lead to failure in, malfunction of, or attacks on such systems.

Requires the Director to conduct regular testing to improve and benchmark the accuracy, efficacy, and bias of biometric identification technologies,

name: Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, Section 11401 ("Grants for Charging and Fueling Infrastructure")
summary:
Directs the Secretary of Transportation to establish a grant program to promote charging and fueling infrastructure for alternative-fuel vehicles.

Allocates a maximum grant amount of $15M.

Requires entities applying for grants to describe how they have considered infrastructure instillation that can accommodate autonomous vehicles and other technology advancements.

name: Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, Section 40210 ("Critical Minerals Mining and Recycling Research")
summary:
Authorizes the use of funds towards examining the application of artificial intelligence for geological exploration of critical minerals, including what size and diversity of data sets would be require

Authorizes the use of funds towards examining the application of machine learning for detection and sorting of critical minerals, including what size and diversity of data sets would be required.

Authorizes the advancement and development of reserach in AI and machine learning.

Addresses government support for AI-related research and development activities.

name: Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, Title V, Subtitle C, Part II ("Smart Manufacturing")
summary:
Defines "smart manufacturing" as advanced technologies in artificial intelligence, computation, and modeling that streamline manufacturing production lines.

Directs the Secretary of Energy the conduct a study on how to increase access to the computing facilities of the National Laboratories for small and medium manufacturers.

Instructs the Secretary to make the National Laboratories' high-performance computing resources available to small and medium manufacturers to increase their manufacturing competitiveness.

Authorizes the Secretary to distribute financial assistance to programs that support the  implementation of smart manufacturing technologies, based on technical merit and research record.

Requires the Secretary to submit an annual report to Congress about the status of smart manufacturing in the United States.

name: Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, Section 25017 ("University Transportation Centers Program")
summary:
Amends previous legislation that directs the Secretary of Transportation to make grants to establish university transportation centers at eligible nonprofit institutions of high education. 

Modifies previously established objectives of the university transportation centers program to include research on the cybersecurity implications of autonomous vehicles, as well as of any other technologies relating to connected vehicles and connected infrastructure.

name: Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, Section 13005 ("Emerging Technology Research Pilot Program")
summary:
Directs the Secretary of Transportation to establish an emerging technology research pilot program that will:

Authorizes research and development activities related to using advanced and additive manufacturing technologies to support the integrity and cost-effectiveness of surface transportation infrastructure

Authorizes research and development activities and pavement testing to reduce the impact of automated driving and advanced driver-assistance systems on pavement and infrastructure, and improve the design of transportation infrastructure to accommodate increasing numbers of automated and advanced driving systems

Authorized to be appropriated $5,000,000 to carry this out for fiscal years 2022 to 2026

name: Research and Development, Competition, and Innovation Act, Title VI, Section 10731 ("Microelectronics research for energy innovation")
summary:
Instructs the Secretary of Energy to carry out a program of research, development, and demonstration of microelectronics, including leveraging artificial intelligence to enhance microelectronics applications. Appropriates $75M-$100M for the microelectronics research program for each fiscal year from 2023 to 2027.

Instructs the Director of the Office of Science to establish 4 Microelectronic Science Research Centers, whose missions include advancing knowledge and experimental capabilities in AI and other computational and theoretical methods.

Promotes coordination of microelectronic research and development across DOE efforts, other Federal agencies, other research centers, and the private sector.

name: Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2021, Division W, Title V, Section 604 ("Assessment of critical technology trends relating to artificial intelligence, microchips, and semiconductors and related supply chains")
summary:
Directs the Director of National Intelligence to assess export controls and other technology transfer measures by partner countries on artificial intelligence enabled technologies critical to US supply chains.

Mandates the Director to identify opportunities for cooperation with partner countries to address technology transfer threats.

Instructs the Director to investigate the effect of computing power trends on global artificial intelligence development and implementation and deliver the report no later than 180 days after the enactment of this piece of legislation.

name: Research and Development, Competition, and Innovation Act, Title I ("Department of Energy Science for the Future")
summary:
Instructs the Secretary of the Advanced Computing Program to maintain foundational research programs in mathematical and computational sciences, including new and emerging computing needs within the mission of the Department like novel approaches to modelling and simulation, artificial intelligence, and machine learning.

Instructs the Secretary to issue and ensure adherence to guidance for the Department, the National Laboratories, and users. This guidance pertains to how high-performance computing systems, including machine learning algorithms for data analysis and artificial intelligence, should be employed. 

Instructed the Director to prioritize research and development of sustainable chemistry, autonomous chemistry, and materials synthesis, leveraging  advances in artificial intelligence.

Instructs the Director to carry out research and testing to improve the effectiveness of artificial intelligence-enabled cybersecurity. 

Instructs the Director to support the development of artificial intelligence and data science. 

Instructs the Director to support the development of technical standards and guidelines- creating a framework for managing risks associated with artificial intelligence systems. 

Instructs the Director to establish testbeds to support the development of robust and trustworthy artificial intelligence and machine learning systems. These testbeds will examine the vulnerabilities and conditions that may lead to failure, malfunction, or attacks on such systems.

Instructs the Director to establish a report on the need, feasibility, and plans to implement a program to recruit and train the next generation of artificial intelligence professionals. This program is meant to meet the needs of Federal, State, local, and Tribal governments.

Provides scholarships through qualified institutions of higher education to students enrolled in programs related to artificial intelligence. Provides fellowships to masters and doctoral students pursuing degrees or research in artificial intelligence and related fields.

Necessitates research and testing to improve the accuracy, efficacy, and bias of biometric identification technologies.

name: Energy Act of 2020, Title VIII, Section 8002 ("Smart grid modeling, visualization, architecture, and controls")
summary:
Directs the Secretary of Energy to support the development of new and emerging technologies to increase the resilience of electrical grid design, planning, and operation.

Mandates the Secretary to bolster the usage of computational tools and technologies in improving the sensing, monitoring, and visualization of the electric grid; models must be able to predict the effects of adverse physical and cyber events on the electric grid.

Instructs the Secretary to research the potential deployment of new and emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, with existing electrical grid infrastructure.

name: Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, Section 40433 ("Digital Climate Solutions Report")
summary:
Defines digital climate solutions as those that use artificial intelligence, blockchain technologies, and the Internet of Things. 

Directs the Secretary of Energy to create a report that contains a full inventory of digital climate solutions, an analysis of how the private sector can use the digital climate solutions, and a summary of opportunities to enhance the standardization of regulatory climate protocols.

name: Hawaii AI Advisory Committee Resolution
summary:
Establishes an AI advisory committee in Hawaii to investigate how to implement, develop, and regulate AI in the state; the committee will be composed of government, academic, and industry stakeholders.

Requires the committee to evaluate and make recommendations on AI applications in other governments, competitive advantages to be gained by integrating AI into Hawaii’s economy, methods for encouraging AI R&D in universities and private sector, the potential danger of integrating AI into state operations, and potential regulatory systems for AI. 

Requires the committee to submit a report of findings and proposed legislation to the Legislature before its convening in 2020.

name: 21 CFR § 870.2790 ("Photoplethysmograph analysis software for over-the-counter use")
summary:
Requires manufacturers of photoplethysmograph analysis software to conduct clinical performance testing that reveals the performance characteristics of the detection algorithms under anticipated use cases.

Requires manufactures to perform verification, validation, and hazard analysis of the software, as well as divulge the software's technical specs including the detection algorithm and its inputs and outputs.

name: 21 CFR § 892.2060 ("Radiological computer-assisted diagnostic software for lesions suspicious of cancer")
summary:
Requires manufacturers of radiological computer-assisted diagnostic software to provide a detailed description of the image analysis algorithms including inputs, outputs, major components, and limitations.

Requires disclosure of pre-specified performance testing protocols used to assess whether the device will improve reader performance as intended.

Requires disclosure of results from performance testing that follows pre-specified protocols.

Requires manufacturers to provide appropriate software documentation including device hazard analysis, software design specs, traceability analysis, and cybersecurity features.

Mandates labeling that details compatible imaging hardware and imaging protocols, as well as the intended reading protocol.

name: 21 CFR § 870.2210 ("Adjunctive predictive cardiovascular indicator")
summary:
Requires that adjunctive predictive cardiovascular indicators -- medical devices used to predict cardiovascular health -- be subject to special controls in the U.S. Those controls include the following:

Requires a risk assessment of the device, including full disclosure of software specs and different inputs considered when making predictions about future cardiovascular health.

Requires scientific justification for the device's efficacy, including verification of algorithm calculations and validation using an independent data set.

Requires a human factors and usability engineering assessment to evaluate the risk of misinterpretation of device output.

Requires a clinical data assessment that specifies the clinical data used and an evaluation of output consistency.

name: 21 CFR § 864.3750 ("Software algorithm device to assist users in digital pathology")
summary:
Classifies a software algorithm device to assist users in digital pathology -- an in vitro device intended to evaluate acquired scanned pathology whole slide images to assist in diagnosis -- into the U.S. Food and Drug Administration's class II, requiring special controls. That set of special controls:

Requires detailed product labeling, including instructions for use and notices of the device's limitations.

Requires performance assessments of the device that meets pre-set standards for rigor, evaluate the device's performance when used by its intended users, and cover the entire spectrum of challenging cases likely to be encountered in the device's operation. 

Requires a detailed description of the workings of the device's software.

Requires a risk management plan, including mechanisms to mitigate cybersecurity risks.

name: 21 CFR § 870.2345 ("Electrocardiograph software for over-the-counter use")
summary:
Labels over-the-counter use of electrocardiograph software devices as Class II (special controls), which requires manufactures to verify, validate, and conduct hazard analysis of detection algorithms in the devices.

Mandates manufactures to produce clinical performance testing results that shows the performance characteristics of the detection algorithm by sensitivity and either specificity or positive predictive value.

Requires manufacturers who fail to conduct non-clinical performance testing to validate detection algorithm performance using a previously adjudicated data set.

Requires human factors and usability testing to demonstrate that the user can correctly interpret the device output and understand when to seek medical care.

name: 21 CFR § 864.3750 ("Adjunctive hemodynamic indicator with decision point")
summary:
Classifies the adjunctive hemodynamic indicator with decision point -- a device that monitors medical conditions relating to blood flow -- into the Food & Drug Administration's class II, requiring special controls. That set of controls:

Requires a full description of the technical parameters of the device's software and sensors.

Requires a risk assessment for the device.

Requires mechanisms designed to mitigate the impact of user error or failure of any subsystem components (signal detection and analysis, data display, and storage) on the accuracy of the device's output.

Requires statistical documentation, based on robust clinical data, of the device's efficacy. The accuracy of the device's algorithm must be tested using an independent dataset. 

Requires a usability assessment to demonstrate that the risk of misinterpretation of the status indicator is appropriately mitigated.

Requires detailed product labeling.

name: Limited Applicability of Consumer Financial Protection Act's “Time or Space” Exception With Respect to Digital Marketing Providers
summary:
Clarifies Section 1002 of the Consumer Financial Protection Act of 2010's definition of "service provider" to include digital marketing providers that use algorithmic models or other analytics to commingle the targeting and delivery of advertisements to consumers, rendering those providers subject to the Act's prohibition on unfair, deceptive, or abusive acts or practices.

Outlines the ways in which digital marketers provide additional services beyond "time or space" and are materially involved in the development of content strategy -- often through the use of targeting and delivering algorithms -- thus qualifying them as "service providers" under the law.

Outlines specific circumstances in which digital marketers are and are not considered service providers under the CFPA; they qualify as service providers when using algorithms and data to target and deliver advertisements with certain characteristics, or when using algorithms and business-specific data to determine when to display specific advertisements to specific consumers.

name: 21 CFR § 882.1491 ("Pediatric Autism Spectrum Disorder diagnosis aid")
summary:
Classifies the Cognoa ASD Diagnosis Aid, a machine-learning software program and device used in the diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder, into the U.S. Food and Drug Administration's class II regulatory category requiring special controls. The mandated special controls are as follows:

Requires clinical performance testing to demonstrate that the device performs as intended under anticipated conditions of use, including an evaluation of sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, and negative predictive value using a reference method of diagnosis and assessment of patient behavioral symptomology.

Requires software verification, validation, and hazard analysis to be provided for the device. Software documentation must include a detailed, technical description of the algorithm(s) used to generate device output(s), and a cybersecurity assessment of the impact of threats and vulnerabilities on device functionality and user(s).

Requires a usability assessment that must demonstrate that the intended user(s) can safely and correctly use the device.

Requires detailed product labeling that includes instructions for the device's use and a summary of any clinical testing done to demonstrate the device's functionality.

name: 21 CFR § 870.1420 ("Coronary artery disease risk indicator using acoustic heart signals")
summary:
Requires disclosure of all inputs and outputs of algorithms used in coronary artery disease risk indicators.

Requires manufacturers to divulge the procedure for segmenting, characterizing, and classifying the acoustic signal.

Mandates the verification of the algorithm calculations and validation using an independent data set.

name: 21 CFR § 892.2070 ("Medical image analyzer")
summary:
Requires disclosure of inputs, outputs, components, and limitations of image analysis algorithms used in medical image analyzers.

Requires performance testing that demonstrates the algorithms meaningfully improve the detection of abnormalities during patient radiographs.

Requires appropriate software documentation including device hazard analysis, software specs, traceability analysis, pass/fail criteria, and cybersecurity.

Requires a detailed summary of the methodology behind the performance testing.

name: 21 CFR § 870.2785 ("Software for optical camera-based measurement of pulse rate, heart rate, breathing rate, and/or respiratory rate")
summary:
Classifies the Oxehealth Vital Signs device -- which uses software to enable camera-based measurement of pulse rate, heart rate, breathing rate, and/or respiratory rate -- into the U.S. Food and Drug Administration's class II, requiring special controls. The set of special controls:

Requires a full characterization of the technical parameters of the device's software, as well as documentation of a cybersecurity vulnerability and management process to assure software functionality.

Requires the results of verification and validation testing based on a comprehensive hazard analysis and risk assessment of the software and associated device, to include a description of all mitigations for user error or failure of any subsystem components (including signal detection, signal analysis, data display, and storage) on output accuracy.

Requires clinical data demonstrating the software and device's efficacy, including comparing the device's output with a clinically accurate patient-contacting relevant comparator device in an accurate and reproducible manner.

Requires a human factors and usability engineering assessment that evaluates the risk of improper measurement.

Requires detailed product labeling, to include instructions for using the device and interpreting its output; warnings of factors that may impede proper functionality; and a description of the measurements the device takes.

name: 21 CFR § 870.1345 ("Intravascular bleed monitor")
summary:
