Requires that the Saranas Early Bird Bleed Monitoring System -- a device that uses measurements of the body's electrical conductivity and an algorithm to monitor potential internal bleeding complications -- be subject to special controls from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Those controls include the following:

Requires performance testing demonstrating that the device meets standards for efficacy, safety, sterility, and usability.

Requires software verification, validation, and hazard analysis to be performed. 

Requires detailed product labeling to include instructions for use and storage, among other product details.

name: 15 CFR part 7 ("Securing the Information and Communications Technology and Services Supply Chain")
summary:
Establishes procedures by which the Secretary of Commerce may determine whether any information and communications technology or service (ICTS) transaction that has been produced or supplied by foreign adversaries poses certain undue or unacceptable cybersecurity risks. Relevant ICTS include drones or any other unmanned aerial systems, autonomous systems, and artificial intelligence and machine learning software.

Establishes procedures by which the Secretary may prohibit and/or direct the timing and manner of the cessation of an ICTS transaction.

Establishes procedures by which the Secretary may consider factors that may mitigate the risks posed by the ICTS transaction. 

Details penalties for entities that violate any issued final determination or direction.

name: LIFT AI Act
summary:
Establishes the "LIFT AI Act" to advance AI literacy in K–12 education.

Empowers the Director of the National Science Foundation to award competitive grants to higher education institutions or nonprofits for developing AI literacy curricula and evaluation methods.

Endorses AI literacy education to prepare a skilled workforce and maintain U.S. leadership in AI.

Recognizes the importance of AI literacy in mitigating ethical challenges and adapting to rapidly evolving AI technologies.

Supports the development of curricula focussed on AI competency, AI literacy evaluation tools, and professional development courses in AI literacy for educators.

Encourages incorporating AI literacy in existing curricula, emphasizing responsible AI use.

name: Artificial Intelligence Acquisitions Act of 2024
summary:
Mandates the development of a list of artificial intelligence products or services posing national security risks, focusing on those associated with foreign entities of concern.

Requires the Executive Director, alongside the Under Secretary of Commerce and the Federal Acquisition Security Council, to publish and annually update this list.

Prohibits federal agencies from purchasing or procuring AI products or services included on this list.

Obligates contractors with federal agencies to divest from listed AI products within specified timeframes.

Allows exceptions for intelligence activities and specific Department of Defense operations related to defense intelligence and adversarial AI research.

Defines key terms including "artificial intelligence," "foreign person of concern," and "country of concern," specifying entities like China, Russia, and Iran as countries of concern.

Sets a timeline for initial list publication within one year of the Act's enactment and mandates public notification if no updates are made annually.

name: Idaho HB 575 (Disclosing Explicit Synthetic Media)
summary:
Establishes the crime of disclosing or threatening to disclose explicit synthetic media without consent, intending to cause distress or obtain valuables, punishable as a misdemeanor or felony for repeat offenders.

Defines "explicit synthetic media" as AI-altered images or videos depicting sexual conduct involving identifiable individuals without their engagement.

Exempts disclosures for lawful purposes, such as criminal investigations, public interest reporting, scientific research, or legal proceedings.

Excludes liability for interactive computer services and telecommunications providers for third-party content, unless they intentionally aid disclosures.

Declares provisions severable, ensuring unaffected sections remain valid if parts are invalidated.

Declares an emergency and sets the effective date for July 1, 2024.

name: S. 3004 (Chief AI Officer Governing Council)
summary:
Establishes the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer Governing Council to oversee and ensure ethical AI and data policies within the Department of Defense.

Requires the Council to oversee AI ethics, governance, and operational usage, with the aim of improving AI governance coordination and mitigating bias in AI systems. 

Mandates the Council to submit reports to the Secretary of Defense and congressional defense committees every 180 days initially and at least every 18 months thereafter.

name: Digital Platform Commission Act of 2023
summary:
Defines algorithmic processes as including artificial intelligence techniques and refers to processes that can make decisions, generate content, or provide information, especially as used in social media

Establishes the Federal Digital Platform Commission to regulate digital platforms, including social media.

Provides for the creation of a Code Council to develop voluntary or enforceable behavioral codes, technical standards, and other policies related to digital platforms and AI processes.

Mandates oversight of algorithmic processes, including those using AI, for fairness, transparency, and safety.

Obligates platforms to ensure recommendation systems and other algorithmic processes are free from harmful, abusive, anticompetitive, or deceptive biases.

Imposes regular public risk assessments for harmful content distribution and steps to mitigate such harms, including those from algorithmic processes..

name: Cooper Davis Act
summary:
Requires electronic communication service providers and remote computing services to report to the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) any knowledge of crimes involving fentanyl, methamphetamine, or counterfeit substances.

Mandates the report to be filed within 60 days of obtaining such knowledge, including detailed contact and relevant information about the involved accounts.

Allows reports based on reasonable belief and includes optional additional information like geographic location and complete communication data.

Subjects providers to criminal and civil penalties for failing to report or submitting false reports.

States that providers are not required to monitor users or the content of communications proactively.

Obliges DEA to review and potentially investigate reports, sharing them with other law enforcement agencies as needed.

Mandates the Attorney General to enforce these requirements and take measures for data minimization.

Requires DEA to publish annual reports on the number and outcomes of reports received.

Exempts broadband internet access service providers from these reporting requirements.

name: AI Ads Act
summary:
Amends the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 to include fraudulent misrepresentation through content generated with artificial intelligence (AI) under its prohibitions.

Clarifies that fraudulent misrepresentation of campaign authority or solicitation of funds includes the use of AI-generated content.

Extends the prohibition against fraudulent misrepresentation beyond candidates to any person misrepresenting candidates, political parties, or committees for any purpose.

Broadens the scope of prohibited fraudulent solicitation to encompass any candidate, political party, or fictitious political organization, not just those directly involving a candidate or party employee.

Expands the provisions to cover AI-generated content used in misrepresentation or solicitation within political campaigns, ensuring comprehensive regulation of AI's role in electoral fraud.

name: Five AIs Act 2024
summary:
Establishes the "Five AIs Strategic Artificial Intelligence Working Group" within 90 days to coordinate AI initiatives among the Five Eyes countries (Australia, Canada, New Zealand, the UK, and the US).

Requires the Secretary of Defense and Director of National Intelligence to lead and designate a head for the Working Group.

Mandates the Working Group to develop strategies for AI interoperability, ethical frameworks, and innovation among the Five Eyes countries.

Instructs testing and evaluation of AI systems for intelligence sharing and battlespace awareness.

Emphasizes leveraging commercial AI technologies and managing data-informed AI systems.

Requires submission of a plan within 60 days and biannual reports on the Working Group's activities.

Specifies control of knowledge and technical data by individual countries under their export laws.

Allows termination of the Working Group on September 30, 2028, with possible extension for national security interests.

name: A bill to prohibit certain US investments in China
summary:
Prohibits U.S. persons from engaging in certain transactions with entities associated with China that involve "prohibited technologies," focusing on national security concerns.

Requires authorities to issue non-binding feedback on covered transactions and imposes civil penalties for violations.

Mandates U.S. persons provide written notification within 30 days post-transaction involving "notifiable technologies."

Establishes a process for identifying transactions lacking notifications and mandates confidentiality of submitted transaction information.

Obliges the Secretary of the Treasury to annually report to Congress on enforcement actions, updates to prohibited technologies, and assessment of national security threats.

Encourages multilateral engagement with U.S. allies to curb prohibited technology development/acquisition by countries of concern, including China.

Potentially establishes a public database for identifying covered foreign persons involved in prohibited technologies.

Exempts certain transactions deemed de minimis or in the national interest, and enables updates to prohibited or notifiable technologies to address national security needs.

name: Preserving American Dominance in Artificial Intelligence Act of 2024
summary:
Establishes the Artificial Intelligence Safety Review Office to oversee national security risks from advanced AI, particularly chemical, biological, radiological, nuclear, and cyber threats.

Mandates developers of AI models with significant computational power to report red-teaming and cybersecurity practices.

Requires evaluations and pre-deployment reviews for AI models posing potential threats, overseen by an Under Secretary of Commerce for AI Safety.

Orders creation of standards for know-your-customer protocols and red-teaming techniques to mitigate advanced AI risks.

Permits the Attorney General to enforce compliance, with civil fines up to $1,000,000 daily and potential imprisonment for violations.

Allocates $50,000,000 for implementing these measures to ensure AI advancements remain secure and beneficial for U.S. interests.

name: AI Act of 2024
summary:
Mandates financial regulators to submit reports within 180 days assessing the benefits and risks of AI in their sectors.

Requires banking regulators to examine AI's role in banking operations, fraud detection, cybersecurity, and fair lending practices, with a focus on smaller and community financial institutions.

Directs the Securities and Exchange Commission to explore AI's use in market research, portfolio management, and fraud detection in securities markets.

Instructs housing and mortgage regulators to evaluate AI's impact on mortgage efficiency, credit decisions, and real estate practices, particularly for underserved communities.

Requests the Treasury Department to report on AI's application in compliance with the Bank Secrecy Act, cybersecurity, and protection against national security threats.

Mandates inclusion of legislative recommendations to responsibly adopt AI across these sectors.

Requires public consultation to gather input for each report, involving self-regulatory organizations and relevant agencies.

name: TBD AI Act of 2024
summary:
Mandates the Director of the National Institute of Standards and Technology to develop guidelines for evaluating the trustworthiness of AI systems within one year, covering models, data, and human-AI interactions.

Requires periodic updates of these guidelines, addressing elements like safety, security, privacy, and bias, especially concerning protected classes under Federal law.

Obliges Federal agencies to ensure new AI systems conform to guidelines before deployment and evaluate existing systems within two years to ensure compliance.

Specifies designation of a Chief AI Officer in each Federal agency responsible for AI governance and guideline implementation.

Requires transparency in labeling AI systems as compliant and mandates agencies to report noncompliance and barriers to Congress within specific timelines.

Encourages collaboration with developers and stakeholders to verify elements of trustworthiness throughout the AI lifecycle. 

Sets the guidelines' effective date as the trigger for these provisions.

name: Chinese Military and Surveillance Company Sanctions Act of 2024
summary:
Mandates the imposition of sanctions on foreign persons engaged in China's defense, military-civil fusion, or surveillance technology sectors, effective 180 days post-enactment.

Prohibits U.S. jurisdictional foreign exchange transactions involving sanctioned entities.

Requires strict conditions or bans on U.S. accounts for foreign financial institutions conducting significant transactions with these entities.

Obliges the President to respond to congressional queries regarding sanction eligibility within 30 days.

Instructs the Secretary of the Treasury to annually assess sanction criteria compliance for specified entities and report to Congress.

Encourages focus on sectors like AI, quantum tech, robotics, and others in sanction assessments.

Implements penalties under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act for violations.

Allows waiver of sanctions if deemed necessary for U.S. national security.

Excludes intelligence, law enforcement, and humanitarian activities from sanctions.

Sunsets authority to impose sanctions 7 years after enactment.

name: Workforce Data Enhancement Act
summary:
Establishes a grant program under the amended Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act for a workforce data quality initiative aimed at integrating and improving statewide longitudinal data systems.

Requires the Secretary to allocate up to 10% of specific funds to eligible entities, mainly state agencies, for enhancing data integration from education and workforce systems to strengthen program quality.

Mandates that eligible entities submit detailed applications describing proposed improvements, expected outcomes, and privacy measures.

Prioritizes grants to entities with multistate collaboration or those focusing on advancing interoperable data, private partnerships, and real-time data reporting, especially concerning emerging technologies like AI.

Permits grant use for developing state data systems, enhancing data standardization, and fostering data-driven decision-making.

Specifies requirements for a maximum three-year grant duration, supplemental funding use, and post-grant reporting on achievements.

Amends funding source provisions to include these new initiatives.

name: Rural Prosperity and Food Security Act of 2024, SEC. 7208. "HIGH-PRIORITY RESEARCH AND EXTENSION INITIATIVES."
summary:
Establishes research and extension grants for developing and evaluating the agricultural application of artificial intelligence.

Emphasizes the use of AI to improve specialty crop production.

Authorizes these initiatives under the amendments to the Food, Agriculture, Conservation, and Trade Act of 1990.

Encourages research projects that focus on innovative methods and technologies enhancing agricultural efficiency.

Places potential emphasis on mechanizing agricultural processes, though AI-specific focus is primarily on specialty crop production.

name: Rural Prosperity and Food Security Act of 2024, SEC. 7518. "DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE, DEPARTMENT OF ENERGY, AND                NATIONAL SCIENCE FOUNDATION JOINT RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT ACTIVITIES."
summary:
Mandates the Department of Agriculture, Department of Energy, and National Science Foundation to conduct joint R&D activities.

Requires establishing memoranda of understanding to coordinate efforts.

Authorizes collaborative research in AI, machine learning, large-scale data analytics, and predictive analysis to optimize agricultural and rural energy systems.

Facilitates development of methods for handling large data sets related to agriculture, environment, and supply chain.

Promotes open data sharing and collaboration between federal agencies, labs, educational and nonprofit institutions, industry, and more, ensuring compliance with federal regulations.

Supports infrastructure and workforce development for research identified as necessary by the involved agencies.

Permits reimbursable agreements and collaborations with other federal agencies to enhance R&D effectiveness.

Requires a report within two years detailing interagency coordination, achievements, future opportunities, and ongoing coordination efforts.

Stipulates consistency with existing research security regulations.

name: Leadership in CET Act
summary:
Establishes a pilot program for expediting patent applications related to critical and emerging technologies, including AI, microelectronics, and quantum information science.

Requires the Director of the United States Patent and Trademark Office to expedite patent processing through petitions.

Permits waiver of certain fees and requirements for accelerated examination processes.

Limits eligibility to U.S.-based entities or inventors and restricts applications to original, nonprovisional patents.

Terminates the program after issuing a patent within five years or upon accepting 10,000 applications, with a potential renewal for the same criteria.

Mandates public availability of information regarding application numbers, acceptance, and issued patents on the Office's website.

Requires a report to Congress assessing the pilot program's effectiveness post-termination, exempting this data collection from the Paperwork Reduction Act.

name: Improving Atmospheric River Forecasts Act
summary:
Mandates the establishment of an atmospheric river forecast improvement program aimed at reducing loss of life and property due to atmospheric river events.

Requires development of quantitative forecast metrics, incorporating machine learning and data assimilation for improved landfall predictions of atmospheric rivers and associated extreme weather conditions.

Directs the enhancement of dynamic modeling systems to provide detailed forecasts, including snow accumulation and hydrological impacts.

Encourages the integration of innovative observation technologies and AI methods to refine forecasting and improve water resource management.

Supports atmospheric river reconnaissance efforts, ensuring data availability and integration into forecasting systems, and mandates the establishment of observatories along the U.S. West Coast.

Focuses on improved communication and categorization of atmospheric river hazards to aid public understanding and preparedness.

Obliges submission of a comprehensive program plan detailing research activities and resources within 270 days of enactment.

name: Protecting AI and Cloud Competition in Defense Act of 2024
summary:
Mandates the Secretary of Defense to require competitive awards for cloud computing, data infrastructure, and foundation model solutions to promote security, resiliency, and competition.

Ensures that the Government retains exclusive data access and use rights.

Requires prioritization of intellectual property, data rights, and interoperability during procurement processes, with consideration for multi-cloud technology where suitable.

Directs updates to the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement to protect government-furnished data used in AI development and prevent unauthorized disclosure.

Imposes penalties for violations, including fines and contract termination, but allows exemptions where national security is not compromised.

Obliges annual reports from the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff assessing competition and market dynamics in the AI industry, with recommendations for legislative and administrative actions.

Ensures public accessibility of these reports through the Department of Defense's website and other no-cost methods.

name: TRAIN Act
summary:
Enacts the "Transparency and Responsibility for Artificial Intelligence Networks Act" or "TRAIN Act."

Requires the United States district court clerk to issue a subpoena to AI model developers or deployers upon request from copyright owners.

Defines artificial intelligence terms including AI models and generative AI models used in the legal context.

Allows copyright owners, with a good faith belief of infringement, to request AI training data records.

Mandates that a subpoena requires model developers or deployers to disclose records of copyrighted works used in AI model training.

Details the procedure for the issuance and execution of subpoenas under the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure.

Creates a rebuttable presumption of copyright copying if the subpoenaed party fails to comply.

Implements the new rules on the date of enactment.

name: Iowa (2019) SB 302 (Automated Driving System Motor Vehicles)
summary:
Defines key terms like "automated driving system" and "driverless-capable vehicle" relevant to motor vehicles operated by autonomous systems.

Allows the operation of driverless-capable vehicles on public highways without a human driver present, provided they meet safety and compliance standards.

Requires system-equipped vehicles to operate within designated operational domains and comply with state traffic and safety laws unless exempted.

Mandates financial liability coverage for system-equipped vehicles before they can operate on public highways.

Stipulates that automated vehicles involved in accidents must remain at the scene and report to law enforcement, holding vehicle owners accountable for compliance.

Permits the operation of on-demand driverless-capable vehicle networks for transporting persons or goods, integrating with digital transport services.

Grants exclusive governance and regulatory authority over automated systems to the state department, prohibiting additional local regulations or taxes on such systems.

name: Advancing Digital Freedom Act of 2024
summary:
Requires the United States to prioritize digital freedom in foreign policy and diplomatic engagements.

Mandates cooperation with countries committed to democratic technology use and development.

Appoints a Coordinator for Digital Freedom within the Bureau of Cyberspace and Digital Policy to advance global digital freedom.

Directs the Coordinator to engage with international actors to counter digital authoritarianism and support human rights-compliant technology governance.

Instructs the Coordinator to promote democratic governance of artificial intelligence, emphasizing human rights and democracy.

Requires ongoing publication of guidelines for protecting digital freedom in cyberspace, including the AI Risk Management Profile.

Obliges annual reporting on global digital freedom, analyzing threats like digital authoritarianism, censorship, and AI governance risks.

Advises on improving digital inclusion and information integrity.

Tasks the Coordinator with making recommendations to enhance digital freedom through diplomatic channels.

name: DOGE Act
summary:
Mandates the prohibition of federal grant awards to applicants submitting duplicative or fraudulent applications, with an exception for institutions of higher education.

Requires the joint determination of appropriate agencies to award grants when duplicative applications are identified.

Obliges the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) to establish an electronic system to track federal grant applications, preventing awards for identical purposes across executive agencies.

Includes specific system requirements, such as storing awardee details and facilitating identification of essentially equivalent work.

Directs the OMB, along with specific federal bodies, to report to Congress on the feasibility of using artificial intelligence to identify duplicative grant applications and detect waste, fraud, and abuse.

Defines terms essential for the Act's implementation, including covered applications and executive agencies.

name: Enable Intelligence Community Partnerships Act of 2024
summary:
Encourages the intelligence community to form private sector capital partnerships and consult with federal partners to improve technological advantages.

Amends public-private talent exchange authority to focus on fields including artificial intelligence, computing, and cybersecurity.

Extends the duration for temporary detail exchanges from 3 to 5 years.

Prohibits detailed private-sector employees from accessing trade secrets or proprietary information of commercial value.

Excludes private-sector organizations involved in employee detail exchanges from being considered as having organizational conflicts of interest by default.

Requires identification and mitigation of conflicts of interest based on specific participation details.

Mandates the Director of National Intelligence to submit annual reports to appropriate Congressional committees on program implementation and recommendations for enhancing the use of authorities.

name: Responsible AI Disclosure Act of 2024
summary:
Enacts the "Responsible AI Disclosure Act of 2024".

Mandates a study by covered agencies to establish and recommend standards for AI data categorization, AI model training practices, and data source identification.

Requires assessment of AI model design, functionality, and compliance with federal laws including anti-discrimination and consumer protection.

Obligates the issuance of a report within six months from enactment, detailing study findings and advising on potential legislative or regulatory revisions regarding AI disclosures.

Empowers covered agencies, post-report, to mandate AI data reporting and disclosure by regulated entities and vendors, including data sources and model training specifics.

Urges implementation of such requirements prior to report completion if deemed necessary.

Defines "covered agencies" as key financial regulatory bodies, and "regulated entities" as those overseen by these agencies, including credit unions and financially regulated persons.

name: American FATE Act, Sec 112 ("Mitigating bias in artificial intelligence use.")
summary:
Require international affairs agencies to employ experts, including technologists, social scientists, and legal experts, to develop a risk-mitigation framework for trustworthy AI systems, addressing bias in AI training data and applications.

Mandate reports from each agency to appropriate congressional committees, describing efforts to ensure safe, secure, and trustworthy AI development and use, including testing and correcting for bias, starting one year after the enactment of the Act and every two years for the following eight years.

Impose a congressional expectation to implement measures addressing AI bias to prevent negative or discriminatory outcomes in agency operations.

name: A bill to require a study on the use of commercial products and AI technologies by the IRS.
summary:
Mandates the Comptroller General to conduct a study and report to Congress on the IRS's use of commercial-off-the-shelf products and AI technologies within 12 months of the Act's enactment.

Identifies the IRS's use of such technologies to enhance operational efficiency, improve taxpayer services, generate cost savings, ensure fair enforcement, and improve tax collection efforts.

Requires the study to assess how the IRS manages AI-related risks, including errors, bias in audit selection, and data security.

Includes information on IT modernization projects, detailing contractors, project scope, costs, and contracting approaches.

Analyzes the allocation of expenses between contractors and IRS employees and compares costs between customized projects and commercial product alternatives.

name: To prohibit the Secretary of Defense from entering into information technology contracts with entities that provide certain services to China, and for other purposes.
summary:
Prohibits the Secretary of Defense from entering, renewing, or extending IT contracts with entities involved with certain AI-related operations in China.

Forbids contracts with entities controlling facilities in China focused on AI research or development.

Restricts contracts with entities that have allowed Chinese entities access to U.S. government software source codes.

Bans contracts with entities providing military, law enforcement, or dual-use software to Chinese entities.

Prohibits contracts with entities operating data centers in China.

Allows the Secretary to waive these prohibitions if necessary for U.S. national security.

Applies these prohibitions to contracts during three years post-enactment.

Defines “covered Chinese entity” and “material interest” for clarity and enforcement.

name: Stop Smuggling Illicit Synthetic Drugs on U.S. Transportation Networks Act of 2024, Section 103. "Development of strategy to accelerate research and development of non-intrusive, advanced inspection technologies to detect illicit synthetic drugs"
summary:
Require the Director of the Office of Science and Technology Policy and the Director of the Office of National Drug Control Policy to develop a strategy for accelerating the research, development, and deployment of advanced inspection technologies, including AI and quantum computing, to detect illicit synthetic drugs.

Mandate coordination with multiple agencies, including the National Science Foundation and the National Institute of Standards and Technology.

Instruct submission of a report on the strategy to specified congressional committees within two years of the Act's enactment.

name: To amend and reauthorize the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act and the Older Americans Act of 1965, Sec. 174., Subsection (a).
summary:
Amends Section 169 of the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act to evaluate programs using emerging technology, including AI, for enhancing labor market information and data integration.

Mandates studies to assess AI's effectiveness in workforce systems, emphasizing technology's impact on service delivery, labor market data, end-user tools, and potential biases.

Requires analysis of how automation affects employment, skills development, and worker displacement.

Demands evaluation of AI and machine learning adoption by States in workforce systems, assessing accuracy and identifying biases.

Calls for alignment studies between workforce and education systems, using data integration to improve outcomes.

Obliges reports on AI-related studies and evaluations to be submitted to relevant Senate and House Committees and published publicly.

Sets limits on using authority if certain evaluations are not initiated or completed timely.

Requires Secretary-conducted evaluations on the effectiveness of programs under various conditions.

name: Transparency in Bureaucratic Communications Act
summary:
Amends the Inspector General Act of 1978 to require a detailed description of communications between federal establishments and internet service or content providers. 

Includes communications concerning content moderation, user content such as posts, photos, and videos, and any interactions related to data inputs, algorithms, modeling, simulation processes, analysis tools, or related technologies.

Aims to enhance transparency in bureaucratic communications with digital platforms.

name: SCAM Platform Act
summary:
Mandates the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to develop an artificial intelligence-based tool to help the public identify likely scams within one year of this Act's enactment.

Requires the AI tool to accept various submission formats including emails, text messages, website URLs, and scans or photographs of physical materials.

Obliges the tool to evaluate the likelihood of submissions being scams and provide a rating to reflect this likelihood.

Defines "artificial intelligence" as per the National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020.

Defines "scam" as any scheme designed to defraud by inducing a recipient to take actions against their interest, through false or misleading information.

name: To amend and reauthorize the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act and the Older Americans Act of 1965, Sec. 119. Subsection (c).
summary:
Amends Section 116(e) of the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act to require the use of data for conducting analyses and ongoing evaluations of state programs.

Allows states to use machine learning and other advanced analytics to enhance program operations and outcomes.

Encourages identification of areas needing further evaluation through advanced data analysis techniques.

name: CISA Securing AI Task Force Act
summary:
Establishes a Task Force within the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency to coordinate efforts related to AI safety and security.

Requires coordination of Agency efforts to improve the safe and secure design, development, adoption, and deployment of AI.

Ensures Agency collaboration in interagency and nongovernment AI-related initiatives.

Mandates assessment and evaluation of Agency safety initiatives to address AI challenges.

Leverages expertise to use AI in defending against cyber threats.

Coordinates efforts to advise stakeholders on AI-related cyber risks.

Identifies AI workforce gaps and proposes solutions.

Promotes secure adoption of AI-based software.

Recommends new initiatives for AI safety and security.

Ensures AI efforts meet privacy, civil rights, and civil liberties standards.

Supports publication and accuracy of the Agency’s AI use inventory.

Mandates biannual briefings to Congress on Task Force activities.

Sunsets the Act 5 years after enactment.

name: No AI Audits Act
summary:
Limits the Internal Revenue Service's (IRS) use of artificial intelligence (AI) for audits or investigations.

Requires any IRS guidance on AI for audits to follow rule-making procedures under Section 553 of Title 5, U.S. Code.

Prohibits the IRS from conducting audits or investigations initiated by AI unless the AI meets explainability principles set by the National Institute of Standards and Technology.

Defines "artificial intelligence" according to the National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020.

Mandates the Comptroller General to audit and report on the IRS's AI use, including a cost-benefit analysis and the impact on taxpayer rights.

Stipulates that IRS investigations or examinations must be initiated by a staff investigator, with documentation including the investigator's contact information.

name: AWARE Act of 2024
summary:
Mandates the Secretary of Defense to create a ledger of all uses by the Department of Defense of AI-enabled weapon, targeting, and decision support systems within three years.

Requires the ledger to be a structured, indexed database that is regularly updated.

Calls on the Secretary of Defense to develop a risk assessment process to evaluate dependability, cybersecurity, privacy, and civilian harm risk for each AI system.

Mandates annual reevaluations of each system, and when an AI model receives an update, a new system is procured, or a new weapons review is conducted.

Requires annotations in the ledger when AI systems are shared, exported, or used internationally, noting additional risks.

Obligates annual progress reports and submissions to Congress, including the ledger and risk assessment findings, to be publicly accessible

name: Data Protection Act of 2024
summary:
Establishes the Data Protection Agency (DPA) as an independent entity responsible for regulating high-risk data practices and the collection, processing, and sharing of personal data. 

Defines high-risk data practices, which include the use of automated decision systems and processes involving biometric information, and mandates high-risk data practice risk assessments and impact evaluations.

Empowers the DPA to issue rules, conduct investigations, enforce federal privacy law, and impose penalties on violators.

Requires large data aggregators, those with significant revenue or who process data of many individuals, to report compliance and undergo regular examinations.

Transfers certain rulemaking and enforcement powers from the Federal Trade Commission to the DPA.

Mandates coordination with other federal and state agencies to ensure consistent privacy regulation.

Allows states to enforce protections, provided they do not conflict with this act. 

Authorizes appropriations for the DPA's operations and activities.

name: New York A 8808, Part MM (Artificial Intelligence Deceptive Practices Act)
summary:
Enacts laws addressing artificial intelligence (AI) deceptive practices to protect privacy and combat unauthorized digital alterations. 

Defines "digitization" as using AI and other technologies to alter realistic images or audio. 

Amends civil rights laws to establish a private right of action for false light invasion of privacy and unauthorized use of likeness or voice, including digitally altered depictions. 

Requires platforms and individuals to obtain consent before disseminating digitized images or audio depicting individuals in sensitive contexts without consent.

Mandates disclosures for political communications produced with digitized deceptive media within 60 days of an election, excluding satire, parody, or news reporting.

Prohibits coercion or impersonation using digitization, with heightened penalties for identity theft involving AI-altered representations. 

Allows legal actions against those intentionally causing emotional, financial, or social harm via AI-fabricated media. 

Incorporates these provisions into criminal and election laws, with penalties for violations and the possibility for injunctive relief.

name: North Carolina HB 591 (Modernize Sex Crimes)
summary:
Amends offenses related to sexual extortion by making it a criminal act to use threats involving private images, including those modified by AI, to coerce victims, punishable as felonies depending on the circumstances.

Enhances definitions related to minors in sexual content, including AI-modified images, and escalates penalties for various degrees of exploitation, employing AI tools.

Mandates reporting to authorities if AI technology is used to distribute unlawful material depicting minors, extending jurisdiction over such offenses.

Incorporates AI-generated images into existing laws against the unauthorized disclosure of private images, classifying violations as felonies and establishing a civil cause of action.

Updates sex offender registration guidelines, emphasizing offenses involving digital or AI-enhanced sexual exploits of minors.

Sets effective date for enforcement of these provisions as December 1, 2024.

name: Proposed Model AI Governance Framework for Generative AI
summary:
Proposes a Model AI Governance Framework for Generative AI emphasizing accountability, data quality, trusted development, and deployment, aligning with global best practices.

Establishes accountability by encouraging clear responsibility allocation among stakeholders within AI development chains and calls for extending cloud shared responsibility models to AI.

Emphasizes data quality, including the use of trusted data sources and addressing issues around personal data and copyright material for model training.

Calls for transparency in AI model safety measures, akin to "food labels," and suggests industry-standard practices for development, safety evaluation, and disclosure.

Proposes implementing incident reporting and third-party testing frameworks for AI safety and assurance.

Advocates for security measures specifically adapted for generative AI, including new tools and methods.

Highlights the importance of research in AI safety and alignment, international cooperation, and the use of AI for public good, including democratization of access and responsible AI adoption in public services.

name: Michigan H 5507 (School Aid)
summary:
Allocates up to $500,000 to enhance awareness and responsible use of artificial intelligence in schools.

Requires Michigan Virtual University to integrate AI principles in its training programs for educational personnel.

Mandates the Michigan Virtual Learning Research Institute to research and recommend virtual education delivery models leveraging AI.

Instructs the institute to analyze and report on AI-enhanced virtual learning effectiveness by reviewing data from virtual course providers.

Encourages partnerships with districts to study AI-driven competency-based virtual learning models.

Tasks the institute with policy recommendations to the governor on AI and virtual learning implementation.

Designates funds for AI-related professional development programs for educators and stakeholders.

Requires ongoing reports on the implementation of AI in virtual education, including its effectiveness, with a focus on elevating education delivery models in Michigan.

Supports the dissemination of best practices and standards for AI-integrated virtual learning across the state.

name: New Jersey S 3432 (Next New Jersey Program Act)
summary:
Establishes the "Next New Jersey Program" to drive investment into New Jersey’s AI sector, creating jobs and economic opportunities.

Requires businesses to invest a minimum of $100 million in capital and create at least 100 new full-time jobs to be eligible for tax credits.

Mandates businesses or divisions engaged in AI or large-scale AI data centers, demonstrating over 50% of revenue or employment in AI activities.

Stipulates collaboration with New Jersey-based research entities or startups.

Enforces compliance with environmental and labor standards, including prevailing wage for construction workers.

Enables businesses meeting criteria to apply for tax credits valid until March 1, 2029.

Empowers the New Jersey Economic Development Authority to oversee eligibility and award decisions, ensuring businesses remain compliant to retain credits.

Allows tax credit transfer certificates, with conditions on their sale and application.

Caps overall tax credits under the act at $250 million annually from a broader $11.5 billion limit across various programs over nine years.

name: Wyoming H 1 (General Government Appropriations), Section 067
summary:
Appropriates $2.5 million for building artificial intelligence expertise at the University of Wyoming, requiring a matching ratio of 1:1 from non-public sources.

Specifies that the AI-related funding should not be included in the university's standard budget for the next fiscal biennium.

Conditions the use of AI funds upon securing matched contributions from individuals, partnerships, corporations, or other entities.

Prohibits the transfer or expenditure of AI appropriation for any purpose other than building AI expertise.

Includes intent for developing AI expertise funding to be temporary and contingent on nonstate matching funds.

States that the appropriation's intent is not to support any office or program related to diversity, equity, and inclusion.

Overall, emphasizes the development of AI expertise through matched funding, with specific conditions and limitations on its use and future budget inclusion.

name: Utah H 534 (Boards and Commissions Modifications), Section 55-56
summary:
Amends legislation to define "deep technology" to include artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies.

Mandates the development and oversight of a deep technology talent initiative by the board, effective May 1, 2024.

Requires institutions of higher education to submit proposals for partnering with employers to create programs in deep technology fields.

Stipulates proposal criteria must include program responsiveness to state needs, partnerships, and employer involvement.

Obligates the advisory council to review and prioritize program proposals based on capacity expansion, integration, and cost-effectiveness.

Directs the board to fund approved programs by evaluating recommendations from the advisory council and considering legislative appropriations.

Requires funded institutions to report annually on program activities and outcomes, including student enrollment and employment metrics.

Compels the board to provide an annual report on program successes and challenges to legislative committees.

name: Measures for Promoting Innovation and Development of Artificial General Intelligence in Beijing
summary:
Mobilizes commercial computing resources to meet the requirements of the AGI sector, showcasing cooperation with cloud service providers to enhance access to diverse and high-quality computing power.

Promotes the construction of new computing facilities, including the Beijing AI Public Computing Power Center, to advance computing capabilities.

Establishes an integrated multi-cloud computing management platform to optimize computing power management and operations.

Collects high-quality training datasets, ensuring legal compliance and promoting the trading of data through legitimate channels.

Plans to set up data training bases and a crowdsourcing service platform for dataset annotation, enhancing data quality and collaboration.

Explores innovative algorithms for large models, supporting an open-source technical ecosystem and developing governance tools for data management.

Facilitates the practical application of AGI in various sectors, including government, medicine, finance, and urban governance.

Innovates regulatory policies, promoting inclusive and prudent supervision systems while strengthening network and data security.

name: Virginia SB 731 (Child Pornography)
summary:
Defines "child pornography" to include sexually explicit visual material involving identifiable or depicted minors, affecting both real and digitally created images.

Establishes penalties for production, solicitation, and financing of child pornography, escalating based on the minor’s age and the offender's age difference, with mandatory minimum sentences.

Infers depicted individuals presented as minors under 18 in visual material are minors for the purposes of prosecution.

Allows prosecution in the jurisdiction where the act occurs, the offender resides, or where the material is associated.

Notes potential increases in imprisonment periods, requiring a minimum fiscal impact assignment of $50,000 due to unknown appropriations for adult and juvenile facilities.

name: G20 Ministerial Statement on Trade and Digital Economy (Annex "G20 AI Principles")
summary:
Support the responsible stewardship of trustworthy AI by engaging stakeholders to achieve inclusive growth, sustainable development, and well-being.

Require AI actors to respect human-centered values, including the rule of law, human rights, and democratic values, throughout the AI lifecycle, supported by appropriate safeguards.

Commit AI actors to transparency and explainability, providing clear information to foster AI understanding and accountability.

Ensure robustness, security, and safety of AI systems, with traceability and systematic risk management throughout their lifecycle.

Hold AI actors accountable for aligning with the principles based on roles and context.

Encourage governments to invest in AI R&D, supporting open, unbiased datasets, and fostering a digital AI ecosystem.

Promote an enabling policy environment for AI, ensuring policy adaptation, assessment mechanisms, and readiness for labor market transformation.

Engage in international cooperation to advance AI principles, share AI knowledge, and develop global technical standards.

Encourage multi-stakeholder collaboration to monitor AI developments and ensure adherence to these principles.

name: DIFC Data Protection Regulations, Regulation 10
authority: Government of the United Arab Emirates
summary:
Requires Deployers and Operators of autonomous and semi-autonomous systems to adhere to personal data processing principles.

Mandates clear notification to users of such systems about underlying technology and data processing purposes, with detailed descriptions of system capabilities and safeguards.

Obligates the provision of evidence of compliance with audit and certification requirements, and human intervention algorithms in cases of bias or legal non-compliance.

Imposes design requirements focused on ethics, fairness, transparency, security, and accountability.

Prohibits systems from processing personal data unless in compliance with human-defined purposes and legal frameworks.

Forbids use in high-risk processing without compliance with certification requirements and appointment of an Autonomous Systems Officer.

Deems Deployers as Controllers and Operators as Processors of personal data.

Allows data subjects to challenge processing outcomes per applicable law.

name: Connecticut SB 260 (Autonomous Vehicles)
summary:
Establishes a pilot program for testing fully autonomous vehicles in up to four municipalities, requiring participation from autonomous vehicle testers and compliance with specific operational constraints.

Mandates that autonomous vehicle testers register vehicles, provide liability insurance, and ensure a licensed operator is present who can take manual control if needed.

Prohibits testing on limited access highways and allows the Secretary of the Office of Policy and Management to halt testing if public safety is at risk or compliance issues arise.

Creates a task force to study autonomous vehicle regulation, evaluate national and state standards, and assess the pilot program, providing reports on findings and recommendations for potential legislation.

Requires the Secretary to submit annual reports on the pilot program's progress to the General Assembly’s transportation committee.

Stipulates the task force composition, appointment deadlines, and reporting requirements, with a final report due by January 1, 2019.

name: Simplify IRS Act, Sec. 201 ("Tax Gap Projection")
summary:
Mandates the Commissioner of Internal Revenue to use artificial intelligence, including neural machine learning, to reduce taxpayer burden during National Research Program audits and improve the accuracy of tax gap projections.

Requires use of AI and data analysis tools to calculate and project the tax gap, which is the difference between taxes owed and taxes collected.

Prohibits conducting more National Research Program audits in any fiscal year than the number conducted in fiscal year 2022. 

Obligates the Commissioner to submit an annual tax gap projection to Congress, detailing the estimate using the latest data available, by July 31 each year.

Defines the term "tax gap" as the difference between tax liabilities owed under the Internal Revenue Code and those actually collected by the IRS.

name: New Mexico S 192 (Appropriations and Legislative Confidentiality), Section 9.
summary: Appropriates $290,000 for the purchase of artificial intelligence equipment and to contract with consultants at the ASK Academy Charter School in Sandoval County.

name: Oklahoma H 3642 (Oklahoma Law on Obscenity and Child Pornography)
summary:
Amends Oklahoma laws to enhance penalties for offenses involving child pornography, specifically targeting AI-generated images. 

Defines "child pornography" to include computer-generated images and altered images that depict minors in sexually explicit conduct, regardless of whether the image is real or synthetic. 

Establishes that possessing, distributing, or creating such images, including those utilizing AI technology, is a felony with penalties up to 20 years imprisonment and a $25,000 fine. 

Specifies that possession of 100 or more images constitutes aggravated possession, punishable by life imprisonment and a $10,000 fine, with required sex offender registration.  

Clarifies that AI-generated and computer-altered images count as independent offenses. 

Mandates that this act becomes effective on November 1, 2024.

name: Minnesota H 4772 (Elections policy), Sec. 76-77
summary:
Amends Minnesota law to criminalize the dissemination of deep fakes intended to influence elections.

Prohibits the distribution of deep fakes within 90 days before elections or political conventions without consent if intended to harm a candidate or influence election outcomes.

Excludes broadcasters following federal law from these prohibitions.

Imposes penalties for violations, including imprisonment up to five years and fines up to $10,000 based on prior offenses or intent to cause harm.

Requires that candidates convicted under this law forfeit their nomination or office.

Disqualifies individuals convicted under this law from holding certain public offices.

Sets the effective date for July 1, 2024, applicable to crimes committed thereafter.

name: Minnesota S 2909 (State Government)
summary:
Requires the superintendent to prepare an annual report on the Minnesota Fusion Center (MNFC), detailing its general activities and monitored types, including AI or social media analysis tools.

Mandates inclusion of the MNFC's budget, staffing, and the technological tools utilized, specifically AI and data analysis technologies.

Obliges reporting on audit findings, data requests, suspicious activity reports (SARs), and the impact of AI tools in processing these reports.

Specifies the report must contain information on the MNFC's collaborations with local, state, and federal agencies, including data sharing and investigations aided by SARs and requests for information (RFIs).

Ensures the report's availability to relevant legislative committees and online by February 15 each year, starting in 2024.

name: California (2017) AB 1444 (Livermore Amador Valley Transit Authority)
summary:
Authorize the Livermore Amador Valley Transit Authority to conduct a shared autonomous vehicle (SAV) demonstration project in the City of Dublin, California, for vehicles lacking traditional controls such as a steering wheel or pedals.

Require vehicles to operate below 35 miles per hour.

Mandate obtaining insurance or self-insurance of five million dollars and approval from local authorities.

Certify compliance with federal safety standards and National Highway Traffic Safety Administration guidance, ensuring vehicles operate only in approved conditions.

Require disclosure of personal data collection to participants and establish a law enforcement interaction plan.

Oblige reporting of accidents and disengagements during testing to the Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV).

Allow the DMV to require data collection for safety evaluations.

Specify that the section becomes inoperative on May 1, 2018, and repeals on January 1, 2019.

Clarify that this project does not influence statewide autonomous vehicle regulations.

name: 2023 Remarks by Ambassador Zhang at the UNSC Briefing on AI
summary:
Calls for adherence to ethical principles in AI development, emphasizing people-oriented AI and the need to establish ethical norms and regulatory systems tailored to national conditions.

Stresses safety and controllability, urging the international community to establish risk control mechanisms and accountability structures to prevent AI misuse and autonomous lethal technologies.

Advocates for fairness and inclusiveness, highlighting the importance of ensuring equal access to AI benefits for developing countries and opposing technological hegemony and exclusionary practices.

Promotes openness and inclusivity, encouraging international cooperation across disciplines, regions, and organizations under the UN framework to create a non-discriminatory environment for AI.

Emphasizes peaceful utilization of AI, underscoring the necessity of AI for sustainable development and responsible defense policies to prevent its misuse in military contexts.

Underlines China's commitment to international cooperation in AI governance, referencing past initiatives and ongoing efforts to establish a global framework for AI security governance.

name: Michigan HB 5143 (Campaign Finance Act)
summary:
Define "artificial intelligence" as a machine-based system capable of making predictions, recommendations, or decisions for human-defined objectives, affecting real or virtual environments, using both machine and human inputs.

Mandate AI systems to perceive environments, abstract perceptions into models through automated analysis, and use model inference for decision-making.

Condition enactment of this amendment on the passage of House Bill No. 5141.

name: California SB 1398 (Consumer notices of automated vehicles)
summary:
Prohibits dealers or manufacturers in California from selling or upgrading vehicles with partial driving automation features without providing a distinct notice, including the feature's name, functions, and limitations.

Prevents manufacturers or dealers from using language in marketing materials that implies partial driving automation features make a vehicle autonomous when it does not.

Defines "partial driving automation feature" according to the Society of Automotive Engineers' Level 2 partial driving automation.

Affirms that compliance with these provisions does not alter existing duty of care or civil liability for manufacturers or dealers.

Obligates manufacturers to provide dealers with necessary information to comply with notice requirements.

Exempts manufacturers from violation if they provide required information to dealers and dealers fail to notify buyers.

States that no reimbursement is needed under California's constitutional provisions due to changes in crime definition or penalties.

name: Google AI Principles
summary:
Commit to developing AI responsibly, focusing on social benefits by evaluating potential applications for transformative impacts in various fields.

Seek to avoid creating or reinforcing unfair biases, particularly concerning sensitive characteristics.

Ensure AI systems are designed and tested for safety, applying strong security practices and closely monitoring post-deployment.

Maintain accountability to people by allowing for feedback, explanations, and human control over AI technologies.

Incorporate privacy principles, offering notice, consent, and transparency, while upholding privacy safeguards in AI architecture.

Aspire to scientific excellence, leveraging AI for advancements in critical scientific areas.

Limit use to applications adhering to these principles, considering factors like purpose, uniqueness, scale, and Google's role.

Prohibit AI involvement in technologies causing harm, weapons, surveillance violating norms, or contravening international law. 

Adapt the prohibitions list as AI experience grows.

name: Maryland H 1390 (Public School Construction Funding and Administration), Sec. 5.
summary:
Directs the Interagency Commission on School Construction to report to the General Assembly by December 15, 2024.

Requires the report to assess the eligibility for school construction funding for artificial intelligence weapon detection systems.

name: Illinois HB 4844, Sec 90 ("Generative AI and Natural Language Processing Task Force")
summary:
Amends the Department of Innovation and Technology Act by establishing the Generative AI and Natural Language Processing Task Force.

Mandates the Task Force to investigate and report on generative AI and natural language processing software.

Comprises the Task Force of government officials, educators, cybersecurity experts, AI experts, business and labor association members, and other stakeholders.

Requires the Task Force to hold at least five public meetings across various Illinois regions in a hybrid format.

Obligates the Task Force to recommend legislation to protect consumer information, suggest model policies for AI use in schools, and assess AI's impact on public services, civil rights, the workforce, and cybersecurity.

Instructs the Department to provide administrative and technical support to the Task Force.

Requires the Task Force to file a report by December 31, 2024, with the Governor and the General Assembly summarizing its findings and recommendations.

name: New Jersey (2019) AJR 164 (Advanced Autonomous Vehicle Task Force)
summary:
Establishes the "New Jersey Advanced Autonomous Vehicle Task Force" to study and recommend policies for the safe integration of autonomous vehicles on state roads.

Comprises 11 members, including key state officials and public experts appointed by the Governor.

Mandates the task force to hold its initial meeting within 90 days of the law's effective date and to elect a chair from among its members.

Requires the task force to issue a report within 180 days after its first meeting, evaluating existing laws, proposing pilot programs, and suggesting legislative measures.

Entitles the task force to utilize the services of state employees and receive assistance from the New Jersey Motor Vehicle Commission, Department of Transportation, and Alan M. Voorhees Transportation Center.

Defines "advanced autonomous vehicle" as one with a driving automation level of 3, 4, or 5, per SAE J3016 standards.

Expires the act upon the report's submission.

name: Iowa S 2243 (Sexual Exploitation of Minors, Use of Falsely Created Images)
summary:
Amends existing law to make it unlawful to knowingly purchase or possess visual depictions of a minor engaging in a prohibited sexual act or its simulation.

Requires separate prosecution and punishment for each different minor depicted in such visual content, though multiple depictions of the same minor are treated as a single offense.

Classifies a first offense as a class "D" felony and a second or subsequent offense as a class "C" felony.

Establishes that prior convictions or deferred judgments under this law, or similar laws in other jurisdictions, constitute second or subsequent offenses.

name: South Carolina 2023 H 4754 (Sec 4)
summary:
Amends Article 7, Chapter 57, Title 40 of the S.C. Code by adding Section 40-57-820.

Holds a licensee accountable for all work produced with the assistance of artificial intelligence, machine learning, or similar programs.

Treats violations committed through the use of these technologies as if committed directly by the licensee.

name: Oregon S 5701 (State Financial Administration), Section 488.
summary:
Increases the General Fund appropriation to the Higher Education Coordinating Commission for public university programs by $100,000.

Allocates this increased funding to the University of Oregon Labor Education and Research Center.

Directs the Center to research the potential workforce impacts of automation and artificial intelligence across Oregon’s key economic industries.

name: G20 Ministerial Statement on Trade and Digital Economy (Sec I, Subsec 3 "Human-centered Artificial Intelligence")
summary:
Endeavors to create an enabling environment for human-centered AI that fosters innovation, investment, digital entrepreneurship, and adoption of AI by MSMEs.

Recognizes AI's potential to promote inclusive economic growth and societal benefits, advancing sustainable and inclusive societies while empowering individuals.

Commits to addressing societal challenges posed by AI, such as transitions in the labor market, privacy, security, and ethical issues, through a human-centered approach guided by the G20 AI Principles.

Stipulates principles of inclusive growth, human-centered values, transparency, robustness, and accountability to maximize AI benefits while minimizing risks, with a focus on international cooperation and inclusion of developing countries.

Affirms the need to promote privacy protection, AI capacity building, and skills development.

Commits to international cooperation in research, policy development, and information sharing through the G20 Repository of Digital Policies and collaborative efforts.

name: North Carolina Current Operations Appropriations Act of 2023, SECTION 7.36.(h)
summary:
Allocates $3.2 million to New Hanover County Schools and $2 million to Davidson County Schools for an AI School Safety Pilot Program.

Requires use of funds to implement AI technology into existing school safety systems, including access controls, alerting protocols, and intercom systems.

Mandates participating public school units to report to the Joint Legislative Education Oversight Committee by January 15, 2025.

Directs reports to include details on school participation, fund usage, impact on safety outcomes, AI system capabilities compared to traditional safety measures, and any additional relevant information.

name: Maryland S 360 (Budget Bill Fiscal Year 2025), Section 21., Subsection (50)
summary:
Adds $500,000 in general funds to support the Center for Equitable Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Systems at Morgan State University.

Prohibits the transfer of unexpended funds to any other purpose.

Requires unspent funds to revert to the General Fund.

name: Maryland S 1068 (Evaluation and Development of a 3-1-1 Portal)
summary:
Requires the Maryland Department of Information Technology to evaluate the potential use of artificial intelligence in developing a statewide virtual 3-1-1 portal for nonemergency government information and services.

Mandates the prioritization of creating the virtual 3-1-1 portal if the AI application is deemed feasible.

Sets the effective date of this Act as July 1, 2024.

Receives approval from the Governor on May 9, 2024.

name: Washington S 5950, Sec. 129, Subsection 50
summary:
Allocate $300,000 from the general fund for fiscal year 2024 to the city of Seattle for leasing space dedicated to nonprofit and academic institutions.

Provide $500,000 for fiscal year 2025 for the same purpose.

Focus efforts on incubating technology business startups with an emphasis on artificial intelligence.

Support the development and teaching of curricula aimed at equipping workers with skills to utilize AI as a business resource.

name: DEEPFAKES Accountability Act, Sec. 2 ("Transparency Requirements")
summary:
Outlines transparency requirements for advanced technological false personation records, requiring producers of such records to include content provenance technologies to identify alterations, as well as disclosures to detail the extent of alterations.

Mandates specific disclosure formats for audiovisual, visual, and audio records.

Imposes criminal penalties, including fines and imprisonment of up to 5 years, for intentionally failing to disclose or altering existing disclosures.

Imposes civil penalties up to $150,000 per violation and allows for private rights of action for damages and injunctive relief.

Establishes coordinators for deepfake-related violations in each U.S. Attorney’s Office.

name: Sensible Classification Act of 2023
summary:
Mandates the research and recommendation of AI and machine learning solutions for efficient classification and declassification systems, to be interoperable across the Federal Government.

Requires the Administrator of the Office of Electronic Government to consult with key defense and intelligence agencies for technology implementation and submit a report on the recommended solution.

name: Federal AI Governance and Transparency Act
summary:
Amends chapter 35 of title 44, United States Code, to establish Federal AI system governance requirements.

Instructs Federal actions involving AI to align with the Constitution, relevant laws, and policies, protecting civil rights and privacy.

Mandates the assessment and management of AI risks before deployment, ensuring AI outcomes remain ethical and accurate.

Requires transparency and explainability of AI systems' purpose, operations, and outcomes to maintain safety and security, and protect against vulnerabilities.

Obligates regular testing and oversight of AI applications to ensure they align with intended purposes and create mechanisms to deactivate AI systems that do not meet standards.

Instructs agencies to publicly disclose AI use to stakeholders and establish notification and appeal processes for AI-based decisions.

Establishes a Federal AI System Inventory for cataloging agency AI governance charters to be publicly available and regularly updated.

name: H.R. 7381 (Health AI)
summary:
Establishes a grant program by the Director of the National Institutes of Health to fund research on the use of generative AI in health care.

Permits research to include enhancing note-taking, reducing administrative burdens, expediting insurance claims, improving customer service efficiency, and other health care improvements.

Prioritizes grants for entities promoting AI adoption in health care, investing in workforce development, mitigating workforce burnout, reducing health disparities, and improving care for medically underserved populations.

Defines eligible entities to include higher education institutions, nonprofit organizations, and various governmental agencies.

Defines "generative artificial intelligence" as AI producing content in response to prompts.

name: Anthropic Responsible Scaling Policy
summary:
Establishes AI Safety Level (ASL) Standards to guide safe deployment and security for current and future AI models, categorizing measures into Deployment and Security Standards.

Requires all current models to meet ASL-2 standards, focusing on safe usage and protection from unauthorized access.

Introduces Capability Thresholds to determine when stronger safeguards (ASL-3 or higher) are needed, specifying Required Safeguards for particular risks including Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear (CBRN) capabilities and Autonomous AI R&D.

Mandates comprehensive assessments to ensure models remain below Capability Thresholds, with stricter ASL-3 standards implemented if thresholds are surpassed.

Outlines internal governance practices including a Responsible Scaling Officer role, transparency measures, and procedures for noncompliance whistleblowing.

Commits to public transparency, expert input, and notifying US Government if standards beyond ASL-2 are needed.

name: TAKE IT DOWN Act
summary:
Amends the Communications Act to criminalize the non-consensual production and dissemination of pornography, especially when intended to cause harm or when involving minors.

Requires covered platforms to establish a takedown process for such depictions, and mandates them to remove the content within 48 hours upon valid request.

Levels criminal punishments, including imprisonment, on violators of this law.

Grants enforcement authority to the Federal Trade Commission.

Defines key terms relevant to the instrument, including "covered platform," "deepfake," and "intimate visual depiction."

name: Safe and Secure Innovation for Frontier AI Act (SB 1047)
summary:
Requires developers of frontier AI models to implement comprehensive safety and security protocols, including cybersecurity protections, full shutdown capabilities, and detailed risk assessments.

Mandates annual independent audits and public disclosure of redacted audit reports and obligates developers to report AI safety incidents to the Attorney General within 72 hours.

Establishes policies for entities operating computer clusters to assess whether customers intend to use the clusters for training covered models.

Creates the Board of Frontier Models to update AI model thresholds and auditing requirements, ensuring alignment with technological advancements and best practices.

Imposes penalties for non-compliance, including civil penalties, injunctive relief, and punitive damages.

Introduces CalCompute, a public cloud computing cluster to support AI research and innovation, with a framework to be developed by a consortium.

name: OpenAI Charter
summary:
Outlines OpenAI's commits to using influence over AGI deployment to ensure it benefits all of humanity and avoids harm or power concentration.

Pledges to assist other safety-conscious AGI projects nearing completion, rather than compete, under specific conditions.

Strive for technical leadership within OpenAI and cooperate with other research and policy institutions.

Commit to multistakeholder cooperation and publish its research while acknowledging potential safety and security constraints on traditional AI research publishing.

name: Provisions on the Administration of Deep Synthesis Internet Information Services
summary:
Prohibits generative AI ("deep synthesis") systems in China from producing a variety of forms of unwanted content, including false information or content that harms lawful rights, national security and "social order."

Requires deep synthesis systems to verify the true identity of each of their users.

Requires deep synthesis developers to assess the security of their AI systems, including by assessing the systems' cybersecurity attributes and their ability to abide by relevant regulations.

Requires deep synthesis systems to notify any individuals whose biometric information is edited in the production of AI-generated content.

Requires the labelling or watermarking  of realistic deep synthesis content that could potentially mislead or confuse the public.

Requires deep synthesis developers to submit filings with the relevant authorities, and requires regulators to carry out inspections of deep synthesis systems.

name: STAND with Taiwan Act
summary:
Mandates the imposition of sanctions on the People's Republic of China if the People’s Liberation Army initiates a military invasion of Taiwan. 

Requires sanctions against Chinese officials and entities involved in military campaigns or efforts undermining Taiwan's security and infrastructure.

Blocks property and imposes visa restrictions on identified Chinese officials and affiliates involved in military and coercive actions against Taiwan.

Prohibits U.S. financial institutions from investments that benefit Chinese government-controlled entities or priority sectors like artificial intelligence and other advanced technologies.

Bans the listing and trading of securities of Chinese entities on U.S. securities exchanges following an invasion.

Prohibits the importation of goods from China post-invasion unless exceptions for national security are made.

Grants the President authority to enforce sanctions and provides for penalties under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act.

name: NIST AI Risk Management Framework
authority: National Institute of Standards and Technology
summary:
Articulates characteristics of trustworthy AI, including validity, reliability, safety, security, accountability, explainability, privacy enhancement, and fairness in managing harmful bias. 

Encourages a balance of these characteristics based on AI systems' context of use, noting tradeoffs such as interpretability versus privacy. 

Emphasizes the importance of human judgment in deciding metrics and thresholds for AI trustworthiness. 

Stipulates that trustworthy AI depends on social and organizational behavior, datasets, model choices, and human interactions. 

Mandates addressing AI risks through ongoing testing, monitoring, and balancing accuracy and robustness. 

Calls for clear information and responsible decision-making to ensure safe AI operation. 

Advocates for secure and resilient AI systems that withstand adverse events and protect against unauthorized access. 

Promotes transparency and accountability to enhance confidence in AI systems, with transparency enabling actionable redress. 

Urges explainability and interpretability to improve understanding of AI system operations and outputs. 

Encourages privacy-enhancing technologies to safeguard autonomy and identity, acknowledging tradeoffs with accuracy. 

Highlights fairness in AI, addressing harmful bias and discrimination, and recognizing systemic, computational, and human-cognitive biases. 

Outlines AI risk management framework (AI RMF) functions: GOVERN, MAP, MEASURE, and MANAGE, emphasizing a continuous and iterative process. 

Specifies GOVERN function for cultivating risk management culture, policies, and accountability in AI development and deployment. 

Describes MAP function for establishing context and understanding AI system impacts to inform risk management decisions. 

Details MEASURE function for using tools and methodologies to assess AI risks and system trustworthiness. 

Explains MANAGE function for prioritizing and responding to AI risks, maximizing benefits, and managing third-party risks.

name: Artificial Intelligence Bug Bounty Act of 2023
summary:
Mandates the Chief Data and Artificial Intelligence Officer of the Department of Defense to develop a bug bounty program for AI products within 180 days of enactment.

Allows collaboration with other government agencies possessing cybersecurity and AI expertise during program development.

Authorizes the implementation of the developed bug bounty program.

Ensures that Department of Defense contracts permit participation in the bug bounty program.

Requires the Chief to brief congressional defense committees within one year on the development, implementation, and long-term plans of relevant bug bounty programs.

name: AI Labeling Act
summary:
Requires content generated by AI to include clear and conspicuous disclosures marking content as AI-generated. 

Mandates the disclosure to identify content as AI-generated, the tool used to create output, and the creation date and time, ensuring disclosures are permanent or not easily removed.

Compels developers and third-party licensees of generative AI systems to implement procedures preventing content distribution without disclosures, including contractual obligations and certifying compliance.

Treats violations as unfair or deceptive acts under the Federal Trade Commission Act, granting enforcement powers to the FTC.

Establishes a working group to develop AI-generated content detection standards and assist platforms in identifying AI-generated content.

Requires the working group to publish a framework with guidelines and submit a report to Congress recommending legislative or administrative actions.

name: Colorado AI Act (SB 205)
summary:
Requires developers of high-risk AI systems to disclose foreseeable uses and risks of their systems, the inputs used in their training data, and how the systems were evaluated for performance.

Requires developers to display these disclosures publicly on their websites in a public use case inventory.

Mandates developers to disclose to the Colorado Attorney General, within 90 days, if their systems have caused or will likely cause algorithmic discrimination.

Requires deployers of high-risk AI systems to notify consumers of how AI is used to make consequential decisions and inform them of their right to opt out of the processing of their personal data.

Requires deployers to give consumers the opportunity to correct erroneous personal data and appeal adverse consequential decisions.

Mandates deployers to make all these disclosures publicly available on their websites.
