Mandates the Secretary of Transportation to commission a study through the National Academies to identify changes needed in public transportation infrastructure to improve accessibility for individuals with disabilities using ride-hail ADS-equipped vehicles.

Authorizes $5,000,000 for the completion of the accessibility infrastructure study, available until expended.

name: DEFIANCE Act of 2024
summary:
Amends the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2022, to include "digital forgery" as any intimate visual depiction created via AI or other technological means to appear indistinguishable from an authentic visual depiction.

Allows identifiable individuals to bring civil action against those who produce, possess, disclose, or solicit digital forgeries without consent, with knowledge or reckless disregard of the lack of consent.

Specifies relief for plaintiffs, including actual or liquidated damages of $150,000, attorney’s fees, and equitable relief such as injunctions.

Permits courts to issue orders to protect plaintiffs' privacy, including the use of pseudonyms and sealing personal identifying information.

Establishes a 10-year statute of limitations for actions, starting from the discovery of the violation or the individual reaching 18 years of age.

Ensures the Act does not preempt state, federal, or tribal laws that provide at least as much protection.

name: TORPEDO Act of 2023,  Sec. 12 (Expedited release of advanced technologies to Australia, Canada, and the United Kingdom through the foreign military sales program)
summary:
Requires the Secretary of State, in coordination with the Secretary of Defense, to compile a list of pre-cleared military technologies and platforms for sale to Australia, Canada, and the UK within 90 days of enactment and annually thereafter.

Expedites the processing of Foreign Military Sales requests from Australia, Canada, and the UK.

Mandates the creation of an anticipatory release policy for key Foreign Military Sales capabilities, including AI, hypersonic missiles, cyber capabilities, and quantum technologies, with a presumption of approval.

Requires the review and update of interagency policies to incorporate these anticipatory release provisions.

name: Intelligence Authorization Act FY 2024, Sec. 909 ("Ensure IC Directives Account for AI and ML Tools in Intelligence Products")
summary:
Requires the Director of National Intelligence to brief congressional intelligence committees within 120 days on whether current intelligence community directives provide sufficient guidance on the use of AI and machine learning tools in intelligence products.

Mandates the briefing to include a determination of whether Intelligence Community Directives 203 and 206, and other relevant directives, offer adequate guidance on using, sourcing, and providing transparency for AI and machine learning tools.

Requires the Director to assess if these directives need updates to enhance guidance and direction.

Obligates the Director to explain why no updates are needed if deemed sufficient, or to provide a plan and timeline for necessary updates if improvements are required.

name: Atomic Energy Advancement Act, Sec. 123 ("Nuclear Regulatory Oversight")
summary:
Requires the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) to report to Congress on actions taken during the COVID-19 emergency, including revised or suspended regulatory policies and their impacts.

Mandates NRC to develop a report within one year identifying improvements in nuclear oversight and inspections using risk-informed, performance-based procedures, information technologies, and AI.

Obligates NRC to seek input from stakeholders like the Secretary of Energy, National Laboratories, and the nuclear energy industry.

Directs NRC to assess the use of AI and machine learning to enhance oversight and inspection decisions.

Instructs NRC to identify specific actions for incorporating advanced technologies into their activities without compromising their mission.

name: Stop Fentanyl at the Border Act
summary:
Appropriates $1,090,000,000 to U.S. Customs and Border Protection for technology improvements, including non-intrusive inspection scanning systems and anomaly detection algorithms, to enhance fentanyl interdiction at land borders.

Appropriates $223,000,000 to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement to expand efforts to interdict fentanyl and disrupt transnational criminal networks, including funds for additional special agents and joint surge operations.

Mandates submission of reports by March 31, 2028, detailing impacts of Border Patrol Processing Coordinator positions, equipment needs for outbound inspections, and summaries of non-intrusive inspection technology at land ports of entry.

Creates penalties for knowingly damaging or evading border controls, with fines and imprisonment up to 5 years for violations aimed at securing financial gain or furthering criminal organizations.

name: Forest Data Modernization Act
summary:
Amends the Forest and Rangeland Renewable Resources Research Act to include forest carbon in resource assessments.

Requires the Secretary to conduct timber products output studies and national woodland owner surveys.

Mandates the integration of forest carbon data in bi-decadal reviews.

Specifies the need for clear definitions of "forest" in reporting data.

Updates strategic plan to include consistent data collection protocols, integration of new technologies, and enhanced transparency.

Ensures collected data is accessible while maintaining confidentiality of sensitive information.

Compiles and publishes biennial national forest statistics.

Establishes an office or platform to handle complex data requests, with possible fees imposed on requestors.

Publishes annual reports detailing progress on strategic plan implementation, including costs and priorities.

Amends Agriculture Improvement Act to utilize advanced remote sensing and machine learning technologies for data collection and modeling.

name: Pandemic Preparedness and Response Act, Sec. 407 ("AI Threats to Health Security")
summary:
Requires the Secretary of Health and Human Services to seek a contract with the National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine to conduct a study on AI-related health security vulnerabilities within 45 days of enactment.

Mandates the study to assess risks posed by AI advancements, including chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear threats.

Describes roles and capabilities of HHS agencies and other Federal entities in identifying and mitigating these vulnerabilities.

Summarizes ongoing Federal activities related to these risks.

Identifies current or anticipated gaps in roles, responsibilities, and capabilities regarding AI-related health security.

Provides recommendations for improving Federal efforts to address these vulnerabilities.

Requires the National Academies to submit a report on the study to relevant Senate and House committees within 2 years.

Mandates the Secretary of HHS to submit a follow-up report on actions taken to mitigate AI-related health security risks within 1 year after the National Academies' report.

name: Intelligence Authorization Act FY 2024, Sec. 906 ("Next-Generation Microelectronics for AI")
summary:
Establishes a program to advance microelectronics research, overseen by the Director of National Intelligence through the Intelligence Advanced Research Projects Activity.

Focuses research on next-generation computing models, materials, devices, architectures, and algorithms to enhance artificial intelligence and machine learning.

Addresses challenges in microelectronics engineering, including physical limits on transistors, interconnects, and memory elements.

Promotes advancements in computing technologies through multidisciplinary research, encompassing algorithm design, compute capability, generative AI, photonics-based microprocessors, new materials, optical networks, and AI safety for the intelligence community.

Requires active collaboration with government agencies, academic institutions, and private industry.

Authorizes appropriations for contracts, grants, and other transactions to support the program.

Mandates regular briefings to congressional intelligence committees on program progress, partnerships, and future research priorities.

name: Advancing Nuclear Regulatory Oversight Act
summary:
Requires the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) to report to Congress within 180 days on regulatory changes made during the COVID-19 emergency, examining their impact on licensing and safety.

Mandates the NRC to develop and submit a report within one year identifying specific improvements in oversight and inspection programs, emphasizing risk-informed, performance-based procedures and the use of advanced technologies, including AI and machine learning.

Instructs the NRC to seek input from stakeholders including the Secretary of Energy, National Laboratories, the nuclear energy industry, and relevant NGOs in developing the report.

Requires assessment of potential modifications to oversight and inspections, improvement measures, and incorporation of advanced technologies to enhance operational efficiency and safety.

Obligates the NRC to identify and implement actions based on assessments and recommendations to improve training, inspection, oversight, and licensing activities without compromising its mission.

name: Advisory for AI-Generated Content Act
summary:
Requires all AI-generated materials to be labeled with a watermark. 

Authorizes the federal government to establish requirements and standards for watermarks.

Enables the federal government to levy penalties against entities that violate the above stipulation.

Defines key terms including AI-generating entity, AI-generated material, and covered AI-generated material, specifying criteria for materials that must be watermarked.

name: SAFE from PRC Investments Act
summary:
Requires public companies and exchange-traded funds (ETFs) investing in companies with ties to the People’s Republic of China (PRC) to disclose whether senior officials of the PRC government or Communist Party of China (CPC) sit on their boards or have executive roles.

Mandates disclosure of cash held in PRC operations, restrictions on cash repatriation, and details of assets, liabilities, and technology transfers.

Obligates reporting on interactions with CPC officials, expenditures on PRC operations, and any lobbying activities in the United States.

Compels ETFs to reveal ownership, CPC branches, contractual agreements, and involvement in PRC industrial policies or military contracts of invested PRC companies.

Requires disclosure of PRC companies’ products and services, U.S. defense contracts, and involvement in sectors like AI, telecommunications, and semiconductors.

name: US-Israel Health Technologies Act
summary:
Authorizes $4,000,000 annually for fiscal years 2024 through 2026 to fund a bilateral cooperative program with Israel for developing health technologies. Emphasizes advancing technology, personalized medicine, and data usage in relation to emerging infectious diseases.

Includes artificial intelligence, drugs, vaccinations, respiratory assist devices, diagnostic tests, and telemedicine as eligible health technologies. Requires matching contributions from the Government of Israel to access funding. Allows funding for existing bilateral programs or the establishment of new programs in consultation with the Secretary of State under the 2008 Science and Technology Cooperation Agreement.

name: Department of State Authorization Act, Sec. 931 ("Priority for Australia and UK in Military Sales")
summary:
Requires the President to institute expedited policies for defense article and service requests from Australia and the United Kingdom under the AUKUS partnership.

Mandates prioritization of these requests over all others, except those from Taiwan and Ukraine.

Instructs the Secretary, in consultation with the Secretary of Defense, to establish an anticipatory release policy for technology transfers to Australia, the UK, and Canada.

Specifies the inclusion of technologies related to submarines, combat systems, hypersonic missiles, cyber capabilities, artificial intelligence, quantum technologies, and other advanced technologies.

Subjects technology transfer reviews to an expedited decision-making process.

Directs the Secretary and the Secretary of Defense to update interagency policies and guidance to incorporate these anticipatory release provisions.

name: Do Not Disturb Act
summary:
Requires disclosure at the beginning of robocalls or text messages if artificial intelligence is used to emulate a human being.

Enhances penalties for robocall and telemarketing violations involving AI impersonation, doubling fines for fraudulent or harmful AI-generated calls or messages.

Mandates the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to offer robocall-blocking services at no charge and to develop a tracking system for the top 100 illegal robocall campaigns.

Obligates Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) providers to verify customer identities, monitor robocall patterns, and report violations.

Directs both the FCC and Federal Trade Commission (FTC) to study and regulate AI usage in robocalls and telemarketing, including text message authentication and inbound call restrictions.

name: Promoting Resilient Supply Chains Act
summary:
Requires the Assistant Secretary of Commerce to promote U.S. leadership in emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI), and strengthen critical supply chains and national security.

Mandates the establishment of a critical supply chain resiliency and crisis response program within the Department of Commerce, which includes mapping and monitoring AI supply chains.

Requires coordination with other agencies, industry, and international partners to identify vulnerabilities and prepare for supply chain shocks affecting AI technologies.

Promotes the growth of domestic manufacturing capacities for AI and other emerging technologies and encourages the relocation of manufacturing facilities to the U.S. or allied countries.

Supports the development and dissemination of best practices for supply chain resilience, including the use of blockchain and other technologies to authenticate and trace critical goods.

Mandates regular reporting on the state of AI and other emerging technology supply chains, including assessments of vulnerabilities and recommendations for enhancing resilience.

name: Promoting Digital Privacy Technologies Act
summary:
Introduces the "Promoting Digital Privacy Technologies Act."

Requires the National Science Foundation to support research on privacy enhancing technologies, including de-identification, pseudonymization, and algorithms for data privacy.

Mandates integration of privacy enhancing technologies into the Computer and Network Security Program as per the Cyber Security Research and Development Act.

Obliges coordination among the Office of Science and Technology Policy, National Science Foundation, National Institute of Standards and Technology, and Federal Trade Commission to expedite development and use of privacy enhancing technologies.

Demands outreach by the National Institute of Standards and Technology to gather stakeholder input and promote private and public sector engagement.

Requires submission of a report within three years on research progress, development of voluntary resources, and policy recommendations to improve communication and coordination among stakeholders.

name: Microreactors for Natural Disaster Response Act
summary:
Mandates the President develop a national strategy for utilizing microreactors to assist with natural disaster response efforts.

Requires consultation with FEMA, DOE, National Guard, Army Corps of Engineers, and Nuclear Regulatory Commission.

Obligates submission of the strategy to Congress within one year and biennially thereafter.

Includes an assessment of current diesel generator usage and environmental impacts compared to microreactors.

Outlines goals and objectives for replacing diesel generators with microreactors.

Calls for a Department of Defense analysis on translating operational microreactor technology for disaster response.

Recommends expedited design approval and licensing for microreactors.

Assesses strategic considerations, including storage, transportation, and integration into existing grids.

Evaluates partnership opportunities for effective deployment.

Encourages the use of AI and predictive tools for disaster preparation involving microreactors.

name: Department of State Authorization Act, Sec. 303 ("AI-enabled influence operations task force")
summary:
Establishes a Countering AI-Enabled Disinformation Task Force within 180 days to identify responses to AI-enabled disinformation threats.

Requires the Task Force to collaborate with private industry and academia to develop digital content provenance detection techniques.

Mandates internal coordination within the Department on AI-enabled disinformation issues.

Directs the Task Force to create a unified international approach for standards and frameworks to counter AI-enabled disinformation.

Requires the Task Force to identify necessary tools and resources for detecting AI-enabled disinformation, producing counter-messaging, expanding digital literacy, and coordinating with various stakeholders.

Mandates a report to Congress within one year on the Task Force’s establishment and progress.

Involves representatives from various relevant offices in the Task Force.

Defines key terms including "artificial intelligence" and "digital content provenance."

name: HEARTS Act
summary:
Prioritizes nonanimal methods in NIH-supported research proposals.

Establishes the National Center for Alternatives to Animals in Research and Testing within NIH.

Requires the new center to develop, promote, and fund nonanimal research methods, including AI.

Mandates the center to provide training and resources to researchers on nonanimal methods.

Obligates federally funded research entities to report the number and species of animals used and plans to reduce their use.

Ensures research proposals are reviewed by experts in nonanimal methods.

Implements a system of incentives to encourage the use of humane and scientifically satisfactory nonanimal methods.

Requires thorough searches for nonanimal alternatives before approving animal use in research.

name: Diversify Tech Act
summary:
Establishes a Tech Industry Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Accessibility (DEIA) Task Force within the Department of Commerce.

Mandates the Task Force to conduct audits on minority representation, hiring policies, and layoff trends in the tech industry.

Requires submission of an initial audit report to Congress within 60 days of the Task Force’s establishment.

Obliges the Task Force to promote DEIA, offer guidance to tech entities, and consult with stakeholders on DEIA issues.

Tasks the Task Force with advising on outreach programs and encouraging venture capital investment in minority-owned startups.

Mandates annual reports evaluating tech industry progress on DEIA goals, the impact of AI on discrimination, and proposing policy solutions for accountability.

Requires a special report on how 2023 tech layoffs affected DEIA, including potential violations of federal laws.

name: Vehicle Technologies R&D Act
summary:
Requires the Secretary of Energy to conduct a research, development, and demonstration program for advanced vehicle technologies, focusing on reducing greenhouse gas emissions and vehicle manufacturing costs.

Mandates coordination with other federal agencies and existing programs on electric vehicle integration and critical material recycling.

Supports the development of advanced batteries, power electronics, electric drive systems, and vehicle electrification technologies.

Includes provisions for cybersecurity and physical security of vehicle interconnections with the electric grid and other infrastructure.

Establishes a program for medium- and heavy-duty commercial and transit vehicles, emphasizing advanced energy technologies and efficiency improvements.

Authorizes the creation of Graduate Automotive Technology Education Centers of Research Excellence to foster advancements in automotive energy technologies.

Allocates substantial funding for these initiatives through fiscal year 2028, with a total authorization exceeding $2.9 billion.

name: Department of State Authorization Act, Sec. 941 ("Reporting Related to AUKUS")
summary:
Mandates the President to submit the text of any non-binding instrument related to the AUKUS partnership to appropriate congressional committees within 30 days of finalization.

Excludes the need to resubmit texts already submitted under other legal provisions, while not relieving other legal submission requirements.

Defines "text" to include all related annexes, appendices, side agreements, and implementing documents.

Requires the Secretary, in coordination with other officials, to submit a biennial report on the AUKUS partnership starting one year after enactment.

Specifies that reports must cover defensive capability gaps, costs, industrial base contributions, military benefits, and assessments of Australia’s nuclear submarine contributions.

Demands updates on progress for Australia’s nuclear submarine development, infrastructure, workforce training, and support facilities.

Requires assessments of trilateral collaboration efforts in areas including underseas capabilities, quantum technologies, AI and autonomy, advanced cyber capabilities, hypersonic technologies, electronic warfare, innovation, and information sharing.

name: Food and Agriculture Industry Cybersecurity Support Act
summary:
Establishes a food and agriculture cybersecurity clearinghouse within the NTIA to provide publicly available online resources focused on cybersecurity for the food and agriculture industry.

Requires the clearinghouse to offer in-person or virtual support, updated FAQs, and materials for small businesses on critical cybersecurity protections and ransomware response.

Mandates the consolidation of public and private sector best practices into voluntary cybersecurity recommendations for the food and agriculture industry, including continuous monitoring and ransomware attack responses.

Instructs the Assistant Secretary to consult with private sector, federal agencies, trade groups, and civil society organizations in implementing the clearinghouse.

Directs the Comptroller General to study and report on federal efforts to improve cybersecurity in the food and agriculture industry, evaluating effectiveness, resources, coordination, and potential risks of coordinated attacks.

Sunsets the section seven years after enactment.

name: Outbound Investment Transparency Act
summary:
Requires mandatory notification by U.S. persons engaging in specific foreign investments related to advanced sectors, including artificial intelligence, to the Secretary of the Treasury.

Defines covered activities involving equity interests, debt obligations with governance rights, and joint ventures in countries of concern, with specific focus on AI and other advanced technologies.

Establishes penalties for non-compliance, including failure to notify or providing false information.

Mandates the creation of regulations to ensure clarity and minimize compliance burdens, with a focus on transparency and stakeholder involvement.

Directs the Secretary of State to engage with allied countries to coordinate investment screening mechanisms and share information on covered activities.

Requires annual reporting to Congress on trends, national security risks, and recommendations related to these foreign investments in AI and other sectors.

name: Health Care Price Transparency Act, Sec. 301 ("Requirements Regarding Prior Authorization Under Medicare Advantage Plans")
summary:
Requires Medicare Advantage plans to establish an electronic prior authorization program by the third plan year after the enactment date.

Mandates that plans meet enrollee protection standards and transparency requirements by the fourth plan year.

Establishes a secure electronic transmission system for prior authorization requests and responses, excluding certain forms like facsimiles and non-compliant payer portals.

Specifies that real-time decisions must be made for certain prior authorization requests, with exceptions for extenuating circumstances.

Demands detailed annual reporting of prior authorization data, including the use of AI and decision-support technologies, and the publication of this information by the Secretary.

Calls for GAO and HHS to submit reports to Congress evaluating the implementation and impact of these requirements.

name: STOP HATE Act
summary:
Requires social media companies to make their terms of service publicly available.

Requires social media companies to disclose content moderation data, including the total number of flagged items, actioned items, user engagement, and how artificial intelligence is used to support content moderation efforts.

Allows Attorney General's office to bring a civil penalty of $5,000,000 per violation per day against social media companies who fail to meet these requirements

name: Medical Debt Transparency Act
summary:
Amends the Public Health Service Act to prohibit health care entities and their debt collectors from initiating extraordinary collection actions if a health insurance appeal is pending.

Mandates health care entities to determine patients' eligibility for assistance programs before commencing extraordinary collection actions.

Prohibits extraordinary collection actions until 180 days after the initial bill is sent to the patient.

Requires health care entities to provide patients with itemized statements and detailed payment receipts, and information on language assistance services.

Establishes a public database for medical debt collection, requiring health care entities to submit detailed annual reports, including data on debt collection practices and patient demographics.

Imposes penalties for non-compliance, including actual damages and additional court-permitted amounts.

Requires the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau to report on medical debt collections, incorporating data from the public database and other sources.

name: Exploitative Workplace Technologies Task Force Act
summary:
Establishes the White House Task Force on Workplace Surveillance and Technologies within 180 days of enactment.

Mandates the Task Force to study and evaluate the use of workplace surveillance and automated decision systems by employers.

Requires the Task Force to analyze the prevalence, types, and impacts of workplace surveillance across industries, including data collection, storage, security, and transfer practices.

Necessitates examination of the effects of workplace surveillance on worker compensation, performance reviews, scheduling, career advancement, safety, health coverage, and discipline.

Obligates the Task Force to consider the impact on vulnerable populations, including workers with disabilities, low-wage workers, and workers of color.

Orders the Task Force to submit initial, interim, and final reports to Congress, detailing findings and providing recommendations on addressing workplace surveillance and related technologies.

Terminates the Task Force 60 days after submitting the final report.

name: CONSULT Act
summary:
Requires the Department of Defense to refrain from awarding contracts to any individual or entity, including those producing AI-powered products and services, that has worked with any organization from a blacklist of national security threats.

Authorizes the DOD to punish any contractor of the Department who has a proven conflict of interest with the DOD and fails to disclose that conflict of interest.

name: Preventing Adversaries from Developing Critical Capabilities Act
summary:
Prohibits U.S. persons from engaging in covered activities involving certain technologies and products in countries of concern, particularly in sectors like AI, if they pose acute national security threats.

Requires the President to annually identify and publish lists of such critical technologies and products.

Mandates U.S. persons to notify the President of any covered activities that may threaten national security.

Empowers the President to impose civil penalties for violations and to delegate enforcement authority to federal agencies.

Encourages bilateral and multilateral engagements to promote compliance with these prohibitions and notifications.

Allocates $25 million annually for implementation and allows direct hiring to support administration.

Permits the President to issue waivers for activities deemed in the national interest, with required congressional notification.

name: Department of State Authorization Act, Sec. 304 ("DOS Chief AI Officer")
summary:
Establishes within the Department of State a Chief Artificial Intelligence Officer (CAIO), potentially dual-hatted as the Department’s Chief Data Officer, and a member of the Senior Executive Service.

Requires the CAIO to evaluate, oversee, and facilitate the responsible adoption of AI and machine learning to inform decisions and support programs and operations.

Designates the CAIO as the principal advisor to the Secretary of State on the ethical use of AI and advanced analytics in diplomacy.

Mandates the CAIO to possess skills in data analytics, AI, machine learning, and organizational change management.

Requires the Chief Information Officer to consult with the CAIO on scaling AI capabilities across software applications.

Defines “artificial intelligence” as per section 238(g) of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2019.

name: Water Infrastructure Modernization Act
summary:
Amends the Federal Water Pollution Control Act and the Safe Drinking Water Act to authorize grants for smart water infrastructure technology.

Requires the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) to provide grants for intelligent wastewater treatment systems using AI for predictive maintenance and real-time monitoring.

Mandates grants for smart drinking water systems with AI tools to reduce water loss, improve decision-making, and enhance operational efficiency.

Specifies that 25% of the grant funds are set aside for rural communities and 10% for Tribal communities.

Obligates the EPA to issue guidance for grant applications within 30 days of enactment and make funding decisions within 60 days.

Requires annual reports to Congress on the projects funded and their impacts.

Authorizes $25 million for fiscal years 2024 through 2028 for both wastewater and drinking water infrastructure projects.

name: SAFE AI Research Grants
summary:
Requires the National Academy of Sciences to establish a grant program for the development of safe AI models and AI research.

Mandates the development of guiding principles and ethical considerations for the grant program.

Directs the Director of the National Academy of Sciences to submit a detailed proposal of the grant program to relevant Congressional committees within one year, including a budget, proposed appropriation request, and an evaluation of existing AI models and methodologies.

name: DOE and NASA Research Coordination Act
summary:
Requires the Department of Energy (DOE) and NASA to coordinate research and development activities, including AI-related areas such as machine learning, data analytics, and predictive analysis.

Mandates the use of memoranda of understanding for coordination.

Allows for competitive awards to support collaborative R&D activities.

Directs the development of methods to handle large data sets on high-performance computing systems.

Promotes data sharing between DOE, NASA, National Laboratories, and other entities, ensuring secure data transfer.

Authorizes reimbursable and non-reimbursable agreements between DOE and NASA.

Ensures competitive awards follow merit-review processes and consider applications from various entities.

Obligates a report within two years on coordination activities, achievements, and future plans.

Requires consistency with research security laws.

name: Coast Guard Authorization Act, Sec. 212 ("Unmanned Systems Capabilities Office")
summary:
Requires the Commandant to submit a report within one year outlining a plan for establishing an unmanned systems capabilities office within the Coast Guard.

Mandates inclusion of a management strategy for acquiring, developing, and deploying unmanned system and counter-unmanned system technologies.

Demands a coordination strategy to synchronize efforts across the Coast Guard and pursue expanded research, development, testing, and evaluation opportunities.

Requires identification of contracting and acquisition authorities needed for expedited technology development and deployment.

Lists the need for a detailed inventory of commercially available unmanned and counter-unmanned systems useful to the Coast Guard.

Calls for a cross-agency collaboration plan with the Department of Homeland Security, Department of Defense, and other relevant agencies.

Encourages opportunities to obtain and share unmanned system data to enhance maritime domain awareness.

Mandates the development of a concept of operations for a data ecosystem integrating unmanned system technologies with AI, machine learning, and information-sharing capabilities.

name: Weather Information for Agriculture Act
summary:
Reauthorizes the National Integrated Drought Information System.

Requires advancement and deployment of AI, machine learning, and cloud technologies for drought forecasting.

Mandates strengthening observational networks and drought indicators, addressing gaps in snowpack and soil moisture monitoring.

Establishes memoranda of understanding with the National Mesonet Program for coordinated drought information.

Requires migration to probabilistic forecasts and incorporation of new modeling tools with the Climate Prediction Center.

Authorizes appropriations from $15,000,000 in fiscal year 2024 to $17,000,000 in fiscal year 2028 for these activities.

Mandates development, deployment, and maintenance of the National Coordinated Soil Moisture Monitoring Network.

Requires establishment of a user-friendly website, high-quality data criteria, and increased in situ soil moisture monitoring stations.

Promotes research, data sharing, and engagement with the citizen science community for soil moisture monitoring.

Allows partnerships to provide nationwide soil moisture information.

name: Intelligence Authorization Act FY 2024, Sec. 758 ("Technology for Classification and Declassification")
summary:
Requires the Administrator of the Office of Electronic Government to research a technology-based solution using machine learning and artificial intelligence for efficient classification and declassification systems within 1 year.

Mandates consultation with various key agencies, including the Secretary of Defense and CIA Director, to ensure a comprehensive approach.

Calls for the solution to be interoperable and federated across the Federal Government.

Obligates the Administrator to submit a recommendation to the President regarding the adoption of the researched technology-based solution.

Permits the Administrator to hire sufficient staff to execute the tasks outlined.

Directs the President to submit a classified report to Congress within 540 days, detailing the recommended solution and the decision on its adoption.

name: Advanced Communications Technology Networks Act
summary:
Directs the Assistant Secretary of Commerce for Communications and Information to support the establishment, prototyping, and implementation of common models and methodologies to inform electromagnetic spectrum management decisions.

Requires the development of technologies and techniques to control radio frequency emissions and interference.

Mandates the prototyping of artificial intelligence systems and technologies capable of operating advanced antenna arrays and dynamic spectrum access.

Encourages the development and participation of a skilled workforce to prototype advanced communications technologies.

Supports partnerships among institutions for workforce development in advanced communications technologies.

Identifies and implements technologies that promote dynamic spectrum access, network sensing, monitoring, and optical and quantum communications.

Amends section 104 of the National Telecommunications and Information Administration Organization Act to include these additional responsibilities for the Assistant Secretary.

name: National Critical Capabilities Defense Act
summary:
Defines "national critical capabilities sector" as sectors, including artificial intelligence, subject to regulation described in the bill.

Establishes the "Committee on National Critical Capabilities" to review U.S. investments in foreign countries that may threaten national security.

Requires U.S. persons to notify the Committee of covered activities in critical sectors, including artificial intelligence, at least 90 days before initiation.

Instructs the Committee to review and potentially mitigate risks posed by such activities, with authority to prohibit or regulate investments.

Defines "covered activities" broadly to include acquisitions, joint ventures, and other engagements with foreign entities in critical sectors.

Identifies countries of concern, including China, Russia, and North Korea, where such investments are scrutinized more closely.

Grants the Committee authority to enforce compliance, including imposing civil penalties up to $250,000 or twice the amount of the covered activity.

name: Black Maternal Health Omnibus Act, Sec. 904 (Report on the Use of Technology in Maternity Care)
summary:
Mandates the Secretary of Health and Human Services to enter an agreement with the National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine to study the use of technology in maternity care.

Requires the study to examine the use of innovative technology, including artificial intelligence, and its impact on racial or ethnic biases in maternal health care.

Includes patient monitoring devices, such as pulse oximeters, in the scope of the study, with a focus on their effect on racial or ethnic biases.

Outlines identification of best practices for reducing and preventing biases in the use of technology and monitoring devices in maternity care.

Requires the study to recommend best practices for using technology and monitoring devices for pregnant and postpartum individuals from minority groups.

Mandates the inclusion of best practices regarding privacy and security safeguards in the use of such technologies.

Directs the National Academies to complete the study and submit a report to Congress within 24 months of the Act's enactment.

name: Wildfire Technology DEMO Act
summary:
Establishes a wildfire technology testbed pilot program within 60 days of the Act's enactment, coordinated by the Secretaries of Agriculture and the Interior.

Incorporates the program into an existing interagency coordinating group on wildfires.

Identifies key technology priority areas, including hazardous fuels reduction, dispatch communications, remote sensing, safety equipment, and operational dashboards.

Partners selected private entities, nonprofits, and higher education institutions with federal agencies for real-time testing during wildfire mitigation.

Prioritizes emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence, quantum sensing, augmented reality, and advanced communications for wildfire mitigation.

Requires covered entities to submit applications, including technology testing proposals.

Mandates annual reports to Congress on participating entities, tested technologies, costs, outreach efforts, and technology assessments.

Terminates the program four years after establishment.

name: DATA Privacy Act
summary:
Establishes national data privacy standards for covered entities handling personal data.

Requires covered entities to post clear, accessible privacy notices detailing data collection, processing, storage, and disclosure practices.

Mandates the FTC to create regulations within one year for reasonable, equitable, and non-deceptive data practices, including opt-out and affirmative consent mechanisms.

Imposes data minimization requirements, limiting data collection to what is necessary for specified purposes and ensuring timely deletion.

Empowers individuals with rights to access, correct, delete, and transfer their data.

Mandates large entities to appoint privacy protection officers to oversee compliance and advocate for privacy policies.

Directs the National Science Foundation to support research on privacy-enhancing technologies.

Grants enforcement authority to the FTC and state attorneys general, with civil penalties for violations.

Allocates resources to the FTC for enforcement and compliance activities.

name: Testing at Residence Telehealth Act, Sec. 2 ("Tests and Assistive Telehealth Consultations Demonstration")
summary:
Establishes a Value-Based Insurance Design Model (VBID) demonstration program to provide Medicare beneficiaries with assistive telehealth consultations and home-based care.

Requires eligible Medicare Advantage (MA) plans to cover medical tests, including those utilizing adaptive AI and machine learning, for various diseases and conditions.

Limits the VBID program to a maximum of 25 MA plans, with at least 10 plans serving rural or underserved areas.

Mandates demographic data collection for reimbursement claims, including age, race, ethnicity, gender, and chronic conditions.

Administers a grant program for state Medicaid programs to cover similar tests and telehealth consultations, with grants awarded to 5-10 states or territories for a 4-year period, not exceeding $12 million per state.

name: National Quantum Initiative Reauthorization Act, Sec. 16 ("DOE Quantum Information Science Research Program")
summary:
Amends the National Quantum Initiative Act to mandate the Secretary of Energy to implement a quantum information science, engineering, and technology research program.

Establishes National Quantum Information Science Research Centers to enhance quantum technology and infrastructure.

Requires cooperative research initiatives with industry, National Laboratories, and academic institutions, covering AI, machine learning, quantum communications, sensing, and other quantum technologies.

Mandates providing research experiences and training for students in quantum fields.

Directs the creation of a 10-year strategic plan for quantum high-performance computing, integrating AI and machine learning, to be submitted to Congress.

Supports industry outreach to promote quantum technology commercialization and advancements in the energy sector.

Allocates up to $130 million annually from 2024 to 2027 for these activities.

name: NTIA Reauthorization Act, Sec. 203 ("Spectrum management improvements")
summary:
Requires the Under Secretary, in coordination with the Commission and in consultation with other relevant Federal agencies, to develop, establish, prototype, and support the implementation of models, methodologies, and inputs for spectrum management decisions involving AI systems, advanced antenna arrays, and dynamic spectrum access technologies.

Mandates the development of AI systems to enable dynamic spectrum access, Internet of Things networks, and other advanced communications technologies.

Amends Section 104 of the National Telecommunications and Information Administration Organization Act to require the identification and facilitation of technologies that promote dynamic spectrum access, network sensing and monitoring, and optical and quantum communications.

Encourages the development of a skilled workforce for prototyping advanced communications technologies.

Supports partnerships among institutions for workforce development in advanced communications technology prototyping.

name: Intelligence Authorization Act FY 2024, Title V ("Emerging Technology Competition"), Subtitle B ("Next Generation AI")
summary:
**Subtitle B—Next-Generation Energy, Biotechnology, And Artificial Intelligence**

**SEC. 511. Expanded Annual Assessment of Economic and Technological Capabilities of the People's Republic of China.**

Requires a detailed assessment of China’s investments in AI, next-generation energy technologies, and biotechnology.

Identifies competitive practices and opportunities to counter them.

Determines U.S. vulnerabilities in the supply chain of these technologies.

**SEC. 514. Policies Established by Director of National Intelligence for Artificial Intelligence Capabilities.**

Mandates the establishment of policies for AI acquisition, adoption, development, use, coordination, and maintenance.

Requires guidelines for evaluating AI model performance, continuous monitoring, and documentation.

Calls for standards on imputed, augmented, or synthetic data used in AI training.

**SEC. 515. Strategy for Submittal of Notice by Private Persons to Federal Agencies Regarding Certain Risks and Threats Relating to Artificial Intelligence.**

Directs the President to establish a strategy for vendors and users to notify the government of AI-related risks.

Includes information security, biosecurity risks, foreign malign influence, and other unlawful activities related to AI.

Outlines a plan for Federal agencies to engage in public education on AI risks.

name: Counseling for Career Choice Act
summary:
Amends the Elementary and Secondary Education Act of 1965 to expand career counseling opportunities.

Requires career counseling programs to leverage resources and emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence.

Mandates the development of professional development or career development training certification programs for counselors and educators.

Encourages partnerships with one-stop centers and integration with local and state workforce entities.

Promotes the establishment and coordination of postsecondary opportunities such as internships, apprenticeships, and dual enrollment programs.

Requires the identification and assessment of school counseling activities and postsecondary options within and outside the state.

Mandates the evaluation of secondary and postsecondary outcomes for individuals served by career counseling programs.

name: National Mesonet Authorization Act
summary:
Establishes the National Mesonet Program within the National Weather Service to improve weather observation and forecasting.

Requires the program to leverage commercial, academic, and other non-Federal weather data to enhance coordination across sectors.

Targets improved environmental observations to support baseline forecasts and warnings, and to enhance numerical weather prediction performance.

Mandates integration of greater density and types of weather observations, including local and regional networks and satellite constellations.

Provides financial and technical assistance for State, Tribal, private, and academic entities to build or upgrade mesonet systems, contingent on agreements to share data.

Forms an advisory committee to recommend improvements and expansions of available data.

Obligates regular briefings to relevant Congressional committees on program activities and progress.

Allocates specified funding amounts for fiscal years 2024 through 2028 to support the program's implementation and expansion.

name: AREA Act, Part B ("National Center for Education Research"), Sec. 133 ("Duties")
summary:
Amends the duties of the Research Commissioner to include maintaining peer-review standards and supporting scientifically valid research.

Requires the Commissioner to propose and implement a research plan, ensuring the research is relevant and informs decision-making.

Mandates the support of evidence-based practices and the dissemination of research findings.

Grants authority to conduct research on underrepresented student populations and to support research-practice partnerships.

Obligates the Commissioner to ensure research is reviewed for inclusion in the National Education Research Database.

Allows for the provision of technical assistance to underrepresented researchers and institutions.

Supports research on educational technology, including artificial intelligence, digital literacy, and other significant educational topics.

name: Digital Defense Content Provenance Act
summary:
Requires the Director of the Defense Media Activity (DMA) to establish a course of education at the Defense Information School (DINFOS) on digital content provenance within one year of enactment.

Mandates the course to cover digital content provenance, challenges posed by digital content forgery, and the use of industry open technical standards for authenticating digital content.

Obligates the Director to start a pilot program within one year to assess the implementation of industry standards for digital content provenance for official Department media.

Sets termination date for the pilot program on January 1, 2027, with an interim report due by January 1, 2026, to assess effectiveness and feasibility.

Defines key terms including "digital content forgery" and "digital content provenance" to ensure clarity in implementation.

name: Solving the Border Crisis Act
summary:
Resumes border wall system construction, requiring the Secretary of Homeland Security to restart halted projects and honor previous agreements.

Prohibits the cancellation of contracts related to border wall construction entered into before January 20, 2021.

Requires the lifting of COVID-19 related suspension of entries and imports not earlier than 120 days after the termination of the public health emergency.

Mandates submission of plans to manage possible influxes related to the termination of COVID-19 suspensions.

Disapproves the rule allowing asylum officers to adjudicate credible fear claims, maintaining exclusive authority for immigration judges.

Amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to require the return of aliens to contiguous territory or detain them for further asylum consideration.

Establishes minimum staffing levels for various immigration and border enforcement offices, including 25,000 U.S. Border Patrol agents.

Ensures funding for sufficient detention facilities to comply with mandatory detention requirements.

Mandates a report within 60 days on how the Department of Homeland Security is mitigating border encounters.

name: Advanced Aviation Integration Act
summary:
Designates the Deputy Administrator of the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) as the executive responsible for advanced aviation integration.

Requires coordination across FAA offices to ensure safe operation and integration of advanced aviation systems, including policy, rulemaking, and workforce planning.

Mandates the Deputy Administrator to report biannually on workforce requirements and recommend staffing and budget resources.

Establishes the Office of Advanced Integration, headed by a Director, to oversee advanced aviation system responsibilities.

Creates the Advanced Aviation Coordination Unit to promote safe integration, improve certification processes, and develop standards for advanced aviation systems.

Forms working groups on unmanned aircraft systems, advanced air mobility, and safety technology integration within the Coordination Unit.

Defines "advanced aviation system" broadly to include unmanned aircraft, powered lift aircraft, and various advanced aviation technologies.

Authorizes the Secretary of Transportation to facilitate interagency coordination to support advanced aviation integration.

name: Combating Cartels on Social Media Act of 2023
summary:
Requires the Secretary of Homeland Security to assess the use of social media and online platforms by transnational criminal organizations for recruitment and illicit activities within 180 days.

Mandates submission of a National Strategy to Combat Illicit Recruitment Activity by Transnational Criminal Organizations on Social Media and Online Platforms within one year.

Proposes improvements in cooperation between government entities and social media operators, enhanced intelligence analysis, and proactive law enforcement efforts.

Requires establishment of a centralized mechanism for reporting recruitment efforts by transnational criminal organizations to the Department of Homeland Security.

Instructs the Secretary to consult with various federal, state, and local entities, as well as social media companies and experts during strategy development and implementation.

Mandates semiannual reporting on the implementation of the strategy and its progress to appropriate congressional committees for five years.

Designates a specific official within U.S. Customs and Border Protection to manage intelligence related to recruitment activities and to facilitate voluntary information reporting from social media operators.

name: Rail Worker and Community Safety Act, Sec. 13 (Equipment Inspections)
summary:
Requires the Secretary of Transportation to issue regulations within 12 months of enactment.

Prohibits the movement of trains from switchyards before completing all required brake inspections.

Allows only Qualified Mechanical Inspectors to sign off on inspection forms for locomotives and rail cars.

Ensures that inspections using AI or camera-based systems under part 215 of title 49, Code of Federal Regulations, require verification by a Qualified Mechanical Inspector.

name: Responsible Financial Innovation Act, Sec. 1001 ("EOP Appropriations")
summary:
Authorize appropriations of $2,500,000 annually from fiscal years 2023 to 2027 to the Office of Science and Technology Policy for hiring specialists in AI, crypto assets, and distributed ledger technology, available until the end of the subsequent fiscal year.

Require these funds to support positions coordinating Federal activities and advising the President on research and development strategies related to these technologies.

Authorize similar appropriations of $2,500,000 annually from fiscal years 2023 to 2027 to the National Economic Council for hiring specialists in AI, crypto assets, and distributed ledger technology, also available until the end of the subsequent fiscal year.

Require these funds to support positions coordinating Federal activities and advising the President on financial and economic policies related to these technologies.

name: Online Privacy Act, Sec. 106 ("Individual autonomy")
summary:
Prohibits covered entities from collecting, processing, maintaining, or disclosing personal information for behavioral personalization without affirmative express consent.

Requires covered entities to obtain express affirmative consent before providing behaviorally personalized products or services, and annually thereafter.

Mandates providing non-personalized versions of products or services if consent is denied, or core aspects if full functionality without personalization is infeasible.

Allows denial of products or services if no core aspect can function without personalization and consent is not given.

Permits processing personal information for usability improvements using aggregated data, provided the output is uniform and independent of individual characteristics.

Excludes optimizations aimed primarily at increasing user engagement time from the definition of "usability."

Exempts small businesses from these requirements.

name: EARN IT Act of 2023, Sec. 3 (National Commission on Online Child Sexual Exploitation Prevention)
summary:
Establishes a National Commission on Online Child Sexual Exploitation Prevention. Tasks the Commission with developing recommended best practices for interactive computer service providers to prevent, reduce, and respond to online child sexual exploitation. 

Composes the Commission of 19 members, including federal officials and appointees with specific expertise in law enforcement, prosecution, victim services, consumer protection, civil liberties, privacy, computer science, and industry representation. Requires two members to have experience in cryptography, data security, or artificial intelligence. Designates the Attorney General or their representative as the Chairperson.

name: Know Your App Act
summary:
Requires covered companies to publicly list the primary country of origin of each application on the app store page with prominent display.

Mandates that covered companies provide an option to filter out apps from countries of concern and display disclaimers if data could be accessed by a foreign government.

Obligates developers to notify covered companies of changes in country of origin or beneficial ownership and certify the accuracy of displayed information annually.

Enforces a series of warnings and potential removal of apps for non-compliance by developers.

Establishes a reporting mechanism for potential violations and provides an appeals process for app removals.

Directs the Treasury and Commerce Secretaries to annually list countries with laws enabling government control over applications, making the list publicly available.

Limits enforcement and regulatory authority to provisions explicitly stated in the Act.

Authorizes the Attorney General to enforce compliance through civil action.

name: Kids PRIVACY Act
summary:
Defines "process" as an operation, potentially automated, performed on "covered information" including collecting, disclosing, inferring, etc.

Mandates obtaining "verifiable consent" from teenagers or parents before processing their data.

Requires operators to minimize data collection and retain data only as necessary.

Obligates transparency and the provision of a clear privacy policy detailing data practices.

Prohibits targeted advertising and harmful data processing practices.

Establishes rights for teenagers and parents to access, correct, and delete data.

Imposes strict security measures for processing children's and teenagers' data.

name: CATCH Fentanyl Act
summary:
Mandates the Secretary of Homeland Security, through the CBP Innovation Team, to establish pilot projects within one year to test and assess technologies enhancing nonintrusive inspection systems at land ports of entry.

Requires testing of at least five technology types, including artificial intelligence, machine learning, and quantum information sciences, to detect contraband, illegal drugs, and threats.

Identifies effective enhancements based on detection accuracy, efficiency, integration capability, cost, safety, and mobility.

Allows private sector input on commercially viable technologies.

Sets termination of pilot projects five years post-enactment.

Requires reporting to Congress within three years and after project termination, detailing effectiveness, recommendations, cost plans, and performance analysis of tested technologies.

name: No ICBMs or Drones for Iran Act of 2023
summary:
Expands sanctions under the Comprehensive Iran Sanctions, Accountability, and Divestment Act of 2010 to include unmanned aerial systems (UAS).

Incorporates UAS under arms embargos of the Countering America’s Adversaries Through Sanctions Act and Iran-Iraq Arms Non-Proliferation Act of 1992.

Requires the President to submit a strategy to counter Iran's UAS program including export controls of US materials, identification of actors supporting Iran's UAS program, assessment of compliance with such restrictions, and coordination with US allies in furtherance of these actions

Mandates a report on support for Iran’s UAS program from domestic industries, individuals, or entities in Iran and related technology transfers to foreign actors, to be updated as necessary.

name: PAID Act, Sec. 3 (Requirements for Private Passenger Automobile Insurers)
summary:
Prohibits private passenger automobile insurers from considering certain factors, such as gender, education level, and ZIP Code, in determining insurance eligibility or rates.

Requires insurers to submit information to the FTC within one year of enactment and biennially thereafter to demonstrate that their practices and algorithms do not disproportionately impact any customer group based on protected characteristics.

Mandates public availability of underwriting rules and rate filings, disallowing them from being proprietary trade secrets.

Exempts individuals from liability if they prove they maintained reasonable compliance procedures.

Clarifies that using prohibited factors to influence insurance premiums constitutes a violation, affecting eligibility, rebates, discounts, and other policy terms.

Preserves the authority of Federal and State agencies to enforce prohibitions against unfair or deceptive practices.

name: Preserving Telehealth, Hospital, and Ambulance Access Act, Sec. 105 (Report on Wearable Medical Devices)
summary:
Mandates the Comptroller General to conduct a technology assessment of wearable medical devices within 18 months of the Act's enactment.

Requires the report to include an analysis of the devices' potential to accurately prescribe treatments.

Examines the benefits and challenges of using artificial intelligence to augment wearable medical devices.

Proposes policy options to enhance benefits and mitigate challenges in developing or using such devices.

name: HOME Act of 2024, Sec. 7 (Identification of Unfair Screening Practices)
summary:
Mandates the Secretary, the Federal Trade Commission, and the Bureau of Consumer Financial Protection to jointly collect information on unfair practices in tenant and applicant screenings, including the use of algorithms.

Requires the identification of practices that prevent access to or retention of rental housing, focusing on tenant background checks, adverse action notices, and tenant income sources.

Obliges the submission of an annual report to Congress detailing the information collected under the program.

name: Countering Antisemitism Act, Sec. 8 (Online Antisemitism, Holocaust Denial, and Distortion)
summary:
Mandates the National Coordinator to Counter Antisemitism to conduct a study on online antisemitism, including Holocaust denial and distortion, within 180 days of the Act's enactment and annually for 10 years.

Requires the study to analyze the prevalence of antisemitic content online.

Recommends to Congress measures to counter online antisemitism, focusing on transparency in algorithmic systems, content moderation, enforcement of community standards, and accountability for individuals and platforms.

Obligates the National Coordinator to submit the report to specific Senate and House committees.

name: Richard L. Trumka Protecting the Right to Organize Act of 2023, Sec. 309 (GAO Report)
summary:
Mandates the Government Accountability Office (GAO) to study the impact of Sections 101(a) and 101(b) on employee coverage under the National Labor Relations Act, focusing on union formation and collective bargaining.

Requires the study to analyze impacts on employee flexibility, compensation, grievance resolution, and technology use, including AI and algorithms.

Directs the GAO to gather input from stakeholders, including business enterprises and labor organizations, consulting relevant congressional committees.

Obliges the GAO to report its findings to the House and Senate committees six months after the study begins and make the report public.

Instructs the President, after the report's release, to consider its findings and potentially recommend modifications to Sections 101(a) or 101(b) within 60 days.

Expresses the House's intent to evaluate any presidential recommendations regarding the modifications.

name: FIT Procurement Act
summary:
Requires the Federal Acquisition Institute to incorporate experiential learning into key acquisition certification programs within 18 months.

Mandates the development and implementation of a cross-functional ICT acquisition training program, emphasizing market research, cloud computing, artificial intelligence, and cybersecurity.

Encourages the use of commercially available off-the-shelf technologies and innovative procurement techniques like oral presentations and product demonstrations.

Reassigns the responsibility for AI training requirements from the Office of Management and Budget to the General Services Administration.

Expands the Commercial Solutions Opening Authority to include commercial services and mandates public reporting and data collection on its use.

Increases the simplified acquisition threshold from $250,000 to $500,000.

Requires the Administrator to issue guidance on using past performance from a broader range of projects to increase competition.

Establishes a working group to address the shrinking Federal vendor base and recommends actions to remove barriers to qualified vendors.

name: Living Wage for Musicians Act of 2024
summary:
Prohibits artificial intelligence entities from being classified as artists under this act.

Requires the establishment of the Artist Compensation Royalty Fund to help provide financial support to those whose employment was negatively impacted by AI.

Mandates service providers to collect and deposit a living wage royalty fee and a percentage of non-subscription revenue into the Fund.

Authorizes the Fund Administrator to impose penalties for violations and non-compliance by service providers.

name: Methane Emissions Mitigation Research and Development Act
summary:
Requires the Secretary of Energy, in consultation with the EPA and other federal agencies, to implement a program for methane emissions detection and mitigation research, development, and demonstration.

Mandates cooperative agreements with state/local governments, higher education institutions, and for-profit entities for technical assistance in preventing and responding to methane releases.

Establishes publicly accessible resources for best practices in pipeline systems, production wells, storage facilities, and emission reduction technologies.

Supports research into technologies for accurate methane emissions quantification, including improvements in data analytics, machine learning platforms, and Lidar detection technologies.

Forms a Methane Emissions Measurement and Mitigation Research Consortium to prioritize research, facilitate data sharing, and develop cooperative leak detection and repair strategies.

Requires annual reporting to Congress on the Consortium's activities, findings, and progress, and a merit review after five years.

Authorizes specific appropriations for the Secretary of Energy and Secretary of Commerce to support these initiatives through 2029.

name: Veterans Appeals Efficiency Act of 2024
summary:
Requires the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to submit an annual report on the average length of time remanded claims are pending.

Mandates the use of technology to track and maintain information on specific claims for benefits, including those continuously pursued, in the National Work Queue, or pending a hearing.

Ensures claimants can view reasons for claim deferrals or suspense dates in the National Work Queue.

Authorizes the Chairman of the Board of Veterans’ Appeals to aggregate appeals with similar questions of law or fact.

Obliges the Board to ensure substantial compliance with its remand decisions, allowing waivers if sufficient evidence resolves underlying issues.

Grants the Court of Appeals for Veterans Claims supplemental jurisdiction to review eligible claims and remand matters for addressing unaddressed issues or inadequate decisions by the Board.

Directs a study, potentially using AI, on common legal or factual questions before the Board and mandates a report on the findings.

Requires the Secretary to develop a plan for timely assignment of claims and submit it to Congress.

name: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
summary:
Directs the NIST to establish task forces focused on the development of technical guidelines for identifying and labeling AI-generated content, including metadata, watermarking, and digital fingerprinting.

Supports the development of standards to provide cryptographically verifiable content provenance metadata and robust watermarks. 

Requires providers of generative AI applications to ensure that content created or modified by such applications includes a disclosure of its AI origin, and to collaborate with providers of covered online platforms to provide these disclosures to users.

Prohibits online platforms from removing such disclosures and mandates clear display of AI origin information to users.

Enforces compliance under the Federal Trade Commission Act.

Defines self-regulatory guidelines approved by the FTC as compliance alternatives.

name: National Patient Safety Board Act of 2024
summary:
Establishes the National Patient Safety Board (NPSB) within the Office of the Secretary of Health and Human Services to prevent and reduce patient safety events.

Empowers the NPSB to support federal agencies in monitoring patient safety, studying causes of patient safety events, and formulating preventive solutions.

Grants the NPSB authority to request changes to patient safety measures, review reports, and make them publicly available within one year of study commencement.

Mandates annual audits and reports to Congress on progress, including detailed solutions and unaddressed needs.

Forms a Patient Safety Research and Development Division to aggregate and analyze patient-level data, identifying and anticipating safety events and disparities.

Requires compliance with privacy laws and AI governance frameworks, including NIST's AI Risk Management Framework and the Blueprint for an AI Bill of Rights.

Prohibits the use of NPSB reports as evidence in civil liability cases but allows their use in developing standards of care.

name: Examining Educational Redlining in Lending Act
summary:
Requires the Bureau of Consumer Financial Protection to assess the use of educational data and automated processes in creditworthiness determinations annually.

Mandates coordination with executive agencies and civil rights stakeholders for these assessments.

Examines the risks and disparate impacts of using automated or algorithmic underwriting processes.

Obligates the Bureau to report findings and recommendations to Congress 60 days post-assessment.

Requires public disclosure of assessment findings, lists of covered persons using educational data, and those employing automated or algorithmic processes.

Defines key terms, including "certain educational data" and "covered person," with references to existing legislation.

name: Advanced Aviation Act
summary:
Redesignates the Office of NextGen as the Office of Advanced Aviation within 1 year.

Appoints an Associate Administrator to oversee the Office of Advanced Aviation.

Coordinates rulemaking and approval processes for advanced aviation systems' standardization, certification, safety, and integration into national airspace.

Establishes an Office of Advanced Integration to manage responsibilities related to advanced aviation systems.

Forms an Advanced Aviation Coordination Unit to promote safe integration and certification of advanced aviation systems.

Redesignates the William J. Hughes Technical Center as the William J. Hughes Technical Center for Advanced Aviation, responsible for research, development, and integration of new aviation technologies.

Establishes an Aviation Innovation Program to evaluate and integrate new aviation-related technologies into the national airspace system.

Defines "advanced aviation systems" to include unmanned aircraft systems, counter-UAS systems, powered lift aircraft, and related technologies.

name: Americas Act, Title II ("Trade and Investment"), Sec. 255 ("Energy Development")
summary:
Amends the BUILD Act of 2018 to define "transformational energy technology," including AI applications for energy efficiency and grid operation.

Inserts a Chief Energy Officer position within the U.S. International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) to promote transformational energy technology exports and ensure at least 30% of DFC support targets such projects.

Requires annual and quarterly reports on transformational energy technology projects and international finance of energy generation.

Establishes an Office of Energy in the Export-Import Bank to promote and finance exports of eligible technologies, including those involving AI.

Mandates the creation of a Joint Energy Export, Development, and Trade Database to coordinate inter-agency efforts.

Increases the DFC's maximum contingent liability and adjusts the Export-Import Bank’s loan, guarantee, and insurance authority limits.

name: Modernizing Retrospective Regulatory Review
summary:
Requires the Director of the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) to report on the Federal Government's progress in making agency regulations available in machine-readable format within 180 days after enactment.

Mandates the OMB Director to issue guidance within 18 months on using technology, including AI, for efficient and accurate retrospective reviews of regulations.

Obliges agency heads to submit a detailed plan within two years for implementing OMB guidance on retrospective reviews, identifying regulations for review, and including necessary data and analysis.

Directs agency heads to implement the submitted plan within 180 days of submission, focusing on retrospective regulatory reviews.

name: Emerging Innovative Border Technologies Act
summary:
Requires the Secretary of Homeland Security to develop and submit a plan within 180 days to identify, integrate, and deploy advanced technologies, including AI and machine learning, to enhance border security operations.

Mandates inclusion of information on how CBP utilizes its Innovation Teams and other mechanisms to achieve these goals.

Requires assessments of technology contributions, team compositions, and coordination efforts within CBP and DHS.

Identifies non-utilized technologies from other federal agencies that could enhance border security.

Includes an analysis of procurement authorities and whether additional ones are needed.

Demands explanations on scaling existing programs and descriptions of planned security technology programs with objectives, goals, and timelines.

Assesses the privacy and security impact on border communities and legacy technology phase-outs.

Requires coordination with DHS's Science and Technology Directorate to develop and incentivize new technologies.

Specifies metrics for evaluating effectiveness and identifies recent technological advancements in various surveillance and inspection technologies.

Authorizes CBP Innovation Teams to research and adapt commercial technologies, establishing procedures and strategic goals.

Requires annual reporting on Innovation Team activities, including successful technology transitions.

name: Child Exploitation and AI Commission Act
summary:
Establishes the Commission of Experts on Child Exploitation and Artificial Intelligence to investigate and recommend solutions for the prevention, detection, and prosecution of child exploitation crimes involving AI.

Directs the Commission to assess the role of AI in child exploitation and evaluate law enforcement's current capabilities to detect and prosecute such crimes.

Requires the Commission to recommend statutory or constitutional amendments to address obstacles to prosecution identified by the Commission and enhance law enforcement's ability to combat AI-facilitated child exploitation.

Mandates the Commission to submit to Congress interim reports as needed and a final report within two years of member appointments.

Details membership of the Commission as composed of 13 appointed experts from various fields, and outlines guidelines on membership qualifications and operational procedures.

Empowers the Commission to hold hearings, obtain official data, and utilize various support services for its operations.

name: ENFORCE Act
summary:
Amends the Export Control Reform Act of 2018 to prevent foreign adversaries from exploiting U.S. artificial intelligence and other critical technologies.

Defines "artificial intelligence" and "artificial intelligence system" as per the National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020.

Specifies an interim and final definition of "covered artificial intelligence system," focusing on AI systems posing serious national security risks.

Authorizes the President to control the activities of U.S. persons related to critical AI systems and emerging technologies essential to national security.

Empowers the President to require U.S. persons to obtain licenses for exporting or transferring critical AI systems and technologies.

Amends the International Emergency Economic Powers Act to align with the updated export control provisions.

name: GenAI Copyright Disclosure Act
summary:
Requires anyone who creates or alters a training dataset used for a generative AI system to submit a notice to the Register of Copyrights with a summary of any copyrighted works used in the dataset and the URL for the dataset.

Requires the notice must be submitted 30 days before the AI system is made available to consumers or within 30 days of the Act taking effect for systems already available.

Imposes a civil penalty of at least $5,000 for non-compliance.

Requires the Register to establish and maintain a public database of filed notices.

name: CONSENT Act
summary:
Establishes a private right of action against individuals who send unsolicited visual depictions of sexually explicit conduct.

Defines “machine-manipulated media” as media substantially modified using machine-learning techniques.

Permits recipients to bring civil actions for statutory damages up to $500, compensatory damages for emotional distress, attorney fees, and injunctive relief.

Exempts third-party providers, good faith medical, educational, or law enforcement senders, and lawful adult websites from liability.

Allows legal guardians to sue on behalf of minors, incompetent, or incapacitated individuals.

Permits plaintiffs who were minors at the time of the incident to use initials for privacy in court documents.

Ensures civil remedies do not modify or supersede criminal laws.

Includes a severability clause to maintain the act’s provisions if parts are deemed unconstitutional.

name: US Leadership in Standards Act
summary:
Directs the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) to brief Congress on opportunities for U.S. participation in developing AI standards within one year.

Requires the establishment of a web portal to inform U.S. industry and federal agencies about international AI standards efforts and participation opportunities.

Mandates federal agencies to report their participation in AI standards activities using a mechanism developed by the NIST.

Initiates a pilot program to support U.S.-based AI standards meetings through grants to eligible entities, with funding covering up to 50% of meeting costs.

Authorizes $10 million for the pilot program from fiscal years 2024 through 2028.

name: Secure A.I. Act
summary:
Requires the Director of the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) to update the National Vulnerability Database to include AI security vulnerabilities.

Establishes a voluntary, comprehensive database to track AI security and safety incidents, ensuring confidentiality and standardized reporting.

Requires the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) to update the Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures Program for AI vulnerabilities.
