Establishes an Artificial Intelligence Security Center within NSA to facilitate AI security research, develop counter-AI techniques, and promote secure AI practices.

name: American Economic Independence Act
summary:
Requires the President, through the Director of the Office of Management and Budget, to submit a report to Congress on the state of economic integration between the U.S. and China, and the national security risks posed by this integration, every three years for 15 years.

Mandates each report to assess the level of economic integration and its changes since 2000, with predictions for the next three years, specifically in priority sectors including artificial intelligence.

Includes analysis of risks such as reliance on Chinese entities, supply chain dependencies, intellectual property theft, and impacts on the U.S. defense industrial base, particularly in the AI sector.

Requires recommendations for mitigating identified risks.

Permits consultation with nongovernmental entities and submission of the report in an unclassified form, potentially with a classified annex.

name: Comment Integrity and Management Act
summary:
Amends the E-Government Act of 2002 to improve the handling of mass and computer-generated comments in the regulatory review process.

Requires agencies to verify whether electronic comments are submitted by humans.

Mandates agencies to identify and label mass comments and allows agencies to post representative samples of these comments.

Directs the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) to issue guidance on verifying human submissions and managing mass comments, including the use of technology tools.

Obliges agencies to establish and publicly post policies on handling computer-generated and mass comments within one year of enactment.

Compels the Government Accountability Office (GAO) to report on the identification and impact of computer-generated comments within two years.

name: DoD Financial Audits Using AI Act
summary:
Directs the Secretary of Defense to ensure the fiscal year 2024 audit of the Department of Defense's financial statements uses AI technology.

Requires the Under Secretary of Defense (Comptroller) and the Inspector General to jointly develop the necessary AI technology for facilitating these audits.

Mandates the use of this AI technology to accelerate the retirement of older financial management systems without compromising essential controls or auditing standards.

Orders the rescission and deposit of any identified surplus funds from the audit into the General Fund of the Treasury for deficit reduction.

Obliges the Secretary of Defense to brief the Senate and House Committees on Armed Services within 180 days on the audit's progress and the AI technology development.

name: Protect Victims of Digital Exploitation and Manipulation Act of 2024
summary:
Prohibits the production or distribution of digital forgeries of intimate visual depictions of identifiable individuals without their consent, under penalty of fines or imprisonment up to 5 years.

Exempts distributions made in good faith to law enforcement, during legal proceedings, for medical purposes, or in reporting/investigating unlawful content or conduct.

Excludes communications service providers from liability unless they knowingly or recklessly distribute such content.

Defines "digital forgery" as intimate visual depictions created or altered using software, machine learning, AI, or other computer-generated means to appear authentic.

Establishes extraterritorial jurisdiction if the offender or victim is a U.S. national.

Ensures severability of the Act’s provisions if any part is found unconstitutional.

name: Countering Communist China Act, Title VII ("Defense"), Sec. 701 ("Emergency Sanctions Regarding Chinese Military Companies")
summary:
Mandates the exercise of emergency sanctions authorities regarding Communist Chinese military companies.

Defines affected companies as those engaged in commercial services, manufacturing, producing, or exporting in the AI sector.

name: Farm, Food, and National Security Act, Title VII ("Research and Extension"), Sec. 7208 ("Centers of Excellence")
summary:
Mandates the Secretary of Agriculture to establish at least one center of excellence to conduct research, extension, and education activities.

Designates eligible host institutions, including land-grant colleges and accredited veterinary schools, and requires geographic diversity in selection.

Limits each institution to host or co-host only one center at a time.

Requires partnerships with federal agencies, state governments, higher education institutions, and agricultural industry groups to enhance coordination and cost-effectiveness.

Focuses on multiple areas, including digital agriculture, artificial intelligence, agricultural biosecurity, cybersecurity, precision agriculture technologies, biotechnology, and crop protection.

Prohibits using funds for new construction or facility alterations.

Requires an annual report on projects, funding, institutional participation, cost-sharing, and intellectual property actions to relevant Congressional committees.

Expands the number of centers from 3 to 8 and extends the program's authorization to 2029.

name: GRIData Act
summary:
Requires the Secretary of Energy to identify, analyze, and share data to improve the reliability and resilience of the electric grid.

Mandates the Secretary to consider data types, temporal frequency, and spatial resolution, especially in rural, low-income, and disadvantaged communities.

Requires collaboration with National Laboratories, NOAA, and other agencies for weather data relevant to grid reliability and resilience.

Considers the use of emerging technologies, including AI and machine learning, to enhance grid reliability and resilience.

Establishes a steering committee with stakeholders from federal agencies, regulators, and the electric power sector to guide data-related activities.

Mandates the submission of a report to Congress within one year, detailing findings and recommendations for data collection and sharing.

Authorizes $10 million for the first fiscal year to support these activities.

name: DOS Foreign Operations Appropriations Act, Title VII ("General Provisions"), Sec. 7032 ("Democracy Programs")
summary:
Requires the allocation of $2,900,000,000 for democracy programs from various appropriations, including $159,240,000 for the Bureau of Democracy, Human Rights, and Labor.

Mandates the submission of a comprehensive five-year strategy for democracy promotion abroad within 180 days, addressing digital security, countering disinformation, and AI-related challenges.

Prohibits foreign governments from having prior approval over the implementation of democracy programs and protects the confidentiality of implementing partners in undemocratic countries.

Allocates $30,000,000 to protect civil society activists and journalists and $20,000,000 for international freedom of expression and independent media.

Requires the regular informing of the National Endowment for Democracy about planned and supported democracy programs.

name: Countering Communist China Act, Title I ("Trade, Investment, and Economic Relations"), Sec. 101 ("Preventing Adversaries from Developing Critical Capabilities")
summary:
Requires the President to identify, list, and annually update categories of technologies and products in the AI sector that pose acute threats to U.S. national security if acquired by adversaries.

Requires the President to prescribe regulations prohibiting U.S. persons from engaging in covered activities involving listed technologies and products in the AI development sector.

Directs the President to submit annual congressional reports on notifications of covered activities and assessing the need for regulatory amendments.

Encourages multilateral engagement to align with allied countries on similar mechanisms for prohibitions and notifications on technologies in the AI sector.

Authorizes $25 million for implementation and allows direct hiring to administer the entire Act.

name: Preparing Election Administrators for AI Act
summary:
Requires the Election Assistance Commission to develop and issue voluntary guidelines for election offices addressing the use and risks of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies in election administration within 60 days of enactment.

Mandates inclusion of guidelines on the risks and benefits of AI in election activities, cybersecurity risks, the impact of AI-generated information on sharing accurate election information, and the spread of election disinformation.

Directs the Election Assistance Commission to study and report on the use and impacts of AI technologies in the 2024 federal elections by November 5, 2025, including the sharing of AI-generated information and the use of AI by election offices.

Requires the Election Assistance Commission to review and update the voluntary guidelines based on the study's findings.

name: Farm, Food, and National Security Act, Title VIII ("Forestry"), Sec. 8414 ("Wildfire Technology Deployment and Testbed Partnership")
summary:
Establishes a deployment and testbed pilot program for new and innovative wildfire prevention, detection, communication, and mitigation technologies.

Requires incorporation of the Pilot Program into an existing interagency coordinating group on wildfires.

Mandates consultation with covered agencies to identify key technology priority areas.

Partners with selected covered entities for real-time and on-the-ground testing of technology during wildfire mitigation activities.

Prioritizes emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, quantum sensing, and augmented reality, for wildfire mitigation.

Requires submission of annual reports to appropriate committees, detailing participating entities, tested technologies, costs, outreach efforts, and assessments.

Expires the Pilot Program on September 30, 2029.

name: Air Tour and Sport Parachuting Safety Improvement Act of 2023
summary:
Requires the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Administrator to issue a final rule within 24 months mandating safety management systems for certain operators under part 135 of title 14.

Prohibits, beginning three years after enactment, commercial air tours without a certificate under part 119 of title 14, unless meeting specific temporary exceptions.

Mandates new or revised regulations within three years to incorporate controlled flight into terrain and in-flight loss of control avoidance training for certificated commercial air tour operators.

Convenes an aviation rulemaking committee to develop standards for flight data monitoring, terrain awareness, and traffic avoidance for commercial air tour operators.

Directs the Administrator to submit reports and issue proposed rulemakings and final rules based on the aviation rulemaking committee's recommendations within specified timelines.

Requires the FAA to improve the process for obtaining operating certificates and report on the efficiency and resource needs of this process.

Authorizes appropriations as necessary to implement the Act.

name: Coast Guard Authorization Act, Title II ("Coast Guard"), Sec. 207 ("unmanned systems capabilities office")
summary:
Mandates the Commandant to submit a report within one year outlining a plan for establishing an unmanned systems capabilities office within the Coast Guard.

Requires the report to include a management strategy for the acquisition, development, and deployment of unmanned and counter-unmanned system technologies.

Specifies the need for a service-wide coordination strategy to synchronize efforts across the Coast Guard.

Identifies contracting and acquisition authorities necessary to expedite technology development and deployment.

Lists commercially available technologies useful for the Coast Guard.

Calls for a cross-agency collaboration plan with the Department of Homeland Security, the Department of Defense, and other relevant agencies.

Highlights opportunities to share unmanned system data to improve maritime domain awareness.

Requires the development of a concept of operations for a data ecosystem supporting unmanned systems, including AI and machine learning tools.

name: Coast Guard Authorization Act, Title III ("Shipping and Navigation"), Sec. 342 ("Advisory Committee on Autonomous Maritime Systems")
summary:
Establishes the National Advisory Committee on Autonomous Maritime Systems.

Advises the Secretary on regulation and use of Autonomous Systems within U.S. territorial waters.

Comprises 9 members appointed by the Secretary with relevant expertise.

Ensures representation from various groups, including marine safety, vessel design, unmanned vehicle production, port authorities, vessel operators, labor unions, maritime pilots, commercial space operators, and academic institutions.

Mandates establishment of the Committee within 90 days post-enactment.

name: 21st Century Peace through Strength Act, Division D ("Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications")
summary:
Prohibits entities from distributing, maintaining, or updating foreign adversary controlled applications within the U.S.

Requires data portability for users before prohibitions apply, enabling users to access their data in a machine-readable format.

Exempts applications undergoing "qualified divestiture" from prohibitions.

Enforces penalties up to $5,000 per user for distribution violations and $500 per user for data portability violations.

Mandates the Attorney General to investigate and enforce compliance through civil penalties or court actions.

Defines "foreign adversary controlled applications" and "qualified divestiture" to ensure clarity in application and exemptions.

Grants judicial review exclusively to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit, with specified time limits for challenges.

name: Farm, Food, and National Security Act, Title VI ("Rural Development"), Sec. 6303 ("Precision Agriculture")
summary:
Promotes United States leadership in developing standards for precision agriculture.

Mandates the Secretary to develop voluntary, consensus-based interconnectivity standards for precision agriculture within two years.

Requires consultation with NIST, FCC, public, and private stakeholders, including voluntary consensus standards development organizations.

Considers the impact of advanced wireless communications technology and artificial intelligence on precision agriculture.

Addresses cybersecurity challenges and connectivity needs of precision agriculture technology.

Directs the Comptroller General to assess the developed standards one year after implementation and biennially for eight years.

Obligates the Comptroller General to report findings to relevant Senate and House committees.

name: Countering Communist China Act, Title VI ("Democracy, Human Rights, and Taiwan"), Sec. 615 ("DATA Act")
summary:
Prohibits U.S. persons from engaging in transactions involving sensitive personal data with entities subject to Chinese influence.

Requires the President to impose sanctions on foreign persons dealing in connected software applications under Chinese control, facilitating military, espionage, or malicious cyber activities.

Mandates sanctions for foreign persons involved in election interference against the U.S. or its allies, or influencing U.S. policy in favor of China.

Directs the President to determine and report on whether entities like ByteDance and TikTok meet criteria for sanctions.

Empowers the President to block all transactions involving property of sanctioned foreign persons within U.S. jurisdiction.

Allows the President to waive sanctions on a case-by-case basis if vital to U.S. national security interests.

Terminates the section's authorities five years after enactment.

name: AI CONSENT Act
summary:
Requires companies to obtain informed consent from consumers before using their data to train AI systems.

Requires companies to explain clearly and concisely how consumer data will be used for AI training.

Mandates disclosure of further data usage, including transfers to third-party entities.

Directs the FTC to issue a report on the progress of converting covered data to de-identified data (for Congress' evaluation).

Treats violations as unfair or deceptive acts under the Federal Trade Commission Act and subjects violators to penalties.

name: Department of Peacebuilding Act, Sec. 107 ("Office of Technology for Peace")
summary:
Establishes an Office of Technology for Peace within the Department, headed by the Assistant Secretary for Technology for Peace.

Tasks the Assistant Secretary with overseeing awareness, study, and ethical implications of technologies, including artificial intelligence, on domestic and international peace.

Mandates the dissemination of applicable policies and research in consultation with the Department of State.

Requires the Assistant Secretary to provide grants for technologies in transportation, communications, agriculture, medicine, and energy that are nonviolent.

Encourages grants that promote conservation and sustainability of natural resources to prevent future conflicts.

Promotes the development of a green, peaceful economy through these grants.

name: Export Controls Enforcement Improvement Act
summary:
Establishes the Export Enforcement Coordination Center within the Department of Homeland Security to coordinate export enforcement among various federal departments and agencies.

Focuses the Center's efforts on sensitive technologies, including advanced artificial intelligence capabilities, semiconductors, and quantum technology.

Designates the Center as the primary forum for coordinating efforts against unlawful transshipment and diversion of exports, particularly to countries like China, Russia, Iran, and North Korea.

Requires the Center to develop best practices and disseminate actionable information to the private sector about export control risks.

Mandates the submission of reports to Congress on the value and logistics of posting U.S. and foreign law enforcement officials to enhance export control enforcement. 

Authorizes $25,000,000 for the establishment of the Center for fiscal year 2025.

name: Countering Communist China Act, Title I ("Trade, Investment, and Economic Relations"), Sec. 102 ("Sanctions for Chinese Military and Surveillance Companies")
summary:
Requires the President to impose sanctions on foreign persons engaged in significant operations in China's defense or surveillance technology sectors.

Focuses particular attention on foreign persons engaged in AI, machine learning, robotics, quantum information science, and other advanced technologies.

Utilizes the International Emergency Economic Powers Act to block and prohibit transactions involving sanctioned foreign persons' property within U.S. jurisdiction.

name: AI PLAN Act
summary:
Requires the Secretary of the Treasury, Secretary of Homeland Security, and Secretary of Commerce to submit a joint report to Congress on the risks of use of AI in financial crimes, including fraud and misinformation, within 180 days of enactment and annually thereafter.

Mandates the inclusion in the report of interagency policies, procedures, and resources needed to defend against AI-driven financial crimes.

Directs the report to include the consideration of risks such as deepfakes, voice cloning, foreign election interference, synthetic identities, false market signals, and overall digital fraud.

Requires the subsequent submission of legislative recommendations and best practices to address risks identified within 90 days of each report.

name: TAME Extreme Weather Act
summary:
Mandates federal agencies to use AI to adapt to extreme weather, improving weather forecasts, electrical grid resilience, resource deployment, and public-private partnerships.

Requires NOAA to develop and curate an Earth system reanalysis dataset, build on existing datasets, and develop AI weather models.

Directs NOAA to explore advanced AI applications for weather forecasting, including data assimilation and model emulation.

Tasks NOAA with providing technical assistance on AI weather models and developing best practices and public datasets.

Establishes programs using AI for wildfire detection, emissions monitoring, and illegal wood product tracking, requiring dataset curation and public access to AI code and data.

Instructs the Department of Energy to optimize energy grids using AI, develop environmental review documents, and ensure public access to AI models and training datasets, while protecting national security interests.

name: National Wildland Fire Risk Reduction Program Act, Sec. 7 (Responsibilities of Program Agencies)
summary:
Mandates NIST to conduct research on wildland fire impacts, firebrands, novel materials, and performance-based mitigation tools.

Requires NIST to coordinate federal wildland-urban interface fire investigations and develop methodologies for assessing fire impacts on communities.

Directs NSF to support research on wildland fire risks, tools, technologies, and the social and economic factors influencing fire risk reduction.

Instructs NOAA to improve wildland fire understanding through research, weather forecasting, data interoperability, and high-performance computing.

Tasks NOAA with establishing a Fire Weather Testbed and supporting extramural research on wildland fires.

Requires FEMA to support community risk assessment tools, public outreach, and best practices for fire-resistant construction and response.

Directs NASA to support wildland fire research, modeling, data systems, and the development of novel monitoring tools.

Instructs EPA to research wildland fire smoke characteristics, impacts on air and water quality, and communication of risk reduction strategies.

Mandates DOE to develop tools for energy sector resilience to wildland fires and coordinate data resources for improved fire understanding and prevention.

name: Free Credit Scores for Consumers Act of 2024
summary:
Expands the definitions of "credit score" and "educational credit score" under the Fair Credit Reporting Act (FCRA).

Requires consumer reporting agencies (CRAs) to provide consumers with detailed explanations of credit score calculations, including key factors affecting scores.

Mandates CRAs to disclose prominently the differences and limitations of credit scores and educational credit scores on their websites and in related materials.

Provides consumers with free credit score disclosures along with their free annual consumer reports upon request.

Requires private educational lenders, motor vehicle lenders, and residential mortgage lenders to provide consumers with free copies of any consumer reports and credit scores used for underwriting before signing loan agreements.

Mandates the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) to issue final rules to implement these amendments within two years of enactment.

name: Kids Online Safety Act, Title II (Filter Bubble Transparency)
summary:
Requires online platforms using opaque algorithms to provide users with clear notice about the use of such algorithms and how user-specific data is utilized. 

Mandates platforms to allow users to easily switch between opaque algorithms and input-transparent algorithms. Prohibits differential pricing or service denial based on a user's choice to use an input-transparent algorithm.

Empowers the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) to enforce these requirements as violations of unfair or deceptive practices under the Federal Trade Commission Act. 

Ensures that trade secrets, confidential business information, or privileged data are not required to be disclosed. Preserves the ability of platforms to allow users to personalize content restrictions and interactions.

name: Government Surveillance Reform Act of 2023, Title VII (Protection of Car Data from Warrantless Searches)
summary:
Prohibits law enforcement from accessing vehicle data without a warrant, except with operator consent or in emergencies. 

Defines "covered vehicle data" to include all onboard and telematics data in noncommercial vehicles, excluding certain data types like automotive software and geolocation data for traffic enforcement.
Prohibits the use of any vehicle data obtained in violation of these provisions as evidence in any legal proceedings. Amends the Driver Privacy Act of 2015 to align with these new restrictions on accessing vehicle data.

name: Deploying American Blockchains Act of 2023
summary:
Designates the Secretary of Commerce as the principal advisor to the President on blockchain technology and related applications.

Requires the Secretary to develop policies and recommendations addressing issues such as decentralized identity, cybersecurity, AI, regulatory compliance, and fraud reduction.

Instructs the Secretary to promote U.S. leadership and competitiveness in blockchain technology through a Blockchain Deployment Program.

Mandates the establishment of advisory committees with diverse stakeholders to support blockchain adoption.

Directs the Secretary to facilitate the development and dissemination of best practices for blockchain technology.

Obligates the Secretary to consult with private sector stakeholders and disseminate research on blockchain technology.

Requires annual reports to Congress on activities, recommendations for legislation, and emerging risks and trends in blockchain technology.

Terminates the Blockchain Deployment Program seven years after enactment.

name: Border Act of 2024, General Provisions Title
summary:
Allocates $170,000,000 for the procurement and deployment of autonomous surveillance tower systems using AI for border security.

Prohibits the use of funds for non-autonomous border security technology.

Defines "autonomous" systems as those utilizing sensors, onboard computing, and AI for identification.

Mandates quarterly reports on the performance and impact of border security technologies, including AI-driven non-intrusive inspection technology.

Requires acquisition of innovative technologies through open competition, integrating AI and machine learning to improve performance.

Obliges U.S. Customs and Border Protection to submit detailed expenditure plans for autonomous systems, including deployment timelines and sustainment costs.

Instructs the Secretary of Homeland Security to conduct cost-benefit analyses before requesting Department of Defense assistance for border operations, including AI technology impacts.

name: Community and Hydropower Improvement Act, Sec. 4 (Approach to Environmental Review)
summary:
Amends Section 2403 of the Energy Policy Act of 1992 to enhance environmental review procedures.

Requires the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) to cooperate with federal, state, local agencies, and Indian Tribes in preparing environmental assessments or impact statements.

Mandates consideration of ongoing and reasonably foreseeable environmental effects of projects, excluding nonrecurring past effects.

Obliges FERC and cooperating entities to evaluate impacts on fish species and consider appropriate mitigation strategies.

Encourages the use of open-sourced technical models for environmental impact assessments, ensuring their validity and accessibility while protecting intellectual property and proprietary data.

Directs FERC to account for hydrologic alterations over the project license term and assess their impacts on public uses and regional benefits.

Necessitates consideration of innovative solutions and emerging technologies to meet regulatory responsibilities cost-effectively.

Requires periodic technical conferences to evaluate new methodologies and technologies for environmental impact quantification.

Stipulates precise citation of evidence in environmental review records to support findings on material facts.

name: Future of Artificial Intelligence Innovation Act of 2024
summary:
Establishes the "Artificial Intelligence Safety Institute" to assist private and public sectors in developing best practices for AI assessment, provide technical assistance, and promote AI innovation, with a director appointed by the Under Secretary of Commerce for Standards and Technology.
Requires the Institute to conduct AI research, develop standards, and create guidelines for safe AI development and deployment, including generative AI and foundation models.

Mandates the formation of an international coalition to harmonize AI standards and support bilateral and multilateral AI research collaborations. Directs the Comptroller General to report on regulatory barriers affecting AI innovation and recommend legislative or administrative actions to enhance AI development.
Orders the development of prioritized public data sets for AI training and evaluation, and the establishment of Federal grand challenges in AI to stimulate research and commercialization in key areas.

name: A Stronger Workforce for America Act, Chapter 3 (Performance Accountability)
summary: Amends the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act to allow states to use machine learning and advanced analytics in the improvement of state program operations and outcomes.

name: AI Grand Challenges Act of 2024
summary:
Establishes the AI Grand Challenges Program to incentivize AI research, development, and commercialization through prize competitions addressing grand challenges in various sectors like national security, health, and environment.

Mandates the Director of the National Science Foundation to coordinate with federal agencies and stakeholders, and public input, to identify and select AI grand challenges.

Designates a specific grand challenge for AI-enabled cancer breakthroughs.

Sets eligibility criteria for participants, requiring private entities to be U.S.-based and individuals to be U.S. citizens or permanent residents.

Requires regular reporting to Congress on the program’s progress and results, ensuring public accessibility of reports and competition information.

name: NSF AI Education Act of 2024
summary:
Establishes the NSF AI Education Act of 2024 to provide scholarships and fellowships for AI education at various educational levels, including undergraduate and graduate studies. 

Mandates the Director of the National Science Foundation (NSF) to award scholarships for AI studies in fields such as agriculture, education, and advanced manufacturing, prioritizing institutions in underserved areas.

Directs the NSF to create professional development fellowships for AI and related emerging technologies, fostering collaboration between academia and industry.

Requires grants for AI training at land-grant colleges and universities, focusing on agricultural applications.

Authorizes the establishment of Centers of AI Excellence at community colleges and vocational schools to advance AI education and training.

Advises on guidelines for AI use in primary and secondary education and supports AI education research.

Prohibits funding to institutions in violation of anti-discrimination laws.

Directs the development of workforce frameworks for AI and other emerging technologies.

name: Preparing Election Administrators for AI Act
summary:
Cites the Act as the “Preparing Election Administrators for AI Act”.

Requires the Election Assistance Commission to submit a report with voluntary guidelines to Congress, State and local election offices, and the public within 60 days of enactment.

Includes guidelines addressing the risks and benefits of using AI in election administration.

Addresses the cybersecurity risks posed by AI technologies in elections.

Guides on managing AI-generated information to ensure the sharing of accurate election information.

Provides strategies for countering AI-driven election disinformation that undermines public trust.

name: AI Advancement and Reliability Act of 2024
summary:
Establishes the Center for AI Advancement and Reliability to ensure U.S. leadership in AI research, development, and evaluation.

Outlines activities of the Center including conducting measurement research to develop best practices for AI reliability and safety, evaluating AI capabilities and developing methods for risk management.

Mandates the Under Secretary of Commerce for Standards and Technology to coordinate with federal agencies in establishing the Center.

Creates a consortium of stakeholders to support the Center and the National Institute of Standards and Technology in AI-related activities.

Authorizes $10 million for fiscal year 2025 for the establishment of the Center.

name: Lummis-Gillibrand Payment Stablecoin Act (Sec. 1-3)
summary:
Prohibits any person from issuing, creating, or originating an algorithmic payment stablecoin in the United States.

Mandates that payment stablecoins can only be issued by a registered non-depository trust company with a limit on nominal value or an authorized depository institution as a national payment stablecoin issuer.

Prohibits the offer or sale of payment stablecoins in the United States except by a U.S. person living in the U.S.

Requires the Board to adjust the issuance threshold for inflation every four years.

Directs the Board to establish safe harbor regulations, allowing limited issuance of payment stablecoins under specific conditions and fostering innovation and competition.

Allows safe harbor status for issuers regulated by equivalent foreign authorities.

Intends the section to have extraterritorial effect, extending its reach beyond U.S. borders.

name: VET Artificial Intelligence Act
summary:
Establishes the "VET Artificial Intelligence Act" to create voluntary guidelines for the testing, evaluation, validation, and verification of AI systems, aiming to enhance trust, adoption, and governance.

Mandates the Director of the National Institute of Standards and Technology to develop and update these guidelines, addressing consumer privacy, harm mitigation, dataset quality, and governance.

Requires the establishment of an Artificial Intelligence Assurance Qualifications Advisory Committee to provide recommendations on qualifications and accreditation for AI assurance processes.

Directs a study to evaluate the capabilities of entities conducting AI assurances, assessing their resources, methodologies, and market demand, and exploring the use of existing accredited facilities for these purposes.

Obliges the publication of guidelines and recommendations for assurance qualifications, ensuring alignment with international standards, without mandating specific technologies. 

Involves stakeholder outreach, public comment, and collaboration with various sectors to refine guidelines.

name: AI Innovation and Development for Efficiency Act of 2024
summary:
Mandates the National Science Foundation Director to support research on AI-enabled efficient technologies through merit-reviewed and competitively awarded projects.

Requires consideration of projects focusing on smart technologies for infrastructure efficiency, pollution minimization, and upgrading existing constructions.

Obliges researchers to conduct impact assessments of energy consumption for AI-enabled technologies.

Prioritizes research conducted at EPSCoR institutions.

Directs the Director to report findings and recommendations on research opportunities and coordination with federal agencies and the private sector within 18 months of enactment.

Requires a report on research results within four years to relevant Senate and House committees.

name: Small Business Artificial Intelligence Training Act of 2024
summary:
Mandates the Secretary of Commerce, in coordination with various agencies, to develop AI training resources for small businesses, including those in rural, Tribal, or underserved areas.

Requires these resources to cover topics such as prompt engineering, financial management, cybersecurity, and government contracting.

Obligates the review and update of these resources every year to ensure relevance and effectiveness.

Coordinates with the Small Business Administration for the distribution of these resources through its network, including development centers and business opportunity centers.

Allows for a grants program to fund training providers using the developed resources.

Demands initial and annual reports to Congress on the progress and impact of the training resources.

Establishes a sunset clause terminating the program three years after the Act's enactment.

name: Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act
summary:
Establishes regulatory sandboxes allowing financial entities to experiment with AI test projects under reduced regulatory burdens.

Requires financial entities to apply for sandbox participation by detailing their AI project, compliance strategies, and potential public benefits.

Mandates applications include risk assessments for systemic financial stability and national security.

Obligates financial regulatory agencies to review applications within 90 days, with provisions for approval, denial, or extension.

Allows joint applications by multiple entities and necessitates notification to all relevant regulatory bodies.

Stipulates data security measures for information provided by AI project sponsors.

Directs each financial regulatory agency to promulgate regulations, including modification procedures and confidentiality protocols, within 180 days of the Act’s enactment.

Mandates annual reporting to Congress on AI test project outcomes.

Permits regulatory agencies to establish additional AI projects as qualifying test projects after public consultation.

name: Department of Energy AI Act
summary:
Establishes the "Department of Energy AI Act" to advance AI capabilities within the Department of Energy (DOE).

Requires the Secretary of Energy to create a centralized AI program focused on research and deployment of AI for science, security, and technology.

Mandates the development of AI training datasets, next-generation computing infrastructure, and safe AI models.

Directs the establishment of at least eight multidisciplinary AI Research and Development Centers to enhance U.S. leadership in AI.

Implements an AI Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Program to address safety and security concerns.

Allocates funds for STEM education and workforce development, emphasizing AI skill training and diversity.

Establishes a program to use AI to improve federal permitting processes for energy projects.

Initiates rulemaking to standardize AI use in grid interconnection.

Requires a report on the impact of AI on data centers and energy security.

Creates the Office of Critical and Emerging Technology to coordinate AI efforts across the DOE and assess technological impacts on national security.

name: PREPARED for AI Act
summary:
Requires the establishment of a Chief Artificial Intelligence Officers Council to coordinate AI use in federal agencies.

Mandates agencies to develop risk classification systems for AI use cases, categorizing them as unacceptable, high, medium, or low risk.

Prohibits AI use for certain activities, such as mapping facial features for emotion detection or categorizing individuals based on biometric data for sensitive traits.

Directs updates to the Federal Acquisition Regulation to ensure AI procurement includes risk and impact assessments.

Requires agencies to implement processes for evaluating AI risks and to conduct ongoing monitoring, especially for high-risk use cases.

Stipulates comprehensive documentation and transparency requirements for AI models and data.

Establishes annual reporting protocols for obstacles in AI testing and evaluation, promoting interagency collaboration to address challenges.

Prohibits the use of AI for certain high-risk applications and mandates public disclosure of AI inventories and risk classifications.

name: Technology in the Parks Act of 2024
summary:
Amends the Communications Act of 1934 to extend E-rate support to local parks, allowing them to access discounted telecommunications services for technology training programs.

Requires the creation of internet safety regulations for parks receiving such services to ensure cybersecurity standards similar to those for schools and libraries.

Mandates the Secretary of Labor to initiate a grant program for technology training directed towards needy families in local parks, focusing on topics like artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, and web development.

Limits grant coverage to 10% of the training programs' operating costs and to a duration of no longer than two years.

name: Securing Elections From AI Deception Act
summary:
Prohibits developers and deployers from using AI to intentionally deceive or defraud individuals of their voting rights in federal, state, or local elections.

Requires election-related AI-generated content to include disclaimers, informing the public that the content was created using AI.

Mandates developers to provide mechanisms ensuring such disclaimers are permanent or difficult to remove.

Directs the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) to issue regulations on disclaimer requirements and enforce compliance.

Obliges developers and deployers to ensure their algorithms meet safety and efficiency standards as outlined.

name: Sensible Classification Act of 2023, Sec. 7: Implementation of Technology for Classification and Declassification
summary:
Requires the Administrator of the Office of Electronic Government of the Office of Management and Budget, in consultation with various federal actors, to research a technology-based solution to reform the classification system employed by the federal government.

Requires a submission of recommendations to the President.

Mandates the President to submit a report on technology-based solutions to Congress no later than 540 days after the date of the enactment of this Act.

name: Small Business Artificial Intelligence Advancement Act
summary:
Amends the National Institute of Standards and Technology Act to mandate the development and dissemination of AI resources for small businesses.

Requires these resources to include technical standards, best practices, benchmarks, methodologies, and case studies, ensuring they are widely applicable and technology-neutral.

Mandates that resources promote understanding and adoption of AI, adhere to international standards, and incorporate federal educational resources.

Obligates the Director to review and update these resources every two years.

Coordinates with the Small Business Administration for the distribution and utilization of AI resources through its partners, emphasizing voluntary use.

Compels a report to Congress within four years, detailing resources, feedback, and recommendations for enhancing AI utilization by small businesses.

name: AI LEAD Act
summary:
Establishes the Chief Artificial Intelligence Officers Council to promote AI innovation, oversee compliance, and advise on best practices for AI technologies.

Requires each agency to designate a Chief Artificial Intelligence Officer responsible for promoting AI use, managing risks, and ensuring transparency and privacy.

Mandates the creation of Artificial Intelligence Coordination Boards within agencies to address AI issues and publish guiding principles and goals.

Directs agencies to develop an AI strategy focused on responsible and trustworthy adoption, public trust, risk mitigation, and interagency coordination.

Requires the Comptroller General to report on the effectiveness of AI Coordination Boards, evaluate Chief AI Officers, and assess AI costs, benefits, and risks, including job impacts.

Directs the Office of Management and Budget Director to issue updated AI governance guidance within five years.

name: Nucleic Acid Standards for Biosecurity Act
summary:
Amends the Research and Development, Competition, and Innovation Act to include best practices and technical standards for managing risks in engineering biology and biomanufacturing, specifically addressing artificial intelligence.

Requires the Director, in consultation with Federal agencies, to conduct measurement research supporting biosecurity measures related to nucleic acid synthesis.

Mandates testing to improve screening accuracy, efficacy, and reliability, along with best practices for operational security and database management.

Directs the development of technical guidance for effective and secure screening and conformity-assessment standards.

Establishes a consortium of stakeholders to develop and update best practices and roadmaps for synthetic nucleic acid procurement screening.

Requires the consortium to report its findings to Congress within 18 months of its first meeting.

Authorizes $5,000,000 annually for fiscal years 2025 through 2029 for scientific and technical research activities under this initiative.

name: Consumers LEARN AI Act
summary:
Directs the Secretary of Commerce to develop a national strategy and and conduct a public service campaign to enhance artificial intelligence consumer literacy.

Requires the strategy to promote understanding of AI capabilities and limitations, and support informed decisions on AI use.

Instructs the Secretary to coordinate with various federal agencies, local governments, and private organizations to ensure comprehensive strategy development.

Requires the creation of specialized use cases for AI literacy in domains like healthcare, finance, and communication.
 
Mandates the dissemination of educational materials through multiple communication channels, including a dedicated website, and requires periodic updates to these materials.

Obliges the Government Accountability Office to report on existing federal AI literacy programs and the Secretary to annually report on the strategy's progress and effectiveness.

Authorizes necessary appropriations for fiscal years 2025 through 2034 to implement the Act's activities.

name: AI ACCORD Act of 2024
summary:
Mandates the Secretary of Defense to submit a strategy to Congress within 180 days to enhance cooperation with Middle Eastern allies using partner-sharing network capabilities for joint defense.

Requires the strategy to include a summary of ongoing efforts, challenges, and recommended actions for implementing joint partner-sharing networks.

Directs the Chief Data and Artificial Intelligence Officer of the Department of Defense to establish a forum for warfighters to coordinate on AI tools, methodologies, and training within 180 days.

Specifies that the forum should identify AI use cases, categorize risks, and prioritize AI tools while considering training shortfalls and opportunities for cooperation with allies.

Obligates the Secretary of Defense to report progress on the forum's establishment and recommend legislative actions to Congress within one year.

name: AI Transparency in Elections Act of 2024
summary:
Amends the Federal Election Campaign Act to require disclaimers on political advertisements containing content generated by AI.

Outlines requirements for clear disclosure in ads using AI-generated images, audio, or video, specifying format requirements for visibility and audibility.

Imposes penalties for non-compliance, with fines up to $50,000 per violation, and establishes enforcement mechanisms.

Obliges the Federal Election Commission to issue regulations within 90 days, outlining criteria for AI content identification and disclosure requirements.

Requires the FEC to report biannually on compliance and enforcement, providing recommendations for improvements.

name: Atomic Supply Chain Solutions Act
summary:
Mandates the Secretary of Energy to evaluate the U.S. nuclear supply chain within 270 days, including past efforts, future needs, and lessons from projects like Vogtle 3 and 4.

Analyzes regulatory challenges, including the necessity of N-stamps for nuclear components, cost implications, and potential certification streamlining.

Considers advanced manufacturing and innovative technologies like AI, 3D printing, and robotics for enhancing the nuclear supply chain, with attention to cybersecurity, efficiency, and workforce training.

Describes U.S.-Canada cooperation on nuclear components, assessing competitiveness and recommending collaboration to enhance North American nuclear leadership.

Assesses the impact of anticipated demand for advanced nuclear technology on the supply chain, proposing strategies for resilience.

Establishes U.S. policy to prioritize a robust HALEU market to strengthen energy independence and national security, addressing risks associated with increased nuclear technology demand.

name: AI Development Practices Act of 2024
summary:
Amends the National Institute of Standards and Technology Act to require the development of voluntary guidelines for AI system development, release, and assessment.

Mandates the Director of NIST to collaborate with public and private organizations to create guidance on AI risk tolerances and communication of system characteristics.

Requires categorization of practices related to security, safety, fairness, privacy, and other attributes of AI systems.

Obligates the Director to update the voluntary risk management framework for trustworthy AI systems.

Prohibits prescribing specific technologies; mandates reliance on international standards and industry best practices.

Requires collaboration with public, industry, and academic entities for guidance development.

Demands a report to Congress within 18 months on new materials or systems produced and policy recommendations for private-public sector coordination.

Defines "artificial intelligence red teaming" and "artificial intelligence system" for clarity.

name: Maintaining Innovation and Safe Technologies Act
summary:
Directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to issue guidance by January 1, 2026, on Medicare payment requirements under part B of title XVIII of the Social Security Act for remote monitoring devices.

Mandates that the guidance specifically address devices that incorporate artificial intelligence components, such as continuous adjustment features.

Requires that these devices must transmit information to healthcare providers for the management and treatment of individuals to qualify for payment.

name: Workforce of the Future Act of 2024
summary:
Mandates the preparation of reports by the Secretary of Labor, the National Science Foundation, and the Secretary of Education on AI's workforce impact, identifying data needs, affected industries, and opportunities for stakeholder influence.

Authorizes the Department of Education to award grants to enhance emerging and advanced technology education from prekindergarten through grade 12, focusing on inclusivity for underrepresented communities.

Requires the Department of Labor to grant funds for upskilling workers in industries significantly impacted by AI, promoting lifelong learning and skill certifications.

Prescribes continuous evaluation and monitoring of grant-funded activities, with a focus on sustaining project activities post-grant.

Demands biannual reporting by grantees on fund usage, disaggregated by demographic factors, and a comprehensive report to Congress within five years.

Amends existing education laws to integrate emerging technology education data, emphasizing competency in AI-related skills among students.

name: PATHS Act
summary:
Extends the research and development acquisition pilot program under the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to September 30, 2027.

Mandates the Secretary of Homeland Security to notify and brief Congress within 72 hours regarding the use or extension of transaction authority involving artificial intelligence technology.

Reduces the threshold for covered contract awards from $4,000,000 to $1,000,000 under the James M. Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023.

name: Civilian Agency AI Watermark Act
summary:
Mandates the Secretary of Homeland Security to consult with the Director of the National Institute of Standards and Technology and the Director of the United States Patent and Trademark Office within eight months to develop an AI watermark and trademark system for identifying Federal agency-approved AI applications for civilian agency use.

Authorizes the appropriation of necessary funds each fiscal year to the Secretary of Homeland Security to implement this AI watermark system.

name: American Privacy Rights Act of 2024, Sec. 114-5
summary:
Establishes a pilot program to encourage private sector use of privacy-enhancing technologies within one year of the Act's enactment to protect covered data.

Requires the Commission to develop a petition process for entities to join the pilot program and implement an auditing system using privacy-enhancing technologies for enforcement purposes.

Mandates ongoing audits of participating entities to ensure compliance with privacy-enhancing technologies.

Allows covered entities deemed compliant to be considered in compliance with section 109, with a rebuttable presumption in certain legal actions.

Obligates the Comptroller General to study the pilot program's progress and effectiveness, with an initial briefing and a final report to Congress.

Creates a new bureau within the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) to enforce the title with experts, including technologists experienced with AI.

Establishes a Privacy and Security Victims Relief Fund for consumer redress and technological research.

Requires the FTC to report to Congress on investigations and future plans related to the title.

name: VOICE Act of 2024
summary:
Establishes a grant program to promote digital citizenship and media literacy among veterans, requiring the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to award grants to eligible entities.

Mandates grant recipients to develop cybersecurity best practices and improve veterans' competencies in digital and media literacy.

Requires grant recipients to submit a report on their activities and effectiveness one year after receiving funds.

Obliges the Secretary to report to Congress on the program's overall activities and effectiveness after receiving the last report from grant recipients.

Authorizes $20 million in appropriations for fiscal years 2023, 2025, and 2027 to fund the program.

Defines key terms such as "cybersecurity best practices," "digital citizenship," "media literacy," and "eligible entity."

Encourages the Secretary to maintain a list of grant recipients and promote communication among them.

Acknowledges the role of foreign influence campaigns and online scams targeting veterans as critical issues that need addressing.

name: Department of Energy AI Act
summary:
Establishes a cross-cutting AI research and development program within the Department of Energy to advance AI tools, systems, and capabilities.

Mandates coordination across relevant offices such as the Office of Science and the Office of Energy Efficiency to carry out this program.

Requires financial assistance for research in areas like AI application in simulations, data analysis, and energy-efficient computing.

Supports technology transfer and the use of high-performance computing infrastructure to develop advanced AI systems.

Establishes data center testbeds to improve energy efficiency in AI training and inference.

Encourages partnerships with federal and private entities to enhance AI research and development.

Emphasizes ethical considerations, cybersecurity, and data privacy in AI projects.

Allocates $300 million annually from 2025 to 2030 for these initiatives.

Requires an assessment of energy security related to data centers and computing resources, with recommendations for policy changes.

name: Secure A.I. Act
summary:
Establishes a voluntary database to track AI security and safety incidents, requiring the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) to develop mechanisms for sharing incident information while preserving confidentiality.

Mandates NIST to update the National Vulnerability Database to incorporate AI security vulnerabilities and identify characteristics that make the database unsuitable for certain AI vulnerabilities.

Prohibits employer retaliation against employees who report AI incidents, allowing legal recourse for aggrieved parties.

Directs the establishment of best practices for addressing AI supply chain risks, involving multiple stakeholders.

Established the Artificial Intelligence Security Center within the National Security Agency to facilitate AI security research, guidance development, and ensure the availability of test-beds for secure AI research.

name: FORECASTS Tracking Act of 2024
summary:
Amends the Food Security Act of 1985 to improve subseasonal-to-seasonal weather forecasting by requiring the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) to enhance research, data collection, and model development.

Mandates the development of multi-model ensemble forecast systems and data management strategies, and the operationalization of new modeling technologies.

Establishes an Internet clearinghouse for forecasts and related information.

Creates the Weather and Earth System Modeling and Data Assimilation Workforce Innovation Program to support education, recruitment, and workforce development in weather modeling and data assimilation, emphasizing artificial intelligence and machine learning.

Requires the Under Secretary to develop and update a workforce human capital plan and report on the program's effectiveness.

Authorizes appropriations for these initiatives, including $40 million annually from 2025 to 2030 for the workforce program and additional funding for NOAA's weather research activities.

name: TAME Extreme Weather Act
summary:
Mandates the development of comprehensive weather forecasting training datasets using AI to improve Earth system modeling and weather forecasts.

Requires collaboration with federal agencies and experts to enhance AI weather models and explore AI's role in public preparedness and resilience.

Directs the use of AI for fire environment modeling to predict, detect, and forecast wildfires and associated hazards.

Establishes an emissions monitoring program using AI to analyze global atmospheric data and improve greenhouse gas emission models.

Encourages partnerships with private and academic entities to advance AI in weather forecasting and environmental predictions.

Calls for recruitment and development of a diverse workforce skilled in AI applications for weather forecasting.

Allows public access to data and code developed under this Act, with safeguards for national security and intellectual property.

Supports ongoing research and data acquisition for AI and numerical weather models, ensuring continued advancement in weather prediction technologies.

name: Digital Social Platform Transparency Act
summary:
Mandates digital social companies to post terms of service for each platform within 180 days, detailing contact information, content flagging processes, and potential actions like banning or demonetization.

Requires translation of terms into all supported languages.

Obligates companies to submit semiannual terms of service reports to the Attorney General, detailing content moderation practices and AI involvement, including flagged content statistics and appeal outcomes.

Establishes penalties up to $15,000 per day for non-compliance, managed by the Attorney General, who can take legal action.

Specifies the creation of a public repository of reports for transparency.

Excludes platforms limited to direct messaging or transactions from the Act's scope and protects end-to-end encryption.

Defines key terms and grants the Attorney General interpretive authority.

Ensures Act's obligations and penalties are additional to existing laws.

name: NSF and USDA Interagency Research Act
summary:
Mandates the Secretary of Agriculture and the Director of the National Science Foundation to conduct collaborative research and development activities, including those involving artificial intelligence and digital agriculture, to advance their mission priorities.

Requires the establishment of memoranda of understanding to coordinate these activities through competitive, merit-based processes.

Permits collaborative research in key areas, such as AI, machine learning, automation, and digital agriculture.

Encourages data sharing and collaboration among federal agencies, educational institutions, and nonprofit entities.

Supports research infrastructure and the development of translational technologies for commercial use.

Facilitates public-private partnerships and awards grants to educational institutions to establish a Center for Agricultural Research, Education, and Workforce Development.

Authorizes reimbursable agreements to enhance research effectiveness and mandates a report to Congress on interagency coordination and future collaboration opportunities.

Ensures research security consistent with the CHIPS Act of 2022.

name: Modernizing Data Practices to Improve Government Act
summary:
Amends section 3520A of title 44, United States Code, to extend the Chief Data Officer Council's authority to improve Federal data governance.

Requires the Council to identify opportunities to enhance data governance for reliable and secure adoption of emerging technologies and AI.

Mandates appointment of a representative from Chief Artificial Intelligence Officers to the Council.

Obligates the Council to submit biennial reports detailing recommendations for developing datasets and data governance policies to support AI adoption.

Instructs the Council to assess data governance challenges, clarify roles among senior agency leaders, and recommend best practices for AI data use.

Requires recommendations for data ownership policies to ensure government rights and pre-procurement AI reviews.

Directs the Director to issue guidance based on Council reports.

Mandates an annual data management report to Congress clarifying Chief Data Officers' roles in AI governance.

Sunsets the amendments seven years after enactment.

name: Fraudulent Artificial Intelligence Regulations (FAIR) Elections Act of 2024
summary:
Prohibits the distribution of false AI-generated election media containing materially false information about election details or voter eligibility with the intent to impede voting in federal elections.

Prohibits the distribution of false AI-generated depictions of election officials intended to intimidate or harass officials or deter voting.

Exempts bona fide news entities from these prohibitions if they clearly disclose the falsity of the AI-generated content.

Empowers the Attorney General to enforce these prohibitions through civil actions in U.S. District Courts.

Amends the National Voter Registration Act to prevent states from using unverified databases to remove voters from official lists, requiring government-verified information approved by the Attorney General.

Sets criteria for source information, including monthly updates and non-violation of the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act.

Ensures severability of the Act’s provisions, maintaining the validity of remaining sections if any part is invalidated.

name: National Windstorm Impact Reduction Program Reauthorization Act of 2024
summary:
Amends the National Windstorm Impact Reduction Act of 2004 to include provisions for understanding climate variability and its impact on windstorms, aiming to inform future building codes.

Supports the integration of emerging technologies, such as machine learning, in research and engineering activities related to windstorm mitigation.

Encourages interdisciplinary research, including collaborations between social scientists and engineers, to enhance atmospheric measurements relevant to building engineering.

Promotes the use of advanced construction methods and materials to strengthen properties against windstorms and related impacts.

Mandates an analysis of the need for a tornado research facility to study tornado impacts on buildings.

Requires research into public response to windstorm risks and factors influencing risk communication and reduction measures.

Allocates specific funding amounts for the program from fiscal years 2025 to 2029.

Sets deadlines for reports and analyses, including future research infrastructure needs, to be completed by specified dates.

name: H.R. 9626, DOD Secure Computing and Data Storage Plan Development
summary:
Mandates the Under Secretary of Defense for Research and Engineering to develop a plan for a secure computing and data storage environment, termed the "AIxBio sandbox," to facilitate the testing of AI models trained on biological data.

Requires the AIxBio sandbox to utilize existing Department of Defense infrastructure when feasible and designates the Under Secretary of Defense for managing and overseeing its activities.

Directs the Under Secretary to select projects for the sandbox that demonstrate potential defense applications at the intersection of AI and biotechnology, such as medical countermeasures and biomanufacturing.

Establishes mechanisms for collaboration between Department of Defense laboratories and academic institutions to support AIxBio projects, with streamlined processes for efficient partnerships.

Obligates the Under Secretary to report and brief Congress on the plan within one year of the Act's enactment.

name: DETECT Fentanyl and Xylazine Act of 2024
summary:
Amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to enhance the detection and disruption of drugs like fentanyl and xylazine using advanced technologies.

Mandates research and development of equipment for drug detection and trafficking disruption, emphasizing minimal handling and separation of complex mixtures.

Incorporates machine learning and artificial intelligence to predict controlled substance analogues and new psychoactive substances.

Requires the Under Secretary for Science and Technology to adhere to the NIST AI Risk Management Framework or its successor.

Establishes research and evaluation priorities using the latest information from reports on drug threats by the Drug Enforcement Administration.

Ensures federal, state, local, tribal, and territorial law enforcement agencies have access to improved detection technologies.

name: State Industrial Competitiveness Act of 2024
summary:
Amends the Energy Policy and Conservation Act to establish the Flex-Tech Energy Program aimed at enhancing manufacturing competitiveness.

Requires the Secretary to provide financial assistance to State energy agencies or Indian Tribes for developing and implementing flex-tech programs, including measures related to advanced manufacturing technologies and artificial intelligence.

Mandates that energy studies of manufacturing facilities evaluate systems, emissions, and potential efficiency measures, including AI applications.

Allocates at least 5% of funds specifically for Indian Tribes or manufacturers in Indian Country.

Limits financial assistance usage, capping administrative expenses at 10% and individual facility funding at $100,000 or 5% of total assistance.

Encourages the use of both public and private financing in program implementation.

Authorizes $100 million annually from 2025 to 2029 for the program.

name: Artificial Intelligence Public Awareness and Education Campaign Act
summary:
Mandates the Secretary of Commerce to conduct a public awareness and education campaign on artificial intelligence within 180 days of the Act's enactment, in coordination with relevant Federal agencies.

Requires determination of key performance indicators for evaluating the AI Campaign’s effectiveness and gathering baseline data for comparison.

Facilitates information exchange on AI to promote knowledge and rights awareness, and identifies best practices for detecting AI-generated media like deepfakes.

Conducts outreach to the public about AI's prevalence and applications in daily life and commercial settings.

Targets outreach to vulnerable groups, such as senior citizens, to prevent AI-enabled fraud.

Promotes workforce opportunities in AI, including Federal Government roles, and engages with educational institutions.

Consults with stakeholders from academia, industry, and community organizations on AI usage.

Requires a report to Congress within one year on the AI Campaign’s activities, key performance indicators, and recommendations for future actions.

Prohibits authorization of additional funds for implementing this Act.

name: Ending FCC Meddling in Our Elections Act
summary:
Prohibits the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) from promulgating or enforcing any rules related to the disclosure of artificial intelligence-generated content in political advertisements.

Restricts the FCC specifically from acting on the draft notice of proposed rulemaking circulated by the Chairwoman on May 22, 2024, concerning AI-generated content disclosure in political ads across television, radio, or other services.

Bars the FCC from enacting any rules substantially similar to the aforementioned proposal.

name: Supercritical Geothermal Research and Development Act
summary:
Amends the Energy Independence and Security Act of 2007 to include machine learning algorithms in geothermal research and development.

Establishes a supercritical geothermal research and development program within the Geothermal Technologies Office, focusing on well completion, permeability, materials, sensors, and water-rock geochemistry.

Requires the creation of a repository for geothermal data, with periodic updates for data standardization and accessibility.

Mandates a memorandum of understanding for data sharing regarding geothermal development among federal departments.

Directs the Secretary of the Interior to drill deep exploration boreholes for geothermal mapping.

Establishes a next-generation geothermal center of excellence to coordinate research, development, and workforce initiatives.

Authorizes $5 million annually from 2026 to 2030 for these activities.

Updates geothermal resource assessments quadrennially to include supercritical geothermal regions.

Requires progress reports on geothermal resource potential and commercialization barriers.

name: SMART in Schools Act
summary:
Mandates the Secretaries of Education and Health & Human Services to develop educational toolkits about artificial intelligence (AI) and social media's impact on youth.

Requires consultation with various relevant stakeholders, including students, parents & guardians, educators, administrators, and healthcare professionals, to develop the toolkits.

Specifies guidelines for each different type of toolkit, to be appropriately targeted to their multiple intended audiences: students, parents & guardians, educators, administrators, and healthcare professionals.

Directs the Secretaries to develop toolkit dissemination strategies, so that the resources reach their intended audiences.

Authorizes $2,000,000 for facilitating the dissemination of the toolkits.

name: BIS IT Modernization Act
summary:
Mandates the Bureau of Industry and Security to adopt advanced data fusion, analytics, and AI capabilities to enhance export control processes and identify evasive trade patterns.

Requires the integration of AI and machine learning into Bureau IT systems to improve decision-making and enforce export controls effectively.

Obligates the Bureau to automate and streamline data sharing with industry, federal agencies, and international partners.

Demands the modernization of IT systems to support seamless data management, enhance security, and facilitate the use of cutting-edge technology.

Stipulates objectives for technology adoption, including productivity enhancement, cost reduction, and improved user experience for U.S. exporters.

Instructs the Under Secretary to reassess staffing needs and consult Congress on personnel adjustments during the modernization.

Authorizes $25 million annually from 2025 to 2028 for these initiatives.

name: Protecting Patients from Deceptive Drug Ads Online Act
summary:
Amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to impose civil penalties on social media influencers and healthcare providers who make false or misleading communications about prescription drugs.

Mandates the issuance of guidance within 180 days to define false or misleading communications and outline compliance procedures.

Expands the definition of "manufacturer, packer, or distributor" to include telehealth providers involved in drug advertising.

Requires reporting of payments related to drug promotion to the Secretary of Health and Human Services.

Authorizes market surveillance activities using AI to monitor prescription drug promotions on social media and coordinate efforts with the Federal Trade Commission.

Allocates $15 million annually for fiscal years 2025 to 2029 to support these activities.

Establishes a process for notifying drug manufacturers of non-compliant communications by influencers or healthcare providers.

Ensures the severability of the Act's provisions, maintaining validity even if parts are invalidated.

name: S.4870, A bill to require reports on artificial intelligence regulation in the financial services industry.
summary:
Require the Federal Reserve, FDIC, OCC, NCUA, and CFPB to report on AI knowledge gaps in financial services within 90 days.

Mandate analysis on AI-assisted tasks in regulated institutions.

Assess current AI governance and oversight standards.

Identify additional regulatory authorities needed for effective mission execution.

Clarify overlapping AI regulatory issues between agencies.

Evaluate current and planned agency use of AI over the next three years, including fiscal and staffing impacts.

Determine necessary resources to adapt to AI changes and oversee its use.

Ensure reports exclude confidential or nonpublic information.

name: Preventing the Algorithmic Facilitation of Rental Housing Cartels Act of 2024
summary:
Prohibits rental property owners from using coordinators for algorithmic price coordination, deeming such actions per se violations of the Sherman Act.

Prohibits coordinators from facilitating non-competitive agreements among rental property owners or performing coordinating functions.

Prohibits coordinators from acquiring another coordinator if it lessens competition, violating the Clayton Act.

Empowers the Federal Trade Commission, the Attorney General, and State Attorneys General to enforce the Act with the same powers and duties as the FTC Act, Sherman Act, and Clayton Act.

Allows civil actions by injured persons to recover treble damages and litigation costs, with the option to invalidate pre-dispute arbitration agreements.

Clarifies that the Act does not preempt State, Tribal, or local laws that supplement its provisions.

Ensures severability of the Act if any provision is deemed unconstitutional, maintaining the effectiveness of remaining provisions.

name: Improving Seniors’ Timely Access to Care Act of 2024
summary:
Mandates Medicare Advantage plans, starting January 1, 2027, to implement an electronic prior authorization program for secure electronic transmission of requests and responses, excluding certain formats like facsimiles.

Requires plans, beginning January 1, 2026, to meet transparency requirements, including submitting annual data on prior authorization requests, appeals, and the use of AI technologies in decision-making.

Obligates plans to provide access to authorization criteria and documentation requirements to providers, suppliers, and enrollees upon request.

Empowers the Secretary of Health and Human Services to establish response timeframes for prior authorization requests, potentially as short as 24 hours.

Tasks the Medicare Payment Advisory Commission with analyzing and reporting on prior authorization use and recommending improvements.

Directs the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services to study and report on real-time decision processes and the impact of AI on patient access, especially for rural and low-income beneficiaries.

name: S.4862, A bill to ensure that new advances in artificial intelligence are ethically adopted to improve the health of all individuals, and for other purposes.
summary:
Amends the Public Health Service Act to mandate the NIH Director develop AI resources and datasets for health research, provide AI expertise, and maintain data access resources.

Authorizes $400 million for NIH AI initiatives in fiscal year 2025.

Directs the National Coordinator for Health IT to utilize electronic health records for research, establish data standards, and align with national interoperability frameworks.

Appropriates $10 million for data collection and $50 million for data standards.

Requires hospitals to request patient consent to use health records for research, contingent upon patient approval.

Expresses the Senate's view that NIH representation is crucial in steering committees for national AI research resources.

Mandates the National Library of Medicine to establish data-sharing facilities and create a core data science program.

Appropriates $100 million each for these library initiatives in fiscal year 2025.

name: Sec. 103, Supporting Affordability and Fairness with Every Bet Act
summary:
Prohibits sports wagering operators from using artificial intelligence to track individual wagers, target specific individuals with offers or promotions, or create gambling products like microbets.

Requires sports wagering operators to ensure data security and to take reasonable steps to prevent unauthorized access or dissemination of wagering and customer data.

Mandates real-time or near-real-time sharing of anonymized sports wagering data with the State regulatory entity.

Imposes strict consumer protections, including restrictions on AI use, limits on deposits, and mandatory affordability checks for high-value wagers.

Establishes comprehensive standards for licensing, recordkeeping, and employee background checks to ensure the integrity and accountability of sports wagering operators.

Requires cooperation with investigations by regulatory authorities and sports organizations, and mandates robust internal controls for operators.

Prohibits advertising targeting problem gamblers or individuals ineligible to wager, and restricts broadcast times and content. 

Enforces restrictions to maintain contest integrity and prevent betting on certain events and by prohibited individuals.

name: Modernizing Retrospective Regulatory Review Act
summary:
Requires the Director of the Office of Management and Budget to report on the progress of making agency regulations available in machine-readable format within 180 days.

Mandates the issuance of guidance within 18 months on using technology, including AI, for conducting retrospective reviews of agency regulations.

Instructs agencies to use technology to identify obsolete, ineffective, or problematic regulations and adequately train personnel in its use.

Obliges agency heads to submit a detailed plan within two years for implementing the guidance, including identifying regulations for review.

Compels agency heads to implement the strategy for retrospective review within 180 days after plan submission.

name: Content Origin Protection and Integrity from Edited and Deepfaked Media Act of 2024
summary:
Mandates the development of standards for content provenance and detection of synthetic and synthetically-modified content through a public-private partnership.

Requires tools used commercially to create synthetic or synthetically-modified content to provide the option of including machine-readable content provenance information, with security measures to prevent tampering.
