Prohibits knowingly removing or altering content provenance information in furtherance of unfair or deceptive acts.

Prohibits the non-consensual use of content with attached provenance information for training AI systems, requiring express consent and adherence to copyright terms.

Empowers the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) and state attorneys general to enforce the Act, treating violations as unfair or deceptive acts.

Permits private parties to bring civil actions for violations involving content provenance information.

Ensures the Act does not alter existing copyright rights and includes provisions for severability, maintaining the Act’s effectiveness even if parts are invalidated.

name: Sec. 2412 of 2023 Consumer Protection Act
summary:
Prohibits non-governmental entities from designing or employing AI, or handling personal data, in a way that will:

(1) Cause physical, psychological, economic, relational, or repetitional injuries to a person;

(2) Discriminate on the basis of standard protected classes, including race and nationality; or

(3) Discriminate in the granting of access to important services and opportunities, including employment, credit, and education.

Exempts private groups not open to the public from the requirements outlined above.

name: Modernizing Wildfire Safety and Prevention Act of 2024, Section 405 ("Joint Office of the Fire Environment Center (Report Recommendations 104, 105, 106)")
summary:
Establishes the Joint Office of the Fire Environment Center within one year, under the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration.

Requires the Data Services branch to test AI and machine learning technologies to aid fire management, suggesting resources based on real-time fire conditions.

Mandates the provision of science-based, data-rich services for fire management, including predictive and decision-support tools.

Develops a technological common operating environment to integrate air quality data and other public health information.

Forms a 12-member board governing the Joint Office, including federal and non-federal wildfire community representatives.

Empowers the Joint Office to contract with government and private entities for necessary supplies and services.

Authorizes $150 million annually from fiscal years 2025 to 2034 for the Joint Office's operations.

name: Sec. 2501 of 2023 Consumer Protection Act
summary:
Requires operators of dominant online platforms with (a) large numbers of users and (b) ownership groups in which at least 10% of the members are citizens of foreign adversaries of the U.S. to sequester any back-end data or algorithm from agents of any foreign entity.

Also regulates foreign ownership of, and the granting of licenses for foreigners to operate, online platforms featuring large numbers of users, regardless of whether the platform uses AI.

name: Health Equity and Accountability Act of 2024, Sec 1013 ("Task Force on Preventing Bias in AI and Algorithms")
summary:
Establishes the Task Force on Preventing AI and Algorithmic Bias in Health Care within 30 days to guide the development of AI technologies that do not exacerbate health disparities.

Composes the Task Force of various health and public officials, including experts on health equity and minority health.

Mandates the Task Force to examine AI and algorithms in healthcare, identifying risks related to civil rights, civil liberties, and discriminatory bias.

Requires submission of a report to Congress within one year detailing findings and recommendations for safe AI implementation in healthcare.

Obliges the Task Force to publish the report on the Department of Health and Human Services' website.

Initiates a public comment period of at least 90 days on the Task Force’s duties and activities.

Allows the Chairperson to appoint additional staff without adherence to certain civil service laws, ensuring flexibility in task force operations.

name: Citizen Engagement on Development of Federal Civilian Agency Use of AI Act
summary:
Mandates the Secretary of Homeland Security to conduct virtual and in-person listening sessions across the United States for discussing Federal civilian agency use of artificial intelligence.

Requires inclusion of diverse groups in these discussions, such as civil rights organizations, immigrant communities, and academia.

Encourages these groups to hold their own listening sessions and report back on AI development and adoption.

Obligates the Secretary of Homeland Security to submit a report to Congress within 240 days of enactment, and annually thereafter, detailing public attitudes and beliefs on Federal civilian agency use of AI.

name: No Robot Bosses Act
summary:
Prohibits employers from making any employment-related decisions -- including to fire or discipline an employee -- based solely on the output of an automated decision system.

Requires any automated decision system used to inform employment-related decisions to be tested before deployment for efficacy and compliance with relevant employment laws & the Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework from the National Institute of Standards & Technology. Systems must also be tested both before deployment and annually after deployment for non-discrimination on the basis of protected classes.

Requires employers to disclose to employees the use of automated decision systems for employment-related decisions and information on the workings of the system and the data used to reach its decision.

Establishes new roles and bodies in the Department of Labor to monitor and enforce this policy and to guide the development of future regulations on the use of automated decision systems in employment-related decision-making.

Establishes protections for whistleblowers who call attention to violations of this policy.

name: MedShield Act of 2024
summary:
Requires the Secretary of Health and Human Services to implement the MedShield program, utilizing artificial intelligence for pandemic preparedness and response.

Mandates the use of AI for developing a global pathogen surveillance system, accelerating vaccine development, and optimizing pathogen tracking and therapeutic interventions.

Obligates the Secretary to integrate recommendations from the National Security Commission on Artificial Intelligence and coordinate with federal agencies and international partners.

Directs the development of a plan to enhance public health and medical services as part of the National Response Framework.

Sets funding authorization at increasing annual amounts from $300 million in fiscal year 2025 to $500 million in fiscal year 2029.

Requires submission of a detailed report on the program's plan to relevant Congressional committees within 180 days of the Act's enactment.

name: Artificial Intelligence Civil Rights Act of 2024
summary:
Prohibits developers and deployers of AI algorithms from causing or contributing to discrimination based on protected characteristics.

Mandates developers and deployers to conduct pre-deployment evaluations and annual impact assessments of AI algorithms to identify potential harms or disparate impacts.

Requires independent audits of AI algorithms and obligates developers to provide relevant information to deployers for compliance.

Imposes transparency obligations, including public disclosures of AI practices and consumer rights, in multiple languages and accessible formats.

Grants the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) enforcement authority, including rulemaking, with violations treated as unfair or deceptive acts.

Provides a private right of action for individuals, enabling lawsuits for violations and barring pre-dispute arbitration agreements.

Establishes federal resources for algorithm auditing, including a new occupational series and additional personnel for the FTC to handle AI-related issues.

name: A bill to require the Secretary of Defense to carry out a pilot program on using artificial intelligence-enabled software to optimize the workflow and operations of depots, shipyards, and other manufacturing facilities run by the Department of Defense, and for other purposes.
summary:
Mandates the Secretary of Defense to initiate a pilot program within 60 days to evaluate artificial intelligence-enabled software for optimizing workflow and operations in Department of Defense facilities, including depots and shipyards.

Requires the assessment of AI software for contract management, particularly by the Defense Contract Management Agency.

Directs the use of best-in-class software platforms and consideration of industry best practices, alongside human-centered design methodologies.

Obligates a minimum expenditure of $35,000,000 for the pilot program.

Requires consultation with the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment and the Secretaries of the Army, Navy, and Air Force.

Mandates a report to Congress within one year detailing software evaluations, workflow modifications, and quantitative impacts observed during the pilot.

name: Fix Our Forests Act, Section 102 ("Fireshed Center")
summary:
Establishes a Fireshed Center through collaboration between the Forest Service and the U.S. Geological Survey, involving multiple federal agencies.

Appoints a Director from the U.S. Geological Survey or the Forest Service for a term of up to seven years.

Utilizes artificial intelligence and data tools to assess and predict fire and smoke at the wildland-urban interface for improved management, risk reduction, and recovery.

Promotes data sharing and coordination across federal, state, local, tribal, and private sectors.

Reduces duplication and fragmentation in predictive services and decision support related to wildland fires.

Streamlines procurement and cybersecurity processes.

Develops and disseminates publicly accessible data, models, and technologies for fire risk reduction and recovery planning.

Maintains the Fireshed Registry and supports its operations with personnel and services from the U.S. Geological Survey and the Forest Service.

name: Intelligence Authorization Act FY 2025, Title V, Section 505 ("Establishment of Artificial Intelligence Security Center")
summary:
Establishes an Artificial Intelligence Security Center within the National Security Agency's Cybersecurity Collaboration Center.

Requires the provision of a research test bed for AI security research to private sector and academic researchers, including secure access to proprietary third-party models with vendor consent.

Develops guidance to prevent or mitigate counter-artificial intelligence techniques.

Promotes secure AI adoption practices for national security systems and the defense industrial base.

Coordinates with the Artificial Intelligence Safety Institute of the National Institute of Standards and Technology.

Mandates terms of usage for researcher access to the test bed, ensuring limited publication to protect classified or proprietary information.

Ensures test bed availability to federal agencies on a cost-recovery basis.

Leverages existing infrastructure and resources for AI security research.

Establishes mechanisms, including contractual incentives, for providing access to proprietary models for qualified researchers.

name: Fix Our Forests Act, Section 303 ("Public-private wildfire technology deployment and demonstration partnership")
summary:
Establishes a deployment and demonstration pilot program for innovative wildfire technologies, including AI, within one year.

Incorporates the program into the National Wildfire Coordinating Group and advances key technology areas like remote sensing and interoperable data.

Requires coordination between selected private entities and federal agencies for real-time technology testing during wildfire mitigation.

Prioritizes entities involved in the Fire Weather Testbed or developing emerging technologies like AI and quantum sensing.

Mandates public outreach to invite applications from entities to demonstrate technologies.

Obligates annual reporting to Congress on program participants, technologies demonstrated, costs, outreach, and recommendations for technology adoption.

Specifies the program's authority will terminate seven years after enactment.

name: Intelligence Authorization Act FY 2025, Title V, Section 510 ("Management of artificial intelligence security risks")
summary:
Mandates the Director of the National Institute of Standards and Technology to update the National Vulnerability Database to incorporate AI security vulnerabilities within 180 days.

Requires the development of a voluntary database to track AI security and safety incidents, ensuring confidentiality and standardized reporting formats.

Instructs the Director to evaluate AI incidents for potential inclusion in the database, prioritizing critical infrastructure and high-impact cases.

Directs the Director of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency to update the Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures Program to address AI security vulnerabilities.

Initiates a multi-stakeholder evaluation of consensus standards for AI vulnerability reporting, with a report due to Congress within 180 days.

Requires collaboration to develop best practices for managing AI supply chain risks, focusing on data collection, documentation, and the use of open-source and proprietary datasets.

name: STAND with Taiwan Act of 2024, Section 11 ("Prohibition on investments by United States financial institutions that benefit the Government of the People's Republic of China or the Chinese Communist Party")
summary:
Prohibits United States financial institutions from making investments benefiting the Government of the People's Republic of China or the Chinese Communist Party.

Mandates the Secretary of the Treasury to enforce this prohibition within three days of a covered determination.

Defines prohibited investments as monetary investments to entities owned or controlled by the Chinese government or military.

Includes investments that benefit priority industrial sectors identified in Chinese strategic plans, such as "Made in China 2025" and the "14th Five Year Smart Manufacturing Development Plan."

Specifies prohibited sectors including artificial intelligence, machine learning, and robotics.

Defines "United States financial institution" to include investment companies, private equity firms, venture capital companies, and hedge funds that qualify as United States persons.

name: Intelligence Authorization Act FY 2025, Title V, Section 504 ("National security procedures to address certain risks and threats relating to artificial intelligence")
summary:
Mandates the President to develop procedures within 180 days to enable vendors, users, and researchers to notify the U.S. Government of AI-related security and biosecurity risks, including malicious software development, system compromise, and foreign malign influence.

Requires federal elements to provide threat briefings to AI vendors about foreign exploitation and threats.

Obligates the President to brief Congress on the procedures, specifying responsible federal agencies and outlining industry outreach and public education plans.

Utilizes existing laws and federal guidelines for research, stakeholder engagement, and risk management frameworks related to AI systems.

name: American Medical Innovation and Investment Act of 2024 (Sec. 5)
summary:
Mandates the Secretary of Health and Human Services to issue guidance on Medicare payment requirements for remote monitoring devices with AI components by January 1, 2026. 

Specifies that the devices, including continuous glucose monitors, must use AI components like continuous adjustment. 

Requires that these devices transmit information to healthcare providers for management and treatment purposes.

name: Synthetic Biology Advancement Act of 2024
summary:
Establishes the National Synthetic Biology Center to award grants for advancing synthetic biology in agriculture.

Requires the Center to prioritize research in areas like cellular biology, gene editing, and digital agriculture.

Mandates the use of artificial intelligence to accelerate modeling and measurement for synthetic biological solutions.

Provides grants to eligible institutions, fostering partnerships with entities such as nonprofits and national laboratories.

Sets criteria for grant applications, emphasizing the promotion of synthetic biology technologies and sustainability in agriculture.

Directs the Center to coordinate with technology transfer offices to commercialize innovations.

Requires the Center to maintain a website for disseminating findings and facilitating collaboration.

Obligates the Center to submit biennial reports to Congress on research findings and grant progress.

Authorizes appropriations for the Center's operation and grant awards from 2025 to 2029.

name: SAFE Bet Act
summary:
Establishes the "SAFE Bet Act," setting minimum federal standards for sports wagering, which includes restrictions on AI use by sports wagering operators. 

Prohibits operators from using AI to track individual wagers, target specific individuals with promotions, or create gambling products like microbets. 

Mandates state sports wagering programs to ensure compliance with standards, including consumer protections and advertising restrictions, and requires operators to maintain data security and recordkeeping. 

Enforces reporting of suspicious transactions and mandates cooperation with investigations into sports wagering activities. 

Creates a national self-exclusion list to prevent individuals from placing sports wagers across states, and establishes public health initiatives to monitor gambling addiction. 

Permits states and tribes to enact stricter sports wagering regulations and does not preempt their authority to tax sports wagering.

name: Land Grant Research Prioritization Act of 2023
summary: Amends the Food, Agriculture, Conservation, and Trade Act of 1990 to allow research and extension grants to be made for developing and evaluating agricultural applications of AI, with an emphasis on the use of AI to improve specialty crop production.

name: Supporting Innovation in Agriculture Act of 2024
summary:
Establishes a 30% tax credit for investments in innovative agricultural technology projects.

Defines qualified property to include tangible personal property, software, and computer systems used in such projects.

Specifies that projects must be placed in service before December 31, 2035, and focus on precision or controlled environment agriculture.

Includes technologies such as AI, machine learning, robotics, and automated systems within the scope of eligible projects.

Allows taxpayers to elect a payment in lieu of the credit for qualifying projects.

Prohibits double benefits for projects also funded by certain federal grants.

Applies the amendments to property construction beginning after January 1, 2023.

name: No CCP Consultants Act
summary:
Prohibits the Department of State from entering, renewing, or extending a contract to contractors that, in the past year, have consulted for foreign entities that pose national security or foreign policy concerns, including any entity under China’s control engaged in national security industries, such as producing AI-related products and services. 

Requires companies seeking to provide consulting services for the Department of State to disclose any conflict of interest with foreign entities above, or they may face a debarment of up to five years.

Requires the Secretary of the Department of State to issue procurement policies for the Department to implement the above prohibition, clarify disclosure requirements and penalties when soliciting contracts, and share best practices for how companies can avoid accidentally contracting with foreign entities that pose national security or foreign policy concerns.

name: Combat Chinese Economic Aggression Act of 2024, Section 4 ("Protection of covered sectors.")
summary:
Amends the Defense Production Act to add Title VIII, focusing on protecting sectors like AI.

Defines "covered activities" involving U.S. persons and foreign entities in countries of concern, including AI-related investments and collaborations.

Mandates the President to publish and annually update a list of technologies posing national security risks.

Empowers the President to prohibit U.S. persons from engaging in certain activities with foreign entities in critical sectors, including AI.

Requires mandatory notifications for covered activities not prohibited, with confidentiality protections for submitted information.

Obligates annual reporting to Congress on notifications, trends, and effectiveness of measures.

Directs the President to issue regulations specifying covered activities and technologies.

Encourages multilateral engagement with U.S. allies to develop comparable mechanisms for managing risks in covered sectors.

Authorizes penalties, including fines and imprisonment, for violations.

Provides for national interest waivers, requiring notification to Congress.

name: Drone Safety and Efficiency Act
summary:
Requires the Administrator of the Federal Aviation Administration to adopt a performance and risk-based approach when reviewing requests for certificates of waiver under Section 107 of Title 14, Code of Federal Regulations, which establishes rules for the operation of small unmanned aircraft systems (sUAS) for commercial purposes. 

Requires the Administrator to use big data analytics and machine learning to conduct the performance and risk-based approach and refrain from using open-ended descriptive prompts in the waiver application.

name: Investing in Tomorrow's Workforce Act of 2023
summary:
Authorizes the Secretary of Labor to award competitive grants to support projects addressing the training needs of workers likely to be displaced by automation.

Prioritizes grants for partnerships in areas with high concentrations of affected populations or industries susceptible to automation.

Requires eligible partnerships to provide training services, develop curricula, and offer employment benefits, such as transportation stipends and paid leave.

Mandates grant recipients to submit comprehensive reports on training outcomes, including transitions to new positions and earnings data.

Expands the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act to include training for workers impacted by automation.

Allocates $40 million annually from 2024 to 2028 for national dislocated worker grants to address impacts of automation.

Ensures grant usage aligns with labor standards and nondiscrimination provisions under the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act.

name: Platform Accountability and Transparency Act, Section 9 ("Rulemaking authority")
summary:
Requires platforms to make available public repositories of highly disseminated content and major public accounts, including content samples and metadata.

Obligates platforms to disclose advertising information, including ad content, targeting parameters, and dissemination metrics, while protecting user privacy.

Requires disclosure of the use of platform algorithms in the recommendation, amplification, or restriction of content and advertising

Compels platforms to report on recommender and ranking algorithms, detailing inputs, objectives, and significant changes, without revealing trade secrets.

Demands transparency in content moderation, with statistics on policy violations, identification methods (including artificial intelligence), and government orders.

name: Cyber PIVOTT Act
summary:
Amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to establish the "PIVOTT Program" for expanding cybersecurity education and training.

Requires CISA to partner with community colleges and technical schools to offer programs and internships aiming to build a skills-based cyber workforce.

Provides full scholarships to eligible students, covering all educational and associated costs.

Mandates a two-year service obligation in a cyber role for program participants, with exceptions for military service.

Specifies eligible institutions and program components, including skills-based exercises and internships.

Directs CISA to conduct outreach initiatives and host recruitment fairs.

Establishes program completion benefits, including access to a cyber training database and additional certification opportunities.

Sets terms for scholarship repayment if obligations are not met and allows for waiver of repayments in cases of hardship.

Outlines enrollment targets and requires reporting on program enrollment and CISA's education and training initiatives.

name: Sustaining America’s Fisheries for the Future Act of 2024, Title IV, Section 402 ("Expanding and improving electronic technologies.")
summary:
Mandates the use of electronic monitoring and other technologies in fisheries data collection, allowing vessels to avoid carrying observers if conditions are unsafe.

Requires the Secretary to integrate electronic monitoring and reporting technologies into fishery information collection programs and review these systems every five years.

Directs the Comptroller General to assess the National Marine Fisheries Service's electronic monitoring capabilities and recommend improvements.

Establishes an electronic technologies innovation prize to encourage advancements in AI, machine learning, and data management for fisheries.

Creates an advisory panel to guide the development and deployment of electronic technologies in fisheries, including performance standards and data ownership.

Exempts the advisory panel from the Federal Advisory Committee Act.

Allows Councils to independently develop electronic technologies for data collection and management.

name: WIOA Performance Accountability Improvement Act, Section 2, Subsection (c) ("Evaluation of State programs.")
summary:
Amends the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act to require states to use data for analyses and ongoing evaluations of programs.

Allows states to use machine learning or other advanced analytics to enhance program operations, outcomes, and identify areas needing further evaluation.

name: To amend the Communications Act of 1934 to establish technical and procedural standards for artificial or prerecorded voice systems created through generative artificial intelligence, and for other purposes.
summary:
Amends the Communications Act of 1934 to establish standards for artificial or prerecorded voice systems created through generative AI.

Includes technologies such as voice cloning and other subsequent technologies as deemed appropriate by the Commission.

Inserts these standards into Section 227(d)(3) to ensure compliance with the updated regulatory framework.

name: Stop Spying Bosses Act
summary:
Prohibits employers from using workplace surveillance to monitor labor activities, ascertain political or religious views, or determine health or immigration status unrelated to job duties.

Requires employers to disclose details about workplace surveillance practices, including data collection methods, frequency, storage locations, business purposes, and third-party transfers, to employees and applicants.

Establishes a Privacy and Technology Division within the Department of Labor to oversee compliance and issue regulations.

Allows employees to access, correct, and request data collected about them and prohibits data transfer to third parties without disclosure and cybersecurity measures.

Grants employees and labor organizations the right to bring civil actions against violations, with potential damages and injunctive relief.

Prohibits predispute arbitration agreements regarding surveillance-related disputes.

Mandates annual reports to Congress on workplace surveillance impacts and recommendations for mitigating harms.

Coordinates with federal and state agencies to ensure consistent regulatory treatment of workplace surveillance.

name: Sustaining America’s Fisheries for the Future Act of 2024, Title IV, Section 401 ("Data modernization.")
summary:
Aligns the national strategic plan for fisheries data with the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration's (NOAA) Artificial Intelligence Strategy to enhance efficiency and interoperability.

Requires the Secretary, through the Assistant Administrator for Fisheries, to provide a strategic plan to Congress within 180 days, detailing goals, implementation schedules, budgets, stakeholder engagement, and system development.

Solicits expertise from data management and technology experts both within and outside the government to support the strategic plan.

Mandates the Secretary to report annually to Congress on progress in implementing the fisheries data modernization efforts.

name: NO FAKES Act of 2024
summary:
Establishes the right for individuals and right holders to authorize the use of their voice or visual likeness in digital replicas, treating it as a property right that is licensable but not assignable during the individual's life.

Allows post-mortem transfer and licensing, enabling rights to be inherited and renewed under specific conditions.

Imposes liability for unauthorized production, distribution, or public display of digital replicas without consent, with certain exclusions for news, historical, and public interest uses.

Provides safe harbors for online services that act promptly to remove unauthorized replicas upon notification.

Preempts conflicting state laws, except for those existing before January 2, 2025, or those addressing sexually explicit or election-related replicas.

Applies only to conduct and contracts occurring after the enactment date, while granting rights retroactively to deceased individuals' estates.

name: SPEED through Screening Act
summary:
Requires the Administrator to submit strategies within one year to reduce patdowns and the need for item divestiture during passenger screening without compromising security.

Considers technological improvements, discrimination reduction among passenger populations, and next-generation screening technologies in developing these strategies.

Mandates a feasibility study on allowing increased volumes of liquids, aerosols, gels, and powders on aircraft without reducing security.

Permits deployment of detection at range technology for screening, subject to feasibility assessments and prioritizes reducing patdowns and enhancing security for vulnerable populations.

Obligates collection and publication of anonymized screening statistics, considering privacy and civil rights, utilizing AI and noninvasive technologies.

Allocates $20 million for fiscal year 2024 to research and deploy improved screening technologies.

Requires annual briefings to congressional committees and a Comptroller General review within two years on the Act's implementation.

name: Better Mental Health Care for Americans Act, Sec. 203
summary:
Amends Section 1851(d)(4) of the Social Security Act to include provisions for behavioral health information starting in 2025.

Requires the provision of information on access to in-network behavioral health providers, including average wait times for new patient appointments and data on provider participation agreements.

Mandates disclosure of payment request statistics for mental health or substance use disorder services, specifying the percentage handled by in-network versus out-of-network providers.

Requires reporting on the number and percentage of denials for prior authorization or payment for mental health services compared to non-mental health services, categorized by denial type and service type.

Specifies the use of decision support, AI, machine learning, clinical decision-making, or other technologies in denial processes, with comparisons to similar physical health conditions.

Aims to promote informed choice by enhancing transparency in behavioral health service coverage.

name: Better Mental Health Care for Americans Act, Sec. 201
summary:
Amends Medicare Advantage plans to require parity in mental health and substance use disorder benefits, ensuring financial and treatment limitations are no more restrictive than those for medical benefits.

Mandates MA organizations to determine medical necessity for mental health and substance use benefits based on generally accepted standards.

Requires MA organizations to conduct and submit comparative analyses of nonquantitative treatment limitations (NQTLs) for mental health and substance use disorder benefits.

Imposes penalties for failing to comply with the mental health parity requirements.

Extends parity provisions to prescription drug plans, ensuring consistent application across Medicare Advantage and prescription drug plans.

Directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to issue implementing regulations within 18 months.

Sets the effective date for amendments to plan years beginning two years post-enactment, with $10 million allocated for implementation funding through the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services.

name: Agriculture and National Security Act of 2024
summary:
Mandates the Secretary of Agriculture to prioritize national security alongside homeland security within the Department of Agriculture, including increasing staff with security clearances.

Establishes the position of Senior Advisor for National Security to advise the Secretary and coordinate with the National Security Council on national security matters related to food and agriculture.

Authorizes the Secretary to exchange personnel with defense, national security, law enforcement, and intelligence agencies to improve information sharing and risk mitigation.

Requires biennial reports to Congress and the National Security Council assessing national security gaps in the food and agriculture sector, including cybersecurity and AI, and detailing actions taken and recommendations for policy changes.

Addresses vulnerabilities concerning agricultural data, foreign influence, and emerging technologies.

name: AI Fraud Deterrence Act
summary:
Amends penalties for financial crimes committed with the assistance of artificial intelligence, increasing fines to $1,000,000 and imprisonment terms.

Mandates fines for AI-assisted money laundering to be not more than $1,000,000 or thrice the value of the funds involved, with imprisonment terms up to 20 years.

Defines "artificial intelligence" according to the National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020 definition.

Codifies increased penalties and definitions within the United States Code to deter AI-assisted financial crimes.

name: Next Generation Military Education Act
summary:
Amends the National Defense Authorization Act to require the Department of Defense to develop and provide distance education courses on artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning for Armed Forces personnel.

Mandates these courses to cover AI literacy, ethical use, data protection, and awareness of AI-generated content.

Requires military departments to ensure access and notify personnel about these courses.

Obligates the Secretary of Defense to report to Congress on the progress of these activities.

Expands participation in the Digital On-Demand Program to all Department of Defense entities and personnel, promoting AI education.

Incorporates AI risks and threats into annual cybersecurity training for Armed Forces and civilian Department of Defense employees.

Requires annual reporting to Congress on the expansion and promotion of the Digital On-Demand Program. 

Defines key terms, including "artificial intelligence" and "Digital On-Demand Program."

name: Eliminating Bias in Algorithmic Systems Act of 2024
summary:
Require each agency that uses, funds, or oversees algorithms to establish an office of civil rights focused on bias, discrimination, and other algorithmic harms.

Mandate these civil rights offices to employ experts and technologists to address issues related to covered algorithms.

Obligate each office of civil rights to submit biennial reports to congressional committees detailing the state of algorithms, risks of bias and discrimination, mitigation steps taken, stakeholder engagement, and recommendations for further actions.

Establish an interagency working group on algorithms and civil rights, led by the Assistant Attorney General of the Civil Rights Division, with membership from each agency's civil rights office.

Authorize necessary appropriations for agencies to implement the Act's provisions.

name: Modernizing Data Practices to Improve Government Act
summary:
Amends title 44 of the United States Code to define "artificial intelligence" and "data governance."

Requires Chief Data Officers to focus on data management and governance, including AI-related data standards.

Mandates the Chief Data Officer Council to enhance data governance, evaluate new technologies, and ensure AI use improves government operations.

Directs the Council to report on data governance progress and provide recommendations for AI and emerging technology adoption, including data transparency and privacy.

Obliges the Director to issue guidance on implementing Council recommendations and maintain a public inventory of Chief Data Officers.

Sets reporting requirements for the Comptroller General on the Council's effectiveness and challenges.

Establishes a sunset clause, rendering the section ineffective after December 14, 2031.

Prohibits the allocation of additional funds to implement the Act.

name: Economic Security and Diplomacy Act of 2024
summary:
Amends the State Department Basic Authorities Act to establish a Deputy Secretary of State for Economic Security, responsible for U.S. economic security matters including sanctions, trade, and supply chains.

Transfers assets, personnel, and duties from existing offices to this new Deputy Secretary role.

Redesignates and relocates various offices and positions, including creating an Assistant Secretary for Technology and Innovation Security, responsible for policy on emerging technologies and research security.

Establishes an Office of Economic Analysis and Targeting to conduct economic analysis, prepare sanctions targeting packages, and manage a federal database on economic security data.

Authorizes $5 million annually for artificial intelligence and machine learning tools to support data analysis.

Allows hiring of additional personnel without standard competitive service requirements to support these new roles and offices.

Designates Foreign Service officers to represent the Deputy Secretary's mission at strategic posts worldwide.

name: Improving Diagnosis in Medicine Act of 2024
summary:
Amends the Public Health Service Act to establish a comprehensive research program on diagnostic safety and quality, focusing on reducing diagnostic errors and integrating AI tools.

Directs funding for new and existing research centers and mandates stakeholder engagement to enhance diagnostic quality and safety.

Requires the convening of an expert panel, including the Chief Artificial Intelligence Officer, to recommend data types and sources for research improvement.

Establishes an Interagency Council on Improving Diagnosis in Health Care, including members from AI-related departments, to enhance diagnosis quality and identify research gaps.

Mandates the creation of a strategic federal plan to improve diagnosis, with updates and progress reports submitted biennially to Congress.

Authorizes appropriations for these initiatives from 2025 to 2029, ensuring sustained financial support for improving diagnostic practices and integrating AI solutions.

name: SUPERSAFE Act
summary:
Directs the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) to establish a consortium representing federal, state, and academic stakeholders. The consortium will use supercomputing and machine learning to develop models that predict adverse health effects from toxic substances, establishing rapid approaches for large-scale identification of toxic substances and the development of safer alternatives.

Requires the Consortium to recommend how the information produced can be used in risk assessments by the EPA, other federal agencies, and industry.

Appropriates funding to the EPA Administrator to carry out the Consortium and requires the Consortium to make its model predictions public and accessible.

name: Block Nuclear Launch by Autonomous Artificial Intelligence Act
summary:
Prohibits the use of federal funds to operate autonomous weapons systems which launch nuclear weapons, or select or engage targets for nuclear weapons, without meaningful human control.

Defines 'meaningful human control' as the ability for humans to control the selection and engagement of targets, as well as the time, location and manner of the use of nuclear weapons.

name: CREATE AI Act of 2023
summary:
Establishes a steering committee to oversee the NAIRR.

Authorizes the National Science Foundation, in coordination with the NAIRR steering committee, to establish the National AI Research Resource.

Creates a NAIRR Program Management Office to manage the NAIRR's day-to-day operations.

Directs the Program Management Office to solicit bids for an Operating Entity for the NAIRR and to oversee that Entity.

Provides for the NAIRR to be resourced with computational resources, data, educational tools and services, and AI testbeds.

Specifies eligibility for access to resources in the NAIRR, including academic, nonprofit, government, and small businesses, among others.

Provides for procedures to establish privacy, ethical, safety and scientific integrity requirements for users of the NAIRR.

Authorizes the NAIRR to charge fees for users at various tiers, including free and subsidized tiers.

Provides for security requirements to prevent unauthorized access and protect research security.

name: FY2021 NDAA
Governance Principles for a New Generation of Artificial Intelligence
summary: Provides eight aspirational principles for the responsible global development of artificial intelligence: harmony and friendliness, fairness and justice, inclusivity and sharing, respect of privacy, safety and controllability, shared responsibility, open collaboration, and agile governance.

name: Digital Fairness Act - Sections 7-9 ("AUTOMATED DECISION SYSTEM IMPACT ASSESSMENTS," etc.)
summary:
Require the state and its entities to conduct Automated Decision System (ADS) Impact Assessments before using any ADS.

Mandate the engagement of a neutral third party to evaluate the ADS, focusing on statistical impacts on protected classes, privacy, and security.

Prohibit purchasing or using ADS without publishing the assessment and considering public comments.

Obligate the state to maintain a list of qualified neutral third parties for conducting assessments.

Require a comprehensive study on the impacts of ADS, particularly on protected classes, to be published within two years.

Demand plain-language notifications to individuals affected by ADS decisions and provide mechanisms for human review.

Ban payments for ADS that do not use open-source software or comply with assessment and policy requirements.

name: New Jersey act against discrimination in automated hiring
summary:
Prohibits the sale of automated decision tools in New Jersey unless they have been subject to a bias audit in the past year, include a free annual bias audit service that provides results to the purchaser, and discloses that the tool is subject to this bill.

Requires anyone who uses an automated employment decision tool to screen candidates to notify each candidate of using the tool within 30 days.

Provides for collecting civil penalties (fines) if the provisions above are violated.

name: New Jersey SB1402
summary:
Bans banks, mortgage companies and other lending institutions from using AI systems which discriminate against members of a protected class; systems are deemed discriminatory if these disproportionately favor or disfavor members of a protected class in the provision of loans and credit terms.

Bans insurance companies from using AI systems which discriminate against members of a protected class; systems are deemed discriminatory if these disproportionately favor or disfavor members of a protected class in providing insurance coverage and setting the terms and rates of such coverage.

Bans health care providers from using AI systems to discriminate against members of a protected class; systems are deemed discriminatory if these disproportionately favor or disfavor members of a protected class in assessing eligibility for healthcare services.

Categorizes the above use of AI systems which discriminate against members of protected classes as unlawful discrimination; such companies and service providers are subject to fines not exceeding $10,000 on the first instance, if these companies have not committed prior violations within five years of the charge, and permits victims to file civil lawsuits against such companies.

name: New York Data Privacy Act, Section 7
summary:
Requires any entity in New York that uses AI or another automated process as the sole basis of a decision that denies access to financial services, insurance, housing, public accommodation, healthcare, or basic necessities to:

(a) Clearly and conspicuously disclose that the decision was made solely on the basis of an automated process; and

(b) Enable any affected individual to appeal the decision, including by giving them the right to have a human review it.

Requires the above entities, and additionally those that use an automated decision systems to determine access to employment and education, to annually solicit an outside auditor to conduct, and make publicly available, an impact assessment of the system that:

(a) Evaluates the system's objectives, design, and training data, as well as how the system was tested for accuracy and discrimination; and 

(b) Assesses whether the system produces discriminatory results on the basis of race, color, ethnicity, religion, national origin, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, familial status, biometric information, lawful source of income, or disability.

name: Voluntary Commitments from Leading Artificial Intelligence Companies
summary:
Acknowledges the voluntary commitments received from Amazon, Anthropic, Google, Inflection, Meta, Microsoft, and OpenAI to the Biden-Harris Administration to help move toward the safe, secure, and transparent development of AI technology.   

Specifies various actionable commitments that will support three broad goals: ensuring products are safe before public release, building systems that put security first, and earning public trust. Commitments include internal and external security testing, sharing information across the industry and with governments, civil society, and academia, and investing in cybersecurity and insider threat safeguards.

Announces the Biden-Harris Administration's development of an executive order and intent to pursue bipartisan legislation in these matters.

name: Blueprint for an AI Bill of Rights
summary:
Requires automated systems to undergo pre-deployment testing, risk identification, mitigation, and ongoing monitoring to ensure safety and effectiveness.

Requires that systems avoid the use of inappropriate or irrelevant data and that independent evaluations and public reporting confirm system safety and effectiveness.

Imposes protections against algorithmic discrimination by incorporating proactive equity assessments, representative data usage, and continuous disparity testing and mitigation.

Enforces data privacy through built-in protections, user consent for data collection, and limitations on data use and sharing, particularly in sensitive domains such as health, education, and finance.

Institutes heightened oversight and limits on surveillance technologies to protect civil liberties, privacy, and democratic values, with specific restrictions on continuous surveillance in sensitive contexts.

Requires designers and deployers of automated systems to provide clear, timely, and accessible notice and explanations of system use, including the rationale behind decisions impacting individuals.

Calls for independent evaluations and public reporting to ensure transparency and accountability in the use of automated systems, with detailed documentation and assessments.

name: Pennsylvania HB 1380 ("Administration of Assistance Programs")
summary:
Authorizes the department to utilize data analytics and artificial intelligence for eligibility verification and fraud detection in public assistance programs.

Permits the department to access data from other state agencies to verify residency and eligibility of applicants.

Empowers the department to establish rules, regulations, and standards for assistance program administration, including eligibility criteria and benefit modifications.

Requires the department to ensure expenditures do not exceed appropriations and to seek necessary federal waivers or approvals.

Allows the establishment of health savings accounts and medical assistance premiums to aid residents transitioning out of assistance programs.

Mandates physical health managed care organizations to share medical assistance claims data with providers.

name: New Jersey Bill A537 ("Discrimination in Automobile Insurance")
summary:
Require automobile insurers using automated or predictive underwriting systems to annually provide the Department of Banking and Insurance with documentation demonstrating no discriminatory outcomes in pricing based on race, ethnicity, sexual orientation, or religion.

Mandate insurers to show that each pricing segment is balanced and not disproportionate to the overall policyholder population.

Define ‚Äúautomated or predictive underwriting system‚Äù as a computer-generated process, including robotic process automation, artificial intelligence, or other specialized technology, used to evaluate risk and determine insurance rates.

Authorize the Commissioner of Banking and Insurance to adopt rules and regulations to implement the act.

Specify that the act takes effect on the first day of the sixth month following enactment and applies to automobile insurance policies initiated or renewed from that date.

name: Pennsylvania HB 49 ("AI Business Registry")
summary:
Establishes a registry of businesses operating artificial intelligence (AI) systems in Pennsylvania.

Requires the Department of State to coordinate with other state agencies to create paper and online registry forms.

Mandates the collection of specific information from businesses, including business name, IP address, type of AI code, software intent, and contact details.

Prohibits the sale or commercial use of collected information and exempts it from Right-to-Know Law disclosure.

Maintains a searchable online database for businesses operating AI systems.

Obligates the Department of State to submit an annual report on the registry to legislative committees, detailing the number of registered businesses, registrant distribution by agency, and incurred expenses.

Defines "artificial intelligence" as computer systems performing tasks requiring human intelligence.

Sets the act to take effect 60 days post-enactment.

name: Rhode Island HB 6286 ("GenAI Operating Standards")
summary:
Prohibits companies from using large-scale generative AI models to engage in targeted bias and discrimination.

Mandates companies to label outputs created using large-scale generative AI models with a distinctive watermark.

Requires companies to secure informed consent from consumers before using their data for training models.

Requires companies, to the best of the their extent, to protect the security of collected data from individuals and shield their identities.

Requires companies to conduct regular risk assessments that identify and mitigate reasonably foreseeable risks and harms.

Mandates companies using large-scale generative AI models to register them with the Rhode Island Attorney General's Office. 

Requires the Rhode Island Attorney General's Office to maintain a public registry of all companies that have registered under the above stipulation.

name: North Carolina SB 460 ("Automation and Workforce")
summary:
Establishes the Study Committee on Automation and the Workforce to analyze the impact of automation on North Carolina's workforce, with a focus on low-income and minority workers.

Requires the Committee to include 11 voting members representing labor organizations, employers, and state legislators, appointed by the Governor and legislative leaders.

Designates seven nonvoting ex officio members from key state departments and educational institutions.

Mandates the Committee to review the effects of automation technologies such as AI, industrial robotics, and self-service technologies on employment.

Instructs the Committee to assess educational and training requirements for workers to adapt to automation.

Requires the Committee to report its findings and recommendations to the Governor and Joint Legislative Commission on Governmental Operations before the 2025 General Assembly and biennially thereafter.

name: New Mexico SM 63 ("Structured Decision-making in Child Abuse")
summary:
Requests the Attorney General to convene a task force to study the Children, Youth, and Families Department's use of structured decision-making tools and philosophy.

Mandates the task force to assess the efficacy, impact, and results of these AI-based tools.

Requires the task force to determine if structured decision-making tools lead to better decisions in child abuse and neglect cases.

Directs the task force to analyze staff training, understanding, and data on repeat maltreatment rates since the tool’s introduction.

Instructs the task force to review the outcomes of voluntary placement agreements and safety plans under this new philosophy.

Obligates the task force to make recommendations for improvements and the future use of these tools.

Involves input from diverse stakeholders, including experts in law enforcement, child maltreatment, behavioral health, and representatives from various departments and communities.

Requires collaboration with a post-secondary institution for research.

Demands findings and recommendations be presented to the legislative health and human services committee by August 1, 2024.

name: Texas HB 4695 ("AI and Mental Health")
summary:
Requires commission approval for AI mental health applications and mandates licensed supervision, informed consent, and clear AI disclosure. Permits liability-free testing with specialized consent. 

Mandates that licensed mental health professionals supervise AI mental health services, ensuring availability for review, communication, and intervention. Obliges providers to obtain informed consent and clearly inform users about the use of AI technology.
Subjects AI mental health service providers to the same disciplinary actions and record-keeping requirements as licensed mental health professionals.

name: New Jersey SB 3876 ("Artificial Intelligence Officer")
summary:
Establishes the position of Artificial Intelligence Officer to develop and update procedures regulating automated systems used by state agencies for critical decisions.

Mandates state agencies to comply with these procedures and submit inventories of their automated systems, which will be published online.

Creates the New Jersey Artificial Intelligence Advisory Board to advise state agencies, hold public hearings on preliminary procedures, and issue reports and recommendations.

Establishes the position of Artificial Intelligence Implementation Officer to review and approve or deny new automated systems based on compliance with procedures, and conduct periodic reevaluations.

Forms a task force to study AI and create an AI Bill of Rights, with a report due within one year.

Subjects officers and the board to open public records laws while protecting trade secrets and work product protections.

name: New York A7106 ("PAID Act")
summary:
Amends the election law to mandate disclosure of synthetic media in political communications.

Requires disclosure for printed or digital political communications to state: "This political communication was created with the assistance of artificial intelligence."

Mandates non-printed or digital political communications to clearly display or speak the same statement.

Defines "synthetic media" as any media created or modified using artificial intelligence algorithms.

Sets the effective date of this act to January 1, 2024.

name: Massachusetts Bill S. 31 ("Regulate GenAI")
summary:
Regulate generative AI models, such as ChatGPT, to protect public safety, privacy, and intellectual property rights.

Define "large-scale generative artificial intelligence model" as those with at least one billion parameters.

Prohibit the use of AI models for discrimination or bias based on protected characteristics.

Mandate AI-generated text to contain a distinctive watermark or offer an authentication process to prevent plagiarism.

Require companies to implement reasonable security measures to protect training data.

Obtain informed consent from individuals before collecting, using, or disclosing their data.

Delete or de-identify data when no longer needed for the intended purpose.

Conduct regular risk assessments to identify and mitigate foreseeable risks and harms.

Mandate companies operating large-scale AI models to register with the attorney general within 90 days, including detailed model and data practices.

Authorize the attorney general to adopt regulations and enforce compliance, including bringing legal action for violations.

name: Massachusetts Bill H.64 ("Automated Decision Making Commission")
summary:
Establishes a commission within the executive office of technology services and security to study and make recommendations on the use of automated decision systems (ADS) by the Commonwealth of Massachusetts.

Requires the commission to survey all uses of ADS by Massachusetts offices, including procurement, evaluation, training, validation, transparency, and accountability.

Mandates the commission to consult experts on machine learning, algorithmic bias, and civil rights, and to examine research on disparate impacts of ADS based on group characteristics.

Obligates the commission to examine data protection, intellectual property issues, and other opportunities and risks associated with ADS.

Compels the commission to meet at least 10 times a year and hold public hearings for feedback.

Requires the commission to submit an annual report detailing activities, findings, and regulatory recommendations to the governor and state legislature.

name: New York Bill A5309 ("Responsible AI Standards")
summary:
Amends the state finance law to require state units to purchase only products or services containing algorithmic decision systems adhering to responsible artificial intelligence standards.

Mandates the avoidance of harm, including minimizing risks of physical or mental injury, unjustified information deletion or disclosure, and unwarranted damage to property, reputation, or the environment.

Emphasizes a commitment to transparency, including full disclosure of the algorithmic decision system's capabilities, limitations, and potential problems.

Prioritizes fairness by eliminating discrimination, promoting equality, and providing feedback mechanisms to redress harms.

Amends the executive law to define "unlawful discriminatory practice" to include actions performed through algorithmic decision systems.

Require the commissioner of taxation and finance to adopt regulations to implement these provisions.

name: New York S7422 ("AI Displacing Actors")
summary:
Exclude productions using AI that displace employees from being considered a "qualified film" for the Empire State Film Production Credit.

Carves out an exception to the above for films covered by current collective bargaining agreements that allow for AI to displace employees.

name: Australia’s AI Ethics Principles
summary:
Prioritizes AI systems that benefit individuals, society, and the environment throughout their lifecycle.

Requires AI systems to respect human rights, diversity, and individual autonomy, promoting an equitable society.

Mandates fairness by ensuring AI inclusivity and accessibility, prohibiting unfair discrimination.

Demands privacy protection and data security, with ongoing data governance and vulnerability assessments.

Ensures AI reliability and safety, mandating operation in line with intended purposes and risk management.

Calls for transparency and explainability, necessitating timely and responsible disclosures of AI impacts.

Establishes contestability, allowing challenges to AI impacts on individuals or communities through clear processes.

Holds relevant parties accountable for AI outcomes, requiring identifiable responsibility and human oversight.

name: Maintaining American Leadership in Artificial Intelligence (EO 13859)
summary:
Mandates the Federal Government to maintain U.S. leadership in AI through a coordinated strategy known as the American AI Initiative.

Requires agencies to pursue strategic guidelines to prioritize AI R&D, enhance data accessibility, and reduce barriers for AI deployment, ensuring protection of civil liberties and privacy.

Obligates agencies to develop technical standards to minimize vulnerabilities and foster public trust in AI systems.

Directs the prioritization and training of American workers in AI-related skills to prepare them for future job markets.

Instructs the development of international standards and promotes global collaboration while safeguarding critical AI technologies from foreign adversaries.

Develops an action plan to protect U.S. advantages in AI technology against strategic competitors and adversaries.

name: NSTC/OSTP Framework for Nucleic Acid Synthesis Screening
authority: Office of Science and Technology Policy
summary:
Mandates the federal government to mitigate misuse risks of synthetic nucleic acids by establishing a procurement screening framework.

Requires synthetic nucleic acid providers and equipment manufacturers to implement comprehensive screening measures for sequences of concern (SOCs) and verify customer legitimacy.

Directs the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) to collaborate with industry to refine technical specifications for effective screening.

Obliges federal funding agencies to ensure compliance with the framework for research funded by federal life sciences grants.

Instructs providers and manufacturers to report suspicious purchase orders to relevant authorities and retain records for at least three years.

Imposes cybersecurity measures to protect sensitive data and customer information, following specific security guidelines.

Anticipates framework updates based on technological advancements and encourages the use of independent audits for compliance verification.

name: AI Liability Directive
summary:
Establishes common rules for non-contractual fault-based civil claims related to damages caused by high-risk AI systems.

Requires disclosure of evidence from AI providers or users to substantiate claims, with courts empowered to order such disclosures.

Presumes non-compliance with duty of care if defendants fail to comply with evidence disclosure orders.

Presumes a causal link between defendant’s fault and AI system's output if certain conditions are met, allowing defendants to rebut the presumption.

Permits Member States to adopt more favorable rules for claimants, compatibility with Union law required.

Mandates evaluation and review by the European Commission within five years, considering the necessity of no-fault liability and insurance for AI operators.

Amends Directive (EU) 2020/1828 to include AI Liability Directive.

Obligates Member States to transpose the Directive into national law within two years and communicate relevant national legislative texts to the Commission.

name: AI Safety Summit - Enhancing Frontier AI Safety (Amazon)
summary:
Facilitates AI development and deployment through Amazon Web Services (AWS), offering a comprehensive suite of AI and ML services, including Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Titan Foundation Models, which support generative AI applications.

Implements risk management and safety protocols, including systematic model evaluation, red teaming, and ongoing security assessments, to mitigate potential AI risks.

Protects AI models and data using robust logical and physical security measures, such as encryption, access controls, and least privilege principles.

Shares AI service information transparently through AI Service Cards, detailing intended use cases, limitations, and responsible AI design considerations.

Encourages responsible AI use and prohibits misuse through the AWS Responsible AI Policy, which addresses concerns like disinformation and privacy violations.

Invests in research and academic partnerships to advance responsible AI practices and develop tools for bias mitigation and human oversight.

Monitors AI misuse post-release, employing classifier guardrails and automated abuse detection to identify and address harmful content and misuse patterns.

name: OpenAI's Approach to Frontier Risk (An Update for the UK AI Safety Summit)
summary:
States that OpenAI's is establishing a Preparedness Framework to manage risks from frontier AI models, focusing on a development process governance structure and preemption of catastrophic outcomes; this work will complement existing risk mitigation work and includes a joint Deployment Safety Board with Microsoft. 

States that OpenAI is creating Superalignment and Preparedness teams within the company to align AI systems with human intent and track and prepare for frontier risks, including cybersecurity, CBRN, persuasion, and autonomous replication and adaptation. Notes that OpenAI is also increasing investment into cybersecurity and insider threat safeguards.

States that OpenAI implemened red-teaming and evaluations to assess new models for safety, including GPT-4 and DALL-E 3, focusing on dual-use capabilities, cybersecurity vulnerabilities, and self-replication.

States that OpenAI will include the publication of a system card in every new AI system, which informs users of key factors impacting system behavior.

States that OpenAI has initiated a reporting mechanism for responsible disclosure of dangerous capabilities among AI labs, focusing on national security-related risks.

Details OpenAI's emphasis post-deployment monitoring for misuse, security controls to protect intellectual property and data, and the development progress provenance techniques to identify AI-generated content.

States that OpenAI implemented data input controls and provides mechanisms for users to opt-out of their data being used for AI training.

name: Inventorship Guidance for AI-Assisted Inventions
summary:
Mandates that inventors named on U.S. patents and applications must be natural persons, reaffirming that AI systems cannot be recognized as inventors.

Clarifies that AI-assisted inventions are not unpatentable due to improper inventorship, provided a natural person significantly contributed to the invention's conception.

Requires that patent applications for AI-assisted inventions name natural persons who meet the Pannu factors as inventors, ensuring each claim has a human contributor.

Outlines the duty of disclosure and reasonable inquiry, emphasizing the importance of factual inventorship claims and compliance with regulations.

Establishes guidelines for correcting inventorship errors and emphasizes that AI systems cannot hold inventorship rights.

Applies guidance to design and plant patents, affirming that significant human contribution is necessary for patent eligibility.

Prohibits naming AI systems as inventors in priority claims for U.S. patents and applications, ensuring compliance with U.S. inventorship requirements.

name: Our Policy on Frontier Safety (Inflection)
summary:
Commits Inflection to a disciplined, phased approach to scaling AI models, emphasizing pre-deployment safety, post-launch monitoring, and global governance.

Requires robust evaluations and third-party red-teaming before public launch to ensure models do not provide harmful information or engage in discriminatory conduct.

Implements strict data input controls and audits, involving executive review and legal evaluations of training data for compliance with legal and ethical standards.

Ensures high-level security controls to prevent unauthorized access and misuse of AI models, including internal restrictions and a bug bounty program.

Maintains around-the-clock monitoring to detect and mitigate model misuse, employing frontier AI to enhance situational awareness.

Publishes model capabilities and limitations, supporting transparency and enabling risk assessment by users and regulators.

Advocates for standardized vulnerability reporting structures and participates in a pilot bug bounty program to encourage third-party disclosures.

Prioritizes research on AI risks and supports the creation of an International Panel on AI Safety.

Promotes cross-industry collaboration for identifying AI-generated material, focusing on child safety and standardized watermarking.

name: Pay Flexibility, Incentive Pay, and Leave and Workforce Flexibility Programs for Artificial Intelligence (AI), AI-enabling, and Other Key Technical Employees (OPM)
summary:
Grants agencies discretionary authority to use various pay flexibilities, incentive pay, and leave and workforce flexibility programs to recruit, relocate, and retain AI and key technical employees.

Allows recruitment, relocation, and retention incentives up to 25% of basic pay, and provides for waivers to increase this limit to 50% based on critical needs.

Enables agencies to repay student loans as an incentive, with limits of $10,000 annually and $60,000 total per employee.

Permits setting higher pay rates for employees with superior qualifications or special needs, and requests OPM approval for special rates and critical position pay.

Authorizes alternative work schedules, telework, and remote work to enhance recruitment and retention.

Provides service credit for non-Federal work experience towards higher annual leave accrual rates.

Encourages collaboration with agency officials to design tailored recruitment and retention strategies utilizing available human resources tools.

name: Bipartisan Framework for U.S. AI Act
summary:
Establishes a licensing regime requiring companies developing sophisticated A.I. models to register with an independent oversight body. 

Requires developers to maintain risk management, pre-deployment testing, and reporting programs as part of licensing conditions.

Grants the oversight body authority to audit companies and cooperate with state Attorneys General.

Mandates Congress to ensure A.I. companies are legally accountable for harms caused by their models, including privacy breaches and civil rights violations.

Urges Congress to use export controls and sanctions to limit A.I. technology transfers to adversary nations.

Promotes transparency by requiring companies to disclose A.I. model information and ensure users know they are interacting with A.I.

Requires A.I. system providers to label deepfakes and maintain a public database of A.I. information.

Obliges companies to implement consumer protections, including safety brakes and data usage control, especially concerning children.

name: Part 170: Health Data, Technology, and Interoperability: Certification Program Updates, Algorithm Transparency, and Information Sharing
authority: Department of Health and Human Services
summary:
Amends health IT certification criteria to include "Predictive Decision Support Intervention," addressing decision-making support based on algorithms for predictions, classifications, and recommendations.

Mandates that health IT systems enable recording of patient demographics, including race, ethnicity, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, and pronouns, using specified standards.

Requires health IT modules to be updated to meet new certification criteria and provide updates to customers as per defined dates.

Outlines certification criteria for health IT, including decision support interventions that must be evidence-based and use specified data standards.

Establishes risk management practices for predictive decision support interventions, including risk analysis, mitigation, and governance.

Incorporates by reference various health information standards, including HL7, LOINC, and SNOMED CT, to ensure interoperability and accuracy in electronic health information exchange.

name: Section 106.11 Application: Nondiscrimination on the Basis of Sex in Education Programs or Activities Receiving Federal Financial Assistance
summary:
Requires recipients to address sex-based harassment within their education programs or activities, including off-campus and remote settings, aligning with recent court decisions.

Clarifies that institutions are responsible for discrimination within contexts they control, such as AI technologies used in educational settings.

Acknowledges requests for examples involving AI and other specific circumstances but declines to provide additional examples or exhaustive lists.

Confirms obligations for conduct during institution-sponsored events, online classes, and use of digital platforms, including AI technologies.

Deletes references to sex-based harassment occurring outside the U.S. but maintains the obligation to address contributing conduct external to the program or activity.

name: Train Crew Size Safety Requirements (New Technology and Automated Operations)
summary:
Require railroads seeking to use automation technology non-compliant with FRA safety regulations to file a petition for rulemaking or a waiver.

Mandate a risk assessment before initiating operations under special approval processes.

Acknowledge freight rail industry's concerns about competition with automated trucking but emphasize rail safety hazards from reduced crew sizes.

Disagree with assertions that labor-saving technologies like PTC justify removal of crew members, stating such technologies are not fully developed.

Support technological advancement in rail through research on AI and automation, including drones and real-time safety systems.

Permit railroads to petition for rulemaking or waivers to use technology that doesn't meet existing regulatory requirements, ensuring safety justifications are provided.

Clarify that the rule does not impede innovation but requires description of technology used to support tasks typically performed by a second crew member.

name: 2023 UK AI Safety Summit Response (Meta)
summary:
Commits Meta to responsible AI development, prioritizing safety and transparency in AI systems, including the Llama 2 model.

Demonstrates actions taken in furtherance of the White House Commitments to establish AI guardrails, focusing on safety, security, and trust.

Conducted extensive model evaluations and red teaming, including external testing at DEFCON, to identify and mitigate risks in AI models including adversarial inputs like unqualified advice.

Requires information sharing and reporting on AI vulnerabilities with established feedback mechanisms for continuous improvement.

Implemented robust security controls for AI model weights to ensure model relliability, treating them as core intellectual property.

Participated in industry initiatives like the Synthetic Media Framework to ensure identification and disclosure of AI-generated content.

Invested in research on AI societal, safety, and security risks, and collaborates with policymakers through the Open Loop program.

Conducted privacy reviews for AI data inputs, excluding private user data, and offers users control over data shared with generative AI features.

name: HHS Public Benefits and AI
authority: Department of Health and Human Services
summary:
Requires the United States Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to promote responsible AI use in public benefits administration by State, Local, Tribal, and Territorial Governments (STLTs).

Encourages STLTs to align with the principles of the National Institute of Standards and Technology AI Risk Management Framework and the Blueprint for an AI Bill of Rights.

Recommends STLTs assess AI systems for equitable outcomes, notify recipients about AI use, and ensure human oversight and appeal processes.

Supports STLTs in developing AI policies and practices through guidance, technical assistance, and resources.

Urges STLTs to focus on safeguarding privacy, civil rights, and safety, and to provide opt-out options for AI systems.

Emphasizes the need for transparency, public engagement, and governance to manage AI-associated risks.

Directs HHS to work with STLTs and other agencies to ensure AI systems in public benefits programs are safe, equitable, and efficient.

name: USDA Framework for State, Local, Tribal, and Territorial Use of Artificial Intelligence for Public Benefit Administration
summary:
The framework mandates the USDA to guide states, localities, tribes, and territories in the responsible use of AI for administering USDA nutrition benefits, as per Executive Order 14110.

Ensures AI systems maximize access for eligible recipients and comply with merit system requirements.

Requires notification to the Secretary in cases of reliance on AI, allowing appeals to human reviewers and ensuring auditability of AI decisions.

Mandates equitable outcomes from AI systems and prohibits AI from directly making adverse decisions in benefits administration.

Advocates for transparency and accountability, providing opt-out options from AI systems.

Encourages responsible innovation, requiring AI usage only with appropriate training and governance.

Requires SLTT agencies to report AI usage and its impact, with ongoing monitoring to mitigate risks and biases.

Stresses collaboration with tribes to respect data sovereignty.

name: Frontier AI Safety Commitments, AI Seoul Summit 2024
summary:
Announces on behalf of the UK and Republic of Korea governments companies, including Amazon, Google, and OpenAI, that have committed to the Frontier AI Safety Commitments. Mandates that companies publish a safety framework, requires transparency on evolving safety approaches, and implement various best practices.

Defines outcome one as organizations identifying, assessing, and managing risks when developing and deploying frontier AI systems. Defines five sub-outcomes, including internal and external evaluations, establishment of risk thresholds and response processes for violations, and investment in risk mitigation effectiveness.

Defines outcome two as organizational accountability established through the development and review of governance frameworks. 

Defines outcome three as established transparency about organizational approaches to frontier AI safety for external actors, including governments. Mandates provision of information about best practice implementation to the public and explanation of how external actors are involved in risk assessment and framework adherence.

name: 2023 UK AI Safety Summit Response (Google DeepMind)
summary:
Describes Google DeepMind's commitment to responsible AI development, emphasizing adherence to AI Principles to ensure technologies are socially beneficial, avoid bias, uphold safety standards, and respect privacy. 

Establishes a Responsible AI Council and Responsible Development and Innovation team to assess ethics and safety risks in AI models, guiding model and product development.
